author: bzorn
body:
This PR follows up #86 with fixes from a second blind rebuild, run on the final merged text. The rebuild passed all 110 scenarios, with 0 failures and 0 blocked, and logged 22 ambiguities. Of those, these needed spec changes:

- **§2.4 item 6 regression (introduced in #86).** The rule rejected any output file that lacked the key the explorer reads. That also rejected the valid JR §6.2 status objects (`{status: unavailable, reason}`). Now a run is rejected only when an output file is not JSON or not a JSON object. Each missing key takes its default value. X82 and X107 cover both sides.
- **§4.7 contradicted §2.7 item 3.** When mode C has no `run.json`, `stages` is now `{}`, as §2.7 says.
- **JR §5.10.2.** The section never defined `evidence_details` on comparison findings, although the explorer joins findings to claims through it. It is now the pair's record, with `claim_id` and `result_id`, which matches the published examples.
- **Small gaps:**
  - an empty `observations` list still produces a visual record;
  - a Markdown reference cycle stops at the repeated file (that reference gets `embedded: null`);
  - a declared index that does not parse does not fall back to probing.

None of the items from #83/#84/#85 came back. The remaining entries are interface choices the spec deliberately leaves open (for example, the flag name) or readings the rebuild already resolved correctly.

author: mmyumu
body:
## What
- **Bot tests fixed**: with Jest 27 three of the four suites failed before running (`fetch is not defined`, `ReadableStream is not defined`: its node environment does not expose them to discord.js). Jest 29 with babel-jest; `ts-jest` removed (no TypeScript in the bot). The production dependencies keep their versions: only a few packages move in the lock file's tree.
- `christianclavier.test.js` reads a live website through the bot's private `config.json`: skipped unless `D2R2_LIVE_TESTS=1`.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the bot's tests on Node 20.17 (as its image), on push to main, pull requests and `workflow_dispatch`.
- **Health checks**: the chatbot and lego-house ask their `/ping` with Python (no curl/wget in those images). The Discord bot serves no HTTP, so it rewrites `/tmp/d2r2-alive` every 30 s while connected to Discord, and its check wants that file younger than two minutes.
- `normandy.json`: the bot (`d2r2`) and the chatbot (`chatbot`) deployed by the release; lego-house as a manual component (it runs on pi3, outside any release); the unused `webserver/` and the docs not deployed. `tests: ["tests.yml"]`.
- `CLAUDE.md` (new): the Normandy conventions.

## Why
`normandy.json` tells Normandy what each part of the repository is and how it is deployed (components, the containers they run as), and which workflows are the tests: Normandy will rerun those every night on the default branch and track their results, so a branch that breaks without any change shows up the next morning instead of on the next pull request. `CLAUDE.md` gets a short Normandy section so these conventions hold in later changes.

## Checked
`npm ci && npx jest` in `node:20.17.0-bullseye`: 3 suites pass, 1 skipped (was 3 failing). The chatbot's check command answers `Pong` inside the running container on the VPS. Every tracked file belongs to a component (Normandy's parser). The workflow runs on this pull request.

author: kumanday
body:
## What

`limits.maxWallClockMs` is optional in the semantic judge request and retained judgment (`schemas/semantic-judge.v1.json`, `src/semantic-judge.ts`, `src/codex-judge.ts`).

- Omitted: the judge waits for the evaluator's native terminal result. Caller cancellation (`AbortSignal`, CLI `SIGINT`) still interrupts both the Claude Agent SDK and the Codex app-server backends.
- Supplied: the declared deadline is enforced exactly as before (100 to 300000 ms).
- `maxBudgetUsd` is independent of the deadline.

Ported from `e0e748b` on `feat/smol-cloud` and re-implemented on the 2.0 judge code (study-runtime wrappers, owned Codex turn).

## One 2.0-specific change: migration accounting

2.0 added a reader profile, `codex-relay-0.162.1-no-wall-limit/v1`, that admitted historical relay judgments whose only schema error was the missing `maxWallClockMs`. With the field optional those judgments are valid current-schema evidence, so that admission path could no longer trigger.

`assertArtifact` now validates first and then, when a study selects the profile, labels a Codex 0.162.1 judgment without the limit with the profile; other artifacts are `current-schema`. Inventories of studies that already select the profile keep the same `validationProfile` rows. A study that does not select it now inventories such a judgment as `current-schema` instead of failing. `docs/development/migration-accounting.md` and the profile test describe that behaviour. The `migration.v1` schema enum is unchanged.

## Verification (Node 26.13.0, npm 12.2.2)

Tests only; no live judge call was made.

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- New checks: request and retained judgment validate without the limit; the Claude backend reaches its native result and stays cancellable without a timer; the Codex backend completes and is interruptible without a deadline; the migration profile test covers labelled and unlabelled inventories.
- `node --test dist/test/codex-judge.test.js dist/test/semantic-judge.test.js dist/test/migration-accounting.test.js`: 31 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped.
- Full suite `npm test`: 1225 tests, 1139 pass, 1 fail, 85 skipped on a machine running several other suites at once. The failure was `CLI signals interrupt and finalize the detached Codex child` (`codex.test.js`, a file this PR does not touch), a timeout waiting for nested session evidence. Rerun alone on this branch: `codex.test.js` 51 tests, 50 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped.

author: justinehler
body:
Review: full

The native Portico Account adapter drops Apple and Google even when rebuilt Services advertises them. Map its existing GET /v1/system capability names into the existing provider view model; email signup/help remains gated by email capability. No new endpoint, screen, layout or hostname change.

This is the first transport piece in the approved sign-in work: provider start/completion still follows in separate PRs through NativePorticoSignIn.provider/finishProvider, the exact entry points Gallery #3905 calls. This change does not establish a working provider round trip by itself. It describes browser capability only; /v1/system does not advertise a native Apple bundle allowlist.

Validation: all 9 focused portico-services-native tests pass against in-memory fakes, including both providers, Google alone, unknown capabilities and email/providers absent. No Services/provider requests or device work. One commit, 2 changed files against pinned main 689e2b0453d94cb80f6f4e039ffa3a62a0f17d35. Full required checks run in GitHub.

author: roryeckel
body:
Closes #231.

> This was first branched on #219 (PR #233), and was **rebased onto master after #219 merged**, now on top of #234 as well. It has seven commits:
>
> 1. `test(playback)`: prevent stops once per event and session
> 2. `feat(opencode)`: report v2 subagent completion as agent.stop
> 3. `docs(opencode)`: describe agent.stop for v2 subagents
> 4. `docs`: regenerate the support page from the agent.stop records
> 5. `test(capture)`: make the follow-up mutant spare the first agent.stop *(review)*
> 6. `test(capture)`: anchor the background boundary mutant on its record *(review)*
> 7. `docs(opencode)`: narrow what the opt-in background argument left open *(review)*

OpenCode v2 now reports a finished subagent as `agent.stop`. On 2.3.0, where every subagent runs in the background and `tool.after` only sees the launch notice (#219), `agent.stop`'s `lastMessage` is how a hook gets the child's result.

## History: the signals predate the adapter

Everything `agent.stop` needs has been on the plugin's event subscription since **2.0.0 (2026-09-11)**: before 2.0.17 (2026-09-25), and before the v2 adapter (2026-09-26). Dates are npm publish times.

| Signal | First seen | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The child's own `session.execution.started`, `session.text.ended`, and `succeeded`/`failed` on the plugin's subscription | 2.0.0 | Loopback drives on 2.0.0 and 2.1.4 (with the opt-in `background` argument; out of range, so README only, ADR-0008); captured on 2.0.17 and 2.3.0 |
| Parent/child link: `session.created` `parentID` + `agent`; the subagent tool result's `sessionID` | 2.0.0 | Same drives; `session-created-child` (2.0.17) |
| The parent's `session.inbox.enqueued` item, `metadata {source: "subagent", childID, agent, state}` | 2.0.0 for an opt-in background child; every child from 2.3.0 | Same drives; `subagent-background/inbox-subagent-completed.json` (2.3.0). 2.3.0 also dropped the event's `location` |
| The child's last text | 2.0.0 | Same drives |

Two later changes matter. From 2.3.0 every subagent runs in the background. And `opencode run --standalone` waits for a late background child on 2.2.6, where 2.0.17 cut it off (probed below). The builds in between were not probed.

The range stays `>=2.0.17 <3`.

## Semantics

- **Source:** a child session's own execution `succeeded` or `failed` event, for a child whose `session.created` (with `parentID`) the plugin saw in its own location. The 2.3.0 inbox item is not used, because it only exists for background children.
- **Fields:**

  | Field | Value | Rating |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `session.id` | the **parent's** session id (as on Claude and Copilot) | |
  | `agent.id`, `correlation.agentId` | the child's session id | exact |
  | `agent.type` | the `agent` from the child's `session.created` | emulated |
  | `correlation.parentAgentId` | the parent's session id | emulated |
  | `lastMessage` | the child's buffered text, only when declared; absent if the child failed before any text | emulated |
  | `correlation.turnId` | none | |

- **Observe-only.** `agent.stop.observe` is `approximate`. `agent.stop.prevent` and `agent.stop.notify` are `unsupported`: by the time the event fires, the child's result has already gone back to the parent or been queued for it, and children take no posts. The shim posts nothing for `agent.stop`.
- **The child's own `turn.stop` is kept,** as before (as on Copilot). It fires first, under the child's session id, and `agent.stop` follows in the same per-session queue. This differs from Claude, where (by its hook documentation) a subagent's stop is a `SubagentStop` and not a `Stop`. A v2 `turn.stop` hook therefore still runs for each child, and can't yet tell a child's stop from a top-level one (#232).
- **Each completion dispatches,** so a follow-up to the same child (the subagent tool's `sessionID`) reports again, with the same `agent.id`.

### Code

- `v2/decode.ts`: a new `child` enrichment (`parentID`, `agent`). A succeeded or failed completion that carries it decodes as `agent.stop` under the parent. An interrupted one stays `turn.stop`.
- `v2/shim.ts`:
  - `children` becomes a map of child to `{parentID, agent}`.
  - Text is also buffered when an `agent.stop` hook declares `lastMessage`.
  - An `agent.stop` hook alone subscribes.
  - A child's completion queues a second run that carries the child info.
  - `post` returns unless the event is `turn.stop`.
- `v2/apply.ts`: plans stop messages for both stop events. This leaves `post`'s guard as the single gate, so its mutant can be killed (see Deviations).
- `v2/profile.ts`: five field ratings and three matrix cells, with rationales. It extends the `turn.stop.observe` and `tool.after.observe` rationales, and appends four validation records.
- `harness-playback.ts`:
  - The playback hook's prevent-once set is keyed by **event and session**. Keyed by session alone, the child's `agent.stop` took the parent's one prevention, and the stop drive timed out.
  - The trace records session, agent and correlation ids, and the agent.stop fields a target rates are declared.

## Evidence

All runs were on Windows, with isolated state and the loopback model (constructed replies). No paid model or credential was used.

- **Captured** (`fixtures/opencode/2.0`):
  - `subagent-stop.{input,enrichment,canonical}.json` from 2.0.17.
  - Replay sequences `subagent-stop/events-2.0.17.jsonl` (foreground child) and `events-2.3.0.jsonl` (background child).
  - These come from the default `hooknostic-v2-*` capture root, promoted with `promote-audits.mjs subagent-stop`, which redacts the account segment to `user`.
- **New drive modes:**
  - `subagent-fail`: the child gets HTTP 400 and fails in about 2 s (a 500 retries for about 90 s).
  - `subagent-followup`: a second call to the same child by `sessionID`, with distinct follow-up text.
  - `subagent-opt-in`: `background: true`, with an optional `HKN_CHILD_DELAY_MS`.
- **Live probes:**
  - A failed child gives `agent.stop` with no `lastMessage`, on 2.0.17 and 2.3.0.
  - A follow-up gives two `agent.stop`s with the same `agent.id` and each execution's own text, on 2.0.17 and 2.3.0.
  - Opt-in background on 2.0.17 and 2.2.6 (repeated after review, with the same results):
    - The launch is reported as `running`, and the child's result reaches the parent as a `<subagent>` message.
    - On 2.0.17 a prompt child dispatched `agent.stop`, and its result started a second parent execution with no turn id.
    - With the child 3 s late, 2.0.17's `run --standalone` exited first: the child only started, and dispatched neither `turn.stop` nor `agent.stop`.
    - 2.2.6 waited for the same late child, whose result again started a second parent execution.
- **Profile records** (append-only):
  - 2.0.17 `captured`
  - 2.3.0 `captured`
  - 2.0.17 `live-probe` (fail, follow-up, opt-in cut-off)
  - 2.2.6 `live-probe` (`run` waited)

## Tests

Every new test was seen failing against its named mutant, and each mutant is in `.capture/opencode-v2/verify-mutations.mjs`. Unit tests run against both captured sequences, so each unit mutant fails twice.

| Test | What it pins | Mutant(s), all killed on 2.0.17 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 fixture loop, `subagent-stop.input.json` | decodes to `agent.stop` under the parent | `agent-stop-decode` (child branch dropped), `agent-stop-session` (child id as `session.id`) |

body:
## ⚠️ Reverses an owner decision (2026-08-11): lengths and offsets are no longer frozen at the author's default

**In plain words:** until now, when a member changed a window length, a history offset or a loop bound of an imported Pine script, the per-bar runtime silently kept using the **author's default**. That was a deliberate owner rule from 2026-08-11 ("folding an input freezes its default into the saved definition"), and it kept the chart's column lane and the runtime agreeing because **both** froze. This PR makes the column lane honour the member's length (settings parity 2a), so a runtime that kept the default became the very divergence the rule existed to prevent (measured on RS Rating: `ta.sma(rs, lenMa)` over SP:SPX kept 21 while the member and the chart had 30). The runtime front end's frozen resolver is therefore **retired**: every such fold now uses the member's value, within the author's own bounds (an out-of-range value is refused by name, never clamped). The owner's 2026-11-16 ask ("every TradingView setting changeable ... essentially a direct copy") supersedes the 2026-08-11 rule. Five tests that pinned the freeze are updated, each saying so (`runtime/__tests__/history`, `historyExpression`, `boundedSlotOffset`, `w4SimpleFolding`).

## Settings parity: an imported Pine script's settings change per chart, its drawings included

The owner's ask: an imported indicator (Fred6724's RS Rating first) lets a member change its settings on the chart as TradingView does. Engine: joins the ENGINE 66 train; the `NUMBER PENDING` history lines are left for the train's number step.

### 2a: a folded length is a chart setting
- The translator folds a window length into the tree as a literal and records where (`compute.paramManifest`). `paramInputs.js` declares each attached parameter on load as an `int` / `float` input `param<N>` with the author's title and bounds; never stored (`stripParamInputs` on every save). `memberDocumentProjection.js` applies the load-time settings after the (unchanged) migration.
- `computeFor` specialises the tree per instance (copy-on-write at the manifest's locators, memoised per value set). A stored value the bounds refuse is refused by name on every column (`setting:param-refused`, a new guard namespace).
- **Alerts compute the same tree** (`api/services/param_inputs.py`): the alert lane evaluates the specialised plot tree for the alert row's `params_json`, and an alert's label names the length its chart set. Parity fixture `param_inputs_parity.json`, written by the JS lane, read by `test_param_inputs.py` (chart == alert at length 30, plus a control that the rail sees a wrong alert).
- Speed: a settings change on 5,000 bars, warm: 15-22 ms.

### 2c: a run half's own settings (the drawings)
- `runHalfInputs.js`: `hostReadNames(source)` is a conservative static closure of what the plots can read, proved over all 266 committed scripts against every input the translator folds into a plot (0 misses after three fixes it found: `else` arms, dotted method calls, named arguments). The script's literal settings no plot reads are declared on load (`fromRunHalf`, never stored).
- The run half is handed the chart's values in its own names; the column rail still holds every mapped run column to the host's at those settings; the run half's program stamp is checked on the stored trees.
- **Evidence per setting.** A moved setting a drawing can read (`drawingReadNames`) is served only when two counted captures were taken with it moved (`runHalfSettingsAdmitted` / server `run_half_settings_admits`, settings cases in `run_half_evidence_parity.json`, both suites). Captures taken at moved settings no longer count for the defaults. A moved setting no drawing reads needs none. Without evidence, or for a moved plot colour, the run half is refused by name and the host object program draws nothing it folded at the default.
- A REASSIGNED input (`if lookback2 == 250 and timeframe.isweekly`) folded at its default in the W4-T2 simple fold (it re-parsed the declaration out of context and lost the bound name); fixed, rail `memberInputFold.test.js`.

### The vendor harness grades a capture at its own settings
`captureInputs.js` maps TradingView's `in_k` to the k-th `name = input(…)` binding and that to our instance key; `ourSide.js` computes at those values (plots, binder pass, object lane); `compare.mjs` grades a capture whose every moved input our side moved too, and still refuses one it did not.

### RS Rating evidence (in this PR)
Captured 2026-11-16 after the close (rig profile; inputs set through the study's own `setInputValues`, read back): defaults, set A and set B on NYSE:RDDT and NASDAQ:ALAB 1D from the listing, with the seed / SPX / industry probes. Supply: the owner's FMP ^GSPC record (2026-11-16T23:13:34Z, through 11/16; rows committed only in the RS supply records under the 2026-11-15 ruling) and a seed replay (812 uploads). Runtime-on, graded on this branch merged with master:

author: marklysze
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

A host that owns timed scheduling needs every assistant profile to accept manual tasks without starting a local scheduler or preventing the host from sleeping. Skipping the poll loop alone still accepts timed tasks and publishes sleep holds.

Add `local_timed_tasks=True` to `ProfileManager`, propagated to each runtime and `TaskService` (also available on `build_gateway`). With `False`:

- Native timed creation, schedule changes to once/cron, resuming legacy timed tasks, and scheduled dispatch are rejected. Manual creation, editing, and Run now keep working.
- No scheduler starts and no scheduled sleep holds are published, including unknown holds for profiles that fail to boot. Active manual runs retain their work holds.
- Existing timed records remain readable and inert. Their readouts identify local scheduling as disabled and omit the next-run timestamp; health reports `disabled by host`. Their stored schedules and history are preserved; the host owns migration or disposition before rollout. Re-enabling the option makes those schedules eligible again.
- Per-turn guidance and native tool descriptions explain the on-demand limitation. The self-knowledge skill retains scheduling-question discovery and describes scheduling conditionally, preserving enabled installs.

The web scheduling controls remain visible; timed saves return HTTP 422 with `Local timed tasks are disabled`. Rejected Enable actions show a dismissible error beside the task list and restore the paused state. Profile changes clear that error, and late failures from the old profile cannot show it again. This adds no external scheduler, platform integration, migration framework, or automatic fallback. `start(scheduler=False)` retains its current worker-only behavior.

## Related issue number

No existing issue.

- [x] I ran `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, and `pytest -m "not integration"` locally and they pass.

Live Chrome pass: enabled a paused legacy task from the drawer and verified the visible error, unchanged paused state, disabled schedule label, missing next-run timestamp, and working Dismiss button. A profile-switch pass confirms the banner is cleared in the new profile. Health shows `disabled by host`. Console and network inspection found only the expected HTTP 422 for the rejected Enable request; other inspected requests returned 200. The regenerated SPA bundle is committed.

Focused tests cover REST/tool errors, scheduled dispatch, legacy storage preservation and readouts, manual execution and holds, all-profile startup/create/restore, failed boots, health, enabled and disabled tool schemas, and actual gateway prompt assembly. author: teamleaderleo
body: Leo, 2026-11-16: "any interesting lessons here: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50517321" The lesson taken from it: "no thundering herd on recovery ... Host boot starts network and broker first, then lanes staged, admitted by measured headroom with jitter." ## What happened On 2026-11-16 one of our agent hosts came back from a stop, and acpmux resumed about 100 chats at once. `resume_queues` gives each restored prompt its own task, and every task called `run_prompt` as soon as startup was done. Nothing limited that, because the host budget meter and `lanes.max_lanes` only warn. The load went to 240-285 on 32 cores. The host's network and broker daemons stopped answering, and `acpmux session info` timed out, so no chat could be moved off the host. The host thrashed at 45 live sessions against its cap of 12. ## The change A restored prompt now waits in `hub/restore_gate.rs` before `run_prompt`. One driver lets the prompts through: 1. **The host's own services come first.** When `ACPMUX_RESTORE_READY_CMD` is set, it must exit 0 before any restored agent starts. A host sets it to its own network and broker checks. The command is retried every 3 s for up to `ACPMUX_RESTORE_READY_WAIT_SECS` (300 by default). After that, restore goes on and `restore.readyCheck` says why. 2. **Chats come back in stages.** Each stage starts cores/8 chats, at least 2, then waits 5 s with jitter of x0.5 to x1.5. A stage starts only while the host budget meter has headroom (load per core, memory pressure, free RAM, swap) and the host is under `lanes.max_lanes`. A chat a stage starts counts as live for up to 120 s, until its agent reports in. Under pressure, one chat still starts per minute, so a busy host makes restore slower but never stuck. 3. **Chats past the cap are parked.** Each parked chat logs `restore_parked` with the reason and is listed in `_acpmux/status` under `restore.parked`, so it can be moved to another host. It resumes when a slot frees. 4. **Spares wait.** Warm spares start only after the restore drains. A person's own prompt is never held. A chat that closes while it waits is skipped. A copy's first start (`clone_boot`) is not gated. `ACPMUX_RESTORE_STAGED=0` brings back the old all-at-once restore. `_acpmux/status` (`acpmux daemon status --json`) has a new `restore` object with `waiting`, `admitted`, `stages`, `holding`, `readyCheck`, `seconds`, `drained` and `parked[]`. ## Tests `hub/restore_gate_tests.rs` runs on tokio's paused clock with a fake host reading. It covers: - The 2026-11-16 restart: 100 chats against a cap of 12 start 2 per stage and stop at 12. The other 88 are parked, each with its reason in its log. - A parked chat starts when a slot frees. - Under pressure, about one chat starts per minute. - With headroom and no cap, every chat starts, and spares wait until the restore drains. - The pure decision functions, `decide` and `stage_size`. Command: `cargo test -p acpmux --lib restore_gate`. Results are posted below. No port: acpmux ships only from feat-cmux-next. ### Observed / Not run - Observed: the pre-push gate passed on this head. - Not yet run: the fleet test run, and a live hard restart of a host. A separate drill, which hard-resets a host under load and times each stage of its return, does that. ## Changelog - Fixed: after a restart, acpmux resumes chats a few at a time while the host has room, instead of all at once. Agent session: [agent session](https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?id=aid-2daaf5548140d656c4ad) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the thundering herd after a host restart: restored chats now resume in headroom-gated stages instead of all at once. On 2026-11-16 a host resumed about 100 chats together after a stop, pushing load to 240–285 on 32 cores and taking down the host's network and broker daemons. A restored prompt now waits at `hub/restore_gate.rs` before its agent starts: - `ACPMUX_RESTORE_READY_CMD` (when set) must exit 0 first, so a host's own network and broker come up before any chat; the command runs once per daemon and the status says what it waits for in fixed words, never the command itself, which may carry a credential. - Chats start in stages: cores/8 per stage (at least 2), gated by the host budget meter and `lanes.max_lanes`, with jittered 5 s gaps. Under pressure one chat still starts per minute, so restore slows down but never stalls. - Chats past the lane cap are parked, each with its reason in its log and in `_acpmux/status` under `restore.parked`; each resumes when a slot frees. Parked entries of closed or deleted chats are pruned. - Warm spares start only after the restore drains; parked chats don't hold them up. - `ACPMUX_RESTORE_STAGED=0` restores the old all-at-once behavior. A person's own prompt is never gated: a new prompt, even one that arrived before startup finished, or an asked resume lets its chat's restored prompt go at once, even past the cap. Another agent's message does not, so lanes can't start each other's parked chats. Chats whose agent host outlived the daemon reattach at once, outside any stage. Creates still starting count toward the cap. If the driver ends early, its waiters go unstaged rather than wait forever. **Tests** `hub/restore_gate_tests.rs` covers the 2026-11-16 scenario (100 chats against a cap of 12), parked chats resuming when slots free, trickle under pressure, a prompt expediting a parked chat, a readiness command never appearing in the status, and the pure `decide`/`stage_size` functions, on tokio's paused clock. Written for commit 00fc14978d06c587965c163c8f88909299832471. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
P1-S13-T03. It depends on P1-S13-T02, which is the human promotion step and not done yet, so this is worked ahead and flagged. The ledger is untouched.

## The result, on main (`fdf093e`)

```
$ python scripts/check_archive_coverage.py --require-one-per-entry
2998 sources as of 2026-11-17T00:33:10Z, SLA 7d: doi-exempt 1249, failed 12, ok 1346, pending 2, withheld 389
309 entries: 309 with a DOI-bearing or archived Source, 0 with only a recorded failure reason, 0 with neither
```

**Every entry already meets the done-when.**

**The seed backlog has cleared.** The rolling archiver worked through it in #154 and #179. Two non-DOI Sources are still `pending`, both inside the 7-day SLA:
- `src-epoch-benchmarks-gpqa-diamond`: the Save Page Now service refuses a re-capture within 24 hours. It is retried after about 2026-11-17 16:00 UTC.
- `src-sceneparsing-csail-eval`.

A follow-up PR records each one as `ok`, or as `failed` with the service's reason (the task's step 2). Neither changes this result, since both entries also cite other archived or DOI Sources.

## What changes

`scripts/check_archive_coverage.py` gains `--require-one-per-entry`. Each curated entry gets one of three states (`data/benchmarks/<family>/*.yaml`; stubs left out):

| State | Meaning | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `archived` | It cites at least one Source with a `doi` or an `archive_url`. | Passes. |
| `recorded` | No such Source, but one of its Sources is `failed` or `withheld` with its `failure_reason`. This is the done-when's "or a recorded failure reason". | Passes, and is listed. |
| `MISSING` | Anything else, for example only `pending` or never-tried Sources. | Fails. |

**How a cited Source is found:** any string in the entry that is a whole Source id, wherever it sits: `source`, `sources`, a `*_source` field, or an evidence row. Prose that merely mentions an id does not count.

**Without the flag, the script is unchanged:** it checks only the SLA. The flag is not added to pr-validate. A newly curated entry's Sources are usually still inside the 7-day window, so it would fail every curation PR. The flag is the exit gate's check.

## Tests

`tests/test_archive_coverage.py` gains three tests:
- the three states over a fixture tree, with Sources cited from `paper.source`, an evidence list, `released_source` and `sources`, and a stub ignored;
- an entry with only a new Source, or citing no Source record, fails, while the same tree passes without the flag;
- `cited()` finds whole ids only.

## Checks run locally

`pytest tests/test_archive_coverage.py`: 46 passed (43 existing, 3 new).

author: boracomet
body:
Phase 2 of the HTML import plan: an Elementor-like structural editor over imported designs, keeping the design's own HTML as the source of truth.

## What changes
- **Seam patch** `0020-elements-seam` (81 lines): a page made only of code sections gets the new canvas and navigator; other pages keep the 0018/0019 behaviour. Editor code lives in `builder/host/elements/`.
- **Source-preserving element operations**: set text/attribute/class, move (any parent, across sections), insert, delete, duplicate (re-ids), wrap / unwrap. Each edit splices the section source at the element's position, so nothing outside the element changes; one labelled undo step each.
- **Full-page frame canvas**: header template + page + footer template in one iframe; header/footer locked with "Edit header/footer"; desktop 1440 logical width fit to the panel, tablet 768, mobile 390, the design's `@media` rules respond.
- **Static edit mode**: design scripts and `on*` attributes neutralised in the frame copy only; Live edit and Preview run them.
- **Selection layer outside the frame**: hover/selection outlines, type label, breadcrumb, toolbar, context menu, keyboard inside the frame (undo/redo, duplicate, delete, Escape → parent, arrows → siblings), in-place text editing.
- **Drag and drop** on the canvas and in the Navigator with direction-aware drop indicator and drop rules (void elements, SVG insides, text-only elements, own subtree, locked parts).
- **Navigator** code branch with element types, reorder/reparent, rename (stored in `content.names`, not in the markup), editor-only hide/show.
- Server: `Boot.codeParts` carries the header/footer templates (contract Go/TS/doc updated); the editor CSP allows the design head's origins (fonts).

## Verification
- `make builder`, `make builder-test` (300 vitest tests incl. new `elements-ops` / `elements-frame`), gofmt/build/vet, Go webbuilder + server subsets pass; new `webbuilder_editor_parts_test.go`.
- Playwright end-to-end on an imported 55-page site: 28/28 (select, keys in frame, drag across columns + undo/redo, wrap/unwrap, text edit, locked header, devices, navigator, script modes, no page errors).
- Publish-unchanged check: stored HTML/CSS and front HTML byte-identical; fidelity tool 0.0000 % at 1440/1024/768/390.
- 703-element page: hover ~16 ms per move, duplicate 52 ms, undo 43 ms.

## Not in this PR
Mixed code + builder pages keep the old per-run frames; Live edit is per session; style editing is phase 3.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large new client editing surface and HTML splice logic affect published markup for code pages; server boot/CSP changes touch editor loading but are scoped to code-section edits and Hello Pursae templates.

> **Overview**
> Adds a **host element editor** for pages made entirely of code sections, wired through patch **`0020-elements-seam`** so `Canvas` and navigator rows delegate to `builder/host/elements` instead of the legacy 0018/0019 frames. Mixed or non-code pages are unchanged.
> 
> The new **full-page iframe canvas** composes locked **header/footer** code templates with page sections (from **`Boot.codeParts`**), supports static / live / preview modes, and edits via source-preserving HTML ops (`data-wbc` ids, drag-and-drop, in-place text, toolbar/context menu/keyboard). The **navigator** exposes the same element tree with rename (`content.names`), hide/show, and cross-section moves.

author: samhv-dev
body:
## What and why

In a simulated cardiac arrest the depth-of-anaesthesia monitor shows an awake brain, and after the circulation returns the cortex is normal again within seconds however long the arrest lasted. The approved plan (`docs/plans/brain-energy-consciousness-recovery.md`, PR 483) repairs both with one brain energy state in the organ model, read by the EEG, by consciousness and by breathing. This PR is its first piece, B1: the state's home, with the one value that already exists (the cortex's metabolic term) moved into it. **No number changes in any patient.**

### The structure

- **`l2/brain/energy.ts`** (new) holds `BrainEnergy`, which is `{ cortex: CortexEntry }`.
  - Every compartment publishes an `EnergyEntry` `{ delivery, fn }`. The cortex's `CortexEntry` adds `metabolic`, its loss of function as the EEG reads it.
  - A compartment's thresholds are data: `Compartment { abnormal, lost }`, with `CORTEX = { DO2_EEG_ABNORMAL, DO2_EEG_LOST }`.
  - The equations are shared: `brainDo2Rel` (moved unchanged) and `functionLoss(delivery, compartment)`, which is main's expression character for character.
  - `metabolic` is the primary value and `fn = 1 − metabolic`. The reverse order would move ischaemic values by one ULP, because `1 − (1 − m) ≠ m` in floating point.
- **`BrainState.energy`** (`l2/brain/model.ts`) is stepped as the last statement of `stepBrain`, on the step's own post-solve `cbfRel` and the blood gases it was computed with. `createBrain` seeds it the same way (one code path).
  - Why this is bit-identical: the EEG used to compute `brainDo2Rel(organs.brain.cbfRel, organs.view.hb/sao2/pao2)`, and `organs.view` is exactly the view whose `brainIn(v)` fed that step.
  - The PbtO2/SjvO2 ratio `r` is unchanged.
- **Constants:** `DO2_EEG_ABNORMAL`, `DO2_EEG_LOST` and `METABOLIC_SLOW_SHARE` move, with their source comments verbatim, from `l2/eeg/state.ts` to `l2/brain/params.ts`.
- **The EEG reads the organ state.**
  - `CortexInputs.do2Rel` is replaced by `metabolic`, the holdable field the MANUAL-depth plan's held patterns need.
  - `cortexStep` takes it and still derives `metSupp` and `suppress` as before.
  - `EegCtx` drops `cbfRel`, `hb`, `sao2` and `pao2` (used only for delivery) and carries `metabolic`. `engine.ts eegCtx` passes `organs.brain.energy.cortex.metabolic`.
- **Snapshot:** `energy` is plain data inside `organs.brain`. `upgradeOrgans` gives a snapshot without the state one derived from the brain's flow and its last view, not reset to normal. A plain default would read `metabolic` 0 until the next 10 Hz step, and an EEG hop can fall into that gap during an arrest.
- **Not in this piece:** no store, no debt, no brainstem entry, no change to consciousness, the artefacts or breathing (plan B2–B8).

### What the later pieces can rely on

- **B6a** adds `store` to `EnergyEntry`. Its demand reads `b.cmro2Rel`, which `stepBrain` sets before the energy step.
- **B6b** adds `debt` and `fnCap`.
- **B5** adds `brainstem` to `BrainEnergy` with its own type (the relocated `anoxS`/gate). **B7** makes it an `EnergyEntry` with its own `Compartment`.
- **B8** adds glucose terms to the supply and to `Compartment`.
- Per-compartment equations with thresholds as data mean regional territories become more entries.
- **B6a must decide** whether `fn` or `metabolic` becomes primary. With a store, `metabolic = 1 − fn` moves ischaemic values by a ULP, and that piece moves values anyway.

### The couplings census

- `neuro.eeg.cortex.metabolic` now reads `organs.brain.energy.cortex.metabolic` (seam `neuro ctx eegCtx.metabolic`) and names only `METABOLIC_SLOW_SHARE`. Its class is still FIT.
- New row `organs.brain.energy.cortex`: from `organs.brain.cbfRel`, `blood.out.hb` (seam `organs ctx organsCtx.blood`), `resp.o2.sa` and `resp.o2.pao2` (seam `organs ctx organsCtx.resp`) to `organs.brain.energy.cortex.metabolic`. It is a threshold row on `DO2_EEG_ABNORMAL` and `DO2_EEG_LOST`, class SOURCED.
- The organ page goes from 6 to 7 rows (SOURCED 0 → 1).
- The four `eegCtx` seams (`cbfRel`, `hb`, `sao2`, `pao2`) are gone. `unregistered.ts` shrinks by two (`organsCtx.blood` and `organsCtx.resp` are now carried). The census page, the model pages and the demo's `registry-data.ts` are regenerated.
- The mechanism tree gains one node and one edge on every trigger. The pins in `graph.test.ts` and `mechanisms.dom.test.ts` move by exactly +1 node and +1 edge (bleed 79/129 → 80/130, propofol 74/123 → 75/124, and so on), and the node count in `labels.test.ts` goes from 152 to 153. The node has a clinical label, "Cortical energy failure" (0–1), unreviewed like every row. `docs/plans/mechanism-tree-labels.md` is the generated copy of that table (`scripts/mechanism-labels.ts`; `labels.test.ts` fails when it is stale), so it was regenerated. That file was not edited by hand.

## The proof that nothing moved

1. **The four arrest courses of research/76, MANUAL and MODELED** (`packages/controller/test/scenario/arrest-cortex.test.ts`). The witnessed-VF card runs through the controller's own `ScenarioDriver` (VF at 120 s; (a) nothing, (b) asystole at +150 s, (c) CPR and bag from +60 s, (d) shock and return of circulation at +120/+121 s), with the EEG on. Every second, the whole `eeg.cortex` state (15 fields) is recorded.
   - The fixture was **recorded on main's code** in the first commit (e12563bd), before any product change. The second commit adds the product change and the fixture is unchanged.
   - The fixture rounds to 1e-9, so a last-ULP libm difference between this Mac (Node 26) and the CI runner (Node 22) cannot fail it except at a rounding edge.
   - Two checks hold exactness. In the test, at **every 20 ms tick** of all eight runs, the organ entry's `delivery` and `metabolic` must equal (`Object.is`) the EEG's old expression on `organs.brain.cbfRel` and `organs.view`. Locally, an uncommitted full-precision copy of the same runs on main (d97830d4) and on this branch gave **byte-identical** JSON, sha256 `4089d5bf…44175`.
2. **Unit tests** (`test/l2/brain/energy.test.ts`):
   - `functionLoss` is `Object.is`-equal to main's expression over delivery 0…1.2 in 0.0005 steps.
   - `stepBrainEnergy` over CBF −0.1…1.4 × three blood-gas sets matches the same reference for delivery and metabolic. `fn = 1 − metabolic`, and `fn` is exactly 1 above the abnormal level.
   - In `stepBrain`, during a shock course, the entry reads the step's own flow and gases at every step.
   - C34's threshold half moved here from `state.test.ts`, which keeps the cortex half (slowing before voltage loss).
3. **Snapshot** (`test/engine/brain-energy-snapshot.test.ts`):
   - A restored engine continues the cortex entry and the EEG cortex bit for bit through an arrest.
   - A snapshot with the state deleted gets it derived on restore, equal to the live one, with `metabolic` > 0.
4. **`eeg-baseline.json`:** untouched, and `eeg-baseline.test.ts` passes on the branch.

Test inputs that built `CortexInputs` with `do2Rel: 1` now use `metabolic: 0`, the same input in the new field. `eeg-cortex.test.ts` used to pass `organs.brain.cbfRel` as if it were delivery. It now reads the published `organs.brain.energy.cortex.metabolic`, which is what the EEG reads; the drug arms never come near the threshold, and the test passes unchanged.

## CI history
- **Final head c60427b1:** ci 43994441757 **success**, with every job green (docs skipped) and no retry-only pass (the only `##[warning]` is the Node.js 20 deprecation). validation 43994441616 **success** (validate success, soak skipped).
- ci run 43989617669 on 61c4c8e8: failure. `e2e (chromium 4/4)` and `e2e (webkit 2/3)` failed in `mechanism-tree.e2e.ts`. Its whole-tree node pins (a copy of graph.test.ts PINS) still said 79/74 where the tree now has 80/75, so both are deterministic +1 pins, not flakes. They are corrected in c60427b1. No job was re-run. No retry-only pass was found in any other e2e job.
- validation run 43989617671 on 61c4c8e8: success (validate succ

body:
Card OPS, PR 11 (tag 5610). Red team RT-1, N6.

## In plain words

A visitor who joins with no key (an old client, or a `?guest=1` tab) used to cost the game five saved rows the moment they arrived, and four of them were kept for good, even if they left without doing anything. Someone could make up ids and spend the game's daily allowance of writes that way. Now a brand-new guest's arrival saves nothing. The first thing actually worth keeping (gold, an item, XP, a pet) saves their character the usual way, and a guest who comes back has it. A normal player who joins with a key is unchanged.

Nothing a player sees changes.

author: mnaimfaizy
body:
## Summary

Production startup (`MODE=production`) now refuses unsafe signing and encryption keys. Development and testing modes are unchanged.

### What production now refuses

Each of `SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_RESET_SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_VERIFICATION_SECRET_KEY` and `ENCRYPT_KEY` must be:

- set (a key no env source supplied no longer falls back to a per-process random value)
- at least 32 characters
- different from the other four
- not a value published in this repository's example or template files (compared by SHA-256 digest; only digests are stored, in `backend/app/core/production_keys.py`)
- not a placeholder: containing `change`, `your-`, `your_`, `replace`, `example`, `placeholder` or `generate`, in any case

One error lists every problem by key name, never by value, for example:

```
Production refuses these key settings: SECRET_KEY is shorter than 32 characters; JWT_RESET_SECRET_KEY and ENCRYPT_KEY have the same value. Each of SECRET_KEY, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY, JWT_RESET_SECRET_KEY, JWT_VERIFICATION_SECRET_KEY, ENCRYPT_KEY needs its own random value. Generate one per key with: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"
```

### Other changes

- `validate_production_settings` raises `ValueError` instead of using `assert`, so `python -O` cannot strip it. The DATABASE_HOST and FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD checks keep their meaning.
- `Settings` sets `hide_input_in_errors=True`, so a startup validation error does not print configured values.
- `JWT_SECRET_KEY` is removed: nothing signed with it. As with `REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS` in #334, a value that is still set is ignored. It is gone from the env examples, docs and hub-runtime bootstraps.
- `backend/.env.example` ships distinct `change-me-dev-*` placeholders, which development and testing accept, plus the generate command.
- Hub-runtime `bootstrap.sh` and `split/_common.sh` generate the five keys as separate random values, and now also add any key line that an older `.env` lacks.
- Hub-runtime bootstraps now generate a `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` that passes the password policy. They used hex, which seeding refused. The generator is the new `_superuser_password.sh`, tested against the real `PasswordValidator`.
- Docs: `SECURITY_FEATURES.md` gains a keys section, and `PRODUCTION_CONFIG_TEMPLATE.md` points at the generate command, replacing the PowerShell `Get-Random` snippets, which were not cryptographically random. The deployment guide, Docker Hub README, `PRODUCTION_SETUP.md`, `backend.md` and the migration guide list all five keys.
- `session-lifecycle.html` is re-anchored. Only `config.py` line numbers changed.

## Breaking change

A production deployment with a missing, short, shared, placeholder or example key now refuses to start, and so does one that never set `JWT_VERIFICATION_SECRET_KEY`. To fix it, generate five distinct keys by running this once per key:

```bash
python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"
```

Rotating `SECRET_KEY` and the JWT keys invalidates existing tokens. Rotating `ENCRYPT_KEY` makes data encrypted with the old key unreadable.

## Tests

- New `backend/test/unit/test_production_key_checks.py` reads every key value from the example and template files at test time and checks that production refuses each one, and that each digest is in the stored set. It also covers each placeholder word, equal keys (named in the message, without the value), a missing or short `JWT_VERIFICATION_SECRET_KEY`, a short `SECRET_KEY`, the `value_error` type, that no configured key is echoed, and that five random keys are accepted. Every env file and key env var is isolated.
- `production_kwargs()` moved to `test/utils.py` and generates distinct random keys. No key literals are committed.
- On unchanged code, 57 of the new and updated tests failed. Now `test/unit` and `test/api` pass with the local env files in place and also with `.env.test` and `.env.test.local` moved aside (CI-like). black, isort, flake8 and mypy are clean.

author: drewstone
body:
## Outcome
Drew can type feedback on any stamped review page and have it reach the session that wrote the page, with no step of his own in between. The stamp line gains a textarea and a **Send** button. The page then shows "Delivered to <name>", or the failure and the command to send it by hand.

## Mechanism
- **`page_author.py`:** each stamp mints a random token (24 url-safe characters). `~/.local/state/page-author/tokens/<token>.json` (0600, in a 0700 directory) records the session id, name, cwd and page. The page script `fetch`es `http://127.0.0.1:47219/feedback` with `Content-Type: text/plain`, so there is no preflight. `PAGE_FEEDBACK_PORT` overrides the port.
- **`page_feedback.py` (new):** the listener. `install.sh` runs it on macOS as the launchd agent `com.dotfiles.page-feedback`, and each install restarts it so it runs the installed code. It binds 127.0.0.1 only.
- **What the listener accepts:** only a POST to `/feedback` with `Origin: null` (file://) and `Host` naming its own port (against DNS rebinding), at most 8 KB, with a known token. It answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` so the page can read the result.
- **Threat model:** any website can POST to localhost, and a sandboxed frame on one also sends `Origin: null`. The token is what keeps them from writing into the owner's agents.
- **Delivery:** the listener runs `page-feedback-send <session id>` from PATH, with `[page feedback] <page path>` and the text on stdin. The private layer supplies the sender.
- **Fallback:** when there is no sender, or the send fails because the session has ended, the message is appended to `inbox.jsonl` (0600). A SessionStart hook (`page_feedback.py --session-start`) gives it to the next session that starts in the author's directory, and the page says the message was queued.

## Checked before merge (listener from this branch on a test port, against a fresh interactive session `pf-proof-cwd-39`)
- **Chrome, file://, headless over CDP:** typed "test feedback 456" and clicked Send. The page read "Delivered to pf-proof-cwd-39." after 505 ms, and the text is in that session's transcript.
- **Safari 26.1, file://:** a self-clicking scratch page posted and then sent back what it read: "safari read the answer: Delivered to pf-proof-cwd-39."
- **Refused:**
  - `Origin: http://evil.example` with a valid token: `403 {"ok": false, "message": "Refused: only a stamped page on this computer can send feedback."}`
  - `Origin: null` with a wrong token: `403 {"ok": false, "message": "Refused: unknown page token, or no text."}`
- **No listener:** "Not delivered: no feedback listener on 127.0.0.1:47298 (Failed to fetch)."
- **Ended session:** the message was queued, the next `--session-start` in that directory printed it, and a second start printed nothing.

## Growth
loc-ratchet counts 223.75 production lines: page_feedback.py 121.6, page_author.py 65.0, install.sh 37.1 and settings.json 5.9 (census token counts / 8). This is a new capability and needs a growth approval from a reviewer other than the author.

author: ouraking
body:
## Objet

Préparer le passage de Vercel à Cloudflare **sans rien couper côté Vercel** : ce changement ajoute seulement des fichiers propres à Cloudflare (ignorés par Vercel via `.vercelignore`). Le site en ligne ne change pas tant que le dépôt n'est pas connecté à Cloudflare.

## Contenu

- `wrangler.jsonc` : site servi tel quel depuis la racine (pas de build), `html_handling: "none"` (sinon `/page.html` serait redirigé vers `/page`, ce qui casserait liens, adresses canoniques, plan du site et précache du service worker), `404.html` pour les pages absentes, Worker lancé seulement pour `/api/*` et `/`.
- `worker/index.js` : portage de `api/contact.js` (origine, champ piège, validation, 5 envois / 10 min, Resend) et `index.html` sur `/`.
- `_headers` : mêmes en-têtes de sécurité et même CSP que `vercel.json`.
- `.assetsignore` : outillage, CI, Worker et fichiers locaux jamais publiés.
- `scripts/ci-security-hygiene.js` : vérifie `_headers` et échoue si sa CSP diffère de celle de `vercel.json`.

## Vérification (local, `wrangler dev`)

- Pages et roadmaps en 200 sans redirection, page 404 servie, fichiers internes (`scripts/`, `worker/`, `.git`, configs) en 404.
- En-têtes de sécurité présents, aucune violation CSP en console, service worker actif.
- Formulaire : 405, 403, piège, 400, 429, 503 puis secours `mailto:` dans la page. Envoi réel non testé (aucune clé Resend en local).

## Frontière de confiance

Nouvel hébergeur et nouvelle fonction serveur : le modèle de menaces (`docs/security/`) sera mis à jour lors de la bascule, avec le changement d'adresse du site.

## Reste à faire (hors de cette PR)

1. Connecter le dépôt dans Cloudflare (Workers Builds, Worker nommé `wiyao`).
2. Ajouter les secrets `RESEND_API_KEY` et `CONTACT_TO` dans le tableau de bord.
3. Domaine propre : remplacer `wiyao.vercel.app` partout (canoniques, plan du site, JSON-LD et son empreinte CSP, images d'aperçu, QR code de l'affiche, mentions « hébergé par »).

author: mmyumu
body:
## What
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, on push to main, pull requests and `workflow_dispatch`:
  - the server's 105 `unittest` tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s backend`, Python 3.12 as the image);
  - every `android/checks` assertion check (Formation … Heat, Diagram), compiled with JDK 17 and org.json from Maven Central. Note: the first command list in the README's *Checking* section no longer compiles without org.json either (`Lineup` uses it).
- `test_requests_are_serial_and_spaced` failed on GitHub's runner: it times requests when they leave, while the gate spaces the slots it grants, and a SQLite write sits between the two. Its interval goes from 25 to 100 ms with a 70 ms floor; the gate itself is unchanged.
- `normandy.json`: the server (container `fonote-backend`) deployed by its release, with the `match.json` it bundles; the Android app as a manual component (`scripts/publish-apk.sh`); docs and checks not deployed. `tests: ["tests.yml"]`.
- `CLAUDE.md`: a Normandy section.

## Why
`normandy.json` tells Normandy what each part of the repository is and how it is deployed (components, the containers they run as), and which workflows are the tests: Normandy will rerun those every night on the default branch and track their results, so a branch that breaks without any change shows up the next morning instead of on the next pull request. `CLAUDE.md` gets a short Normandy section so these conventions hold in later changes. The image already has its health check.

## Checked
Locally: 105 server tests OK, the gate test 15 times in a row; all eleven Java checks pass in `eclipse-temurin:17-jdk` with the same commands. Every tracked file belongs to a component (Normandy's parser).

body:
BUG FIX · EMOJI DISCOVERY · FIXES #3492 ### Adding a relay no longer hides an older emoji set. Discovery stopped after 120 events, before removing overlapping revisions. Three relays could exhaust that budget with only 40 sets. ## The fix Remove one event-level cutoff in `ingest_discovered_sets`. ```diff -for event in events.into_iter().take(MAX_DISCOVERY_EMOJI_SETS * 2) { +for event in events { ```
Regression coverage The regression feeds signed revisions representing two account relays and one configured relay through production ingestion into SQLite, without relay sockets. It checks that all 41 coordinates survive, each shared coordinate retains its newest revision, and a separate case still stops at 60 coordinates. It failed before the fix with 40 discovered sets instead of 41, then passed in 4.364 seconds.
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Emoji set discovery now applies its 60-set limit after deduplicating overlapping revisions, so duplicate sets from multiple relays no longer crowd out older distinct sets.

author: craabreu
body:
## PyPI release workflow

- `.github/workflows/PyPI.yml` builds one abi3 wheel per platform (Linux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x64), for Python 3.11 and later, plus the sdist. Each native wheel is installed and run before upload.
- On a published release it checks that the tag matches the version in `pyproject.toml`, then uploads through trusted publishing from the `pypi` environment (required reviewer, `v*` tags only). The publish action checks the metadata (`twine check`) before uploading.
- On pull requests that touch the build, or run by hand, it builds everything and uploads nothing, as a dry run. This PR runs it.
- The extension now targets the stable ABI (`abi3-py311`). On 1,000 pilot pairs it gives identical results to the version-specific build at the same speed, and the wheel passes the test suite on Python 3.13.
- The README installs with `pip install atommapper`; `pyproject.toml` gains the project URLs and the license; the Rust crate gains its license and repository.

author: sawyerrensel
body:
## Summary

This lands the 3D graph view's first working version. It also carries the mind map work done on the same stack. It covers 270 commits since #47: rounds 3–11, T38–T89. Base is `release/0.0.6`, and the stack started from `feature/3d-graph-view`.

```text
src/
├── graph3d/                 # pure model, unit-tested (107 files): model, settle, flatten,
│                            #   planets, overlays, near, edit, selection-edit, depth, flight
├── views/
│   ├── Graph3DView.ts       # view shell: shared 2D|3D header, toolbar, find bar, settings
│   ├── Graph3DScene.ts      # lazily imported Three.js scene: plates, edges, ribbons, boundaries
│   ├── Graph3DPlates.ts     # glyph-atlas plates (instanced, one draw call)
│   ├── Graph3DNear.ts       # near-tier live Markdown panels (CSS3D in Planets)
│   ├── Graph3DStudy.ts      # relational study: due-driven path, trails, occlusion cards
│   └── MindMapView.ts       # 2D: shared edit pipeline, line groups, boundaries, perf (T77–T89)
├── mindmap-edit.ts          # edit ops shared by 2D and 3D, with a per-file undo history
├── branch-to-note.ts        # Convert branch to note (2D + 3D)
└── line-groups.ts           # adjacent lines form one node (T75)
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Note[Markdown note] --> Model[graph3d model + settle]
  Model --> Layout{Layout}
  Layout --> Organic & Flat & Planets
  Organic & Flat & Planets --> Scene[Graph3DScene: plates · edges · near panels]
  Scene -- edits --> Pipeline[mindmap-edit pipeline + undo]
  MindMap[2D MindMapView] -- edits --> Pipeline
  Pipeline --> Note
```

Headline features:
- **3D layouts:** Organic, Flat branches (ring slices), and Planets (continents, face-up plates, core-layer shells).
- **Moving around:** focus note, hops, follow a link, back/forward, gizmos, joysticks, touchpad orbit, coasting.
- **Editing in 3D:** inline edit, structural edits, multi-select, drag-to-link / Add link menu, Find and Replace. All of it runs through the edit pipeline the 2D map uses.
- **Shared styles:** `osmosis-styles` (fill, border, shape, boundary, branch line) apply in 2D and 3D, and the Osmosis bar is shared too.
- **Relational study** in the 3D graph.
- **2D mind map perf (T77–T89):** batched size reads, a fitted first view, compositor pan, and no scrolled or positioned node content.

New dependencies: `three@0.186.1`, `3d-force-graph@1.80.1`, `@types/three`. The `three/webgpu` alias in `esbuild.config.mjs` stays.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `release/0.0.6` has no 3D graph view.
  **After:** `npm run lint` is clean. `vitest run` passes: **138 files, 3346 tests**. Nothing is marked `it.fails` or `.skip`.
- Fixtures are in `e2e/fixtures/graph3d/` (stress web generator, near-tier, heading links) and `e2e/fixtures/adjacent-lines.md`, mirrored into `vault/tests/`.
- Manual testing went in batches through test-queues 2–8. **Many tickets are still `In-Review`** in `vault/Planner/`: 101 In-Review, 5 Done. Round 11 (T81–T89) has not been manually tested yet, and T89 is unmeasured.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way, mostly.

The code reverts cleanly. A few changes write to the user's notes or settings in ways a revert won't undo:
- Node links now read `[[Note#^id|-->]]`, and new `os-` block IDs are stamped onto styled lines.
- Edits now keep adjacent heading/prose lines together as **one node / one line card** (T75), because the normalizer no longer splits them on write. "Generate flashcards" tags a run once, on its last line.
- `loadSettings` deletes `graph3dPositions` and `graph3dTouchDrag`.
- A heading rename in a node editor rewrites links across the vault when Obsidian's link auto-update is on.

**Blast Radius:** wide

- The 2D mind map is heavily changed (`MindMapView.ts` +3.1k/−1.7k), including how it renders, pans and edits. Regressions would show up for everyone using the mind map, not only 3D users.
- Line-card identity changes for adjacent-line runs (T75) and could affect existing schedules.
- `main.js` grows with Three.js. The 3D scene is lazily imported.
- Mobile: new Osmosis bar layout, the keyboard-resize FOV fix, touch gestures.

Pool item: tests-campaign-ask-answer-is-an-empty-line

Checks (changed files): eslint and prettier pass; the changed test passes at the old pinned seed and fails there on main's code; the pool check passes once this pull request's number is filled in. Typecheck, the other campaign tests and the release check were not run here.

**What changed for the player.** When you ask the people you know to volunteer or to endorse you, every answer now shows who answered and what they said. Before, someone you knew only in passing answered with no name and a blank line.

## The cause

The ask goes to everyone on the candidate's list of people they know. At St. Hedwig, Texas one of them was still in the counted population, not a full person. The volunteer ask read no person there and recorded a no, and the words engine has no speaker to word, so the answer came back empty. The code is `campaignAct` in `src/bench/campaign.ts`.

## What changed

- Before asking, `campaignAct` fills in each person it asks with `personOrFillIn`, the game's own call for someone the player deals with (the two-level rule). An id that no record holds is not asked.
- This runs only for the volunteer and endorsement asks, not for a contribution or a poll.
- The test's expected-failure mark comes off, it draws its place again, and its pass line names the place and every place it passed over.
- Its limit goes back to 1,800 seconds, its own limit before it was pinned.

## Done when

| Done-when line | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| The pinned case passes on the Train with the cause named in the PR body by record | At the old pinned seed (`GOLDEN_PATH_SEED=pin-campaign-asks-spoken`), St. Hedwig, Texas (4864172), the test passes. Jennifer Olsen answers the volunteer ask "I'd like to, but I can't spare the time right now." The answer that was empty came from person_08ff0f2079a06a98. |
| A second session runs the file and then replays the case in a drawn place | Not yet: a second session runs it on a fresh draw. |

**How a second session checks it in the game.** File for a race, open the campaign, and ask your acquaintances to volunteer and then to endorse you. Every answer has a name and words. Then run `npx vitest run src/bench/campaign-asks-spoken.test.ts` on a fresh draw.

**Break-it check.** With `src/bench/campaign.ts` from main and the new test, the same seed fails: "person_08ff0f2079a06a98: expected '' to be truthy". With the fix it passes.

**The guard on this change.** #9752's check-changes reports one dropped case and one dropped assertion. They are the case that checked the fixed seed drew St. Hedwig, which has nothing to check once the place is drawn (the same pattern as #9766). This pull request needs the CTO's line for that.

**For Screens.** The change is in `src/bench/campaign.ts`, the campaign's handler, not a screen file; it is ten lines and posted on the crew issue.

**Removed.** The fixed seed, the pin-checking case and the expected-failure mark.

## How it was checked

- At seed pin-campaign-asks-spoken the test passed with the fix in 139 seconds, one worker.
- With main's `campaign.ts` and the same seed, it failed on the empty line.
- eslint and prettier on the changed files; `npm run pool -- --check` for this item.
- Not run: typecheck, the other tests that call `campaignAct`, and the release check (this cloud clone is shallow; CI runs it).

author: luisfpires18
body:
Tier: Standard. Implementation of #293 (tracker #303). Plan was accepted; no deviations.

Owner deferred CI and local Playwright E2E to the tracker end.

## Approach

Extend the #288 mechanism with the Comic formats. No new column, migration, class, endpoint or domain. Comic projects get the same optional `Format` already stored in `CreativeProjects.Format` (nullable, max 40).

Format ids (kebab, stable), all mapped to `ProjectKind.Comic` in `src/LorEvolve.Api/Features/Projects/ProjectFormats.cs`:
`western-comic`, `manga`, `graphic-novel`, `one-shot`, `webcomic` (label "Webcomic / Webtoon").

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All five formats selectable: five lines in `ProjectFormats.KindOf`; `CINEMA_FORMATS` in `src/LorEvolve.Web/src/projects/sections.ts` gets five Comic rows (list renamed `PROJECT_FORMATS`), so the existing New project format select (`pages/ProjectPage.tsx`, `formatsFor(kind)`) shows them for Comic. Default for Comic is the first, Western Comic. API theory per format; E2E spec.
- [x] Selection persists after reload: stored column, returned in `ProjectDetail`. API create-then-get theory; E2E reload check.
- [x] Project listings display format: `ProjectsPage` row (`project-row-format`) and overview (`project-format`) already render any `project.format` through `formatLabel`; add the five labels. Overview already shows "Format not set" when `formatsFor(kind)` is non-empty, so legacy Comics read "Format not set" with no code change.
- [x] Existing Comics remain accessible: null stays null on read, update and backup. API test: Comic created with no format reads back null and is saved again as null.
- [x] Invalid formats rejected: existing `ProjectEndpoints.Validate` (`ProjectFormats.Allows(kind, format)`). Tests: unknown id, `tv-show` + Comic, `manga` + Film, `manga` + Series, each 400 with `format` error. Backup validation already refuses a mismatch (`BackupValidation.cs`); add one Comic mismatch case.
- [x] Changing format never silently discards content: see "Format change" below. #293 adds no content and touches none.
- [x] Project identity/ownership unchanged: test saves a Comic with a new format and asserts same id, universe and owner.

## Files to touch

- `src/LorEvolve.Api/Features/Projects/ProjectFormats.cs`: five entries, doc line.
- `src/LorEvolve.Api/Features/ProjectEntities/ProjectTemplates.cs` and `ProjectEntityTypeEndpoints.cs` (two `ProjectTemplates.For(project.Kind, project.Subtype)` calls, lines ~735 and ~777): see "Starter templates".
- `src/LorEvolve.Web/src/projects/sections.ts` (rows, `formatLabel` cases), `projects/types.ts` (comment), `i18n/en/projects.ts`, `i18n/pt-PT/projects.ts` (five `projects.format.*` keys).
- Tests: extend `tests/LorEvolve.Api.Tests/ProjectFormatTests.cs` (theory rows, wrong-kind rows, legacy null, ownership, backup round trip with a Comic format), a `ProjectTemplates` test for the pick, `tests/LorEvolve.E2E/specs/project-cinema-formats.spec.ts` (add Comic cases; written, not run). No new UI component. Follows `docs/design/ui-components.md`.
- MCP `list_projects` / `get_project`: already return `format`; no change. Add one assertion for a Comic if a project tool test exists.

## Starter templates

`ProjectTemplates.For(kind, subtype)` picks Manga (unit Chapter, extra "First appears in"), Webtoon (unit Episode) or plain Comic (unit Issue) from the free-text Subtype. Decision: a set Format drives the pick, falling back to Subtype when Format is null. Add an optional `format` parameter: `manga` -> Manga, `webcomic` -> Webtoon, `western-comic`, `graphic-novel`, `one-shot` -> plain Comic; null -> today's Subtype rule unchanged. Both endpoint call sites pass `project.Format`. Subtype is never read-modified or rewritten. Templates are offered and written only on request, so a format change never re-applies or alters types already created.

## Format change

Allowed within Comic via the existing whole-save PUT (same validation: a format can only sit on its own kind). It changes metadata only: no endpoint converts, moves or deletes pages, panels, entries, types or fields. There is no project edit form yet, so the UI cannot change a format (same limit as #288). Note for #294: structure validation must never delete existing nodes when the format changes. It should either refuse a format change that would orphan existing structure (e.g. Issues under a format that has no Issues) or keep showing and keeping that structure.

## Backup and restore

No format bump. The column and `BackupCreativeProject.Format` exist since v49 and only the allowed value set grows. Checked behaviour: `BackupValidation.cs` (~line 1157) refuses a format that `ProjectFormats.Allows` does not accept for the kind with `InvalidValue`, so a backup with a Comic format restored by a build that lacks these ids is refused whole, not silently stripped. Same-build and newer builds restore it. Accepted: older builds also refuse v49 backups for formats they do not know, the same as #288.

## Data model / migration

None. Pending-model-changes check still run.

## Verification (cheaper model can run)

- `dotnet build src/LorEvolve.Api -c Release`
- `dotnet test tests/LorEvolve.Api.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ProjectFormatTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProjectEndpointTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProjectTemplate|FullyQualifiedName~BackupValidationTests|FullyQualifiedName~BackupRoundTripTests|FullyQualifiedName~McpToolTests"`
- `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes --project src/LorEvolve.Api`
- From `src/LorEvolve.Web`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm test`, `npm run build`
- `cd tests/LorEvolve.E2E && npx playwright test --list`

## Results (personally executed)

- `dotnet build src/LorEvolve.Api -c Release`: 0 errors.
- `dotnet test` filtered to ProjectFormatTests, ProjectEndpointTests, ProjectComicTests, BackupValidationTests, McpToolTests: 64 passed, 0 failed. New: five Comic theory rows, wrong-kind rows (tv-show, manga on Film and Series), legacy null plus identity test, template pick test, backup refusal of a Comic carrying a Film format.
- `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes`: none.
- Web: typecheck, lint, format:check, build pass. `npm test` has one failure that is not from this PR: the stylesheet guard flags `.types__game` in `UniverseTypes.tsx` (from #280, already on `dev`; this PR touches neither file).
- `npx playwright test --list`: 671 tests load. The spec gained five Comic rows (written, not run).

## Deferred checks

Milestone checks, deferred to the tracker end: CI and local Playwright E2E.

Deferred owner checks (on DEV): create one Comic per format, reload, open an older Comic and confirm it reads "Format not set".

## Decisions taken

- Ids: `western-comic`, `manga`, `graphic-novel`, `one-shot`, `webcomic`; label for the last is "Webcomic / Webtoon".
- Legacy Comics keep null; nothing assigns a format. The New project form preselects Western Comic (the author sees and can change it).
- Format drives the starter template pick, Subtype fallback, Subtype untouched.
- No backup bump; unknown ids are refused on restore.
- Hierarchies are #294; they key off `Format`.

body:
## Description

This module's XAPI dependencies are bumped to the releases that no longer carry `AutoMapper`, removing it from this module entirely.

`Xapi.Core` carried `AutoMapper` as a transitive package dependency up to and including 3.1027.0; 3.1028.0 dropped it. AutoMapper also reached this module *indirectly*, through XAPI module packages that were themselves built against an older `Xapi.Core` — so bumping those upstreams is part of the fix, not housekeeping. They have just been re-released from the same effort:

- `VirtoCommerce.FileExperienceApi.Data` 3.1006.0 to 3.1009.0
- `VirtoCommerce.ProfileExperienceApiModule.Data` 3.1020.0 to 3.1025.0
- `VirtoCommerce.XCatalog.Core` 3.1023.0 to 3.1025.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Xapi.Core` 3.1026.0 to 3.1031.0

After this change `AutoMapper` is absent from the restore graph and from the published `deps.json`, verified against the package built by `vc-build Compress`.

`AutoMapper` 12.0.1 is covered by GHSA-6vhm-j9h7-f9gh and GHSA-gpwp-5797-mjff, both high severity, published 2026-11-13. With the solution-wide `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, NU1903 fails restore wherever it is still reachable. No release below 15.1.4 fixes the advisories and 15.x requires a paid commercial licence, so upgrading in place is not an option.

`Xapi.Core` 3.1031.0 floors `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Core` at 3.1097.0, and `vc-build`'s `MatchVersions` requires every `VirtoCommerce.Platform.*` package and the manifest `platformVersion` to agree, so they move together:

- `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Core` 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Data` 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Data.MySql` 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Data.PostgreSql` 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Platform.Data.SqlServer` 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0

Floors pulled in by the upstream packages above:

- `VirtoCommerce.CustomerModule.Core` 3.1028.0 to 3.1033.0
- `VirtoCommerce.StoreModule.Core` 3.1009.0 to 3.1013.0

`module.manifest` dependency versions are synced to the packages actually referenced, which `MatchVersions` also enforces:

- `VirtoCommerce.Customer` 3.1028.0 to 3.1033.0
- `VirtoCommerce.FileExperienceApi` 3.1006.0 to 3.1009.0
- `VirtoCommerce.ProfileExperienceApiModule` 3.1020.0 to 3.1025.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Store` 3.1009.0 to 3.1013.0
- `VirtoCommerce.XCatalog` 3.1023.0 to 3.1025.0
- `VirtoCommerce.Xapi` 3.1026.0 to 3.1031.0

The `AutoMapper.dll` and `AutoMapper.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection.dll` entries are removed from `module.ignore`: those assemblies are no longer produced, so the entries were dead.

No schema change, no migrations, no new settings, no new dependencies.

## New GraphQL queries and mutations

None — this PR adds no query or mutation.

## Changes to existing GraphQL queries and mutations

None — no schema type, field, argument or resolver signature is touched.

## New public services / interfaces / methods

None.

## New protected methods (extensibility)

None.

## Breaking changes

**Package upgrade** — the module's minimum platform version rises from 3.1091.0 to 3.1097.0. A solution on a platform below 3.1097.0 cannot take this module version. This floor is imposed by Xapi.Core 3.1031.0, not chosen here.

**Package upgrade** — the declared module dependencies rise as listed above, so the matching modules must be at those versions or later.

**Package upgrade** — consumers that were resolving `AutoMapper` transitively through this module's packages will no longer get it. Any downstream project still calling AutoMapper must reference it directly.

No compile-level or runtime behaviour break: no public or `virtual` member is removed, resignatured or changed in runtime type. No `[Obsolete]` was introduced — nothing on the published surface was removed.

## New dependencies

None — this PR removes one.

> **Note (why the cutoff is 3.1028.0, not 3.1026.0)** — the comment in `VirtoCommerce.Xapi.Web.csproj` states that modules built against Xapi.Core "3.1026.0 or earlier" carry AutoMapper. Checked against the published nuspecs on nuget.org, 3.1027.0 still lists both AutoMapper packages; 3.1028.0 is the first clean release. That comment is off by one and should be corrected when the compatibility shim is removed from x-api.

> **Note (verification)** — `vc-build Compress` was run locally on this branch and succeeded through Restore, Compile, Test, Publish and Compress. The resulting `VirtoCommerce.CustomerReviews_3.1011.0.zip` contains no `AutoMapper*` file and no AutoMapper entry in its `deps.json`.

body:
## Summary

The generated request resources give SSM's `parameter`, `document` and `association` types the `aws:ResourceTag/` key, and the first two `ssm:resourceTag/` too (`resourceTagKeys`, read from the Service Reference), which `IamConditionContextResolver` values from the namespace's `StoredResourceArns.storedTags` ([#8359](https://github.com/floci-io/floci/pull/8359)). `SsmService` answered no tags, so a policy condition on an SSM resource's tags saw none. Same change as [#8676](https://github.com/floci-io/floci/pull/8676) made for ECR.

- **The service only looks up.** `SsmService.storedTags` reads the parameter, document or association stored under the ARN in the account and Region it names, in place, matched on the whole ARN. A parameter ARN names `/<name>` before `<name>`, as the tagging operations read it, and must be the parameter's own stored ARN. SSM's other tagged types are ones Floci keeps no record of (maintenance windows, patch baselines, OpsItems and the like), or are EC2 and ECS ARNs, so they hold none here.
- **One whole tag map.** Adding and removing tags now put a new map in place of the held one, so the lookup always reads one whole map; a parameter's is filled one entry at a time, as the old one was, so ListTagsForResource lists tags in the same order. The parameter tag writes the CloudFormation provisioner calls directly were outside the service's lock and edited the map in place; they now take the lock the other SSM writers take. The tag fields are volatile.
- **Docs.** `docs/services/iam.md` names SSM among the services that answer it, and `StoredResourceArns` says what SSM answers.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [ ] Docs / chore

## AWS Compatibility

A policy condition such as `"StringEquals": {"ssm:resourceTag/team": "data"}` or `"aws:ResourceTag/team"` on an SSM action now reads the tags of the parameter, document or association the request names. AWS's Service Authorization Reference gives `aws:ResourceTag/${TagKey}` on all three, and `ssm:resourceTag/${TagKey}` ("Filters access by a tag key-value pair assigned to the Systems Manager resource") on parameters and documents. Before, the condition saw no tags, so such an Allow never applied and such a Deny never matched.

## Checklist

- [ ] `./mvnw test` passes locally (ran the SSM service, tagging and CloudFormation SSM test classes and the request resource enforcement test class, not the whole suite)
- [x] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [ ] I have no more than 2 open, non-draft pull requests and no more than 4 open pull requests in total (drafts included) in this repository (maintainers and dependency bots are exempt).
