author: jairik
body:
The Pi currently builds all eight images on every deploy. That normally takes 3–4 minutes, and it took 30 minutes on Nov 16 when the Go build ran from a cold cache (`go build` alone took 1,700 s). Two deploys hit the 30-minute timeout while they were still in the Dashboard's `pnpm build`. This PR moves the builds to GitHub Actions, and the Pi pulls the result.

## What changes

- **New `Pi images` workflow** (`.github/workflows/images.yml`)
  - Runs on pushes to `main` and by hand only. It does not run on pull requests, so this PR doesn't trigger it.
  - A plan job computes a content key per service and skips any key already published to `ghcr.io/jairik/clanka-bot/<service>:key-<key>`.
  - The remaining services build in parallel on native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners, each with its own GitHub Actions layer cache.
  - A manual run with **rebuild** checked forces every image to rebuild, which picks up base image updates.
- **`scripts/image-keys.py`** builds the key from:
  - the committed files in the service's build context (the git tree id);
  - its Dockerfile;
  - its resolved Compose build args;
  - the platform.

  CI and the Pi both run this script, so they always agree on which image a commit needs.
- **`deploy.sh`**
  - Pulls each active service by key, tags it `clanka/<service>:<sha>`, and starts the stack with `up --no-build`.
  - If a service has no published image, it builds just that service locally and logs a warning.
  - Setting `DEPLOY_REGISTRY=` (empty) restores the old behaviour of building everything on the Pi.
  - Rollback and pruning are unchanged.
- **Fewer rebuilds**
  - A commit that only changes docs builds nothing.
  - A Go-only commit builds only `assistant`. `dashboard-web` is keyed on `assistant/web` alone.
  - Its `X-Dashboard-UI-Version` now comes from the runtime environment, set to `GIT_SHA`, instead of being baked into the image. That keeps the image's key stable across commits.
  - The Go stage cross-compiles on the build machine (`--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM`) and uses cache mounts, so a fallback build on the Pi doesn't recompile every package.
- **`deploy/pi-images.env`** holds the Pi's build args (for example `TTS_LANGUAGE=english_18m_2026-10`). CI builds with these values.

## Before or after merge
- [ ] After the first run on `main`, make the 8 `clanka-bot/<service>` packages public, or `docker login ghcr.io` on the Pi with a `read:packages` token. Until then the Pi still deploys, but it builds locally.
- [ ] Whenever a build arg changes in the Pi's `.env`, change `deploy/pi-images.env` in the same PR.

## Testing
- `deploy_test.sh`: 124 passed. New cases cover pulling a published image, building an unpublished one locally, running without a registry, and key stability.
- `deploy_watch_test.sh`: 110 passed. `check_compose_test.sh`: 75 passed. `check-compose.sh`: OK. `check_dockerignore_test.sh`: 48 passed.
- Built the assistant and dashboard-web images locally (amd64). The web image serves `X-Dashboard-UI-Version` from its runtime environment.
- For the Pi's current commit, the keys from the Pi's own `.env` match the keys from `deploy/pi-images.env` on all 8 services.
- I couldn't run the workflow itself before merge, because it only runs on `main`.

author: nielsfranke
body:
## What

- **GUQ1 qualification (G21), measurement:** Rawtonic's Guided Upright was compared with Camera Raw 18.7, using the same guide lines drawn in Camera Raw, on 24 CC0 photos (58 guides). It is **at or above Camera Raw**, so the guided correction itself needed no change.
  - Guide residual: 0.00° median for Rawtonic vs 0.02° for Camera Raw (max 0.01° vs 0.19°).
  - Other straight lines, crop-independent: 0.49° vs 0.54° median; equal on 21 of 24 photos, better on 2, worse on 1.
  - Failures: 0 vs 0.
  - Frame kept: 0.92 vs 0.90 median (more on 15 of 24).
  - Evidence: notes `benchmark-results/guq1-2026-11-17/REPORT.md`.
- **New: Lightroom catalog import keeps Guided Upright.** Before, `library_import` ignored `crs:PerspectiveUpright` and the guides, so such photos arrived uncorrected. `rawtonic_engine::lightroom_upright` now reads `UprightFourSegments_N` (Camera Raw's keys, found by drawing guides in a scratch session).
  - Each guide end is mapped from the sensor image into the developed frame (`frame_and_sensor`, as Lightroom's crop).
  - Where Lightroom's lens profile was on, the end then goes through the photo's own lens correction (`WarpPoints::to_output`). Measured: Camera Raw stores guides before the profile, up to 9 % of the radius off the drawn position.
  - The ends are turned with the photo's EXIF orientation (review round 1).
  - Sony ARWs set to another aspect ratio in the camera are left out, because Lightroom's frame for them is not settled (B488).
  - The import sets `guidedPerspective {enabled, lines, upright: "guided"}`.
  - Checked against the measured lines: 22 of 24 photos within 2.3 px at 1600 px and 0.19°. Ignoring the lens profile would leave up to 1.6° on the guides.

## Decisions (pro view)

- **Constrain crop when the photo has no Lightroom crop.** Constrain crop (`autoCrop`) is on, so no blank corners appear.
- **Lightroom's own crop is kept when it comes along.** When Lightroom's crop is imported, it is kept and Constrain crop is off, so the photographer's framing is not lost. Not verified: whether Lightroom's crop numbers after Upright frame exactly the same content in Rawtonic's warp.

## Open (recorded in G21)

- Sony aspect-ratio ARWs (B488): neither the 16:9 frame nor the 3:2 sensor fits both guides, so these files are not imported. Lightroom crop imports of those files likely have the same question.
- Lightroom Classic catalog form is assumed to be the flat Lua keys (covered by the `to_xmp` test, not read from a real catalog).
- Capture One's keystone guides were not measured.

## Checks

- `scripts/check.sh --brief` passes.
- New tests: `lightroom_upright::tests` (parsing, other modes, malformed guide, aspect-crop frame mapping, EXIF 6/8, lens round trip) and `library_import::tests::lightroom_catalog_guided_upright_keeps_its_guides`.
- Rendering code is untouched (import only), so no version key and saved edits are unaffected.

## Second-model review

Verdict on 473cc5936d65f927cb9b685a26001b1d8e44cd22 by codex (author: claude): **approve**. No blocking findings. The orientation defect is fixed; Sony aspect-ratio imports are safely skipped and documented, while their coordinate mapping remains unresolved. Review was read-only; tests were not run.
- [should_fix] `crates/engine/src/lightroom_upright.rs:182` The new Sony exclusion has no regression coverage. Existing tests exercise parsing and guide mapping but never this metadata-dependent guard. Add coverage showing that an aspect-ratio ARW is skipped while a full-sensor ARW still imports its guides.

author: bryce496913
body:
## Classification

**READY PENDING XCODE VALIDATION.** No native SwiftUI/SwiftData compilation, migration, XCTest, simulator, device/offline-relaunch or performance success is claimed. Begin with isolated/copied data on Apple platforms. No merge, TestFlight upload or next development pass.

## Confirmed source defects and repairs

- **Nested commit/rollback composition:** a public committing writer invoked from `writeTransaction` could save the outer operation's pending changes before a subsequent outer failure. Current reviewed production callers use staging helpers rather than intentionally nesting commits, but the API lacked protection against this composition. Added main-actor ownership checks at all three commit entry points (`writeTransaction`, Library mutation, Library removal). Reentry throws before inner mutation/save; the outer boundary owns rollback and the guard is released on all exits. No second ModelContext or persistence layer.
- **Collection-only offline lookup:** `offlineMedia(for:)` checked Library/reviews/diary/seasons but omitted collection memberships. A removed/restored title with only a membership could return nil from the shared route, notably losing the offline snapshot path for unknown/legacy namespaces. Existing indexed membership identity now returns a placeholder, without fetching metadata or recreating a removed Library row.
- **Ambiguous removal scope:** the existing main removal dialog omitted collections. It now explicitly states that memberships remain, and that unavailable metadata can display by ID, alongside the existing explicit rating/status/favorite removal warning.

## Library / collection decision

Memberships are independent scalar references to exact typed/provider MediaID, not foreign keys to a Library row. Retaining them is deliberate and supports statusless titles, separate list ownership and non-destructive personal-only restore. No cascade or automatic row recreation is introduced.

Main **Remove from Library** continues to remove the confirmed row/rating/status/favorite, preserve separate reviews/diary/progress, and archive legacy text. Collection A/B memberships and manual order survive as valid identity references. Remove from one collection affects that collection only; Delete Collection removes only its memberships. The clarified dialog makes this scope explicit instead of silently implying lists disappeared. Offline navigation now recognizes the retained identity consistently.

## Areas reviewed and retained

- Collection membership/reorder use one LibraryStore transaction, stable IDs, dense positions and original-order validation. `ensureLibraryEntry` stages without committing; pending identity reuse is tested.
- Pre-save integrity audit, explicit save/publication and failed-write rollback remain authoritative. Existing collection/reorder/restore failure coverage is retained.
- V3 and all historical entity declarations, additive migration chain, current store location and Xcode project/settings are unchanged. Existing reconstructed historical/V2→V3/corrupt/unknown-store fixtures remain; no new historical shape is implied by these non-schema fixes. Real historical-store migration coverage remains unverified.
- Portable backup v2/v1 and internal recovery 2/1 remain unchanged: membership UUID/order, reviews/diary/flags and intentional absence of a removed Library row survive personal-only restore. Existing populated merge/name/UUID/relationship/version conflicts, cancellation, rollback and repeat-import tests remain.
- Continue Watching exact-next eligibility, independent series/status/ratings/reviews, specials/future/unknown coverage, duplicate Home actions and offline/save-failure behavior retain existing selectors/writers/tests.
- Discovery Watchlist/collection pools, full MediaID dedup, OR genres, year/runtime/unknown/expiry rules, bounded eligible random sampling, cancellation and no writes retain existing code/tests.
- Artwork remains bounded/coalesced memory-only with cancellation/clear/credential generation checks. Persistent caching stays BLOCKED; the 150-day metadata lease and personal preservation are unchanged.
- Existing benchmarks remain intact. No complex concurrency change or fabricated timing/speedup.

## Focused tests

Four new unit methods in existing files:

1. Disk nested-writer regression covering transaction/mutation/removal/restore variants: no inner save flushes an outer pending insert, prior values remain, retry succeeds, disk reopens correctly.
2. Repeated staging helper calls reuse the same pending identity in one transaction.
3. Full shared A/B movie flow: statusless membership, rating/status/favorite edits, main removal, collection route identity, export/fresh disk restore/repeat import, deletion isolation and another reopen; no silent row recreation.
4. Failed main removal retains rating/legacy text/memberships; retry imports text exactly once and repeated removal is idempotent.

Strengthened the existing collection-only removal test to require the actual shared offline result, load its detail model with no provider and verify no personal row is recreated. Existing rollback, migration, backup, Home, discovery and artwork suites are reused.

All new/existing XCTest methods are **UNRUN**. Source inventory: **392 unit/benchmark + 80 UI = 472 methods**, not executed pass counts.

## Actual checks on Linux

| Command/check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node /workspace/scratch/ios-foundation/validate.cjs` | PASS: OpenStep project, references, all three target memberships, grammar parse of 148 Swift files, asset JSON; **not compilation/type checking** |
| `python3 scripts/validate-design-tokens.py` | PASS: 44 intended adaptive text pairs ≥4.5:1 |
| Frozen/current schema/entity/migration/project comparison with main | PASS: unchanged |
| Changed relative documentation links | PASS |
| `git diff --check` / staged equivalent | PASS |
| `scripts/validate-v06.sh simulator-unavailable` | Expected prerequisite rejection, exit 69; no native test ran |
| Xcode/native tests/migrations/simulator/device/benchmarks | **UNRUN** |

No Swift compiler, Xcode, Apple SDK or simulator is available. No GitHub Xcode CI, app identity/signing change or screenshot claim.

## Documentation and remaining requirements

Added `docs/PRE_DEVICE_HARDENING.md`; updated only affected Library/collection removal, backup coverage, known issues and README guidance.

Run `scripts/validate-v06.sh <installed-test-simulator-UUID>` on macOS. Prioritize DataIntegrityTests, CollectionTests, LibraryStoreTests, DataMigrationTests, CollectionBackupTests, BackupRestoreTests, TVProgressTests, WatchDiscoveryTests and OfflineArtworkTests, then the existing UI suites. Complete the V0.6 matrix for compact/larger iPhones, VoiceOver/large text, removal confirmations, keyboard/safe areas and actual termination/relaunch offline.

Outstanding integrity risks are native evidence gaps: SwiftData pending-fetch visibility, rollback/index publication, real historical-store adoption and disk/document-picker durability have not executed. No confirmed source defect from this pass remains unaddressed, but source inspection cannot prove an absence of runtime defects. Preserve source databases/journals and safety archives; do not reset/reinstall to bypass failures. Validate disposable/copied stores before valuable personal data. Persistent artwork and live provider authorization remain gated.

author: hbhflw2000
body:
## Summary

Add MiniCPM-o 4.5 Thinker Megatron training for AVQA image/audio understanding. Reuse the existing processor, dataset, choice reward, rollout adapter and shared Megatron YAML. A model-scoped BSHD forward preserves sample media, positions, label shifting and gradients; a narrow adapter hook binds per-run processor metadata without model-specific branches in the engine.

Scope: dense TP, PP=CP=1, frozen perception towers/projectors, full language-decoder training. Speech generation, packed sequences, SP, MTP, quantization and Megatron LoRA are excluded.

## Dependency blocker

**Keep draft until the verl builder prerequisite lands.** [Megatron-Bridge#6630](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6630) is merged, but the current verl pin still constructs through the provider-only API. MiniCPM-o requires builder-based construction and preservation of its pre-wrap hooks. This PR does not vendor verl or change public pins/CI.

The experiment used development overrides: verl `fefb0802` plus the builder prerequisite, Bridge `e7a6dbfe` with its paired Core `e0a4bfed`, vLLM 0.30.0, vLLM-Omni `12e92800`, Transformers 5.14.1. The 100-step result does not qualify the rebased head or today's public pins. Exact revisions, source hashes and diagnostic limits are in [the evidence](https://github.com/hbhflw2000/verl-omni/blob/c6e75b1804c5d076d64c70d67d662b6329c7f649/docs/evidence/minicpmo-megatron-100step-20261116/README.md).

## Validation

Eight H200 GPUs; 100 optimizer updates; 4,435 training questions; 1,911 fixed validation questions at steps 0, 10, ..., 100. All 21,021 validation and 800 training outputs passed independent choice-reward regrading with zero mismatches.

| Step | Correct / 1911 | Val-core |

author: ecto
body:
Follow-up to #1220. That PR made the kernel record a wrong-geometry event when a Difference provably missed its cut, and `vcad_eval` exposes it as `EvaluatedScene::warnings`. But vcad-render builds its own per-part log and report, so `vcad eval-json`, `vcad-render --eval-json` and `render_view` still reported such a part as clean.

**What changed**
- `PartReport.warnings` (left out of the JSON when empty) and `EvalReport.parts_warned`. `ok` stays true because the part has geometry to draw, but the warning is visible next to the wrong `volume`/`bbox`.
  - Roots take the warning from `scene.warnings`.
  - Instances take it from the part definition's provenance, falling back to `scene.warnings` for that definition.
- stderr summary ("N part(s) built with geometry known to be WRONG …") from both CLIs' eval-json and from every render path (it hooks into `warn_dropped`).
- **Two cache holes closed.** Both stored the wrong mesh, so the next warm run served it with no construction history and no warning.
  - `vcad_eval`'s part-definition store never got the gate #1220 added to the root store. It now skips storing and pushes a `partDef[..]` warning.
  - `place_parts_cached` (vcad-render's placed-instance store) also skips known-wrong solids. A missed-cut solid is still `Analytic`, so the existing `as_brep()` filter didn't catch it.

**Test:** `crates/vcad-render/tests/eval_report_wrong_geometry.rs` runs the counterbored-block repro from #1220 under `VCAD_NO_MISSED_CUT_SWAP=1`:
- As a root: cold run, then warm run on a shared `MemoryMeshCache`. Both must report a "cut was missed" warning with `ok: true`, and nothing may be stored.
- As an assembly instance: the same, plus an SVG render. Nothing may be stored.
- Control with the swap on: reported clean, and the cache does store, so the zeros above come from the gate.

**Checks (on mew):**
- fmt clean.
- clippy `--lib --bins -D warnings` clean on vcad-render/vcad-eval/vcad.
- vcad-render `--tests` clippy clean.
- nextest for vcad-render + vcad-eval + vcad: 515/518 passed, including the new test (in its earlier, larger form). The 3 failures were GPU photoreal tests killed by mew's OOM killer at load ~700, not by this change.
- Unrelated: clippy 1.98 `--all-targets` flags two existing `chunks_exact` lints in vcad-eval test code (`evaluate.rs` test module, `tests/sequential_cutouts.rs`). Not touched here.

**Not done:** vcad-render's partDef failure lookup formats the scope as `partDef[id]`, but vcad_eval writes `partDef["id"]` (Debug), so that existing lookup never matches. The new warning lookup matches by node id instead.

author: imozart
body:
## O que muda

Corrige a atualização do ZIP portátil do Windows, que parava na extração com `EBUSY ... rmdir '.gnupdate-stage\resources\app.asar'`.

- `installer.ts`: novo `removeTree()`, que apaga com `process.noAsar = true` (síncrono, restaurando o valor depois). É usado em `extractZip`, `prepareStage` e `cleanupUpdateFiles`.
- `installer.ts`: `cleanupUpdateFiles` agora registra no log o que não conseguiu apagar, em vez de engolir o erro.
- `installer.ts`: o script de troca (`SWAP_SCRIPT`) liga `process.noAsar` no início, para conseguir apagar o `.gnupdate-old` (que também traz um `app.asar`).
- `main.ts`: a limpeza ao abrir o app passa o log da atualização.

## Por quê

No processo principal do Electron o `fs` trata todo `.asar` como pasta virtual. O `rm` recursivo sobre o `app.asar` real da pasta de preparo chamava `rmdir` num arquivo e dava `EBUSY`; como a limpeza engolia o erro, a pasta antiga ficava e toda nova tentativa falhava igual. Sem isso, o `.gnupdate-old` também nunca seria apagado depois de uma troca.

Closes #134

## Como testar

- `pnpm test` (`apps/studio/test/installer.test.ts` e `portable-update.test.ts`): o novo teste cobre uma pasta de preparo com `resources/app.asar` e confere que `process.noAsar` volta ao valor anterior. No Node puro ele não reproduz o `EBUSY`, que só existe dentro do Electron.
- Manual: com um ZIP portátil de versão anterior e uma `.gnupdate-stage` deixada por tentativa anterior, baixar a atualização; a extração deve seguir e a troca concluir. Quem está na 1.12.0 precisa apagar a `.gnupdate-stage` e o `gnupdate-*.zip` à mão e instalar esta versão manualmente uma vez.

## Checklist

- [x] O **título** segue o Conventional Commits (`tipo(escopo): descrição`) e tem **no máximo 100 caracteres**, e a **branch** é `tipo/descricao` com o mesmo tipo
- [x] As **mensagens dos commits** também seguem o padrão (delas saem a versão e o `CHANGELOG.md`)
- [x] Testes escritos ou ajustados (`pnpm typecheck` e `pnpm test` passam)
- [x] Textos novos da interface estão em `pt-BR.ts` **e** `en.ts`
- [x] Documentação atualizada, se a mudança afeta o uso ou a infraestrutura
- [x] Sem segredos, tokens, caminhos pessoais ou dados de clientes (código, testes, imagens, GIFs)

author: potoior
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #50892.

On a hybrid-SWA (joint-window) model with HiCache, a host hit can include FULL rows that are **still device-resident**, blocked only by a host-only window/state entry. Those rows need no H2D: `build_hicache_transfers` asks to copy only the missing ones, the load-back budget is reserved for that smaller amount, and `init_load_back` (via `collect_full_device_indices`) reports only the newly landed rows. The integrity check in `PrefillAdder.add_one_req` nevertheless compared `host_loaded_length` against **`req.host_hit_length`**, so a legitimate partial load-back aborted the whole scheduler and dropped every in-flight request on every TP rank:

```
RuntimeError: HiCache load-back must commit all promised FULL tokens or none:
  req=... promised=136192 loaded=41728
```

The reporter's 94464-row difference is exactly the already-resident portion of the hit — no data was actually missing.

## Modifications

`schedule_policy.py`, one variable: the check (and the zero-landing recompute `elif` next to it) now compares against **what the load actually promised to copy** — `full_load_tokens`, which is `req.host_hit_length` everywhere except the joint-window branch, where it counts only the rows the FULL transfer spec asked to copy (the same value the budget was reserved with, computed a few lines above). The check keeps its strength:

- landing **fewer rows than the transfer spec promised** still aborts (genuine partial commit);
- non-hybrid load-backs are unchanged (the promise stays the whole host hit);
- a fully device-resident hit (empty transfer spec, `loaded == 0`) now keeps its host hit instead of being recomputed from scratch — the old `elif` misfired on that case too.

## Regression Tests

New `TestHiCacheLoadBackPromise` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_policy.py` (CPU suite) drives `add_one_req` through the load-back path with a stubbed cache/budget and pins all four edges:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| joint window, half the hit already resident, load lands exactly the promised rows | `CONTINUE` — **aborts on the pre-fix code** |
| joint window, load lands fewer rows than the transfer spec promised | still `RuntimeError` with `promised=<transfer rows>` |
| non-hybrid, load lands half the host hit | still `RuntimeError` with `promised=<host hit>` (original protection) |
| fully resident hit, nothing to copy | `CONTINUE` with the host hit kept and no admission recompute — **recomputes on the pre-fix code** |

Verified the suite bites: with the fix stashed, the first and last cases fail; with the fix, 15/15 pass. Full `test_schedule_policy.py` + `test_prefill_memory_budget.py` + `test_fcfs_waiting_prefix_refresh.py`: 37 passed, no regressions.

Note: the GPU-tier `test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py` fixture does not run in this offline environment (torch stream stand-in incompatibility), so the e2e-shaped coverage of this path is the mock-level suite above plus the reporter's 2×L20 reproduction.

## Checklist

- [x] I have referenced the issue fixed (#50892).
- [x] I have created at least one test case for the fix.

author: nledford
body:
Closes #903

## What changed and why

Escape on "Sign in again" ended the requests that waited, but nothing remembered the closing. Any refusal that came back after it opened the dialog again under the reader, and focus moved back into a dialog they had just dismissed (A1). Two sources did it:

- the start page sends its plans read and its Full Disk Access read at once. When the second refusal landed after Escape, the dialog opened again. That is the CI failure of `sign_in.feature:430` ("A page whose reading waited for a sign-in that never came…"), reproduced on main by holding the plans read until after Escape: `24 × locator resolved to visible <dialog open="" aria-labelledby="session-ended-title" …>`, CI's exact text;
- the Operations page's own retry of its history read, 1 s after Escape, opened it again every time.

The fix:

- `session::Dismissals` (host-tested) counts the closings and keeps whether one happened since the last sign-in. A refused request waits in the dialog when it is open. Otherwise it opens the dialog only if it was sent after the last closing, and after a closing only for a request the person made (a link, a button), never for a page's own read.
- The Operations page told any answer but the history apart from nothing: after Escape its refused read showed "Cannot reach Ladderback" for good. `ws::watch` now tells a refusal from no answer (`got_as`, which `get` and `read_as` share). The page says the refusal where its table goes, through the catalog and `sentence_view`, until a read gets the history again. A host test covers the new `Shown::Refused`.
- components.md §4.5 says what Escape does now, including a request refused after the dialog has opened again, which waits in it.

## Evidence

Reds at the `test:` commit:

- unit, `cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'test(/session::tests::/)'`: `4 tests run: 0 passed, 4 failed` (`todo!()` stubs).
- UI, Chromium, the two new scenarios: `2 scenarios (2 failed)`:
  - "A page's own reading after the dialog was closed…": `Then the dialog "Sign in again" stays closed`, `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: the dialog "Sign in again" opened again`;
  - "A reading refused after the dialog was closed…": timed out at `Then the page shows a message containing "Sign in to Ladderback with the admin password to go on."`.
- The Operations heading step, proven by hand with the dialog fix in and the Operations fix taken out (`ws.rs` and `routes.rs` at the commit before it): `And the main heading reads "Operations"`, `Error: function timed out, ensure the promise resolves within 30000 milliseconds`; `1 scenario (1 failed)`, `23 steps (18 passed, 4 skipped, 1 failed)`.

Narrow checks at the head:

- `cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'test(/session::tests::|routes::tests::/)'`: `87 tests run: 87 passed`.
- `cargo clippy -p web --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the same with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: clean.
- `just test-ui chromium --name '[Ss]ign in again|[Ss]ign(s|ed)? out|waited for a sign-in that never came|after the dialog was closed'`: `11 scenarios (11 passed)`, `218 steps (218 passed)`.
- `node scripts/check-paragraph-length.ts`: ok.

Final checks at head `de559c291` on origin/main `c4145ae26` (the `@ui` runs cover every sign-in, sign-out and Operations page scenario):

- merge-tree with origin/main: clean
- quick-ci: exit 0; Summary [  87.575s] 4502 tests run: 4502 passed, 0 skipped; 872 scenarios (872 passed)
- test-wasm: exit 0; test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 filtered out test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 filtered out test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 filtered out 
- test-ui chromium: exit 0; 31 scenarios (31 passed)
- test-ui firefox: exit 0; 31 scenarios (31 passed)
- test-ui webkit: exit 0; 31 scenarios (31 passed)
- red-first: exit 0; 8 red, 0 GREEN
- mutants (CARGO_TARGET_DIR unset, full scope): exit 0; 14 mutants tested in 3m: 13 caught, 1 unviable

## Review

One independent review: no P1.

- P2: both new scenarios now skip to the content first, as the keyboard walks since #909 do. Fixed in the `test:` commit.
- P2: after Escape the Operations page said "Cannot reach Ladderback" for good. Fixed (above), with a heading step that fails without it.
- P3: §4.5 didn't say what happens to a request refused after the dialog has opened again. Added: it waits in the dialog.
- P3: `session_ended` clears the lease before it decides. Kept: it matters only for a request sent before a sign-in and refused after it (below), and there main is worse, as it opens the dialog again.
- P3: the held-read step raced the page's patience. Fixed in the `test:` commit.

## Left alone, for the maintainer

- A request sent with the old session and refused after the reader signs in again in the dialog clears the new lease, and on main opens the dialog again. Not reproduced; filed as #911. A fix would count sign-ins in `Dismissals` and send such a request again.
- On the Operations page after Escape, the plans read's refusal and the history read's refusal both say "Sign in to Ladderback…", one where the plans' buttons go and one where the table goes. Each is about its own read, so both stay.

author: jayostis
body:
Closes #827
Part of jayostis/cascade-vocabulary#415

## What changes
`pod.import` takes two new options, `timeBudgetSeconds` and `memoryBudgetMiB`. Each is passed to every document's convert call in the Bridge, which already reads both (cascade-bridge-rs `crates/bridge-wasm/src/lib.rs`; defaults 120 s and 1024 MiB). Left out, nothing is sent and the defaults stand. A conversion that passes either budget rejects the import with a `BridgeError` of kind `bridge` and files nothing; the next import on the same pod converts again. `pod.import` itself refuses, with a `TypeError` naming the option and before any engine loads (the Node and the browser pod alike), a `timeBudgetSeconds` that is not a finite number above zero and a `memoryBudgetMiB` that is not a positive whole number; `null`, strings, `NaN` and `Infinity` are refused too. The upper memory cap is the Bridge's own to refuse and is not restated here. A trip of a caller's budget behaves exactly as a trip of the Bridge's default budget does today (a thrown `BridgeError`, nothing written, the pod usable): this PR adds a knob, not a new failure kind. The `ImportOptions` TSDoc is the only place import options are documented (no guide or README lists them). The CLI takes no budget; out of scope, the issue names an import option.

Path: `ImportOptions` (cascade-runtime `pod.ts`) -> `CorePod.import` -> `fileExport` -> `adapter.convert(document, budget)`; `ConvertOptions` in runtime `bridge.ts` gains the two fields.

## Tests
Red commit 65839c1f (log `C:/Users/Jay/AppData/Local/Temp/g4red.log`): the option was refused as unknown. Green: in `packages/cascade-runtime/test/options.test.ts`, one fast case (no engine) refuses twelve invalid values naming the option; in `pod.test.ts`, one case on one pod: a tiny time budget and a 1 MiB memory budget each reject with the Bridge's budget error and write nothing, then both defaults given explicitly convert the kit export. The validation fix followed review and its unit case was written with it, not red first. `options.test.ts` expectations updated for the longer accepted-key list. Local runs through heavy.sh: tsc -b, prettier, eslint, pod.test.js, options.test.js, stems.test.js. One local failure, `replayKit ... opens without matching it again` (`replayed.opened` was not undefined), is in code this change does not touch; CI decides.

## Breaking
None

## Notes
The Bridge is unchanged and already ships both options, so this PR has no partner.

author: brianacrm
body:
## What was wrong

`_amazon_item_price` returned the first OffersV2 listing that had an amount. OffersV2 can return several listings per item, and only the one flagged `isBuyBoxWinner` is the price on the product page.

Checked against the live Amazon pages on 2026-11-16, after the owner reported the first three prices on the board were wrong:

| Product | Feed | Amazon page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Simazine 4L `B0GJ6SLY12` | $69.99 | $89.19 |
| Talstar XTRA `B084HJW4YL` | $72.41 | no featured offer ("See All Buying Options") |
| Nixlo IGR `B0CKG7ZPN2` | $42.99 | $42.99 |

For Simazine, a sweep and a fast-lane run minutes apart read 89.19 and 69.99, which raised a 22% price-drop alert for a drop that never happened. Its daily record flips between the two values eleven times since Oct 16.

## Fix

- Request `offersV2.listings.isBuyBoxWinner`, `.condition`, `.type`.
- Price and availability come only from the featured, new-condition, one-time listing. Subscribe & Save, used, and MAP-hidden prices are never the price.
- No featured offer: no price (the link stays, unpriced), matching what the page shows.
- If the flag is missing from every listing, fall back to the first new one-time listing so a missing field cannot blank every Amazon price.

Source for the field meanings: Amazon Creators API reference, OffersV2 resources ("IsBuyBoxWinner ... This featured offer is seen on Detail Page"; Type: LIGHTNING_DEAL, SUBSCRIBE_AND_SAVE).

## Tests

`scraper/test_amazon_featured_offer.py` (9, all fail on the old code). Also exercised against the SDK's real `OfferListingV2` model. Full suite: 217 pass.

## Not fixed here

Points already in `price-history.json` that came from a non-featured listing stay in the record; there is no way to tell them apart after the fact.

author: pavithira-r
body:
### Summary of Changes
Comprehensive security audit and defense-in-depth remediation across the entire ReViveX application:

1. **Cloud Firestore Rules (`firestore.rules`):**
   - Disallow `ADMIN` self-assignment on public registration.
   - Enforce account field immutability (`role`, `isActive`, `email`).
   - Restrict updates to non-sensitive profile fields (`name`, `phone`, `profileImage`, `latitude`, `longitude`).
   - Enforce participant-only chat conversations and message length boundaries (≤ 1,000 characters).
   - Prevent self-reviews, validate rating bounds (1–5), and enforce deterministic review IDs.
   - Restrict eco action creation to the exact point formula (`DONATE: 25`, `REPAIR: 20`, `REUSE/RECYCLE: 15`, `SELL: 10`) with immutable audit logs.
   - Restrict notifications to recipient-only read access and `isRead` modification.

2. **Authentication & User Privacy:**
   - Introduced `PublicUser` interface and `authService.getPublicProfile()` to prevent exposing sensitive user information (email, phone, coordinates).
   - Added client-level `requireAdmin()` check before executing administrative operations.

3. **Repair Module Security:**
   - Removed provider self-verification in `saveMyProviderProfile` and prevented rating inflation.
   - Persisted repair bookings to the Cloud Firestore `bookings` collection and connected `bookingService.getBookingById`.
   - Added caller UID authorization checks on quotations, acceptances, rejections, and status progression.

4. **Marketplace & Recycling Security:**
   - Prohibited self-dealing in offers (`listing.owner.id !== user.id` and `offer.buyerId !== ownerId`).
   - Enforced valid state transitions in recycling requests within atomic transactions.

5. **Discovery & Verification Normalization:**
   - Fixed `pureSearchAndDiscovery.ts`: unverified providers strictly default to `isVerified: false`.
   - Defaulted unrated providers to 0 stars and 0 reviews.

### Verification
- **TypeScript:** `npx tsc --noEmit` passed with 0 errors.
- **Jest Test Suite:** 16/16 test suites passed (83/83 tests, 100% pass rate).
- **Documentation:** Full audit report documented in `docs/SECURITY_FIX_REPORT.md`.

author: nicibarrap
body:
## Resumen

Quinta vuelta sobre el mismo bug reportado: otorgarle un módulo a un empleado ya conectado seguía mostrando "no tienes acceso" **incluso con la navegación dura** del PR #174. Esta vez la causa no estaba en el código del cliente — estaba en la configuración de la plataforma de Vercel.

**Evidencia encontrada en los logs de error de Vercel (`get_runtime_errors`):**
```
[middleware] fetch a /api/check-session falló
count=91 users=6 routes=/middleware
SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON
```
91 ocurrencias en 24 horas, contra 6 usuarios distintos — no una rareza, un patrón consistente.

**Causa raíz:** el proyecto tiene "Vercel Authentication" (SSO Protection) activada, con `deploymentType: "all_except_custom_domains"` (confirmado con `get_project`). El fetch interno del middleware armaba su URL con `VERCEL_URL`, que apunta justo a una de las URLs *protegidas* del despliegue (`nelyx-xxxxx-....vercel.app`). Ese fetch, sin ningún token de bypass de Vercel, chocaba con el challenge de autenticación de Vercel y recibía HTML en vez de JSON — reventando en `res.json()` y cayendo al respaldo que usa `session.user.modulosPermitidos` del JWT (congelado desde el login). Eso reproduce exactamente el síntoma reportado.

**Fix:** usar `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (el dominio propio, `app.nelyx.cl`, ya usado en el resto de la plataforma para links de correo — ver `lib/email.ts`) en vez de `VERCEL_URL`. Ese dominio queda afuera de la protección SSO por diseño, y al ser siempre el dominio final (no uno con un redirect por delante) no reaparece el problema original que hizo descartar `req.url` en el diseño anterior.

## Por qué esto no se detectó en las 4 rondas anteriores

La protección SSO es una regla de la plataforma de Vercel, inexistente en `localhost` — ninguna prueba local (Playwright incluido) podía reproducirla. Las cuatro rondas previas (caché de `fetch()`, Router Cache del cliente, prefetch obsoleto, navegación dura) corrigieron problemas reales y necesarios, pero ninguna tocaba este fetch específico porque el problema vivía en la infraestructura, no en el código de React/Next.

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` limpio.
- Suite completa: 357/357 tests pasan.
- Esta causa específica **no se puede reproducir localmente** (depende de una configuración de Vercel). La verificación real es post-deploy: revisar `get_runtime_errors` y confirmar que el error `[middleware] fetch a /api/check-session falló` deja de aparecer.

## Test plan

- [ ] Desplegar y, tras unos minutos de tráfico real, revisar `get_runtime_errors` — el error debería desaparecer o caer a cero.
- [ ] Repetir el escenario reportado: dueño otorga un módulo nuevo a un empleado ya conectado en otra pantalla, sin sacarle nada; el empleado hace click en el módulo recién aparecido y entra sin "no tienes acceso".

author: sgryjp
body:
AI-assisted draft - human review required.

## Summary

```text
configuration + shared Rule metadata
  ├─ CLI / Web: default JSONC with $schema
  └─ CLI: --print-config-schema
       └─ site/commit-msg-lint.schema.json → GitHub Pages
            └─ pre-commit: regenerate and fail on changes
```

The published URL tracks `main`; before 1.0.0 it may differ from an installed CLI. The CLI
can generate its own matching schema. Runtime parsing remains authoritative for JSONC and
constraints JSON Schema cannot express. Rule metadata was refactored in a separate commit.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The CLI did not expose a configuration schema or `$schema` metadata.
  **After:** Draft-07 and parser agreement tests cover defaults, Rule options, and cross-field
  conditions; `cargo test --locked --workspace` passes.
- **Before:** No generated-schema synchronization check was available.
  **After:** `prek run --all-files`, `pre-commit run --all-files`, and all 11 Python sync-hook
  tests pass, including regeneration, deletion, and generator failure cases.
- The WASM target builds. The VS Code 1.146 bundled JSON language server reports no diagnostics
  for valid JSONC with trailing commas and reports an invalid boolean; this was a language-server
  check, not a GUI test.
- Two independent `claude-sonnet-5.5` review agents found no confirmed standards or spec gaps.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

The published URL can become a dependency for editor configurations. Removing it after
publication could break those integrations.

**Blast Radius:** configuration

CLI and Web default output gain `$schema`; editors may observe schema changes from `main`
before their installed CLI is updated. The parser does not fetch the schema URL.

author: meszmate
body:
roll apps: import another platform's config as a roll project, as Render's Heroku migration and Railway's and Koyeb's imports do. It's stacked on #176.

## In this PR

- **`POST /v1/apps/import`** takes these beside `roll_toml` and `compose`, one at a time and each at most 1 MiB:
  - `{ render }`: a Blueprint's `render.yaml`
  - `{ fly }`: `fly.toml`
  - `{ railway }`: `railway.json` or `railway.toml`
  - `{ heroku, procfile? }`: `app.json` and its Procfile

  Each is read as roll.toml, with `notes` on what isn't carried over, and checked as `roll up --all` checks it before it's answered.
- **What maps** (`apps-build/src/imports.rs`, reading text only, beside the Compose converter):
  - **Render:** web, private (`public = false`), worker and cron services; image or `rootDir`; start and pre-deploy commands; health path; instances. `keyvalue`/`redis` and `databases` become roll's own databases. `fromDatabase` becomes a link, and `generateValue` and `sync: false` become variables that are generated or asked for.
  - **Fly:** each process becomes a service (the HTTP ones `web`). Also its build image, `env`, internal port, `min_machines_running`, release command, and VM memory and CPUs.
  - **Railway:** start, pre-deploy (one command or a list), health path, replicas, cron schedule, restart policy and sleep.
  - **Heroku:** a service per Procfile process, with `release` as the web one's pre-deploy, and formation quantities. Heroku Postgres and Redis become roll databases linked from every service. `generator: secret` and required variables without a value are generated or asked for.
- **Notes:** build commands (roll detects the build), disks and mounts (set in Settings), env groups (roll secrets hold shared values), add-ons roll doesn't have, and `postdeploy` scripts.
- **Dashboard.** "From a file" picks the kind by the file's name (`render.yaml`, `fly.toml`, `railway.json`/`.toml`, `app.json`) and offers to save the result as roll.toml.
- **`## Next`:** the item is done.

## Checked

- `imports` unit test: one file of each kind read as a valid project (links, generated and asked variables, ports, memory, pre-deploy, the notes).
- `a_compose_file_is_read_as_a_project_without_making_anything`: a Render Blueprint over the API (a link to its database, a generated secret), and two files at once refused.
- OpenAPI regenerated; clippy and tests for apps-build and apps-control, typecheck, `pnpm test:apps`, roll-mcp, rolld's unit and auth tests.

author: fujibee
body:
## Problem

`agmsg delivery agmsgd` for grok-build sets `use_leader = true` under `[cli]` in `~/.grok/config.toml`, and the user restarts the Grok session. The TUI then runs in leader mode: `grok --resume <id>` has a `grok agent leader` child, and `~/.grok/leader.sock` is listening. But it does not pass `GROK_LEADER_SOCKET` to its hooks. Measured on Grok Build 1.0.77: the variable is absent from the TUI, from its leader, and from the hook shell.

The hooks took the socket from that variable only, because of the fix that removed the blind default-path fallback. So the witness of every such seat recorded `"leader_socket": ""`. `agmsg daemon status` said "grok is not running in leader mode", and agmsgd never delivered to the seat. Earlier real-machine checks started the TUI with an explicit `--leader-socket`, which does pass the variable, so this path was not exercised.

## Change

`agmsg_grok_leader_socket_for <session_pid> <grok_home>` (scripts/internal/grok-session-witness.sh) answers with one of three verdicts: `found <socket>`, `none`, or `unknown <reason>`.

1. If `GROK_LEADER_SOCKET` is set, the verdict is found, with that value, as before.
2. Otherwise, `ps -A -o pid= -o ppid= -o comm=` lists the children of the session's own process (the pid from `active_sessions.json`). pid and ppid are separate columns, and the command comes last, so a path with spaces stays whole. A child counts only when:
   - the basename of its executable is exactly `grok`, and
   - its argv begins exactly `agent leader`. The argv is read from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` where that exists (exact, NUL-separated). Elsewhere it comes from `ps -p <pid> -o args=`, checked against the exact executable path as its prefix.
3. The child's `--leader-socket` (either form) is read without splitting on spaces: from the cmdline on Linux, or on macOS from the leader's own bound unix socket (one `lsof -U` call, only when the flag is present). With no flag, the socket is `GROK_HOME/leader.sock`.
4. Any of these gives `unknown` with the reason, never "no leader": a ps failure, a `grok` child whose own argv cannot be read (`/proc` cmdline or `ps -p` failing or empty), or a `--leader-socket` whose path cannot be read.

Both hooks use it:

- SessionStart, once the session's pid is known.
- Stop, when it creates a witness.
- Stop also fills the socket into this session's existing witness when that witness was written empty. It clears or rewrites the pending reason only after the witness update succeeds. A failed update records why, in the same order the recovery branch uses.

When the verdict is `unknown`, the witness keeps an empty socket and the reason is written as the seat's pending reason. `agmsg daemon status` shows that reason instead of "grok is not running in leader mode". Only a confirmed `none` produces that message.

## What stays the same

- A TUI with no leader child keeps an empty socket. agmsgd's connect probe then never connects to it, and never has a leader started for it, which is what the earlier fallback removal was for.
- A leader started by an earlier TUI and merely shared by this one is not this session's child. It is not adopted, and that seat keeps the "not in leader mode" reason.
- No new stop or refusal; this removes a case where delivery silently never happened.
- Windows (MSYS) is unchanged.

## Process spawns

These run only while `GROK_LEADER_SOCKET` is unset, and in Stop only while the witness's socket is still empty. Once the socket is recorded, the per-turn cost is zero.

- One `ps` for the process table.
- Per `grok` child: one `ps -p`, or `tr` over its `/proc` cmdline plus two `sed`.
- With `--leader-socket`: `lsof`, `sed`, `sort` and `grep`.
- Reading the result: one `$(…)` capture plus two `sed` (`agmsg_grok_resolve_leader_socket`).
- Stop's fill-in path also has the `_wpid` sed/head capture and the JSON escape sed capture.
- Measured about 70 ms per lookup on macOS.

## Tests

`tests/test_grok_session_witness.bats` uses a stub `ps` (table plus `-p … -o args=`), a stub `lsof`, and a fake `/proc` through `AGMSG_GROK_PROC_DIR`:

- The session's own child leader gives `GROK_HOME/leader.sock`.
- An executable path with spaces is matched whole.
- A `--leader-socket` with spaces is read whole from the bound socket, in both flag forms (ps args path).
- `/proc` cmdline gives the exact argv, with a socket containing spaces, in both flag forms.
- `notgrok`, `grok agent stdio`, and a leader that is not this session's child are not adopted. The result is `none`, with no pending reason.
- `ps` exiting non-zero is `unknown`, recorded as the pending reason.
- `--leader-socket` with an unreadable path is `unknown`.
- Stop fills an empty socket once the leader is found, and clears the pending reason.
- A grok child whose argv cannot be read is `unknown`.
- When the socket is found but the witness update fails, the reason is recorded and the pending reason is not just cleared.
- Existing cases still pass.

`tests/agmsgd_status_display.test.mjs` covers `leader_socket_unknown:<reason>`, which shows the reason.

## Real-machine check

To be run on this Mac's live install after it lands in `integration/1.8.1`:

- agmsgd launched by launchd.
- The mode switched with `agmsg delivery agmsgd`.
- A Grok TUI in leader mode through `use_leader`, resumed the normal way.
- A message round trip.

The lookup itself was checked against the live process table: it returns `~/.grok/leader.sock` for a `use_leader` session and nothing for a non-leader Grok session.

## What this adds

**Interact now works out the battlefield by the layer rules (CR 613).** The cards you pick count as permanents that arrived in the order shown. For each one it shows the final types, colors, abilities, power/toughness and controller, the steps in layer order with rule cites, the state-based actions that follow, and every other result when the arrival order changes the answer. Anything it cannot read is listed under "Not modeled" instead of being guessed.

- `docs/effects.js` reads continuous effects from oracle text.
- `docs/layers.js` applies rule 613: copy effects, control, types, colors, abilities, power/toughness 7a–7d, timestamps, dependency (613.8), 305.7 for basic land types, 611.2c for resolved effects, then state-based actions.
- `docs/synergy.js` and a "Cards that work with these" block: known combos from Commander Spellbook first, then possible loops and text-found links. Each suggestion is checked against the layer engine.
- Wording notes now show only when they can change the answer for the chosen cards; the full list is folded away.
- For the judge: `node tools/layers.js "Card A" "Card B"` and `node tools/synergy.js "Card A" "Card B"`; `CLAUDE.md` says when to use them.
- `cards.json` gains a color field on the 488 cards whose mana cost does not give their color (from the source data's own color field).

## Tests

- `node tools/tests/layers.js`: 61 passed. Every example under rule 613, the Humility + Opalescence rulings in all orders, Turn to Frog, Darksteel Mutation, Inside Out, Mycosynth Lattice + March of the Machines, Blood Moon + Urborg, Clone and other copy examples, and derived cases. Each test checks that the ruling or rules example it relies on is still in the data.
- `node tools/tests/logic.js`: 46 passed.
- Browser checks at phone (390 px) and desktop (1280 px) size: 25 checks each, no errors, no sideways scroll, plus a regression pass over the other tabs.

## Honest numbers

- Effect reader coverage: 73.8% of the 10,256 continuous effects in the card data are read exactly, 12.1% are read but need something the board cannot see, 14.1% are not modeled. Always-on abilities: 92.6% read.
- Synergy finder, text-found links only (combo list off), on 400 known three-card combos with one card hidden: the hidden card is in the top 10 in 0.8% of cases. With the combo list on, a listed combo's missing card is always in the first tier. The text links are weak leads today; the combo list and layer checks carry it.
- Triggers, replacement effects and combat are not simulated; the older pattern-based links still cover those.

The push to `main` touches `tools/`, so the "Refresh card data" workflow runs and Pages redeploys. `HANDOFF.md` is updated: Step 6 done, Step 7 next.

`connect()` (`src/app/actions.ts`) dispatches `connectError` with the described error, but nothing reads `state.connectError`. Connecting from the tree (Enter, double click, the Connect menu item) to a server that fails, on the real desktop app:

## Summary

Docs-only follow-up recording two related staging rollouts as one security-and-deployment-control change: PR #21 and PR #22.

### PR #21: Data API privilege closure (merge `35ca09c`)
- **Migration 67**, `20261021120000_revoke_data_api_role_privileges`, changes privileges only. It makes no schema or application-data change and is idempotent.
- On staging, `anon` and `authenticated` now reach:
  - 0 of the 70 public tables;
  - neither of the 2 sequences.
- They also have no CREATE on `public`.
- `service_role` is unchanged.
- The migration-guard routine check distinguishes FUNCTION, PROCEDURE and ROUTINE correctly (`1da61fa`).
- Verification:
  - guard tests 105/105;
  - full Vitest 6,837 passed, 0 failed, 119 skipped;
  - merge deployment `dpl_Aa8vioZkq2SBy2qcTkGop1kRPr2K`: Ready, with health, `/ar` and `/en` returning 200, and 67 migrations, none pending.
- **Known limit, also recorded:** the migration cannot change the default privileges owned by `supabase_admin`. This is not a vulnerability-free state.

### The PR #21 Preview incident
Opening PR #21 triggered `barq-staging` **Preview** deployment `dpl_HivKn574U6tuYF2FHEuA5ki9pLMv`.
- That build ran `prisma migrate deploy` against the **shared staging database**.
- It applied migration 67 **before merge**: started 2026-11-14 00:18:27 UTC, finished 00:18:28 UTC.
- No agent ran it manually, and the application stayed healthy.
- It is documented as a pipeline defect (Preview builds inherited the staging database and migrated before merge), not as intended behaviour.

### PR #22: Preview migration isolation (merge `8e9ee1a`)
- `vercel-build` is now `npm run validate-env && node scripts/vercel-migrate.mjs && next build`.
- With `VERCEL_ENV=preview`:
  - `prisma migrate deploy` is **skipped**, with an explicit log line;
  - environment validation and `next build` still run.
- **Preview proof:** deployment `dpl_B3tRKSr1GKW47vftsXc8mEpAXywc` logged the skip, never invoked Prisma, and completed.
- The staging migration fingerprint stayed at `46809d9a126fd0411f9f3121dca77881` (67/67).

### Production-target proof that migrations still run after merge
Merge deployment `dpl_2xhmbbwFRiss3m6gyZGqS8FjGxBz`, built from `8e9ee1a`, logged:
- environment validation;
- `vercel-migrate: running \`prisma migrate deploy\` (VERCEL_ENV=production).`;
- 67 migrations found, none pending;
- the build completed.

`/api/health`, `/ar` and `/en` returned 200, and post-merge CI and Secret scan passed.

### Accepted trade-off
A Preview whose code needs a migration that is not yet applied may fail or be incomplete until that migration is merged and applied by the `staging` build.

body:
## Summary

Add an experimental host-only CPU detector that preserves the pinned OpenCV contour-based detection behavior while reducing steady-state latency. It accepts host grayscale images and returns host IDs/corners without CUDA, tracking, skipped frames, or reuse of previous-frame images/results.

The implementation reuses workspaces, shares adaptive-threshold calculations, filters contours before allocation, computes demanded current-frame pyramid regions, caches refinement storage, and uses immutable exact dictionary lookup. Independent switches retain comparison routes and explicitly separate algorithm-changing experiments. The installed CUDA API is unchanged.

The standalone CPU build, exact-output tests, benchmark/resource/video tools, provenance records, and README comparison tables are included. OpenCV is pinned to 4.14.0 (`0654a42e19215ef25b1d367d822f3c630447e7c7`).

## Measured results

Six hosts used the same 16 industrial photographs, matching settings, one/four pinned physical cores, and three independent processes per condition. Startup, image decoding, setup and warm-up are excluded. Values below are median per-image OpenCV/optimized p50 ratios.

| CPU | ArUco3 on, 1t | On, 4t | Off, 1t | Off, 4t |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DGX Spark GB10 | 1.577x | 1.674x | 1.660x | 1.838x |
| Jetson AGX Orin | 1.539x | 1.389x | 1.513x | 1.358x |
| Intel N97 | 1.509x | 1.443x | 1.469x | 1.277x |
| Xeon w7-3565X | 1.481x | 1.328x | 1.364x | 1.159x |
| Jetson AGX Thor | 1.629x | 1.623x | 1.639x | 1.961x |
| Core i9-12900KS | 1.450x | 1.442x | 1.356x | 1.242x |

All 384 image/configuration aggregates beat OpenCV at p50/p95/p99, with exact output agreement; all 24 positive controls detected the expected four markers. The weakest per-image aggregate gain is 1.041x. Existing workloads/power policies were retained, and these still photographs do not establish universal speedups, field recall, or video throughput. Earlier synthetic experiments also retain conditions where OpenCV is faster.

See [six-host report](https://github.com/MasakazuTobeta/ArUco3-CUDA/blob/feat/cpu-detector/docs/cpu-multihost-report.md), [steady-state report](https://github.com/MasakazuTobeta/ArUco3-CUDA/blob/feat/cpu-detector/docs/cpu-steady-state-report.md), and [CPU design](https://github.com/MasakazuTobeta/ArUco3-CUDA/blob/feat/cpu-detector/docs/design/cpu-optimization.md).

## Validation

- Fresh randomized Release suite: all 46 C++ cases passed.
- Fresh full ASan/UBSan suite: all 47 CTest entries passed (46 C++ cases and the Python suite), with leak detection and halt-on-error enabled. No sanitizer diagnostics or timeouts; 760.27 seconds total.
- All 24 Python measurement-tool regression tests passed; these now run in GitHub CI and standalone CPU CTest.
- Additional adversarial detector/helper probes passed in Release and under ASan/UBSan, including sparse sampling, poisoned cache storage, projective warps, contour ordering, numeric boundaries, and allocation-failure recovery. Counts and limitations are in the [adversarial review record](https://github.com/MasakazuTobeta/ArUco3-CUDA/blob/feat/cpu-detector/docs/cpu-adversarial-review.md).
- Recorded CPU-module coverage: 96.2% lines, 100% functions, 67.8% branches. Coverage was not rerun for the tooling follow-up; the 100% branch-coverage goal remains unmet.
- Independent six-host audit: 2,304 timed rows, exact inputs/configuration/outputs, positive controls, recomputed summaries and x86 runtime library hashes. All 24 group summaries reproduce exactly with the stricter summarizer.
- The initial publication tree matched all 173 frozen C++/CMake source hashes from the measured implementation. The review follow-up changes only the test CMake registration among those files; production detector C++ and published latency values are unchanged.
- Publication checks: clang-format 18 (138 files), Doxygen (45 headers), SPDX identifiers, relative documentation links (428), and `git diff --check` pass.

GitHub CI passes for the tooling fix and runs the new Python regression tests. It does not build/run the OpenCV-dependent CPU detector; the recorded local CPU tests and physical-host checks supply that validation.

## Review follow-up

Address the reported metadata-overwrite defect and independently reproduced issues in related measurement tools:

- Atomically claim a fresh result directory after preflight; reject existing, partial and symlink destinations without changing old measurements or provenance.
- Resolve the executable once so binary hashing and execution identify the same file.
- Refuse optimized Python execution that would disable the six-host runner's or audit tool's assertions.
- Reject incomplete, empty, inconsistently configured or malformed batches and mismatching input dimensions/hashes before aggregation.

The review reproduced no additional production-detector defect. Exploratory checks do not establish equivalence for every image or parameter combination; the OpenCV shared libraries were not sanitizer-instrumented. New sanitizer/probe execution was on DGX Spark, not a repeated six-host performance campaign.

## Scope and follow-up

No new raw CPU measurement logs, images, binaries or generated result bundles are included. Reports, conditions, reproduction/audit sources and required fixed manifests are retained, with CPU-specific ignore rules for generated output.

body:
Fixes the Sol findings Mason's agents raised on the staging billing migrations (#1904 comment, 16 Nov). They block #1878, #1880, #1885 and #1889.

## What changes
| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **BLOCKER**: return credit for delivered-but-unbilled quantity refused (`20270109100400` freeze) | The freeze skips unlinked lines: that quantity was never billed, so the credit carries no tax. Credit issues with 0 tax. |
| **HIGH**: standing discount lowers invoice profit, but order-based profit stays undiscounted (`20270109100100`) | Financial dashboard, profitability report, per-payer sales reports, season comparison and the sale page's profit and margin now count the discount (cancelled and voided invoices excluded; margin on what's billed). |
| **HIGH ×2 / MED**: discount and tax setters roll back on a field-split draft or a zero-quantity Bill Split sliver | `set_invoice_standing_discount` refuses that draft in plain words ("void the group and redraft it"); `set_order_sales_tax` applies to the sale and keeps that draft as it was, and the toast names it. |
| **HIGH**: "Use the customer's rate" bills the customer's *current* rate | It restores the rate the sale was drafted with (new `drafted_rate_pct`, backfilled for existing overrides from the audit log). A note under the button says which rate: "Goes back to 10%, the customer's rate when this sale was drafted." |
| HIGH: tax-inclusive typed credit memos | No change: office credit memos never include tax (Mason, 16 Nov). |

**Deliberately unchanged:** the stored `orders.total_profit` and `total_price` stay undiscounted because commission reads them. That moves with commission-after-discount (week 4 item 6), which is also what turns the discount on for live.

## Migrations
- `20270117120000_billing_sol_fixes_staging` (A, D, E)
- `20270117130000_standing_discount_in_order_profit` (B)

Restamped from `20270109100500/600` after staging moved past them (SQL byte-identical). Each has a preflight pin on every function it replaces; both apply cleanly on a local rebuild of current staging in stamp order.

## Proof
- Local DB, old code vs new code: A unbilled return credit refused → issued with 0 tax; D tax switch rolled back → applies, split draft kept; E revert went to the customer's new rate → back to the drafted rate; B dashboard profit = invoice P&L, sale page profit falls by the discount, cancelled/voided invoices drop out, a rep can't call the helper, commission unchanged.
- Re-run on the merged branch (current staging + this): all of the above hold.
- Manual test in the app, 9 steps (customer 10% → sale → delivery → profit tile → override 5% → customer 20% → "Use the customer's rate" back to 10% → dashboard): all pass. Taha's OK 17 Nov.
- Unit: `salesTaxToast`, `errorSanitizer`, `StandingDiscountControl` (note shown, and not shown when the drafted rate is unknown).
- Reviews: Luna to clean; attack run; Sol 4 rounds at `c06c2c2a6` (all fixed or answered below).

## Known and accepted
- **Release order (Sol HIGH, answered with live evidence):** at release, `20270109100400`'s backfill runs before this fix and still refuses a *posted* return credit with an unlinked line. Live had **0 posted return credits** (read-only check, 16 Nov, Taha's OK). Live keeps issuing credits until the release, so **re-check this on live right before the release applies**; if one exists, the apply stops cleanly (one transaction) and nothing is half-applied.
- MED: a kept split draft can still post with the tax it had (the toast names it).
- MED: dashboard cost on a large discounted ledger (81 ms → 794 ms at 150 discounted sales locally); no effect on live until the discount is on.
- LOW: a part-invoiced sale shows only its invoiced share of the discount; sales detail shows the undiscounted unit price beside the discounted total.

author: shrwnsan
body:
## What

One rule added to `## Files` in `global/AGENTS.md`:

```
- Jails (pi-lid/bwrap, PILID_LANE set): paths outside PILID_WORKSPACE are read-only by design. EROFS there is sandbox shape, not disk failure - check the lane before diagnosing. Mount-option strings (e.g. errors=remount-ro) are static config, not evidence an event fired.
```

## Why (live incident)

An agent session in the pi-lid `lid` lane hit EROFS writing outside `PILID_WORKSPACE` and diagnosed it as an ext4 `errors=remount-ro` disk event — recommending an unnecessary fsck and deferring work 'until remount'. The user later switched lanes (`free`) and the same fs was rw. The ro root was just bwrap design: only `PILID_WORKSPACE` gets an rw bind mount. Bonus: that same ro mount is what contained an earlier runaway `rm -rf` inside the jail.

Two failure modes this rule prevents:
1. False disk-failure diagnosis → wasted fsck/remount advice, needless deferral.
2. Over-trust of mount-option strings — `errors=remount-ro` appears in every mount listing as static config, healthy or not.

## Rollout

Local `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` copies updated in the same session (rule lands in the local copy at merge time).

author: lxj808624
body:
关联 #24。

## 问题

官方目录地址（`raw.githubusercontent.com/...`）在部分网络下不可达时，宿主抛的是带码的 `QuantSkillsHostError('Unable to fetch the QuantSkills catalog.', 'CATALOG_FETCH_FAILED')`，但错误穿过 remote 网关后 `code` 被压成 `gateway/internal`。前端 `catalogFailureLabel` 只认 `CATALOG_INVALID` / `CATALOG_FETCH_FAILED`，其余回落成「无法连接 QuantSkills 宿主服务。」，把「远端目录不可达」误报成「宿主连不上」，用户排查方向完全错。

## 改动

`packages/ui-quantskills/src/client/catalog.ts`

- `catalogFailureLabel` 增加第二个入参 `message`；当码被网关压平时，按宿主自己的措辞（`Unable to fetch the QuantSkills catalog` / `QuantSkills catalog request timed out`）识别为目录抓取失败，复用仓库里已有文案「宿主暂时无法读取 QuantSkills 官方目录。」
- 调用处传入 `error instanceof Error ? error.message : undefined`
- 不记录、不外泄宿主细节（原有「不把 Host 细节写进快照」的测试仍然通过）

## 测试

新增回归用例：码为 `gateway/internal`、消息为 `Unable to fetch the QuantSkills catalog.` 时，快照必须显示目录失败文案。

```
pnpm vitest run packages/ui-quantskills/tests/catalog.client.spec.ts
✓ 25 tests passed
```

## 未覆盖

网关侧保留 `CATALOG_FETCH_FAILED` 才是根治——那需要改 remote 协议的错误序列化，不在本仓库范围，留作后续。#24 里也提到。

另外建议给目录地址一个可配置的界面入口（宿主侧已支持 `catalogUrl` 配置）。

author: nurgeldiserikbay
body: Adds opt-in authenticated receiver request boundary helper. Server-owned receiverScope (never client-controlled), SHA-256 timing-safe static bearer-token comparison, strict Content-Type, Idempotency-Key, bounded canonical JSON body (rejects duplicate property names), and routing to durable alert ingress only after validation. Unit tests prove wrong tokens/malformed bodies/accessor-backed values cause no SQL calls. Checklist documents remaining operational gates. Not exposed as an HTTP controller or scheduled receiver; requires CI and operator-approved deployment.

author: wdconinc
body:
This PR adds the spectral decomposition of the Euclidean two- and three-point correlators and proves the ratio method for single-hadron matrix elements: under a spectral gap, `C₃(t, τ) / C₂(t)` converges to the ground-state matrix element `⟨0|O|0⟩`, with a remainder bounded by an explicit constant times `e^{-Δ τ} + e^{-Δ (t - τ)}`.

Roadmap target: `EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/LatticeBridge/README.md`, Layer 0, §0.5 "Single-hadron matrix elements from Euclidean correlators". It supplies the §0.5 definitions and theorem (ii). `SpectralData ι` holds energies `E n`, overlaps `Z n = ⟨Ω|χ|n⟩` and matrix elements `⟨n|O|m⟩`. From these, `SpectralData.twoPoint` (`∑ₙ |Z n|² e^{-E n t}`) and `SpectralData.threePoint` (`∑ₙ,ₘ Z n ⟨n|O|m⟩ conj (Z m) e^{-E n (t-τ)} e^{-E m τ}`) are the two- and three-point correlators. `SpectralData.HasSpectralGap S n₀ Δ` is the spectral-gap hypothesis.

The ground-state term and remainder of each correlator are given by `twoPoint_mul_exp_sub_le` / `sq_norm_overlap_le_twoPoint_mul_exp` (`0 ≤ C₂ e^{E₀t} - |Z₀|² ≤ K₂ e^{-Δt}`) and `norm_threePoint_mul_exp_sub_le`. Theorem (ii) is `norm_threePoint_div_twoPoint_sub_le` (quantitative) and `tendsto_threePoint_div_twoPoint` (along any filter on which `τ` and `t - τ` both tend to infinity). Following the README's "gap named honestly", the constant is not bounded by the gap: it is written out as the excited-state weights `K₂ = ∑ₙ |Z n|² - |Z₀|²` and `K₃ = ∑ₙ,ₘ |Z n| ‖⟨n|O|m⟩‖ |Z m| - |Z₀|² ‖⟨0|O|0⟩‖`, and only summability is assumed of them. `twoPoint_pos` and `tendsto_twoPoint_mul_exp` (ground-state dominance) round out the two-point API.

The new file is `EpsilonEridani/QFT/Lattice/Correlator/Basic.lean` (382 lines), a new `Correlator/` directory next to the existing `Continuation/`. It uses only Mathlib (`hasSum_ite_sub_hasSum`, `tsum_of_norm_bounded`, `hasSum_le`). The physics follows the standard transfer-matrix decomposition at infinite time extent (Gattringer–Lang, *Quantum Chromodynamics on the Lattice*, Ch. 6), which is cited in the module docstring. Layer 0 §0.1–0.3 are on `main` (#93, #130) or open (#203, the Euclidean dataset), and this PR does not overlap them.

What remains of §0.5 after this PR: theorem (i), that `C₂` is the Laplace transform of a positive spectral measure (stated against `TauCeti.Analysis.CompletelyMonotone.Stieltjes.Laplace`), and (iii), the determination of the spectral measure from the correlator on a half-line, together with the two-state example.

Roadmap: LatticeBridge

author: hklion
body:
## Summary

With `driver.couple_currents = true` the ocean sends its surface current to the atmosphere
with the SST, and ERF takes its surface stress from the wind relative to the moving water
surface, as COAWST's WRF does with ROMS's `UOCE`/`VOCE`. This is the last piece of the
wind-current coupling: REMORA packs the current (seahorce-scidac/REMORA#860), ERF applies it
(erf-model/ERF#5121, which took in erf-model/ERF#5122), and this PR connects them. Both are in the submodules
development already points at (#46), and the current follows the east/north convention of #43.

## Changes

- `Source/ERFRemoraCouplingContract.H`: two ocean-to-atmosphere lanes after the SST, `Uoce` and
  `Voce`, the eastward and northward current at ERF's cell centres in m/s.
- `Source/ERFRemoraMultiBlockContainer.H/.cpp`:
  - `driver.couple_currents` (default false). Without it the run has the SST lane alone, so
    its checks, diagnostics and exchange plotfiles are unchanged. It needs
    `driver.coupling_direction = two_way`.
  - `PackOceanToAtmos` packs the SST and, when coupled, the current
    (`REMORA::PackSurfaceCurrents`: REMORA's top-level velocity at rho points, turned from its
    grid axes to east and north with its `angle`), with the SST's weights and ERF land mask.
    It replaces the two copies of the SST pack (start-up and exchange).
  - The lanes go to `ERF::ApplyOceanSurfaceState` with the SST's coverage flag; ERF turns
    them to its grid axes with its lat/lon and averages them to the faces of its surface.
  - The ocean state is applied once per exchange instead of at every ERF substep. ERF keeps
    what it is given in its own arrays, which its surface layer reads every step, so the
    repeats did nothing; this answers a point from the review of erf-model/ERF#5122.
    Results are unchanged (see Testing).
  - The active ocean-to-atmosphere lane names are kept with the lanes, for the non-finite
    checks, diagnostics, NaN injection and exchange plotfiles.
- `Source/main.cpp`: `driver.couple_currents` sets ERF's `erf.use_coupled_currents`, as two-way
  coupling sets `erf.use_coupled_sst`, so the two can't disagree. Setting
  `erf.use_coupled_currents` alone stops the run at start-up: ERF would otherwise wait for a
  current the driver never sends and stop at the first exchange.
- `Source/StandaloneSolverRuns.H`, `Source/RunREMORAStandalone.cpp`: `REMORAPackSurfaceCurrents`.
- `cmake/run_coupled_surface_current.cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt`: the test below, registered when fcompare is built, like the other tests that use it.
- `README.md`, `INSTALL.md`: the option and the lanes.

REMORA's own relative wind (`remora.bulk_flux_relative_wind`) is the ocean-side counterpart in
state mode; with `driver.atm2ocn_mode = flux` REMORA computes no bulk fluxes, and ERF's stress
already uses the relative wind when the current is coupled.

## Testing

Release build, MPI, CPU.

`reproducer_coupled_surface_current` (new), on `Exec/Upwelling/inputs_twoway` (flux mode), every
step an exchange:

| Case | Checks |
|---|---|
| `current` | runs; the ocean-to-atmosphere exchange plotfile has `Uoce` and `Voce`, not all zero (max 6e-8 and 1.7e-4 m/s after 4 steps) |
| `rest`, `rest_again` | same deck without the option, twice; ERF's velocities differ from `current`'s (by 1.1e-7 m/s), and by at least a thousand times more than the two runs without it differ from each other (they agree exactly on CPU), so the current reached ERF's surface layer |
| `one_way` | `driver.couple_currents` with `ERFtoREMORA` stops at start-up with the two-way message |
| `erf_only` | `erf.use_coupled_currents` alone stops at start-up, naming `driver.couple_currents` |

Under `ctest -j 2` on a 4-core machine, 17 more of the restart and reproducer tests failed, and
all of them passed when rerun one at a time. `reproducer_coupled_sst_coverage`, which failed on
development before #46, passes.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Full `ctest` run serially | 69 of 71 pass |
| `reproducer_restart_independent_exchange_30`, `_60` | fail, as with the ERF that development points at: since erf-model/ERF#5124 removed the MYNN length-scale taper, ERF's state after a restart drifts from the continuous run's (about 1e-6 in the eddy viscosities), past the tests' 2e-10 tolerance |
| Upwelling two-way, 10 ERF substeps per exchange, ocean state applied once per exchange against at every substep, with and without the current | every ERF and REMORA field bit-identical |

The Upwelling grids are not rotated, so the turning of the current to east and north and back
is exercised with angle 0 only; the angle conventions on both sides are the ones #43 uses for
the wind and stress.

## Not in this PR

- The current on ERF's refined levels (ERF applies it on level 0 only and warns).
- A deck in `Exec/` that turns the option on; OCCAMS would be the natural one once #43's
  rotation has been checked there.

author: maxgb23
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #391 — the number-addressed detection lands here; the flow-style `with:` gap it exposed is #405, and #391 stays open until that closes.

## Type

- [x] Bug fix — `type:bug`

## What

`pull-request-target` reported a counted **pass** for a head reached by pull request number. That is the one defect the loop found where the tool lets a real attack through: `pull_request_target` runs with the base repository's privileges, so checking the fork's head out inside it runs code nobody reviewed.

Four shapes, each `{"error":0,"pass":1}` before this change, each a `pull-request-target-checkout` at its own step line after it:

```
with: { ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head }     → refs/pull/<n>/head
with: { ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge }    → refs/pull/<n>/merge
run: gh pr checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}                → gh pr checkout <n>
run: git fetch origin pull/<n>/head && git checkout FETCH_HEAD            → fetch then FETCH_HEAD
```

The number may be literal (`refs/pull/7/head`) or an expression; either way the reference is matched **as written**, and nothing is resolved — which is why R11's existing "does not resolve the expression" limit never covered this and why the spec change was a widening, not an exception.

RED, observed before the fix:

```
flags a head reached by pull request number, not only by an expression
  'pass' !== 'fail'
  exit 0  summary {"error":0,...,"pass":1,"verdict":"pass"}  findings 0
```

## What did not move

The plain-checkout pass, the `on: pull_request` pass, all three skip codes, the human renderer still printing no code, and the `manual` remediation. A pull-head fetch followed by `git checkout main` is a **pass**, not a false positive — that boundary is asserted.

## The limit this exposed, stated where a reader looks

A `with:` map in **flow style** is not read at all: the structural reader models block mappings only (`docs/decisions.md` I-79). The page's Limits and the catalog `limits` now say so, with the reproduction, instead of leaving a reader to assume the form does not matter. Opened as **#405**, because the cure belongs in the shared reader and reaches every rule that reads `with:`.

## Test plan

```sh
node --test tests/rules/pull-request-target.test.js tests/docs-contract.test.js   # 28 tests: 28 passing
node --test                                                                        # 904 tests: 903 passing, 1 skipped, 0 failing
```

No golden moved: `node scripts/gen-golden.js` rewrote all six identically, because the vulnerable fixture still fails on the unchanged `head.sha` expression.

Risk: item 3 — this widens a detection contract. The spec change (#404) preceded it, and the four shapes above are the measurement.

author: gossling8-debug
mraible
body:
The pylint job installed its tools by name (`pip install pylint crowdstrike-falconpy pyyaml tomli`), and `requirements-test.txt` listed pytest and pytest-cov without versions. Dependabot never sees packages installed that way, so the dev tools floated to whatever was latest on each run, and a new release could break CI with no change in this repo.

This PR pins pylint, pytest, and pytest-cov exactly in `requirements-test.txt`, and the pylint job now installs that file with `pip install -r`, which also drops `tomli` since Python 3.11+ doesn't need it. Dependabot now has a `pip` entry for the repo root on the same weekly schedule as the Actions updates. `crowdstrike-falconpy` stays unpinned in `requirements.txt`, which Dependabot leaves alone.

Pylint is pinned to 4.1.3 and pytest to 9.2.0, matching the Falcon Foundry samples, and Dependabot will bump them from there. Locally, pylint scores 10.00/10 and all 664 tests pass with 94.59% coverage.

author: mlpditto
body:
## Why

A sequel article ("… (2)") opens in the middle of the story — "The uncle nods and asks at once…" — and a reader who never saw part 1 (new interns, for one) has no way back to it: articles did not know about each other. Owner pick B from `mockup-article-sequel/`: a ⏪ link to the previous part plus a one-line recap.

## What changes (admin V102.673, intern V101.320)

**Admin — Articles editor**
- A **⏪ chip** leads the 🩺 💊 🔗 chips in the title box. Tap → a small picker (the article with the same title minus "(n)" comes first; a box filters the list).
- Under the title: the picked previous part, ✕ to remove it, and a **one-line recap** box — per language, 120 characters, kept apart from the body (it does not use the 2000-character budget). **✨** writes it from the previous part's text (one AI call, `article_recap`, told to add no fact).
- The 📱 Preview shows the ⏪ line as it is typed.
- **✨ Ep n+1** sets the previous part by itself.
- Saved as `articles/{id}.prev = { id, title {lang}, recap {lang} }` (`prev: null` when there is none). `title` is a copy of the previous part's titles, so the intern's line needs no second read.

**Intern — the article popup**
- One line under the title: `⏪ Before · <recap>` — the recap in the reader's language, else the previous part's title.
- A tap shows the previous part in the same sheet, whole text, one button `‹ Back`. It is a look: no Got it, nothing is written. When the previous part is not a scheduled article (the intern may not read it) the line is plain text.

No rule change: `prev` rides on the article document, which only admins write.

## Checked

- `articles-sequel-qa` (new, 26 checks: editor at 1360 px, popup at 390 px).
- Updated for the fourth chip: `articles-editor-lean-qa`, `articles-topic-chips-qa`. All 31 `articles-*-qa` scripts pass.
- Whole local sweep before the push.

## Not checked

- No real model call for ✨ recap. Not opened signed in or in LINE.
- The label says "Before" / "ภาคก่อน", not "Part 1" as in the mockup — the app does not know the part number for sure.
- 🎬 clips and the History page do not show the recap.
- An existing "(2)" article needs one tap on ⏪ to pick its previous part.

- nalaze reviewa c.6940264171 i c.6940490921.

Rad je sačuvan na lokalnoj grani za 1d3.

## Polja iz §14
