author: moneer-s
body:
Adds auditd beside Sysmon for Linux, so that a write to an existing shell start file, which Sysmon does not record, leaves telemetry.

## What this does

Sysmon for Linux reports a file only when it is created. Appending a command to `~/.bashrc` (T1546.004) therefore left no telemetry in every run so far. auditd, from Ubuntu's archive at a pinned version, now records too, with the watches in `lab/sensors/audit.rules`: writes and changes of permissions, owner and extended attributes of the files that run code when an account logs in or starts a shell. Nothing else is watched, so auditd adds no process events. It also keeps what programs report about themselves, such as `useradd` adding an account or `sudo` running a command.

- `bluefire-lab run --audit-rules <file>` fills in the test account's home, loads the rules, waits until auditd records a probe write as well as Sysmon's probe command, reads auditd's lost count before and after the tests, and exports auditd's log as `audit.txt`.
- `bluefire-lab evaluate` joins auditd's records into events by their time and serial. An auditd event belongs to a test when the process that wrote it is one of the test's, by the rules that tie Sysmon's events to it: the launcher and the processes of the attack session after it, or what cron or systemd started for the test inside its window. That leaves out the driver's own records in the session, such as the change of login uid that starts it. Zircolite evaluates the pinned SigmaHQ auditd rules over the records, one record per line; a match is tied back to its record by its line, which the evaluator checks against the record's type.
- auditd's events and matches count in a test's visibility like Sysmon's, and in the ordinary activity that the lab's own rules are judged on.
- Controls: readiness also needs auditd's probe before the first test, loss needs auditd's lost count unchanged, and the engine control covers the auditd rules.
- The report names both sensors, shows auditd's rules, and lists auditd's events beside Sysmon's.

## What it could break

A run's answers can change where auditd sees what Sysmon does not: that is the point. A run without `--audit-rules` evaluates as before.

## How it was checked

- `pytest` over `lab/tests`, `ruff` and `actionlint`. The tests cover the reader on lines in the shape auditd wrote them on a runner (useradd's record is copied from run 44029759448), a record of the test's own process counting, the driver's and another step's records not counting, a process started for the test outside its session counting inside the window, one serial with two times making two events, readiness and loss failing on a missing or late probe and on lost records, and a rule matched on an auditd event being cited.
- Run 44022042190's artifact, which has no auditd, evaluated with this code from source gives the same answers as published.
- The first two runs with auditd showed two mistakes, both fixed here. In [44024453182](https://github.com/Moneer-S/BlueFire-Nexus/actions/runs/44024453182) the kernel's record of the driver's change of login uid, which starts each step's session, counted as an event of every test. In [44025501112](https://github.com/Moneer-S/BlueFire-Nexus/actions/runs/44025501112), counting only the events a watch recorded left out what the tests' own programs wrote, such as useradd's record of T1136.001.
- Run [44029759448](https://github.com/Moneer-S/BlueFire-Nexus/actions/runs/44029759448) on commit c16fbdff, all seven controls passing. T1546.004 has one auditd event, the shell opening `/home/bluefire-lab/.bashrc` for writing in its attack session, matched by "Unix Shell Configuration Modification" (medium) and "Use Of Hidden Paths Or Files" (low). The hardened run of the same test is still blocked, and its refused write is recorded. T1136.001 has useradd's record, matched by "Creation Of An User Account" (medium); the setuid and setgid tests have sudo's records of their commands, and the crontab test has cron's record of starting the planted job. The run's comparison with `main`'s run 44027624414: the `.bashrc` test and its hardened run went from no telemetry to telemetry only, and the other 32 runs gave the same answers.
- Commit f3c76b7b reads a program's own fields from inside `msg='...'`; before it the report showed those records as `acct=root res=success'`. Evaluating run 44029759448's artifact with it from source gives the same answers for all 34 runs and all seven controls passing, with the records reading `op=adding user res=success` and `cmd=chmod u+xs /tmp/evilBinary res=success`. The lab run on that commit, [44031730805](https://github.com/Moneer-S/BlueFire-Nexus/actions/runs/44031730805), on the other kernel the runner label hands out (7.0.0-1017-azure), gives the same answers with all seven controls passing.

author: neelsatyavolu
body:
## Summary
InFocus Cut: FilmCraft with team editing over InFocus Drive, for InFocus members on their own Macs.

- **Team projects on InFocus Drive.** A project is split into a shared part and one part per sequence. One person edits a sequence at a time (a lock kept alive by heartbeats). Other Macs see changes through the Drive's events stream, and a lost lock keeps the work as a "Recovered" copy.
- **Sign-in.** One "Sign in with InFocus Drive" button (browser sign-in with PKCE), an account chip with Switch Account and Sign Out, and plain errors for offline, unreachable Drive and non-members.
- **Projects and invites.** New project → add footage → invite teammates (skippable). Invitations show in the Team panel with Join and Decline, and members can leave a project. The panel shows members, who is online, and who is editing which sequence.
- **Footage.** Any member can add footage from the app (chunked, parallel, resumable uploads) or from the editing dashboard. Each Mac downloads only what the open sequences use, the open sequence first, large files in parallel ranges, and builds its own proxies as files land. Export waits until the footage is on the Mac.
- **Cleanup.** A project's local footage is removed 30 days after the project was last opened on that Mac (200 GB cache cap).
- **Fork identity.** Renamed to InFocus Cut (`org.infocus.cut`), with ArtCraft brand marks removed. The updater only looks at this fork's releases. The version is now `1.0.0-beta.1`, and macOS notarization can use an App Store Connect API key.
- New crates: `crates/team` (split/merge, cache), `crates/drive` (Drive client), `crates/team-link` (controller). The engine side is `crates/engine/src/team*.rs`.

Server side: neelsatyavolu/infocus-drive#19.

## Test plan
- [x] Crate tests for drive, team, team-link, engine, ui-egui, filmcraft and filmcraft-cli. Clippy `-D warnings`, `fmt --check` and `xtask layers` are clean.
- [x] `scripts/team-e2e.sh` with three members against the Drive's dev server:
  - create, upload, invite, join and decline; a non-member is refused and the admin can see the project
  - checksum-checked downloads and local proxies, including footage a second member adds
  - concurrent edits on different sequences, a refused lock, and leave
- [x] Against the production Drive, as two devices on one account: create and upload, open on the second device, download byte for byte, proxy, refused lock, edits from both sides syncing, and new footage reaching the first device and being proxied there.
- [x] The release build contains none of the debug-only test hooks.
- [ ] A real two-Mac test with two different members on the school network.

author: itstimwhite
body:
## What

Visual & A11y run 44019595382 on main `ea33a138` (#25562, ds-cert E4 chunk 0) failed shards 3/5/7/8 of 16 at "Run Storybook A11y Tests" — six failing stories across four shards, three root causes, all fixed with real a11y fixes or deterministic story setups. No axe rule disabled, no story skipped or excluded, no threshold loosened, no baseline touched.

**1. Error-state stories assert before the error UI lands (shards 3, 7, 8).** `SettingsPaySection.states > Error Summary Failed`, `SettingsContactsSection > Error Load Failed`, and `SettingsBillingSection.states > Retry Billing` seed the query cache with an error state, then assert the error panel with a single synchronous `getBy*` at play start. The seeded error can be superseded by a mount refetch (and the billing hook adds one classified retry with backoff, `useBillingStatusQuery.ts:74-75`), so the error UI lands a beat after the assert — empirically intermittent (failed on `ea33a138` and on `b08a49ba`; passed between). The play functions now poll with `waitFor` — the same pattern the passing `SettingsAppearanceSection.states` stories use in the same directory.

**2. ListenNowForm save stories lose a retry-backoff race (shard 7).** `ErrorSaveFailed` and `OfflineSave` failed all 4 attempts with "Unable to find an element with the text: Failed to update music links": `useProfileMutation` sets its own classified retry (`useProfileMutation.ts:226` — two retries) which overrides the story client's `retry: false`, and the default exponential backoff (~1s + 2s ≈ 3s to the terminal error) outlasts `findByText`'s 1s default window while the form stays in its loading state. The story's `FormColumnDecorator` client now sets `mutations.retryDelay: 0` — the full retry path still executes (stub 500 / network rejection both still retried twice and still end in the same error UI); it just lands in milliseconds instead of 3 seconds. The assertions are unchanged.

**3. ArtistCard's initials fallback failed axe `label-content-name-mismatch` (shard 3).** With no photo, the card renders the artist's initials ("AG") as visible text inside the profile link, but the accessible name ("View Ariana Grande's profile") didn't include them — speech input pointing at the rendered glyphs cannot match, and this is the same class fixed for the profile avatar link earlier (aria-hidden does not help; axe counts rendered text). The fallback path's `aria-label` now carries the initials (`View Ariana Grande's profile — AG`, via the same canonical `getInitials` from `@jovie/ui` the Avatar renders). The image path's accessible name is byte-identical to before.

**4. LiquidGlassMenu states could not reach the mobile-only bar (shard 5, 5 stories).** The component's `lg:hidden` is correct product behavior (it is the mobile bottom nav), but the runner's viewport is desktop-width and addon-vitest does not apply Storybook `viewport` parameters (verified against the pinned addon source — no viewport handling in `@storybook/addon-vitest@10.6.7`), so `openMoreMenu`'s "More options" button was `display: none` in every attempt ("There are no accessible roles"). The states stories pin the bar's mobile presentation with a story-scoped `<style>` override on `[data-mobile-navigation='true']` — the same story-scoped override pattern as `NumberedSection.states`' scroll-animation settle. The component is unchanged; the bar's real DOM, contrast, focus and interactions are all still fully scanned and exercised.

## Red-before-green

- Failing command: `pnpm --filter @jovie/web test:a11y -- --shard=3/16` (also shards 5/7/8; CI: Storybook A11y Checks (3/16), 2 failed / 375 passed)
- Failing run (before fix): https://github.com/JovieInc/Jovie/actions/runs/44019595382

Shard 3 excerpt (both failures; shards 5/7/8 same run):

```text
FAIL storybook: components/molecules/ArtistCard.states.stories.tsx > Partial No Photo (initial run, 1st retry, 2nd retry, 3rd retry)
Expected the HTML found at $('.group') to have no violations:
"Elements must have their visible text as part of their accessible name (label-content-name-mismatch)"
FAIL storybook: components/features/dashboard/organisms/SettingsPaySection.states.stories.tsx > Error Summary Failed (initial run, 1st retry, 2nd retry, 3rd retry)
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: Could not load your payments summary right now.
Test Files  2 failed | 116 passed (118)
```

## Blast radius

- What could break: (1) the ArtistCard fallback link's announced name changes only in the no-photo case (`src` empty) — the image path's name is byte-identical, and no test, e2e or story outside the colocated test locates the fallback name (checked repo-wide). (2) The LiquidGlassMenu states stories now render the mobile bar visible at desktop, which also puts the (previously hidden, never-scanned) open-menu DOM under axe — its visible labels are AA tokens (`text-secondary-token` on the glass surface; `text-tertiary-token` only on aria-hidden icons). (3) The story-only changes (waitFor, retryDelay) affect no product code.
- Proof: biome check (repo-pinned 2.6.6 standalone) clean on all seven touched files; the ArtistCard image-path name is pinned unchanged in the colocated test; colocated `ArtistCard.test.tsx` updated in the same diff (fallback name now includes the initials and is asserted exactly), satisfying the component/test pairing gate.

## Self-review

- Gaps: repo-wide grep for the seeded-error pattern found one more story family with the identical latent race — `SettingsBillingSection.states > Retry Billing` (error-seeded + sync `getByRole` on the error UI; passed the failing run by timing luck) — fixed here with the same waitFor wrap. `SettingsUsageStatsSection.states`, `LeadPipelineControls.states`, `ConnectorCard.states`, `JovieWorkFeed.states`, `PipelineBottleneckBanner.states` and `OvieCertificationsWorkspace.states` also seed error/loading states, but their plays either assert deterministic states or have no play function; they passed both recent runs and are flagged here only, not touched.
- Conflicts: no open PR touches any of the seven files (#25586 and #25612, the chunks that landed them, are merged/closed; remaining open claude/ds-cert-* and #25602 diffs checked — no overlap).
- Adjacent: `MobileNav.stories` (passing, same open-menu pattern) left alone — its toggle is not viewport-hidden.

## Verification

- `biome check` (repo-pinned 2.6.6 standalone) on all seven files: clean.
- axe contrast/name analysis done statically against the checked-in tokens; the runner viewport and addon-vitest viewport-gap verified against the pinned addon source from jsDelivr.
- Deferred to CI, stated explicitly: the sandbox cannot execute this lane (live Storybook + Chromium in 4 GB) and the npm registry is unreachable from it, so the shard re-run and the vitest unit run happen in CI (the a11y lane runs on the next main push; PR CI covers lint/typecheck/affected units on this diff). No gate, threshold, rule exclusion, or story skip was touched to go green. Left ready with auto-merge off — Tim merges (Nov 10 stop).

author: gilbert-g
body:
Found while leaving the box in a canonical state: a **manual** staging run without `DEPLOY_BASIC_AUTH` got 401 from the public assertion and **rolled back a build that was already live and 200 on loopback**. 401 is nginx's auth layer, not an application failure — rolling back is the wrong reaction, and on a real staging incident it would take a good deploy offline.

Now: 401 + no credentials → log the reason, exit non-zero, **leave the build serving**. Every other non-200 still rolls back.

Also adds `### Operational notes learned on the first cut` to `docs/vitrine-staging.md`: the fresh-checkout bootstrap fast-forward, the `DEPLOY_BASIC_AUTH` requirement, the `.next.prev` ignore rule, and the rollback drill with its actual output — including why my first drill attempt was invalid (HEAD was already on the broken commit, so it restored the build but not the source).

author: neo1228
body:
## 목적
- 해결할 문제: buyer `GET /api/products` global listing은 `(seller_id, product_id)`를 Java UUID natural order로 변환한 computed key로 정렬합니다. 기존 `product_seller_idx`는 Seller equality에만 맞아 global query가 매 요청 **전체 Product를 sequential scan + top-N sort**했습니다.
- 변경이 필요한 이유: EXP-015의 100k global plan은 parallel seq scan + top-N heapsort(2,038 shared-hit blocks)였고, EXP-018 fuller listing query는 warm-cache 100k median 221.708 ms를 기록했습니다. 비용이 catalog 크기에 비례하므로 신규 Product가 늘수록 모든 buyer의 첫 페이지가 느려집니다.

## 변경 범위
- 포함: V40 `product_listing_sort_idx` exact-order expression B-tree, 100k dataset plan 회귀 테스트, EXP-028 측정, ADR-0040, D-099.
- 제외: UUID ordering/cursor 계약 변경, substring/full-text search index, sort key column materialization, seller-scoped 경로 변경(V7 index 유지).

## 근거와 설계
- 확인된 사실·가정: cursor와 `ORDER BY`는 `encode(set_byte(...uuid_send(seller_id)...),'hex') COLLATE "C"`, 같은 방식의 `product_id` key를 사용합니다. `product_seller_idx (seller_id, product_id)`의 leading column은 global scope에서 unconstrained이며 raw UUID key는 computed key와 다릅니다.
- 결정과 이유: index key를 query의 **정확한 두 표현식과 collation, 순서**로 정의했습니다. PostgreSQL이 ordered index scan으로 `LIMIT`에 조기 종료할 수 있고, cursor predicate도 같은 index 순서를 활용합니다. 표현식이 정확히 일치하므로 query 수정이나 ordering contract 변경이 필요 없습니다.
- 대안·trade-off: raw UUID B-tree는 Java UUID order와 달라 사용할 수 없습니다. UUID order 자체를 바꾸면 cursor 호환성이 깨집니다. generated column은 쓰기 경로와 schema를 넓힙니다. expression index는 product insert 시 key 계산·유지 비용과 저장 공간(100k synthetic에서 9,352 kB)을 추가하며, **INSERT/UPDATE 비용은 이번에 측정하지 않았습니다**. 또한 정규 `CREATE INDEX`이므로 대형 table에서는 build 시간·lock 영향을 배포 전에 평가해야 합니다.
- 데이터·API·상태 영향: 신규 index 1개. 데이터 변경, 응답 schema, cursor format, 상태 전이 변경 없음.
- 영향 범위: Flyway V40 추가만으로 동작하며 애플리케이션 코드 변경은 없습니다.
- 검증 근거와 한계: EXP-028은 로컬 단일 세션, warm cache, 합성 100k Product, `LIMIT 101` SQL-only 측정입니다. HTTP latency·동시 부하·production data skew·쓰기 처리량은 측정하지 않았습니다.

## 시각화
- Diagram 또는 N/A 사유: N/A — 실행 계획(access path) 변화이며 계층·상태 전이가 아닙니다. 대신 plan 전후를 글로 적습니다.

```text
변경 전: Parallel Seq Scan on product → Sort(top-N heapsort) → LIMIT 101
변경 후: Index Scan using product_listing_sort_idx → LIMIT 101 (Sort 없음)
```

## 추적
- Issues: Closes #305 — [Issue #305](https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/issues/305)
- 요구사항·결정·규칙 ID: [D-099, ADR-0040](https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/blob/main/docs/02-decisions/adr/ADR-0040-global-catalog-listing-sort-index.md)
- 기준 문서·외부 참고자료: [ADR-0019](https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/blob/main/docs/02-decisions/adr/ADR-0019-seller-product-categories.md), [EXP-015](https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/blob/main/docs/03-experiments/EXP-015-catalog-listing-performance.md), [EXP-028](https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/blob/main/docs/03-experiments/EXP-028-catalog-global-listing-sort-index.md)
- 커밋 링크: https://github.com/Neo1228/ATLAS/commit/85b58cc

## 변경 요약
- [x] 변경: global listing order에 정확히 대응하는 expression index를 추가했습니다.

## 검증
- [x] 실행한 명령과 결과: `./gradlew --init-script /tmp/atlas-jdk21-check.init.gradle check --no-daemon` 전체 통과.
  - `ProductListingSortIndexMigrationIntegrationTest`: 100k Product + ONLINE_STORE availability에서 첫 페이지와 cursor 페이지 `EXPLAIN` 모두 `product_listing_sort_idx`를 사용하고 `Sort`/`Seq Scan on product`가 없음을 검증.
  - `CatalogIntegrationTest`(8), `ProductCategoryHierarchyIntegrationTest`(2) 통과 — 페이지 순서, cursor 연속성, 가격/channel filter 의미 보존.
  - EXP-028 3회 반복 median: global 277.666 → 35.717 ms, broad 241.486 → 31.816 ms, needle 238.280 → 45.883 ms.
- [x] 관련 문서·기록 갱신: ADR-0040, EXP-028(측정·재현 SQL), decision log D-099.

## 위험·후속 작업
- 알려진 위험·한계: index 유지비·저장 공간이 증가하고, write 비용은 측정하지 않았습니다. substring keyword search는 여전히 ordered entry를 순차적으로 filter하므로 selective keyword에서 index scan이 길어질 수 있습니다. 정규 `CREATE INDEX`는 대형 table에서 build 시간이 깁니다.
- 후속 작업: production 규모에서 `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` 필요 여부와 index bloat/write 비용 확인, 필요 시 search 전용 access path 별도 설계.

## 검토 체크리스트
- [x] 변경 범위가 하나의 목적과 검토 가능한 경계에 맞음.
- [x] 실행하지 않은 검증·성과를 주장하지 않음.
- [x] 데이터·보안·금전 상태·복구 영향을 검토함; 금전·재고 상태 영향 없음.
- [x] Issue 번호·링크가 일치하며 `Closes #N` 형식이 plain text임.
- [x] 복잡한 변경의 사실·가정·근거·영향을 본문에서 설명함.
- [x] API 변경 시 오류/status contract와 GET side effect를 확인함; API·응답 변경 없음, GET은 여전히 부수 효과 없음.
- [x] 필요한 경우 diagram을 사용함; 실행 계획 변화로 N/A 사유를 위에 작성.
- [x] Java 주석은 한국어; API 식별자·오류 코드 변경 없음.
- [x] 체크리스트 전체 완료.

author: liyu-ma
body:
#### Reason to change

The polling loop requires a non-zero pod count before exiting. If failed pods are garbage-collected before the next poll, subsequent successful but empty responses cause polling to continue indefinitely until the job timeout.

Example: [run 86743](https://dev.azure.com/akstelescope/telescope/_build/results?buildId=86743&view=logs&j=72a60387-941e-520b-8627-d26fb095ed8f&t=379910c3-7bd5-554b-f221-bb283273f51f). The pod list became empty at **15:06:56 UTC on November 16**, but the CL2 step continued until **00:10:43 UTC on November 17**, when the outer job timed out. The step lasted **9h 22m**.

#### Changes

- Extract CL2 Job name and namespace from the supplied manifest using `kubectl create --dry-run=client --validate=false`, to prevent inconsistent input from param and manifest file.
- Remove the redundant namespace argument from `RunClusterLoader2` and update all three callers.
- Use the discovered Job's terminal conditions instead of pod counts: `Failed=True` exits 1; `Complete=True` exits 0.
- Update the three affected generated pipelines.

#### Validation

- All 10 pipelines regenerate and match committed YAML using CI's directory-based command and the KCL 0.13.0 edition specified in kcl.mod; all seven generated CL2 scripts passed Bash syntax checks.
- Corrected generated-YAML whitespace using the CI-matched KCL version. The earlier local Bootstrap error came from compiling a single file rather than the pipeline directory; full directory-based regeneration passes.

author: zsuroy
body:
The SSH agent connection used for public-key signers is now properly closed once authentication completes instead of staying open for the life of the process. This prevents resource leaks and ensures proper cleanup of agent connections.

This change addresses the issue where SFTP sessions were leaking SSH agent connections, which could lead to resource exhaustion over time. The cleanup is now handled through a deferred function in the ConnectWithAuth function, ensuring the agent connection is released as soon as authentication is complete.

author: albertoleon7794
body:
The row agreed with 72 for #1022 once #1095 landed (main 2669cb884). Tests only, in `vtiIdentityListeners.test.ts`:

- **A shared sign-in let go at its limit** (#1095): the identity it went for has no own session lent while the shared session holds the turn or gives it up, and once its listener listens again it lends a **fresh** session, never the one from before. So an ask as it falls back to the shared way (`VtiNoOwnSession`) and never goes out on a socket the listener gave up.
- **A trip to the background**: the session is taken back, and the return lends a fresh one.

Mutant, run singly through `tools/jest72dw.sh`: removing the take-back in `stopOne` (`dropOwnSession`) fails each new row on its own; restored after. Suite 27/27.

No change to #1095 was needed: the take-back already happens before the shared session signs in as an identity, so a let-go attempt never meets a lent session.

author: seriesoftubez
body:
## What

Part 2 of planning#360: `GET /api/findings/{id}` now returns `timeline`, a list of the dates we hold for the finding, sorted by date. Trace question 3 (planning#362) will draw it. This PR is API only; the Timeline tab is not touched.

Each event is `{kind, date, precision, at, source}`. Kinds: `cve_published`, `listed_exploited_cisa`, `listed_exploited_vulncheck`, `acquired`, `claimed`, `first_seen`, `ownership_confirmed`, `due`.

- `date` is a UTC calendar day, and `precision` is `day`, `month` or `year`. `at` is the full timestamp when the record has one.
- A date we do not hold is left out. No event is ever emitted with a null date.
- `acquired`: one event per distinct (acquired entity, acquirer) on the attribution chains. It takes the date of the most precise dated row (ties go to the earliest). Other rows with a different date ride along in `other_dates`. The event carries the entity's id and name and the acquirer's id.
- `claimed`: one event per claimed target, with its id and value.
- Acquired and claimed events come from the `attribution` the route already builds, so there is no second walk and the read scope is the attribution's.
- `source` names where the date came from: `vulncheck_nvd2`, `cisa_kev`, `vulncheck_kev`, the observer for an acquisition, or `bod_26_04`. It is null for dates that are our own record.
- `due` is `bod_sla.due_date` from the same response.

Decisions: planning#360 comments 6935155582 (decision 5) and 6938589844.

## Files

- `backend/app/schemas/finding_timeline.py`: `TimelineEvent`, `TimelineDate`.
- `backend/app/services/finding_timeline.py`: `build_timeline()` is pure; `cve_record_for()` looks the record up by the upper-cased CVE id.
- `backend/app/api/findings.py`: builds the attribution once and passes it on. `FindingDetailResponse.timeline` documents the field in OpenAPI.
- Tests: `test_finding_timeline.py` (27 unit tests, no DB), `test_finding_timeline_route.py` (3 route tests).

## Verification

- Full backend suite on the branch: 4494 passed, 45 skipped (dev was 4389 before PR 156).
- Mutation checks: 20 mutations on the builder and the route, 18 killed. The two survivors are equivalent: dropping "skip a duplicate acquisition or claim already seen" only changes which duplicate's identical data wins.
- Semgrep (security-audit, owasp-top-ten, python) on the changed files: clean.
- No migration, no UI.

## Not covered

- No test reads the route as a read-scoped user. The timeline takes its acquisitions and claims only from the scoped attribution, which `test_attribution_chain_scope.py` covers, but no test asserts that a hidden acquisition stays out of `timeline`.
- The route branch for a finding with no asset (`attribution=None`) is unit-tested only.
- When two acquisition rows have the same date and precision, the order falls to `relation_id` (it decides which source is named). No test pins it.

Closes SeriesOfTubez/constellus-planning#360

body:
## What

The rest of the v2 company flow, plus the Applications list, role suggestions and auto mode.

**Compose**
- A "Start from" list (saved templates, or "Let Claude write") beside a live preview.
- The preview fills in the first selected person's name, the company and the role, with tabs for the recruiter and engineer versions.
- Instructions go in one field with a Presets menu, and the rail lists what Claude will use.

**Review**
- One email card per version, because drafts are made from two versions with "Hi {first name}," added per person.
- Each card shows who gets it and has inline subject and body editing, the résumé attachment, a word count, and "Use the other version".
- The rail's "Before you send" list checks the greeting, the résumé, leftover placeholders (`{company}`, `[Name]`) and length.

**Draft & send**
- **Before drafting:** you choose drafts only, drafts and send now, or schedule (quick picks or a custom time). The button shows the credit cost, and the rail lists each recipient with credits left after.
- **After drafting:** a done screen with a row per person (sent, scheduled, draft with Send/Schedule, or failed with a plain reason), plus Send all, Schedule and Start another company.
- **Remake drafts** is offered only while nothing has been sent or scheduled.

**Applications list:** In progress, Sent and All tabs, search and step filters, grouped by what each company waits on. The breadcrumb, the sidebar and "See all" all open it.

**Role suggestions:** your application's role plus the company's open roles from Apollo job postings (free), or "Use as written".

**Auto mode**
- **Switch:** in the top bar. Settings are in the Details rail: recruiters + engineers to pick, template, and a credit limit per company.
- **When it runs:** only after you click Find people.
- **What it does:** picks people (the strong JD matches, or the rule), writes, checks and makes the drafts, then stops. It never sends, and hands back at the step where a problem shows up.
- **While running:** a step list and a "Take over manually" button.

**Other pages:** one shared v2 skin over the pages that keep their own markup: sentence-case labels instead of uppercase mono, quieter pills and buttons, and no stat tiles.

## Reviewer notes

- **`runSearch`, `generateEmails` and `createDrafts` now take optional explicit inputs and return what they made.** Auto mode needs that to chain them before React state settles. Existing callers behave the same.
- **Saved data still loads.** Only optional fields were added. Auto settings live in `warmreach:v1:auto`.
- **Checks run:**
  - `tsc --noEmit` is clean on this branch alone.
  - All pages return 200.
  - In the browser: Compose, Review, the Send choices, the done screen, the list, the role dropdown, and the auto mode switch and settings.
- **Not run end to end:** auto mode. A real run makes Gmail drafts and can spend credits.
- **Still different from the design:**
  - Campaigns keeps its old horizontal stepper rather than the campaign cards.
  - Tsenta, Follow-ups and Résumé keep their layouts under the new skin.
  - The list's group bulk actions ("Send all 3", "Auto-select for all") and archive aren't built.

author: williamthorsen
body:
## What

Fixes the issue that the `@williamthorsen/tsconfig` readyup kit treated a tsconfig whose `extends` chain it could not read in full as one that does not adopt the base. Adds a note to each of the kit's checks that names every such tsconfig and the reason that its chain was not read, and makes a check that could read none of the chains skip instead of reporting a verdict.

## Why

A consumer running the tsconfig kit against a repo with a broken or misspelt tsconfig was told to extend the base, or got a pass that silently left the config out, so the report pointed at the wrong fix or hid the problem. The kit now says which configs it could not read and why, as the typescript kit does.

## Details

### 🐛 Bug fixes

- Fixes the issue that the `@williamthorsen/tsconfig` readyup kit failed a tsconfig that does not parse, or whose chain stops at an unresolved `extends`, as not reaching the base, and that the escaping-paths check passed such a tsconfig without counting it; each check that reads chains now names those tsconfigs and why their chains were not read.

## How to test

1. In a scratch repo containing a `package.json` and a `tsconfig.json` whose only content is `{"extends": "./tsconfg.json"}`, run `pnpm exec rdy run --file <path to this checkout>/packages/tsconfig/.readyup/kits/default.js`.
2. Confirm that the adoption check skips with "Could not read the tsconfig chain of tsconfig.json (extends "./tsconfg.json" in tsconfig.json does not resolve or does not parse)" rather than failing with "no extends chain reaches the base".
3. Replace the file's content with `{` and run the kit again; confirm that the checks name tsconfig.json with "(it does not parse)".

Closes #374

```change-record
title: Report a tsconfig chain that the kit could not read in full
entries_commit: 7496c7a
entries:
  - type: fix
    scopes: [tsconfig]
    text: Fixes the issue that the `@williamthorsen/tsconfig` readyup kit failed a
      tsconfig that does not parse, or whose chain stops at an unresolved
      `extends`, as not reaching the base, and that the escaping-paths check
      passed such a tsconfig without counting it; each check that reads chains
      now names those tsconfigs and why their chains were not read.
```

## Summary
- Return a durable `202` handle for human production approval and run the expensive graph in a bounded worker queue.
- Persist executing state before dispatch, make duplicate approvals idempotent, reconcile terminal state and gallery artifacts, and resume interrupted approvals on startup.

## Risks and limits
- The queue is process-local and SQLite-backed; it is not a distributed queue. Provider and GPU acceptance remain separate.

body: ## 개요 사무실 3D 화면 머리 위 이름표를 키우고 앱 글꼴로 또렷하게 그리며, 의자·칸막이·유리벽에 가리지 않게 했습니다(S15P31A108-450). 내 캐릭터 이름표를 '나'로 쓰고 나·사람 팀원·에이전트를 색으로 나눴습니다(S15P31A108-451). 커밋은 티켓별로 하나씩, 두 개입니다. ## 작업 내용 ### S15P31A108-450 이름표 크기·글꼴·가림 (b109722e) - 원인 - 512px 캔버스에 30px 글자를 그려 화면에서 190px 폭으로 줄였습니다. 화면 글자가 약 11px이고, 밉맵 축소로 흐렸습니다. - 글꼴 문자열이 `Geist`라 실제 등록 이름(`Geist Variable`)과 달라 무시됐습니다. - 스프라이트 재질이 ACES 톤 매핑을 거쳐 흰 알약이 회색으로 보였습니다. - 깊이 검사가 켜져 있어 칸막이·유리벽·기둥에 가렸습니다. - 고친 것 - 1·3인칭 모두 거리·줌과 상관없이 화면에서 같은 크기로 그립니다(이름 15px semibold, 상태는 400으로 옅게, 알약 높이 28px). - `renderer.getPixelRatio()`로 캔버스를 화면 픽셀과 1:1로 그리고, Nearest 필터에 밉맵을 끕니다. 2배 화면에서도 흐리지 않습니다. - 글꼴은 앱과 같은 값(`getComputedStyle(html).fontFamily`)을 씁니다. 웹폰트가 늦게 오면 한 번 다시 그립니다. 새 웹폰트·의존성은 없습니다. - 내 캐릭터 머리 위에 '나' 이름표를 답니다. 1인칭에서는 내 몸이 숨어 있어 보이지 않습니다. - 앱 팔레트에서 고른 역할 색입니다. 글자 대비는 모두 4.5:1 이상이고 단위 테스트로 확인합니다. | 역할 | 알약 | 글자 | 대비 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 나 | 꿀색 `#f3c530` (primary) | `#322710` | 8.96:1 | | 사람 팀원 | 흰색 `#ffffff` (card) | `#2c291f`, 상태 `#5c5647` | 14.54:1, 7.30:1 | | 에이전트 | 짙은 갈색 `#2c291f` (foreground) | `#fcfaf4`, 상태 `#d9d1bd` | 13.93:1, 9.56:1 | | 말풍선(대기 이유) | `#fff3c4` | `#6e5200` | 6.57:1 | - 팀원 개인 색(이니셜 원·에이전트 스카프)은 이름표에 쓰지 않아 역할 색과 섞이지 않습니다. - 비비는 지금 이름표가 없습니다(`officeActors`가 `tag`를 주지 않음). 이름표가 생기면 AI라 에이전트 색을 씁니다(`tagRole`). ## 변경 사항 - `frontend/src/three/office/OfficeRenderer3D.ts`: `nameTag()`를 다시 쓰고 `placeTags()`를 더했습니다. 옛 `tagWidth`(3인칭 190px, 1인칭 2.1 m)는 지웠습니다. - author: ryanportfolio
body:
Every headed Chrome started through `launchPlacedChrome()` waited a few seconds on a bookkeeping step before the caller got its browser. This change removes most of that wait.

## What was slow

`launchPlacedChrome()` (`scripts/lib/launch-chrome.mjs`) ends by calling `registerByMarker()` in the `servers` skill's script, so `/servers` can later say which session opened a browser. That function took a snapshot of the whole machine: the process list and two connection queries (`Get-NetTCPConnection` on Windows, `lsof` elsewhere). It then looked one process up by a marker in its command line, which needs only the process list.

## What changed

- `snapshot({ net: false })` asks for processes only and returns empty `listeners` and `conns`. The default is unchanged.
- `registerByMarker()` uses it. It is the only caller that changed; listing, triage and closing still take the full snapshot.
- The Codex copy (`.agents/skills/servers/scripts/servers.mjs`) has the same change and stays byte-identical to the Claude copy. The `servers` baseline in `.agents/skill-sources.json` was recorded in this repository with `sync-codex-skills.mjs --baseline servers`.
- Changelog entry under Unreleased. The plugin version is left alone: it has not moved since #231 and goes up with a release, and the plugin does not ship `launch-chrome.mjs`, so plugin installs would not get the speedup anyway.

The process query is the same in both modes, so the start time written into a record still equals the one a full snapshot reports. That equality is how a record is matched to its process later.

## Checked

Run from this branch on Windows, against a real headed Chrome (offscreen, muted, closed after each round), three rounds each, alternating:

| Record step | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` file | 3.7 s | 3.5 s | 3.2 s |
| this branch | 1.2 s | 1.2 s | 1.2 s |

- In all six rounds the record named the launched Chrome (same pid), was stored in the registry with its kind, purpose and start time, and its start time equalled the one a full snapshot reported for that pid. The same comparison was run against another process's start time and failed there, so it can fail.
- A full `snapshot()` from the changed file still returned ports: 25 listeners, 51 loopback connections, about 295 processes. `snapshot({ net: false })` returned 0, 0 and 296.
- `sync-codex-skills.mjs --check` warned that `servers` had changed before the baseline was recorded, and reports `Codex skills current (51 native)` after.
- Also run locally: `check-skill-size.mjs`, `test-codex-contract.mjs`, the three Codex sync test files (43 tests pass), `check-template-manifest.mjs`, `removed-skills.mjs`.

The same change in a project made from this template measured 6.2 to 7.3 s before and 1.2 to 2.2 s after. The two connection queries took less time during this run than during that one, so the saving depends on how long they take on the machine at that moment.

## Not done here

- The Linux and macOS branch (`net: false` returns before the two `lsof` calls) was not run. It only removes work.
- About one second remains in the record step: starting PowerShell and listing processes.
- New projects get this at creation. Existing projects get it when they next pull from the template with `sync-starter`.

author: fennecs-system
body:
## Why

Live run -140 (local Qwen 27B, 32k): the lead diagnosed "the Oracle JDK hard-codes `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, absent in the Nix image". After 9 in-turn summarisations it forgot this, guessed "wrong-arch binary" and re-ran the same ELF checks. The in-turn summaries kept the actions and dropped the findings.

## What

It follows Control's tree compaction throughout: `cut`, verbatim steps near the focus, older aligned blocks folded into immutable nodes built from their children, and recall over the same tree. It adds no separate format or store.

1. **One structured summary format for every tree node** (`compaction::SYSTEM`), used by chat blocks and in-turn step blocks alike. The sections are Goal & constraints, Findings (with exact paths/names/values), Errors & fixes, Decisions/plan, Open questions and Next step. A parent merges its children's sections and keeps every finding unless later evidence replaces it. The prompt is kept under 640 bytes so tiny compactors still fit a leaf (an existing 2k-context test enforces this). Changing the prompt changes summary identity, so existing chat summaries are rebuilt once.
2. **Marked findings survive any number of folds.** The local system prompt asks the agent to write `Finding:` / `Decision:` lines (`Diagnosis:`, `Root cause:` and `Plan:` also count, after list or emphasis markup). The lens collects those lines from the replies and from the reasoning, which is never transcript, of the steps a node covers. Each node carries them verbatim under its summary (newest first, within 1.6 KB), and the deterministic digest fallback carries them too. The compactor also sees marked reasoning.
3. **Working-notes nudge.** The context note (80% or first fold), the step-cap note and the deadline note now say to record key findings and the current plan in the working notes, `control_turn_handoff` `payload.findings` and `payload.next`. An omitted payload keeps the older notes. The no-handoff context note asks for `Finding:` lines.
4. **Recall of compacted in-turn steps through `control_history_read`.**
   - Each step that leaves the verbatim window becomes a leaf `Node` of the conversation's summary tree. It uses the same struct, checksum and shape checks as chat nodes, and its source is the original step (up to 96 KiB).
   - Each folded block becomes a node over its two retained children, or over one original per step when it was summarized directly.
   - Files live at `summaries/turns/ATTEMPT/` (content-addressed). Only the roots of each attempt's cut are registered, in memory, for the 8 most recent local attempts. Evicted attempts' files are deleted, and files a restart left unregistered are deleted after an hour.
   - `control_history_read`'s listing gains `turns`, and those roots read like chat roots (`path`, `source`, `offset`).
   - The new `query` field works like pi's `session_history`. All terms must match, and it searches newest attempt and steps first, in summaries and original steps. It returns at most 8 verbatim excerpts of about 600 bytes, each with `root`/`path`/step/`offset`. It reads at most 256 nodes within `limit_bytes`. It makes no model calls and uses the same authorization and bounds.
   - `/chat/ID/compaction` status lists them as `turn_trees`, which is the data the MemoryTree page renders.
   - A failed write records a `local-recall` activity and never fails the turn.

## Tests (mock endpoint / mock compactor)

- `local_agent::tests::a_diagnosis_survives_many_in_turn_compactions` replays the run -140 shape. The finding comes from a reply and the decision from reasoning. The run has at least 3 compactions with a compactor whose summaries never mention either line, and both are still in the last request.
- `local_agent::context::tests::a_marked_finding_survives_every_fold_even_when_summaries_drop_it` covers at least 9 folds on a growing turn. The finding and decision appear under the first node in every view. Every retained node has a valid tree shape, parents are built over their children, and each step is retained once.
- `local_agent::context::tests::the_digest_fallback_keeps_marked_findings`
- `local_agent::context::tests::marked_lines_are_found_through_list_and_emphasis_markup`
- `worker_tools::nudges::tests::*` and `local_agent::tests::a_long_turn_compacts_before_its_context_is_exhausted_and_is_told_once`: the note text includes the working-notes instruction.
- `compaction::turn::tests::compacted_steps_join_the_tree_and_recall_returns_their_verbatim_excerpts` calls the agent's `control_history_read` end to end: listing, a `query` hit on a compacted step's verbatim text, reading on from the hit's root/path/offset, and refusals.
- `compaction::turn::tests::only_recent_attempts_stay_recallable` and `every_tree_node_uses_one_structured_summary_format`

## Local checks (all pass)

All runs used scratch `CONTROL_STATE_DIR`/`CONTROL_CONFIG_DIR` and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/summary-findings`.

- `cargo test --locked --workspace` passes (922 in the binary, plus crates).
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib --bin control` and its Clippy check
- Web, in a temporary sibling worktree that has since been removed: `cargo test --locked --manifest-path web/Cargo.toml`, web Clippy and `trunk build --release --locked`
- `cargo build --release --locked --bins`

There was no live-model run; the effect on a real Qwen compactor still has to be measured.

## Rebase notes for #277 (MemoryTree)

- The change in `recall.rs` is small: a `query` field on `Read`, `load` becomes `pub(super)`, and a `Next` dispatch in `Tools::call`. The turn logic lives in the new `src/compaction/turn.rs`.
- Turn-root reads build their own `Plan` on purpose. After #277 adds `Plan.edits`, compilation fails there, and it must be `Edits::default()`. A chat's operator edits index conversation positions, but a turn tree's positions are steps.
- `query` searches local turns only, so it never bypasses #277's drop redaction of chat sources. Extending it to chat sources should apply `edits.source_text`.
- `status()` gains one `turn_trees` line, away from #277's hunk.
- `compaction::build` is unchanged. The child-merge wording lives in `SYSTEM`.

body:
Second step of the owner's Lucene/OpenNLP convergence (2026-11-17), after #3213. Owner's choice for OpenNLP's logging
dependency: **relocate the SLF4J API into a concealed package**, nothing else in OpenNLP changes.

## What is added to `src/jdk.m3.search/providers/classes`

| Library | Sources | Resources | Packages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lucene analysis-common 9.10.0 | 514 | 40 word lists, 2 stemmer tables, 1 DTD | upstream (`org.apache.lucene.analysis.*`) |
| Snowball stemmers (part of analysis-common) | 38 | - | `org.tartarus.snowball`, `.ext` |
| Lucene analysis-opennlp (fork `hsoliwal/lucene` `d1b7235f`, unchanged) | 20 | - | `org.apache.lucene.analysis.opennlp`, `.tools` |
| Apache OpenNLP Tools 2.4.0 | 729 | version file, affix list, 2 feature descriptors, GIS note | upstream (`opennlp.tools.*`) |
| SLF4J API 2.0.12 | 46 | - | relocated: `jdk.internal.search.slf4j` (concealed) |

The relocated package has no `m3` segment on purpose: the M3 naming gate judges M3 namespaces, and SLF4J is third-party
code. OpenNLP's `org.slf4j` imports follow the relocation (the provider pipeline's package rename); an application's own
SLF4J is never shadowed, even with the module added.

OpenNLP's 70 packages and the relocated SLF4J's provider-lookup `uses` (213 exports, 9 uses, 8 provides); `Java.gmk`
disables deprecation lint for the module (its descriptor provides factories Lucene deprecates but still registers, and
the build's descriptor merge `GenModuleInfoSource` refuses an annotation on the module declaration) and copies the new
resource types; legal: `lucene.md` (both NOTICEs), `opennlp.md`, `slf4j.md`; 33 Lucene files of #3213 lose a
now-redundant `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")`.

## Proof (stock JDK 21; provider pipeline and single-module proof of the Guava inline)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Provider pipeline per provider (reference compile, fix rounds with the JDK flags, final `-Werror` module compile) | Lucene x6: PASS; Snowball: PASS; OpenNLP: PASS (doclint: one `{@code}` in a link label unwrapped, one `<ul>` closed); SLF4J: PASS (doclint: empty paragraphs, a `Deque<String>` escaped) |

| Runtime, exploded module + COPY resources and a jlinked image (`--do-not-resolve-by-default`) | Lucene99 codec, IDVersion postings; French stop words from the resource (154); 15 tokenizers, 114 filters, `openNlp` tokenizer and `openNlpChunker` filter registered; Snowball "Running strings converged" -> `run string converg`; OpenNLP version 2.4.0 from its resource, `SimpleTokenizer` tokens; SLF4J prints its usual no-provider warning, as upstream |

author: everton-dgn
body:
Related to #2387, which fixes the same thing for `pnpx`.

For `npx --package=pnpm pnpm exec tsx ./main.ts`, Knip didn't see `tsx`. The resolver always drops the first input forwarded from the command, assuming it's the package's own binary, but here that first input is `tsx`. It's now only dropped when it matches the package's binary and runs from the same directory, so the inner `yarn` in `npx yarn --cwd tools run yarn --version` is kept too.

author: yuvaldim
body:
Closes #1281.

## Problem

A capability that deliberately declines with exit 3 (the manifest contract's `capability-unavailable`) blocked a batch as `gate-inconclusive:<cap>` for good when it ran as a member gate. `cap run` turned exit 3 into `task-failed`, or into `automation-broken` when it finished under `min_duration_ms`. Both route to the block path, and `sched resume --batch` re-ran the gate, which declined again. This was seen in a downstream monorepo whose `test.focused` declines when a change needs full verification.

## Changes, one per ask

1. **`cap run` maps exit 3 to `capability-unavailable`** (`cli/src/capability.ts`). It keeps `exit_code: 3` in the envelope and checks it before the `min_duration_ms` floor, so a fast decline is never reclassified. An undeclared or shadow id is still `capability-unavailable` with `exit_code: null`; that null-vs-number difference is how consumers tell the two apart.
2. **Member gate: a decline skips that gate, and the batch gate covers the member.** This is the conservative reading of the issue. `CapabilityGateResult` gains `exitCode`. In `evaluateIncrementalGate`, a `capability-unavailable` with a numeric exit code journals `gate-skipped-declined:<cap>` with the capability's output, records `capability-unavailable` on `member_gates` and writes the gate log. It never reports `gate-inconclusive`. `resumeBlockedGate` dissolves a block when the recheck declines, the same way #681 handles a timeout, so batches already blocked by the old classification can be resumed. Undeclared ids keep #625's `gate-skipped:<cap>`.
   - Aggregate gate: a `gate.batch` or `test.full` that declines now blocks `suite-unreadable` with the decline as its detail. Before, it would have fallen through to `dispatch.suite_command` or a detected runner. This matches how exit 3 already ended there (task-failed with no report), so the batch does not run a suite the repo just said it cannot vouch for.
   - `worktree.prepare` exiting 3 now falls through to the generic warm-up instead of failing batch setup.
3. **Member gates get `DOSSIER_BATCH_ID` and `DOSSIER_BATCH_INTEGRATION_REF`.** The new `CapabilityGateContext` is passed as an optional third argument to `runCapability`, and the CLI exports it as env. The ref is the batch's local integration branch, which member worktrees fork from, so `git merge-base "$DOSSIER_BATCH_INTEGRATION_REF" HEAD` gives the member's fork point and the diff excludes siblings that already landed. The ref is **not** set in two cases:
   - On a `sched resume --batch` recheck, because the live gate lands the member before blocking, so the diff would be empty and a scoped script would pass trivially.
   - When the gate runs in the shared batch worktree (pre-#677 batches), for the same reason.

   Inherited `DOSSIER_BATCH_INTEGRATION_REF` / `DOSSIER_BATCH_BASE` values are dropped from member-gate envs.

Versions: `@ai-dossier/sched` 0.71.0, `@ai-dossier/cli` 0.94.0, with cli depending on `^0.71.0`. Docs are updated in `docs/reference/capabilities.md` and `packages/sched/README.md`, with a new trap row and a CHANGELOG entry.

## Tests

The new regression tests fail against `origin/main` sources: 7 in the cli, 2 in sched. The #625 slug test is a guard and passes on both.
- `cap.test.ts`: exit 3 becomes `capability-unavailable` with `exit_code: 3`, and a fast exit 3 under `min_duration_ms: 60000` is still not `automation-broken`.
- `batch-capability-runner.test.ts`: `exitCode` passes through; batch env is set when a context is given and absent without one; inherited refs don't leak.
- `batch-suite-runner.test.ts`: a declining `gate.batch` or `test.full` is terminal-unreadable and no lower tier runs. The #793 fixture was corrected to `exit_code: null`, which is what `cap run` actually emits for an id it cannot see.
- `batch-integration.test.ts` (real git and spawned agents):
  - a fast exit-3 member gate gives `gate-skipped-declined`, never `gate-inconclusive`, and both gates receive `{batchId, integrationRef: batch.branch}`;
  - an undeclared id keeps `gate-skipped`;
  - a batch blocked by the old floor classification is dissolved by a declining `resume --batch`, and the recheck context has no ref.

Gates: `make lint` is clean, `make build-all` passes, and `make test` passes across all workspaces. An independent review agent found nothing blocking. I applied its should-fixes: the tier table layout in the docs, and no integration ref on the shared-worktree fallback. I also applied its env-leak and documentation nits.

author: arozumenko
body:
Closes #667

Echo asks for models by Claude's names: `haiku` for live notes and Needs you now, `sonnet` for minutes, thread sync and prep, and whatever a routine picks. A gateway, a company's Claude Code wrapper or a local server may name its models otherwise. Then jobs on that profile fail, or run on a model nobody chose. The user put it this way: wrappers "may have different names and fuck us up".

**What it does**
- `Profile.models` (`ai::Models`): an optional model for each of `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`. `Profile::model(name)` returns the one set, else the name as it is. Any other model name (a full id, a routine's "Other…") passes unchanged.
- **Applied where a model reaches the provider:**
  - `claude_session::complete_claude_with`: every one-shot job, Needs you now included;
  - `livenotes::complete_local_body`;
  - the live-notes agent's `--model`;
  - minutes, thread sync, routine and Yolo runs;
  - the local terminal session.
  - A `local` profile's `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL` / `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` use each name's own model when set; otherwise its minutes model, as before.
- **Set only by the user:** Settings → AI & minutes, where each row says what its names run and has "Models…" with three fields. Or `echoctl ai set <id> --model sonnet=<model>` (repeatable; empty clears).
  - Every name is checked before any is written. A model is one word, doesn't start with "-", and isn't itself one of the three names.
  - Never on the built-in profile, which is the user's own Claude Code setup.
  - Never inside a run Echo started; `--notes-model` is now refused there too.
- **On claude and wrapper profiles** only what Echo asks for is mapped. Claude Code's own background requests and the folder and call sessions keep Claude's names, because their routing variables stay the user's (R6/R12).
- **A plugin's wrapper offer can't name the mapping.** echo-plugins R24 allows only a name and a command; that would need its own `Rules:` PR.

**Weighed against**
- A model dropdown per job: 10+ dropdowns, each repeating names that differ per profile.
- Setting `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` for claude and wrapper profiles too: those are routing variables, and those profiles run on the user's own setup (claude-code-runs R6/R12). Mapping `--model` in Echo covers what Echo asks for without touching their environment.

**Tests**
- Unit:
  - `a_local_profile_runs_its_own_model_for_each_of_claudes_names` (routing env, `Profile::model`);
  - `a_profile_maps_claudes_names_all_checked_first_never_on_system_or_in_a_run` (the setter: case, clearing, all-or-nothing, refusals);
  - `a_routine_and_a_yolo_task_run_as_the_folder_session_does` (a routine asking `opus` runs and logs the mapped model).
- Functional: settings/TC-034 (new), all 7 steps run on the rebuilt binary with the virtual model.
  - The row's states and the CLI refusals.
  - A thread sync asking for `sonnet` sent all 5 of its requests as `virtual-sonnet`, and the run finished.
  - A bad name keeps the fields open with a notice and saves nothing; a good one saves and closes.
- Gates: clippy clean; `cargo test` 805 + 1 passed; `scripts/check-mod.sh` exit 0.

author: dhanushkummari
body:
Notebook 07 now lists the complete BR-Gen archive: 13 volumes, 180,003 files, 68.6 GB, read in 21.5 s for 0.015 CU. But it paired **0** images with masks, because the code expected the README layout (`Au/`, `Tp/`, `Gt/`, `<stem>_mask.png`). This PR fixes the parser.

## The released layout
I read this from `brgen_listing.json` and `brgen_members.txt.gz`, file names only; no image was read.

| Path | Count |
|---|---|
| `BR-Gen/Forged/<Method>/<Region>/<Source>/<stem>_<region>.png` | 5 methods (BrushNet, LaMa, MAT, PowerPaint, SDXL) × 2 regions (Background, Stuff) × 3 sources (COCO, ImageNet, Places) × **5,000** = 150,000 |
| `BR-Gen/Mask/<Region>/<Source>/<stem>_<region>.png` | 30,000. Each mask is **shared by the five methods**; every forged file has one (0 missing). |
| `BR-Gen/RealImage/<Source>/<Source>_image_list.txt` | 3 lists. **No real image is in the archive.** |

The same 15,000 source images (5,000 per source) appear in both regions.

## Changes
- **`data/brgen.py`**
  - **Parsing:** `parse_member` reads the method, region, source and name from a path.
  - **Helpers:** `kind`, `method_of`, `stratum_key` and the pairing key now use those fields. Strata are method/region/source; the pairing key is region/source/name. The README layout is still recognised as a fallback.
  - **Pairing:** `pair_masks` pairs every image that shares a mask. A key counts as ambiguous only when it has more than one mask.
  - **Summary:** `summarize` adds the layout, strata, mask strata, source-image counts and the real-image lists.
  - **Fakes:** `released_paths` and `fake_listing(layout="released")` provide a small archive for tests and dry runs.
- **Notebook 07**
  - The dry-run archive uses the released layout.
  - On the released layout, the listing asserts that the number of pairs equals the number of forged images.
  - The subset step no longer needs `STRATUM_DEPTH`.
  - The sample check records a size mismatch instead of crashing.
- **`docs/TESTING.md`:** a new entry.

## Checks run in the sandbox (on `91a3ab6`)
- `ruff check src tests` and `ruff format --check src tests`: clean.
- `python -m pytest -p no:warnings`: **413 passed**.
  - New test on the released layout: parsing, pairing (60 of 60), 30 strata, per-source counts, the real-image lists, and a subset with one image per stratum.
  - The README-layout tests still pass.
- `python -m eviground.utils.repo_audit --history`: ok.
- `EVIGROUND_DRY_RUN=1 pytest --nbmake notebooks/07_cp4_prep.ipynb`: passed, including the pairs = forged assertion.

## Not run here
- The real listing with the fixed parser. Dhanush reruns notebook 07 on a CPU runtime. The volumes are already on Drive, so it takes about 1 min and costs under 0.02 CU. It is expected to report 150,000 pairs.

author: deep1012
body:
Staff can create inactive invite-only accounts and email single-use onboarding links. The follow-up closes account-takeover paths where an old invite survived an administrative account edit, or an invitation/email edit bypassed the existing credential-reset permission ceiling.

Behavior:
- Initial invited accounts stay within the creator's permission and branch ceiling. A private initial-invite path is reachable only after the service creates a new account.
- Send/resend for an existing account requires strictly higher access, except for the owner. A peer administrator cannot use reactivation as a password reset. Revocation remains within the ordinary management ceiling.
- Acceptance requires the account to remain inactive. Token issuance checks the intended inactive email while holding the user lock; acceptance and account edits follow user-to-token lock order.
- Administrative email/password/status changes revoke outstanding invite and reset links inside the same transaction. Peer login-email changes use the strict credential-reset ceiling, comparing the current email under lock. Harmless unchanged-email edits and existing self-email behavior are preserved.
- Invite and password-reset purposes remain separate. Acceptance records activation in the audit log. Links require configured SMTP and PUBLIC_URL; tests use mocked mail, never real recipients.

TDD and validation:
- RED: original follow-up regressions produced 7 failures; the peer-invite bypass regression also failed; #250 peer-email/stale-snapshot regressions produced 2 failures before fixes.
- GREEN: 3 targeted unit suites / 79 tests passed.
- GREEN: staff-invite and password-reset database suites / 26 tests passed on disposable PostgreSQL 16 with all 69 migrations. Includes stale-recipient issuance, old-link rejection after account edits, equal-peer denial, equal-role initial onboarding, and deterministic acceptance/admin-edit locking. The #250 API regression verifies rejected email takeover cannot trigger a reset email to the controlled address.
- Backend TypeScript passes. Targeted non-fixing ESLint: 0 errors, 54 test-type warnings. Whitespace checks pass.
- No new migrations, dependencies, lockfiles or workflows. The auth-token migration from merged #244 is already on staging. Existing large locale dictionaries receive only the original invite strings; new/changed code files remain below 800 lines.

Codex takeover uses an isolated codex/223-invite-token-hardening worktree. The original Claude local worktree is untouched. Full independent security review and structural audit are recorded against the final head in PR comments before ready/CI/merge.

Closes #223
Closes #250

author: tian-tom
body:
架构设计第 8.2 节第 7 项的提示词部分：现有六份提示词从头重写，按速览、精读分目录放。重点章节的结构和校验在 #84，问答的分块顺序在 #87，这个 PR 只改提示词的内容、目录和随之变的输出结构。

## `prompts/` 的约定

画面解释的提示词照这个加。

- 按模式分目录：`skim/` 是速览的（`chapters.md` 章节和金句、`verdict.md` 一句话结论和重点章节），`study/` 是精读的（`translation.md`、`explain.md`、`note-polish.md`），`common/` 是两种模式共用的（`qa.md`）。画面解释属于精读，放 `study/frame-explain.md`。
- 每份开头写用途、输入、输出和常见的坏输出。下面是 `## 系统提示词` 和 `## 用户提示词` 两个代码块；代码块里不要有以 `## ` 开头的行，取小节时会被当成下一节。
- 系统提示词不含变量，同一个功能每次逐字节一致，前缀缓存才能命中。用户提示词里先放不变的（视频信息），再放每次都变的。要分块发、打缓存标记的，像问答那样拆成几个 `## 用户消息：…` 小节，由服务拼成部件。
- 时间一律让模型照抄字幕行开头的 `分:秒`，秒数由本机换算，不让模型做算术。
- 字幕、标题、简介、选中的文字都写明是视频内容，里面的要求不是指令。
- 新文件加进 `src/background/prompts.ts`、`src/background/ai.ts` 的功能表，以及 `tests/unit/core/ai/prompt.test.ts`、`tests/build-output.test.ts` 的清单。

## 每份改了什么

- **章节和金句**（原 `analysis.md`）：写给还没决定看不看的人，标题要说出具体内容，摘要写观点、数据、步骤或例子；金句每段 0 到 4 句，宁少勿滥。输出改成 `start`（照抄的时间）加 `title`、`summary`，金句是 `start` 加 `quote`，去掉了 `timestamp` 和 `timestampSeconds` 两个字段。原来要模型自己把 `分:秒` 换算成秒，一小时以上的视频常算错；现在本机换算（`core/ai/validate.ts` 的 `chunkFromModel`），旧写法的 `timestamp`、`timestampSeconds` 照样认。用户消息先放视频信息，再放这一段的范围和字幕，各段共用的前缀更长。代码里的分段说明和上一段末尾的说法跟着改。
- **一句话结论**：先写理由再下判断，理由要落到具体章节；判断时把时长算进去，不按是否认同观点判断；标题许诺的内容没兑现算可以跳过。四档的名字没变。重点章节的说法从 #84 的一行补丁写成完整的规则。
- **问答**：说明摘录只是相关的几段，找不到时说「给到的字幕里没有讲到」，不断言整个视频没讲，同时说说这几段讲了什么；出处只写单个时间点。
- **翻译**：说明译文和原文并排读、字幕常从半句断开；中英两套规则重写。
- **划词解释**：选中外语时先给中文意思；同音错字先给正确写法；不编视频里的具体情节和数字。
- **笔记润色**：从当前那一行所在的完整意思起止，原话是什么语言就用什么语言写。

## 输出结构和测试

- `ANALYSIS_CHUNK` 换成上面的字段；`VERDICT` 的字段顺序改成 `summary`、`value`、`reason`、`verdict`、`keyChapters`。逐字节测试跟着改；「示例输出符合 schema」改成直接从提示词里取示例。
- 新增 `chunkFromModel` 的测试；`startSecondsOf` 挪到 `core/transcript/segment.ts`，和 `formatTimestamp` 放在一起。
- 原来的「来自 Digest for Bilibili 的提示词保留署名」测试换成「每份按模式放在三个目录之一、后台内联的就是这几份」。
- 端到端的模拟服务按新的提示词认请求，章节和金句用 `start` 回。
- 架构设计第 5.3 节写明 `prompts/` 的约定。

黄金样本：没有改动。分块校验 `validateAnalysis` 本身没变，新写法在它之前换算。

数据说明和同意版本不用动：发给模型的还是标题、作者、简介、时长、字幕、章节和金句、选中的文字和问题，类别、用途、接收方和发送时机都没变，只是措辞和顺序变了。

提示词的版本是全文的指纹，所以这次以后，已经存下的概览、问答不受影响，只是新任务和旧任务不再算等价。

效果没有在真实模型上比过，要开发者本人用自己的密钥在真实视频上对比。

验证：`npm run check`、`npm run test:pages`、`npm run test:e2e` 本机通过。

La page dit que l'auto-évaluation gratuite donne une première lecture, pas le palier : elle utilise une autre échelle. **Ailleurs** : accueil (l'offre, sa méthode, son logiciel), menu et pied de page Produits, hub Produits (« Voir l'offre »), Approche & Méthode (étape 2), rapport gratuit, page Workbench, registre des actifs. **Contrôles** : `check-diagnostic-entry` vérifie désormais l'offre unique (nom, prix, durée, paliers, limites, redirections) au lieu d'exiger trois offres et l'absence de prix. `check-portfolio`, `check-commercial-browser`, `check-workbench-*` et `check-asset-registry` suivent la nouvelle route. Contrôles locaux au vert : build, check:links (143 pages), check:assets (+ unit), check:process-roles, check-pathway et les 18 scripts navigateur et de contenu des workflows. Pas de débordement à 375 px sur la page de l'offre. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01CwwQST4CG6GiocpbB1JAhc)_ --- ## Summary by cubic Replaces the three diagnostic offers with a single one — Leap Readiness (EUR 5,000, one week, one scope) — and reorganizes the header navigation around four visitor-journey sections. The three diagnostic pages now redirect to the offer page. **Offer** - `/portfolio/diagnostic/` and `/diagnostic-execution/` (FR and EN) redirect to the offer page. - The offer page states price, duration, scope, the six maturity tiers, the week, the three follow-up engagements and the limits — no commercial conditions — and says the free self-assessment uses its own scale, not the tiers. author: mihilbabin
body:
Ticket: https://upperhand.atlassian.net/browse/UHET-1206

`PaysafeApiClient#process_request` built `Net::HTTP` without timeouts, so Ruby's 60 s defaults applied. That's longer than the app's 29 s `Rack::Timeout`, so a slow Paysafe call held a Puma thread until Rack killed the request with a 500. Last night's dbat peak had 25 such requests on Paysafe/Stripe paths (`payment_methods`, `customers/:id`, `clients/:id/payment`).

**Changes**
- `PaysafeApiClient.open_timeout` (default 5 s) and `.read_timeout` (default 20 s), applied to every request.
- `Net::OpenTimeout` / `Net::ReadTimeout` raise `Paysafe::APIError` with http_code 504 and a Paysafe-shaped body, `{error: {code: "504", message: ...}}`. Callers such as the refund, auth and reversal handlers do `Integer(e.message.dig(:error, :code))`, so an empty body would make them raise `TypeError`. The app already rescues `APIError` → 502 with the "payment provider unavailable" message.

**Read timeout choice:** 20 s, not "a few seconds". A read timeout on an auth/refund POST can leave Paysafe having processed a request we never recorded. That risk exists today when `Rack::Timeout` kills the request at 29 s, so 20 s is no worse, and it still frees the thread before Rack does. We can lower it for GETs later if needed.

**Testing:** smoke test stubbing `Net::HTTP#request` to raise each timeout → `Paysafe::APIError`, `http_code` 504, with timeouts 5/20 set on the connection.

The api_core_rails PR that picks this up follows.

길동무 수가 **장소 방문 때** 보이도록 문구와 규칙을 고쳤습니다.
- 홈 한마디(game_flow 4-2행): 길동무 수와 "빈 칸 N곳" 숫자를 빼고 "오늘 이 조건으로 비어 있는 칸이 있어요! 오늘 페이지에서 같이 볼래요?"로 바꿈

body:
## Why
Post-verify for business date D runs at D+1 14:20 TW (R33 B#1 `postclose-research-dispatch`), after the next session opened. `resolveEveningChainRunAuthority().allowed` is therefore always false, and since 10/07 every live-only post-verify task has been skipped. Wei chose plan B on 11/16; target release is 11/18 (Wed).

## What
- **`eveningChainRunAuthority.ts`** adds `liveEffectsAllowed`/`liveEffectsReason`.
  - It is true only for `post_verify_chain` with `next_executable_session_opened_use_snapshot_only_repair`, when both the stage `queued_at` and now fall in [next session 13:30 TW, following official session 09:00 TW).
  - The following session comes from the official calendar only; a FinLab gap cannot stretch the window.
  - `allowed` is unchanged.
- **`postMarketChain.ts`**: `POST_CLOSE_LIVE_EFFECT_TASKS` run on `liveEffectsAllowed`. These are paper-intraday-cache-clear, linucb-reward-ledger, daily-report, paper-active-postmarket and meta-learning-shadow. The other live tasks stay gated by `allowed`: adapt, ga-shadow-daily, obsidian-sync, artifact-auto-promotion, and the strategy-learning policy (evidence_only).
- **`postVerifyTaskCheckpoint.ts`** adds `independentEffect`:
  - An unknown remote outcome settles as a never-rerun ERROR instead of an UNCERTAIN receipt that blocks the date.
  - An expired-lease RUNNING claim of such a task closes as an optional ERROR (`critical:false`), and the same task replays it without rerunning the producer.
  - `scripts/postVerifyReceiptReconcile.ts` matches this.
- **`dailyReport.ts`** takes the report date (`ctx.runDate`):
  - The `market_risk` fallback is bounded by `date<=D`.
  - The US signal falls back to `us_market_signals` (date UNIQUE) when the 24h KV copy has expired.

Native identity: none of these files are in `release_admission.native_identity_inputs`, so a normal Worker CD is enough.

## Verification
- `tsc` passes on `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- `postVerifyTaskCheckpoint` 66/66, and all 25 related test files pass.
- Covered cases:
  - Window edges: 13:30 is included, D+2 09:00 is excluded.
  - Holiday-extended window; a FinLab-gap date gets no window.
  - Old-date replay and screener_v2 get no window.
  - A chain with 5xx from released tasks still reaches strategy-learning, with 0 uncertain receipts.
  - A hung daily-report followed by a lease takeover makes the chain succeed, and the report is not resent.
- Counter-checks: with the reclaim clause or the `critical:false` close removed, the new tests fail.
- Three rounds of independent review. Remaining Low: after a version change, an expired claim of these five tasks may rerun once under the new identity.
- Post-deploy read-only verifier: `output/herdr-handoff-20261018/sys-cleanup-20261028/live_auth_b_verify.sh 2026-11-17`, run after the 11/18 14:20 post-verify.

body:
> 🤖 Opened by UMCEKO's AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5), not by UMCEKO personally.

Launcher split, **B5 native**, game side: item 4 of A1's "What B5 must do" (#1474) for `internals_sync` and `registry_lock`. **Stacked on #2102** (`native-check`).

## What

The launcher does two jobs for mod authors with the native build's code linked in:
- `native-build --sync-internals` and `--catalog` discover which game internals a mod names. `cargo sunrise-mod internals sync` and `internals add` run these.
- `native-lock` pins a mod's registry dependencies.

Once the launcher spawns the SDK's tool instead, it hands the tool the toolchain it manages, as it does for `native-build`:

```sh
cargo sunrise-mod native-discover < plan.json   # {"internals": [...]}, or with "catalog": {"catalog": dir}
cargo sunrise-mod native-lock < plan.json       # {"lock": path}
```

- **Plans:** `{contract: 2, work, toolchain, mods}`, plus `catalog` for discovery or `update` for the lock.
- **Exit codes:** 0 reply, 1 error reply, 2 no plan, 3 another contract.
- **Error reply:** one line, `{"contract": 2, "error": {"kind", "message"}}`. The kinds are `source` (the pinned game's source couldn't be had), `discover` and `lock`.

## One implementation

- Discovery moves whole from `launcher/src/native_mods/internals_sync.rs` (495 lines) into `sunrise-native-build::discover`, with its seven tests and their fixtures:
  - staging the pinned game's source with the mod's `[[native.module]]` rows;
  - the check with `deprecated` forced on the mod alone;
  - mapping the diagnostics to catalog entries.
- It takes the toolchain as an argument. `cargo-sunrise-mod` runs itself as Cargo's rustc wrapper for the check, as the launcher did.
- The launcher keeps what's its own: consent, its native cache lease and its managed Rust. It calls `discover` until it spawns the tool (B5 native, launcher side).
- The lease is now held across the copy into `--catalog-output`, so `DiscoveryCatalog` and its snapshot test go. They existed only to copy after the lease.
- Mod authors still run `cargo sunrise-mod internals sync` and `sunrise-launcher native-lock`. The launcher still manages their Rust, so the docs and the template don't change.

## Tests

- The seven discovery tests pass in their new home: `cargo test -p sunrise-native-build --lib` (94 passed).
- `discover_and_lock_name_their_step_when_the_folder_is_no_native_mod` covers the error replies.
- `cargo clippy -p cargo-sunrise-mod -p sunrise-native-build --all-targets -D warnings` passes.
- `launcher/`: `cargo test --locked --lib native_mods` (55 passed), including the consent test now on `catalog`.
- Not run: a real discovery against a pinned game's source. It needs that source and the SDK's Rust, and the moved code is unchanged apart from taking the toolchain and the host's `mark_used`.

ONE fresh parallel Standards/Spec round, original reports retained, no rereview. Fresh independent result verifier as below.

# Standards

Проверен полный закреплённый diff `b1ecdc8064c27271bdd630079b4a20f7c76aa1c0..c08acef3e587666ece214a29daea72f053fa1b8d`. В нём один файл, `apps/web/test/module/mutation-operation.test.ts`, коммит `c08acef3e`. Рабочая ветка не использовалась как источник проверяемого содержимого.

Нарушений документированных правил: **0**. Замечаний по эвристикам Fowler: **0**.

Прочитаны корневые и Web `AGENTS.md`, оба `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `docs/agents/testing.md`, `implementation.md`, `human-review.md`, `issue-tracker.md` и ADR 0038. Проверены реальные factory, браузерный decoder, обработчик, session adapter, Logto SDK boundary, конфигурация, вспомогательные модули и настройки Vitest на закреплённом head.

Подмена собственного модуля сессии удалена. `sessionRead` наблюдает за настоящим `sessionAdapter.accessToken` и не меняет его реализацию. `realBffSession` создаёт настоящую зашифрованную cookie и область запроса Next.js. Отсутствующая cookie проходит реальную проверку сессии, а недоступность identity воспроизводится на внешнем HTTP-порту с отдельной проверкой origin и метода запроса. Время фиксируется до создания cookie, затем восстанавливается; Vitest восстанавливает spies, окружение и глобальные подмены между тестами.

Синтетическая `renameOperation` настраивает объявленный callback `execute` настоящих factory и handler. Это разрешено разделом Substitutes для общего транспортного контракта; продуктовая операция не заменяется.

Каждый именованный сбой доставки допускает только точный POST URL, вызывает настоящий обработчик и потребляет его JSON. Независимые assertions после `send` проверяют исходные 200, полный корректный payload и `bodyUsed`, поэтому браузерный `catch` не скрывает отказ этих проверок. Парный нормальный путь сохранён. Случаи ограничены синтетическими ошибками доставки и не доказывают повреждение настоящей сети. Сохранён существующий mock `next/cache` на границе фреймворка.

Проверки лимитов тела, схемы, Origin до чтения сессии, остановки потока и сброса кеша остаются. Новых правил продукта, публичных контрактов или пользовательского поведения diff не вводит. Это статический Standards review; команды тестов повторно не запускались.


# Spec review, mutation-operation

Проверен полный закреплённый diff `b1ecdc8064c27271bdd630079b4a20f7c76aa1c0..c08acef3e587666ece214a29daea72f053fa1b8d`, один коммит `c08acef3e`, единственный файл `apps/web/test/module/mutation-operation.test.ts`. Источники: `source-2292-current.json`, `source-2244-current.json`, `browser-boundary-decision.md`, `issue-wire-boundary.md` ([публичная запись решения](https://github.com/sachkov-inside/platform/issues/2292#issuecomment-6937746149)), закреплённые `AGENTS.md`, `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/testing.md`, `docs/agents/human-review.md`, исходный тест на базе. Прочитаны настоящие factory, handler, session adapter, чтение токена через Logto SDK, session/runtime fixtures, маршрутизатор и настройки Vitest.

## Находки

0. Потерь требований, неверной реализации и расширения продуктового объёма не найдено.

Удалена единственная подмена собственного модуля. Настоящие конфигурация, SDK и зашифрованная cookie исполняются через `realBffSession`; `spyOn(sessionAdapter, "accessToken")` сохраняет реализацию и проверку отказа до чтения сессии. Отсутствующая cookie и недоступность identity проверяются через настоящую цепочку. Сохранены прежние Origin, размеры тела и потока, JSON/schema, RangeError, приватные заголовки и сброс каталога при успехе и ошибке. Все прежние 15 воздействий сохранены: один тест с тремя транспортными сбоями разделён на три, поэтому число случаев выросло с 13 до 15. Ожидания остаются независимыми литералами.

Граница A соблюдена. Каждый именованный fault ограничен точным POST/URL, вызывает настоящий обработчик, потребляет его тело и сохраняет receipt. После browser-вызова, вне его перехвата ошибок, проверяются 200, полный литеральный payload, `bodyUsed` и единственный вызов `execute`. Меняются только доставленные данные либо доставка отклоняется. Парный обычный успех проходит ту же цепочку. Неожиданный запрос оставляет неверный receipt и проваливает тест. Искусственный fault не заявлен доказательством физического повреждения сети.

Синтетические operation и обязательный `execute` являются разрешённым общим транспортным контрактом. Этот файл не заменяет бизнесоперацию и не доказывает backend mapping или отдельный malformed-backend→BFF503 сценарий.

## Последствия и доказательства

Продуктовый код, UI, права, деньги и публичные контракты не меняются. Согласованного сценария живого интерфейса нет; оснований требовать новую бизнес-приёмку или security review по этому diff не найдено. Проверка приложения не требуется по правилу внутренних изменений, а не по общему исключению для браузерных тестов.

15 focused tests и статические проверки заявлены исполнителем. Сам их не запускал. Независимый verifier ещё ожидается: требование A о RED со сломанным browser decoder и GREEN после восстановления нельзя считать выполненным этим review. Это оставшееся техническое доказательство для доставки, не вопрос владельцу.

**PASS** для `c08acef3e587666ece214a29daea72f053fa1b8d`. На точном содержимом коммита прошли 15 тестов. Независимые поломки настоящей конфигурации и браузерного декодера вызвали ожидаемые падения. body:
## What changed
On the hosted site, a chosen transcript PDF can now be read. One small server function sends the PDF once to Google Gemini's paid service and returns the course rows it read. The browser then checks every row with the same code as before, so nothing counts unless it passes those checks.

- Nothing is stored, and nothing of the PDF or its rows is written to any log.
- The Gemini key stays in Netlify. It is not in the repository, the built site or any browser request.
- While a PDF is being read, the page says "Reading your transcript…".
- The privacy sentence is now yours of 2026-11-17: "Google reads your PDF and may keep it briefly. Your result stays in this browser."
- On localhost nothing changes: only the two made-up transcripts work, and nothing is sent anywhere.

It is checked on your private preview with the real Gemini: both made-up transcripts were read exactly as prepared, three times each.

## Why
Feature F21, the first of M2 (brief §7): "The only server piece. One function that sends the PDF to paid Google Gemini and returns the course rows."

## How to check it yourself
1. Log in to Netlify, then open the preview link that Netlify posts on this pull request.
2. Click **See what I have left**. If an earlier result is shown, click **Use another transcript** first.
3. Click **Browse files** and pick `synthetic/transcripts/sample-a.pdf`.
4. You should see "Reading your transcript…" for a few seconds, then the page "Check what was read" with 17 rows.
5. Click **Continue**. You should see 81 credits left.

## Tests and evidence
- Sprint contract and QA rounds: `docs/sprints/F21.md` — evaluator verdict PASS, scores 5/5/5/5 (Functionality/Clarity/Visual/Truthfulness)
- `npm run check` — PASS (664 tests)
- `node scripts/reader-check.mjs https://deploy-preview-32--pathcheck.netlify.app` (the test against the real Gemini, run by you on 2026-11-17) — PASS (six runs, model gemini-3.5-flash-lite)
- The hosted page, from your screenshots: one request to PathCheck's function answered 200, none to Google, no console error; 81 credits left for `sample-a.pdf`
- Reviewer: no blocker (round 3); the findings of all rounds are fixed

## Risks
- **Merging this publishes nothing.** You locked publishing; the main address keeps the M1 build until you publish. The key is set for previews only, so even a published build would say "Upload isn’t available right now — try again tomorrow" until you add the key for Production (after F22).
- **Before you upload your own transcript (F24):** the label "Synthetic transcript result" on the result page would be untrue over a real transcript. I need your choice for it.
- **The model is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, as you decided on 2026-11-17.** By Google's price list a normal transcript costs under one cent and the most one upload can cost is about 12 cents. Two things in that sum are not confirmed for this model (how many tokens a page counts as, and whether the model's thinking is billed). What an upload really costs can be read on your Spend page in Google AI Studio; the function will measure it itself in F22.
- **Until F22 (the upload limits) is merged, the function has no limit of its own.** While the project is Private only you can reach it. Your balance and spend cap at Google are the stop.
- **Your tries on the private preview first said "Upload isn’t available right now — try again tomorrow", for two reasons, both fixed.** The page sent its request without your Netlify login, which a private site needs: it now goes with this site's own cookies (to this site only; PathCheck sets none of its own, and the function reads nothing of a request but its type and its length). Then Gemini answered "not found" for the first model: Google keeps the 2.5 models for projects that already used them.
- **The privacy sentence also shows on localhost**, where nothing is sent to Google: only the two made-up transcripts are read there, inside the browser.
- **"Reading your transcript…" is my wording**, not yours. Say if you want other words.
- **With an earlier result remembered, choosing a new file reads nothing** and shows that result; the reason is said only to screen readers. You asked for it to be shown on the page: that is the next pull request, not this one.
- `features.json`: F21 is marked as passing, with its evidence and tests.
