author: jgoetzmann-bot
body:
Closes #4012

## What changed

- [01_schema_invariants.sql](crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql): appended CHECK 22 (no `public` view without `security_invoker = true`), CHECK 23 (no `public` materialized view), CHECK 24 (every `SECURITY DEFINER` function in `public`/`app` pins `search_path`, reading the catalog where CHECK 17 follows a list), and CHECK 25 (no `SECURITY DEFINER` function in `public`/`app` executable by `anon`/`authenticated`/`PUBLIC` outside a one-entry allowlist). Each check prints a diagnostic `select`, proves its detector with a failing probe first (CHECK 25's failing case is the pre-0094 schema itself, per plan), and asserts the real schema is clean.
- [0094_revoke_on_profile_activated.sql](crates/server/migrations/0094_revoke_on_profile_activated.sql) (new): `REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION app.on_profile_activated() FROM PUBLIC` plus `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role`. A survey of all migrations confirmed the plan's prediction: `on_profile_activated` (0002's pending-to-active launch-grant trigger) is the only `DEFINER` function never revoked from `PUBLIC`, so its default `EXECUTE`-to-`PUBLIC` grant left it callable by clients. Trigger firing needs no grant (`handle_new_user` precedent); the `service_role` grant keeps the server path working.
- Wiring: one `MIGRATIONS` entry in [migrate.rs](crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs), the `0028-0094` loop plus refuse-unknown entry in [run.sh](crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh), and the `PINNED` row (`2ac06ed4`) in [migrations_pinned.rs](crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs).
- CHECK 25's allowlist holds exactly `app.profile_is_active()` for `authenticated` (the 0002/0003/0004 RLS policies call it, and it is `DEFINER` so it reads `profiles` without recursing into policies). `app.current_profile_id()` is also granted to `authenticated` but is `SECURITY INVOKER`, so it is out of scope. No spec or ruling change: database hardening, no game-rules decision.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store migrations_pinned`: 9 passed, 0 failed (the failure output first reported the new checksum, which I copied into `PINNED`).
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `sh -n` on `run.sh`: OK.
- Full-file parse of `01_schema_invariants.sql` (78 statements) and migration 0094 (2 statements) with `pglast`, which embeds the real Postgres grammar. This caught one genuine bug: CHECK 24's probe used `as $$ select 1 $$` inside a `DO $$` body, which would close the outer string early in real Postgres too; the probe now uses `$fn$` quoting.
- **Not run: `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`.** This machine has no Docker (`docker: not found`), no root/sudo, and no Postgres binaries, so the container suites cannot execute here. By the survey above, pre-0094 CHECK 25 fails naming exactly `app.on_profile_activated:PUBLIC`, and post-0094 all four checks are clean; CI's `db` job is the real proof — if it names any additional offender I did not predict, that function needs the same revoke-plus-grant treatment, not an allowlist entry.

## Decisions

- Followed the plan's no-synthetic-probe call for CHECK 25; added only small vacuity guards in the file's stated convention (CHECK 25 counts in-scope `DEFINER` functions; every probe asserts the detector names it).
- Left CHECK 2's "0001-0093" heading and 83-table list untouched: 0094 adds no tables.
- Rejected widening CHECK 25 to the `auth` schema: `auth.uid()` is granted to clients by design and would false-positive.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

<details><summary>Rounds and checks</summary>

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | build, 31.6 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 8s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 443s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 2s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 7s |

</details>

body:
## Summary

Implements **CC-7 Care log and PDF export** (Step 17 G1) targeting `batch/s15-18`:
- **`/log` Care log timeline (`apps/carecircle/app/log.tsx`, `apps/carecircle/src/features/log/`):**
  - Timeline of `log_entries` for the circle ordered newest first, paged 50 entries at a time (`range(offset, offset + 49)`), with filters by `log_type` (`dose`, `med_change`, `appointment`, `task`, `visit_note`, `member`) and by person (`created_by`).
  - Readable by all circle roles (`owner`, `helper`, `viewer`) with `EmptyState` and `ErrorState`.
  - Entry point row (`testID="circle-care-log-button"`) added on `/circle` (`CircleSettingsScreen.tsx` & `app/circle.tsx`).
  - `"Export PDF"` card with date range inputs (`from`, `to`, defaulting to the last 30 days inclusive in the circle's timezone). On a free circle, opens `PaywallSheet` and fires `cc_paywall_viewed` (`{ trigger: 'pdf_export' }`). On success, opens the signed `pdfUrl` with the system share sheet (`Share.share`) and fires `cc_log_exported` once with `{ days }` only.
- **Edge Function `export-log` (`supabase/carecircle/functions/export-log/`):**
  - PDF library: **`npm:pdf-lib@1.17.1`** (`PDFDocument`, `StandardFonts.Helvetica`, `StandardFonts.HelveticaBold`), with stream decompression and text extraction helper (`extractTextFromPdfBytes` using `node:zlib` `inflateSync`).
  - Requires a valid Supabase JWT (`401` when missing/invalid) and verifies the caller is a member of `circleId` (any role: `owner`, `helper`, `viewer`), returning `403` with no detail otherwise.
  - Verifies Family plan via `verifyCircleFamilyEntitlement` (shared owner-entitlement helper) **before** reading any circle metadata or log entries, returning `402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` on free circles even if forged entitlement fields are sent in the request body.
  - Validates `from <= to` and inclusive range `<= 90` days (`400 RANGE_INVALID`).
  - Pages `log_entries` in batches of 500, generates the PDF with the care recipient's name, date range, and one `[ENTRY]` line per log entry (timestamp in the circle's timezone, type, summary, actor), uploads to `log-exports/{circleId}/{uuid}.pdf` via `service_role`, and returns `{ ok: true, pdfUrl }` signed for `3600` seconds.
  - Logs only counts and IDs (`circleId`, `exportId`, `entryCount`), never PDF content or care recipient name.
- **Private Storage bucket `log-exports` & 24h cleanup (`supabase/carecircle/migrations/20261116000004_log_exports_storage.sql`, `supabase/carecircle/tests/cc7_log_exports_storage.test.sql`, `cleanup-prescription-photos/handler.ts`):**
  - Creates private `log-exports` bucket (`public = false`, `application/pdf`) with zero policies for `authenticated` or `anon` (service role only) and 20 pgTAP assertions proving `authenticated` and `anon` cannot `select`, `insert`, `update`, or `delete` in `log-exports`.
  - Adds `public.list_expired_log_exports` (`security definer`, `service_role` only), daily pg_cron cleanup job, and `log-exports` support in `cleanup-prescription-photos/handler.ts`.

## Done when
- `/log` renders `log_entries` newest first, paged 50 at a time, with type and person filters, `EmptyState`, and `ErrorState`, reachable from `/circle` and readable by viewers.
- `export-log` enforces membership (`403`), Family plan (`402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` before reading data), and `<= 90` days (`400 RANGE_INVALID`), builds a multi-page PDF via `npm:pdf-lib@1.17.1`, stores it in `log-exports/{circleId}/{uuid}.pdf`, and returns a 3600s signed URL.
- `cc7_log_exports_storage.test.sql` (20 pgTAP tests), `export-log/index_test.ts` (7 Deno tests including 30-day fixture text extraction), `cleanup-prescription-photos/log_exports_test.ts` (2 Deno tests), and `apps/carecircle/src/care-log.test.tsx` (4 real-router Jest tests) pass.

## Not done
- Server-side plan limit tests for Step 18 (`CC-8 [safety 1/2]` and `CC-10 [safety 1/2]`), which are separate PRs in Step 18.

## Break checks
- Verified that a non-member calling `export-log` gets `403` with `0` calls to `getCircle` or `listLogEntries`.
- Verified that a free circle calling `export-log` (even with `{ entitlements: { carecircle_family: true, active: true } }` in the body) gets `402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` with `0` calls to `getCircle` or `listLogEntries`.
- Verified that a 91-day range (`2026-01-01` to `2026-04-01`) and `from > to` return `400 RANGE_INVALID`, while a 90-day range (`2026-01-01` to `2026-03-31`) returns `200`.
- Verified via `extractTextFromPdfBytes` on the 30-day fixture circle (35 entries) that the generated PDF bytes contain `Care recipient: Nadia Bensalem`, `Date range: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30 (America/New_York)`, and `35` `[ENTRY]` lines.
- Verified in `care-log.test.tsx` that `cc_log_exported` sends `{ days: 30 }` only and contains no recipient name, summary text, or URL.

## Found, not fixed
- None.

## Blocked
- As documented on PR #42, 8 pre-CC-5a tests in `supabase/carecircle/functions/ai/{index_test,providers_test,rx_storage_auth_test}.ts` are protected by `batch-guard` and fail in `CI / quality` because `summarizeVisit` now requires `circleId` and Family plan entitlement on `batch/s15-18`. All `export-log` and `cleanup-prescription-photos` Deno tests (`15 passed | 0 failed`) pass.

body:
Closes #150.

Adds a `netlify-project` destination: `keypin publish` writes a key to a Netlify project's environment variables for one deploy context.

```toml
[[keys.API_TOKEN.prod.publish]]
to = "netlify-project"
team = "<team slug>"
project = "my-project.netlify.app"
context = "production"
```

## What it does

- Signs in with a personal access token in `KEYPIN_NETLIFY_TOKEN`, the same way Vercel uses `KEYPIN_VERCEL_TOKEN`. It doesn't read the `netlify login` config or `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`; the message says so when `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set.
- The account check reads the project (`GET /sites/{project}`) and refuses when it belongs to another team, naming the real team. `team` accepts the team slug or account ID; `project` accepts the project ID or its domain, both of which Netlify's API takes in place of `site_id`.
- Writes through the account env endpoints scoped to the site (`/accounts/{slug}/env?site_id=`): it creates a new variable with `is_secret: true` and scopes builds, functions and runtime, or `PATCH`es only its context's value on an existing one. Other contexts and branch values stay as they are.
- One destination per deploy context: `production`, `deploy-preview`, `branch-deploy` and `dev-server` (Preview Servers), like Vercel's one per environment.
- The plan says Netlify uses the new value only from the next build and deploy. keypin doesn't start a deploy.
- It never reads a value back. Netlify secret values are write-only anyway.

## Refusals

- `context = "dev"`: Netlify keeps local development values readable to the team, even on a secret variable. The error points to `keypin run -- netlify dev`. `all` and other values are refused too.
- An existing variable not marked as secret: keypin stops rather than write a readable value, and says how to mark it in Netlify.
- Names Netlify reserves (its read-only build and function variables) and names that don't start with a letter fail when the map is parsed.
- A refused token (401), a project the token can't reach (403/404, including SAML teams that didn't grant the token access), and 429s each get their own message. Error messages never include the value or the token.

## Left out on purpose

- Triggering a build or deploy (v1, per the issue).
- Branch values (`context = "branch"` with a branch name). Wildcards and the per-branch override need their own design.
- Team-level shared variables. Only Team Owners can edit those, and they apply to every project.
- Granular scopes. Netlify offers them only on Pro and above; secrets can't use post-processing, so new variables get the other three.
- Reading the `netlify login` config file. It's a CLI implementation detail, not a stable interface, same as Vercel's.
- OAuth app tokens. Any token sent as `Bearer` works, but the docs and messages only name personal access tokens.

## Verified

- `bun run check`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (74 files, 1466 tests) all pass.
- The shared destination contract runs in `tests/netlify/contract.test.ts`, plus 23 focused tests for writes, refusals, sign-in and map parsing, all against `netlifyFetch`, a fake. No real Netlify or 1Password calls.
- Two terminal journeys (publish shows the rebuild note and writes once; `check` without the token says how to sign in). With the registration in `start.ts` removed, both fail.

author: tommy-couzens
body:
## Purpose
Death AI sends small groups into a bigger army, spreads its workers unevenly across its bases, and keeps fighting when the enemy pulls workers in. Death V2 fixes those while keeping how Death plays, credited to DeathStroke. The original Death AI stays as it is, so the two can be compared by ranked MMR.

## Approach
Like Death AI, each game a coin flip picks a style: soldiers and archers from barracks, or wolves and snakes from wolves dens (the first 6 units wolves, then half and half, with beast upgrades from an Animal Testing Lab).

Both styles balance workers across every goldmine, defend with only as many workers as a fight needs, repair, scout for proxies and expand. The barracks style gathers a big army and only moves out with a clear margin. The wolf style keeps a wolf scouting the enemy main and goldmines, moves out early, and commits only to a target where it outweighs what it has seen there, pulling back on the wolves' speed when a fight turns.

Headless CPU vs CPU games on the 8 ranked maps, one seed, both slots, up to an hour of game time (wins-losses-draws of 16):

| Opponent | Wolf style | Barracks style |
|---|---|---|
| Beginner Bot | 16-0-0 | 16-0-0 |
| Malfizars AI | 16-0-0 | 16-0-0 |
| Campaign AI | 16-0-0 | 16-0-0 |
| Death AI | 15-1-0 | 15-1-0 |
| Hurricane AI | 13-3-0 | 12-3-1 |
| Slammer Bot (#24) | 12-4-0 | 14-2-0 |
| Macro bot (#26) | 14-2-0 | 10-4-2 |
| Aggro bot (#23) | 10-6-0 | 7-9-0 |

The wolf style beats the barracks style 11-5. Aggro bot's early proxy rush is the weak spot for both, and a maxed wolf army is weaker than a maxed barracks one, so it can end up banking gold late.

author: timoshinoleg-eng
body:
## Problem and change

In PR #285, the 250 ms counter cooldown can hide the combo badge and leave kill counts stale. The publisher also allocates a snapshot before deciding whether to publish, and onboarding analytics reads the second-granularity registry time.

Compare source primitives before materializing snapshots; publish changes to combo and counters on the next update. Read live game time for onboarding step and exit with registry fallback. Add a browser contract covering deterministic cooldown reproduction, idle snapshot calls, immutable published snapshots, forced pickup ordering and locally intercepted onboarding events.

## Verification

- RED on #285 HEAD: combo 1 vs live 24, five snapshot calls for five unchanged publications, stale kills, and onboarding 7000 vs live 7871 ms.
- Browser contract GREEN, plus HUD hierarchy smoke at six viewport sizes and long kill counts.
- `npm run build` and `npm run test:bundle-shape` on c7d1f9a0a20980371c3a7254af7b4a055cc3750e; onboarding, analytics and runtime-quality contracts passed.
- On c7d1f9a, browser-smoke initially failed in Muse convergence when a mutation modal did not close; the same scenario passed locally and CI passed on rerun. The cause remains unconfirmed. CI on the current HEAD 9dc1af2 passed after rerun.

## Limits and tradeoff

Synthetic changes to kills on all 60 calls produce 60 snapshots: this prioritizes current HUD values and removes idle allocations, but does not establish a dense-combat performance win. Compare physical-device FPS and GC before release. Analytics test uses locally intercepted fixture requests; no production API, Telegram/MAX device or real payments were tested. This PR targets #285, not main.

The original extended test mistakenly called the #285-specific publisher on main; that was not a valid main control. The current test was run against exact main 2bd6320 (behavioral checks pass; optimization checks are inapplicable), original #285 8c0dec2 (RED) and the follow-up (GREEN).

CI on 9dc1af2: snapshot test passed, but browser-smoke failed at the same Muse mutation selection as a prior run on c7d1f9a. A paired Linux repro passed 3/3 each on the #285 base and follow-up; this does not identify the CI failure cause. Failed job rerun on 9dc1af2 passed; the initial CI failure remains unexplained. Logs: /tmp/ofeliya-{base,fix}-{1,2,3}.log in the local WSL environment.

author: s0up4200
body:
## Description

Adds the two building blocks that the Problem report service (#4247) needs, with no change that users see. The log hub can return its history from a minimum level up, and the redact package removes more forms of secrets.

- `Hub.HistoryFrom(minLevel, n)`: the last `n` lines at `minLevel` or above, oldest first. It filters before it counts, so "the last 200 warnings" holds 200 warning or error lines when the buffer has them. It reads the `level` field of a JSON line, or the level word of a console-format line, and keeps a line whose level it cannot read. `History` and the Logs page are unchanged.
- `redact.Text(s)`: runs `String`, then removes the value of each JSON field and `key: value` pair whose name holds key, pass, token, secret or auth (any case, also escaped JSON inside a log message; a flat list or object becomes `"REDACTED"` whole), and the value after `Authorization:` for any scheme.
- `redact.Secrets(s, secrets)`: removes each exact value of a list of secrets, longest first. It skips values shorter than 6 characters.
- `redact.String` now also finds `udp://`, `ws://` and `wss://` URLs in free text, so a passkey in their path is removed. Other schemes stay out on purpose: matching them sent notification URLs in error texts through the URL rewrite, which reorders their queries.

The departures from the spec are in the [Brief amendment](https://github.com/autobrr/qui/issues/4248#issuecomment-6945662388) on the issue.

Closes #4248

**Merge danger:** two-way door, small: no caller uses the new functions yet, and the only changed output is a removed passkey in a udp/ws/wss URL in an error log line.

## Breaking change

No breaking change.

## Behaviour change

An error log line that holds a `udp://`, `ws://` or `wss://` URL now shows a long path segment (a passkey) as `REDACTED`, as http URLs already did.

## How has this been tested?

Live run on a local rig (built binary, stub qBittorrent with 20 torrents, instance added through `POST /api/instances`): the Logs stream history (`/api/logs/stream`) equals the qui log file line for line and in order, at INFO (11 lines) and DEBUG (24 lines, with the instance add). `limit=5` returns the 5 newest lines.

## Performance

`redact.String` is about 1 µs slower on a short error text and about 25 µs slower on a 2 KB one, because the wider URL pattern has no literal prefix. It runs only on error log paths, so no user notices it. The new functions have no caller yet.

| Input to `redact.String` | Time | Memory | Allocs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short error, no URL (52 B) | 5.73 → 6.34 µs +10.8% | 577 → 577 B ~ | 12 → 12 ~ |
| Error with http apikey URL (133 B) | 13.69 → 13.99 µs ~ | 2.04 → 2.04 KiB ~ | 27 → 27 ~ |
| Error with udp announce URL (265 B) | 31.49 → 29.70 µs −5.7% | 2.32 → 4.00 KiB +72% | 12 → 36 +200% |
| 2 KB text, no URL | 203.8 → 228.9 µs +12.4% | 16.10 → 16.09 KiB ~ | 12 → 12 ~ |
| 2 KB text, 3 URLs | 223.2 → 242.6 µs +8.7% | 20.93 → 23.02 KiB +10% | 45 → 51 +13% |

Old and new `redact.go` copied into a scratch module, `go test -bench -benchmem -count=10` with `b.Loop()`, compared with benchstat; a second run in reverse order gave the same direction (short error +23.8%, 2 KB no URL +11.2%). The udp case allocates more because the udp URL now goes through the full URL redaction. Base ce54665f6, head 68072352d, go1.27.4 on a Ryzen 7 8745HS. `HistoryFrom` decodes at most 1,000 lines outside the hub lock, on demand only.

## Checklist

- [x] My PR title follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format (it becomes the squashed commit message)
- [ ] If this changes the database schema, I have added migrations for both SQLite and PostgreSQL
- [x] I completed the [mandatory performance checks](https://github.com/autobrr/qui/blob/develop/docs/agents/performance-checks.md) and recorded the outcome in Performance

author: hsw
body:
Fixes #99.

## What

- `ngx_ssl_fp_sort_uint16()`: the existing ja4 insertion sort for up to 32 entries, heapsort above; no comparator, no recursion. The heap picks the larger child with arithmetic, not an `if`: gcc -O2 compiles the `if` into a jump on a ~50% unpredictable compare, which doubles the sort time.
- `ngx_ssl_ja3()` copies the non-GREASE extensions into a pool buffer and sorts it, replacing the repeated min-scan; `ngx_ssl_ja4()` calls the helper for ciphers and extensions.

Output is byte-identical; typical lists (≤ 32 entries) stay on the insertion loop.

## Why

The ja3 min-scan is O(n·d) in a client-chosen count: ~500 unknown extensions fit the 1024-byte capture buffer. With 480 extensions, `ngx_ja3 on` costs ~0.75 ms of worker CPU per handshake on x86 (Cascade Lake).

## Verification

- `ngx_ssl_ja3()` on 504 extensions, x86: 0.36–1.15 ms → 12–15 µs at nginx's default `-O`, 887 µs → 13.5 µs at `-O2`. Per crafted handshake (480 extensions, ja3 on minus off): +2.66 M → +62 k worker user cycles. An ordinary ClientHello: no change.
- Threshold 32: the insertion/heapsort crossover on reverse input is 24–40 entries (gcc 15 / clang 21, `-O1`/`-O2`); at 32 insertion loses at most ~50 ns.
- ja3/ja4 strings unchanged on existing and new vectors (around the threshold, random order, duplicates, GREASE-interleaved, up to 504 entries); libFuzzer with a qsort oracle for both, no findings.
- `tests/run.sh` and tlsfuzzer pass on nginx 1.29.8 / 1.30.0 / 1.31.7 / 1.31.8 × OpenSSL 3.5.6 / 3.6.2; no new warnings with `-Wextra` (gcc, clang).

Offers **Compress text and code** in production, for 3.0.0. Since #2500, `compressDeployments` no longer compresses anything by itself: it means "offer the checkbox" in the upload review's Options, on public drives, off every time a review opens. With this PR production users see that checkbox; nothing is compressed unless they tick it.

body:
## What changes

Where she is has **one channel and no second writer**: the event manager tells `WhereSheIs` once a physics tick, and nothing else tells an event where she is.

- **The halo's word on the point no longer reaches an event.** `ExcitementSource.set_player_at()` is split: every source takes her motion through `set_her_motion(velocity, decay_rate, sensitivity)`, which `ExcitementHalo` calls once a frame; a crowd body, which hears no manager's word, is told the point through its own `CrowdExcitement.set_her_at()`, which the halo calls for a crowd source only. An event's source has no point to be handed (`EventExcitement._her_at()` reads its handle), and a source with no account of its own measures from nowhere.
- **`notice_her_at()` writes nothing into `WhereSheIs`.** Its position stays an argument as an order's input (the heading, the notice clock, `EventPursuit.was_set_on_her()`); every caller already passes the point the tick tells. `WhereSheIs.see_her_at()`, its stored point and its word counter are deleted. The director's rig-only fallback to the contact point (no player) sets the man heading there; he then hears nowhere until a manager tells a word.
- The queue bullet's premise was stale: the halo already told every candidate. What was wrong was two writers. The one-channel reading is the orchestrator's, open to the player ("whatever is the *correct* implementation", inbox #1278 in olive-ferret); it overturns the orchestrator's earlier reading of the notice's point as an order kept on the handle.

## In play and in the run log

Nothing she sees. `tests/probes/excitement_fingerprint.gd` at main and at this head: the `XF` lines are identical (20515 each, `diff` empty).

## The checks

- The split of `set_player_at()` holds the halo's half of the guarantee by its signature: the halo hands a source only her motion (`set_her_motion()`, which takes no point), and only a crowd body is told her position (`CrowdExcitement.set_her_at()`), so no check can state it. The check that fails at main is `test_where_she_is`: a robber set on a far point (`notice_her_at()`) read that point back through `sight_line_to_her()`. `test_excitement_source` holds that an event's caret reads the point its instance's handle says.
- `test_where_she_is`: a pursuer set on a far point (`notice_her_at()`) and a source told her motion still hear her where the tick put her, and the next word moves it.
- Six suites that placed her for an event through the halo's call now tell the event's `WhereSheIs`; the crowd's tests tell `set_her_at()`; the position arguments that did nothing are gone from `test_danger` and `test_event_redraw`.

## Verification

`check.sh`, `lint.sh`, `check_layers.py` and every `tools/check_*.py` pass. The full local suite ran under heavy machine load: 3 of 4 shards were killed at the shard timeout with 0 failures in what ran (233 suites); I reran the 33 suites they never reached by name, 0 failures. Main was merged twice: #1497 at `a48bb95a5`, with no conflicts (an empty `--remerge-diff`), and #1499 (`field_reaches` with the field's real shape) at `a2c5b8360`, which conflicted in `docs/todo/2026-10-18-minty-quail/event-interface.md` (section 2.10 and point 6 of section 7). The three versions of each hunk and the resolution are in the PR's conversation.

## Architecture questions

1. Layer: simulation (`EventExcitement`, `CrowdExcitement`, `WhereSheIs`, `EventInstance`), the data/world base `ExcitementSource`, and the view's `ExcitementHalo`; methods are split and removed, no piece added.
2. Dependencies: the halo (view) names `CrowdExcitement` (simulation), downward; `tools/check_layers.py` passes.
3. Handed and fetched: unchanged; an event's source reads her point from the handle it is handed and nothing else.
4. Reuse: the one channel is the existing `WhereSheIs`; nothing is copied.
5. The fix lands in the shared mechanism (the sources), not in a branch on a row.
6. Isolation: tests hand an instance a `WhereSheIs` and tell it, as the spawner does.
7. Docs: `event-interface.md` and the classes' doc comments; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` lists no member this touches.

## Queue

author: andrea-forbicia
body:
## What this does

Updates the open notes in `docs/status.md`: `main` is now protected and secret scanning is on. Only adding the reviewer as a collaborator is still open.

## Why it is done this way

`main` is protected by a repository **ruleset** (`protect-main`):

| Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Require a pull request, 0 approvals | Nothing reaches `main` without a PR. A sole owner cannot approve their own PR, so 1 approval would block every merge |
| Require status check `lint-and-test`, branch up to date | CI must be green on code that already includes the latest `main` |
| Block force pushes, restrict deletions | `main` history cannot be rewritten or deleted |
| Empty bypass list | The rules apply to the owner too |

On top of that, secret scanning and push protection are enabled. Push protection rejects a `git push` that contains a recognisable token, before it enters the history. It is the server-side complement of the `detect-private-key` pre-commit hook.

This PR is also the first one merged under the new rules.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Classic branch protection rules:** they would enforce the same rules, but rulesets are GitHub's current recommendation and anyone with read access can see them.

body: `TaskView`, `AddressView`, and `PointView` are a third sample type. They are not a mode of `Task` / `TaskLazy`, and the plugin does not emit them. `TaskView::parse` scans the caller's buffer once with `RecordScanner` and stores scalars plus spans. Getters do not walk that buffer again. String and bytes getters return subslices of the original buffer, and UTF-8 is checked on each string get. Repeated numericals are copied during the scan. `labels()` and `attributes()` iterate the stored spans, so a caller can stop before a later element. A singular message merges each LEN into one child view. Unknown field numbers, including unknown groups, are skipped. `to_owned` decodes the same bytes with eager `Task`. An absent explicit field stays `None` (`max_retries` does not fill in `3`). A closed-enum number outside the set does not replace a value already stored. `cargo test -p puroro-sample-generated` passed, including 10 new `task_view` tests. Clippy `-D warnings` on that package passed.

author: carlos-vera
body:
## What

Quick Peek linked only the paths in Claude's replies. Now the paths in a prompt you sent take the hover and the click too. A dropped image or a file copied from Finder shows the same preview as one Claude names.

- **Paths with spaces.** A path in single or double quotes is one path, spaces and all (`'/Users/you/Library/Application Support/x.webp'`, the way a drop or a Finder copy writes it). A quote that closes a word (`it's`) is not counted. An unquoted absolute or `~` path takes up to 8 of the words after it, and the longest one that is there on disk wins (`$.fs.stat`, with the same cache as replies). An escaped `\ ` counts as a space.
- **Claude Code still draws the prompt.** A `ui.render` hook on `UserMessage` leaves its text as it is. Over each part of a path it lays a bare `Client` (`isBare`, an empty `Box`) of that part's width, `position: "absolute"`, at its row and column.
- **Wrapped lines.** The rows come from the same `wrap()` replies use, given the row's width after `❯ `. A new `isCutAtFolder` flag (default `true`, so replies don't change) cuts a path where the row ends, the way Claude Code wraps a prompt, instead of after a `/`. A path that wraps gets one region on each row it lands on.

## Limits

- Only lines Claude Code draws as written. The mod stops at the first blank line, or at the first line its Markdown would draw differently (backticks, `*`, `_emphasis_`, a link, a heading, a list or quote marker, HTML). Past that it can't tell where the text lands.
- A prompt over 4000 characters gets no links.
- No underline on hover: the region is unpainted, so Claude Code's text shows through as it is.
- The prompt box while you type is left alone, as before.
- I tried it live in fullscreen on Claude Code 2.1.326 with a quoted path with spaces. Wrapped rows follow how the engine lays out a prompt, but tests can't prove the live layout, because the engine draws the prompt itself.

README: the feature, the limits and how it works. I didn't bump the version.

## How I checked it

- `claude plugin test ./plugins/quick-peek`: 22 pass (16 on main). 6 new tests: quoted and spaced-out paths found in text; a quoted path with spaces in a sent prompt is a bare region over the engine's text; an unquoted path with spaces is found whole, and one that isn't on disk is no target; a path that wraps lands on each row where the engine wraps it; replies still link with prompts hooked too; with no window, a prompt's path carries the card.
- `claude plugin validate ./plugins/quick-peek` passes. `npm run validate` passes, and `npm run test:node` passes (157).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Adds the Maven module `src/trade-desk-java` (Spring Boot 3.5.11, Java 17, Spring Data JPA, Db2 JCC driver). It ports `src/base/cobol_src/DBCRFUN.cbl` and is added to the root reactor `pom.xml`. `POST /api/dbcrfun` takes `DbcrfunRequest` (PAYDBCR fields: `accno`, `amt`, `sortc`, `origin{applid,userid,facilityName,netwrkId,faciltype}`) and returns `DbcrfunResponse` (`success`, `failCode`, `avBal`, `actBal`). `DbcrfunService.process` is one `@Transactional` method that keeps the COBOL branch order: ``` findForUpdate(sortcode, accno) empty -> N/1, DataAccessException -> N/2 if amt < 0: 496 && type in {HOSPITAL, "TENDER "} -> N/4 496 && avail + amt < 0 -> N/3 (tellers may overdraw) 496 && type in {HOSPITAL, "TENDER "} -> N/4 (unconditional repeat, so payment credits are blocked too) avail += amt; actual += amt; saveAndFlush error -> N/2 insert PROCTRAN: PRTR, DD.MM.YYYY, HHMMSS, ref, DEB "COUNTER WTHDRW" | PDR origin(1:14) | CRE "COUNTER RECVED" | PCR origin(1:14) error -> setRollbackOnly, N/02 Y/0 + new balances ``` Parity details that are easy to miss: - **Account type** is padded to `PIC X(8)` before comparing, so `TENDER` and `TENDER ` both match. - **`amt = 0`** takes the COBOL ELSE branch, so it is a credit (`CRE`/`PCR`). - **Origin description** is `COMM-ORIGIN(1:14)`: `applid` padded to 8, then the first 6 characters of `userid` (for example `"PAYAPPL PAYUSE"`). - **Request `sortc` is ignored.** As in the COBOL, the bank sort code from config is used (`dbcrfun.sortcode`, replaces `SORTCODE.cpy`, default `987654`). `accno` is zero-filled like `PIC 9(8)`. - **Balances on failure**: on N/2 (update) and N/02, `avBal`/`actBal` hold the computed new balances, because the COBOL moves them to the COMMAREA before checking SQLCODE. - **`failCode "02"`** follows the spec. In the COBOL, `COMM-FAIL-CODE` is `PIC X`, so `MOVE '02'` actually stores only `'0'`. Change `FAIL_PROCTRAN` if byte-level parity is needed. - **Rollback**: every DataAccessException path calls `TransactionRollback.markRollbackOnly()`. This replaces `SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK` and stops Spring from throwing `UnexpectedRollbackException` on commit. Changes beyond the COBOL: - **Row lock**: the account is read with `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE`. - **PROCTRAN_REF**: `EIBTASKN` is replaced by an injectable `ProcTranReferenceGenerator` (default is a 12-digit counter). - **Clock**: date and time come from an injectable `Clock`. - **Not ported**: CICS storm drain, ABNDPROC and abend handling. - **PROCTRAN_DATE**: the DDL declares `DATE`, but the column is bound as `DD.MM.YYYY` text, the same as the COBOL host variable `PIC X(10)`. - **Validation**: a request with no `accno` or `amt` returns HTTP 400. **Duplicate:** open PR #38 (https://github.com/COG-GTM/Tradewinds-COBOL-Modernization/pull/38) ports DBCRFUN into the same path from an earlier request. Only one of the two should land. ## Testing - `mvn -B test` in `src/trade-desk-java`: 23 tests, 0 failures. - `DbcrfunServiceTest` (Mockito, 19 tests) covers the 12 requested branches plus edge cases. - `DbcrfunServiceIntegrationTest` (H2) checks the real commit, and checks that a PROCTRAN failure rolls the balance back to 100.00. - `DbcrfunControllerTest` covers the HTTP layer. - Mutation check: removing `markRollbackOnly()` on the PROCTRAN path makes the integration rollback test fail. - Ran the app locally on H2 (`mvn spring-boot:test-run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=local`) and called it with curl. Results: not found N/1, teller overdraft Y/0, payment with insufficient funds N/3, HOSPITAL payment debit N/4, TENDER payment credit N/4, HOSPITAL teller debit Y/0, missing `amt` HTTP 400. - **Not tested against a real Db2.** The JCC driver and the `IBMUSER` schema config are untested. +description: Use when a change adds shared state, a new module, adapter, tool or script, a flow across screens, or a new requirement that breaks a rule of the current design. Use it also when the request says to write the code now. Decide and review the code design before the code.

Model the states and events first. | 22 |

Find the first wrong decision. | 25 |

| `principle-check-approval` | Check authority when a fix changes approved behaviour, scope, contracts, or protected operations. | Use when a fix changes approved behaviour, scope, a contract, or a protected operation such as a migration. Check that an approval covers it. | 24 |
| `principle-automate-checks` | Replace repeated corrections with enforcement, or put judgment rules in one authoritative place. | Use when the same correction or review issue repeats, or a rule has several copies. Add a check, or give the rule one home. | 24 |
| `principle-script-the-work` | Write a script that does or proves non-trivial edits, analyses, or checks, so that a reviewer can rerun the work. | Use when an edit, analysis or check covers many places or is hard to check by eye. Write a script that a reviewer can rerun. | 25 |
| `principle-safe-test-data` | Create synthetic fixtures when tests or examples need values that resemble credentials or private data. | Use when a test, fixture or example needs a value that looks like a credential, key, token or private data. Build a synthetic value. | 24 |

## Why

The owner asked for a test of `principle-design-first` with NVIDIA SkillEvaluator 0.9.0, approved its new description after the results, and then asked for a review of the other principles on the base of that change (session of 2026-11-17). No task brief applies.

The live test ran Claude Code (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Docker on cases from the project records, 3 attempts for each case, with the skill and without it. With the old description, the skill did not load in 6 of the 15 trials that needed it, and in those 6 trials the agent wrote the code immediately. Each part of the new text answers one result:

| Change | Result with the old description |

| "a new module, adapter, tool or script" replaces "a module boundary" | Case 003 (a new script in a PR under review) loaded the skill in 0 of 3 trials. Case 004 (a new adapter) loaded it in 2 of 3 |
| "a new requirement that breaks a rule of the current design" replaces "a requirement that changes a design" | Case 005 (Trash against the never-delete rule) loaded it in 1 of 3 |
| "Use it also when the request says to write the code now" | Each case asked for code immediately |
| "Use when" at the start | Tier 1 of the tool: "Description has no 'Use when ...' trigger", and the Hermes 60-character finding |


The other thirteen descriptions had the form that failed in that test: the action first, then abstract words for the trigger. Their new text follows three rules from the test:

1. The trigger comes first.
2. The trigger uses words that a request contains, such as "a bug", "a PR", "a migration" or "a library".
3. The scope of the skill stays the same. I compared each new description with the steps of its skill.

**My error in the first version of this PR.** I changed the `principle-design-first` description before I read "Maintain principles" in `.agents/skills/README.md`. Its rule 7 limits a description to 25 words, and the new text has 51. The owner decided on 2026-11-17 to keep the tested text: "If current description works better, than keep it like that. No needs to reduce the words". Commit `e630d45` records that exception in rule 7. For the other thirteen I followed the maintenance steps: I read all 16 principle files, kept each description at 25 words or less, and ran the STE checker and the skill validator.

author: tsukasai
body:
Closes #273
Closes #275

intent(walker): a file argument spelled differently from the cwd was matched against directories above the project (#273), and directory arguments anchored patterns at themselves and were never excluded (#275)
decision(walker): resolve the argument to its canonical location and match it relative to the cwd (#273 option A, #275 option A)
decision(walker): filter walk entries ourselves (`filter_entry`) instead of `builder.overrides`, which matches the entry path as typed
constraint(walker): BREAKING for a pattern written relative to a directory argument: with `fini src`, `/gen/` or `gen/sub/` used to mean `src/gen`, and is now relative to the cwd

## The rule

- An argument inside the cwd (file or directory, however it is spelled: `./x`, an absolute path, through a symlinked directory, with `..`) is resolved to its canonical location and matched relative to the cwd. The argument itself and each directory between it and the cwd are tested, so `fini vendor` and `fini vendor/lib.js` are skipped when `vendor/` is excluded. Entries found under a directory argument are matched by their cwd-relative path, so `fini src` and `fini .` agree on `src/gen/`.
- The final path component is not resolved, so a symlink is matched by where the link sits (same rule as `dedup_key`, which `cwd_relative` reuses).
- If resolving leads out of the cwd (a symlinked directory such as `data -> /mnt/data`), the path is matched as typed, provided its text alone places it below the cwd (no `..`).
- An argument outside the cwd anchors patterns at itself: entries under a directory argument are matched relative to it (as before), and a file argument is matched by its file name only (`*.snap` applies, `vendor/` cannot).
- The tracked-but-gitignored rescue uses the same matcher, so it anchors patterns the same way.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test`: 262 unit, 138 integration, 0 failed
- With `cwd_relative` reduced to a lexical `strip_prefix` on the typed path, four of the walker tests fail on macOS (the temp dir is reached through a symlink there). On Linux the temp path is already canonical; `test_issue_273_parent_component_is_resolved_before_matching` and `test_issue_273_symlinked_directory_component_is_resolved` cover it there. The Linux behavior is reasoned from the code and from CI passing, not from a local run.

## Review

`code-reviewer` approved (no critical/high; 2 medium, 5 low). The re-review of `ab56992` reported findings 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 resolved and no new critical/high; its three new low findings are under "Not filed".

Decided by the owner during review, implemented in `ab56992`:

- Finding 1 (medium), option A: the typed-path fallback for a symlinked directory that leaves the cwd. `src/walker.rs:246`
- Finding 2 (medium), option A: a file argument outside the cwd is matched by its file name only. This revises the "never excluded" part of #273 option A. `src/walker.rs:284`

Finding 3 (low, an excluded directory argument is not reported) is covered by #274, already decided (count in the summary, list under `--verbose`); its implementation will include directory arguments.

## Auto-fixed

All in `ab56992` (`7	3	README.md`, `141	9	src/walker.rs`, `47	0	tests/integration.rs`, shared with the two decided changes above):

- Finding 4: no test resolved a symlinked directory component on Linux. `src/walker.rs:1034`
- Finding 5: no test for the unresolved final component or for an unresolved cwd. `src/walker.rs:1057`, `src/walker.rs:1012`
- Finding 6: the README said symlinks are resolved, which is wrong for the last component. `README.md:113`

## Not filed
<!-- not-filed:v1 -->
- low, the PR title carries no breaking-change marker although the body says BREAKING, PR title, A: retitle to `fix(walker)!: ...`; B: leave as is, since the project is pre-1.0 and has no changelog
- low, the typed-path fallback misses an absolute argument spelled through a non-canonical cwd (`/tmp/proj/data/x.csv` while the cwd resolves to `/private/tmp/proj`), so only its file name is tested, `src/walker.rs:247`, A: find the typed ancestor whose canonical form equals the cwd and take the typed remainder; B: leave it and say "relative or starting with the resolved current directory" in the README
- low, a root-anchored single-name pattern (`/README.md`, meant as `<cwd>/README.md`) now also skips a same-named file passed from outside the cwd, `src/walker.rs:284`, A: leave as is, consistent with how a directory argument outside the cwd treats it; B: apply only slash-free patterns to an outside file
- low, a directory argument behind an outward symlink (`fini data/sub`) is now excluded by `data/` and anchors patterns at the cwd, with no test, `src/walker.rs:234`, A: add a unit test for `data/sub` with `data/` and with `data/sub/gen/`; B: leave

## Not in this PR

- #274: reporting arguments skipped by an exclude. It rewrites the same lines and follows this PR.
- A symlinked directory that stays inside the cwd is matched by where it resolves, not as typed: with `link -> src`, `fini link/a.rs` is excluded by `src/` and not by `link/`.

author: kratosdatagod
body:
Before: on this PC, Spark's regular expressions ran with DuckDB's RE2 as written. Some Java syntax stopped with RE2's own error: named groups `(?<n>...)`, `\p{Alpha}`, lookarounds and backreferences. Other syntax matched differently: `\s` without the vertical tab. `regexp_replace('100-200', '(\d+)-(\d+)', '$2-$1')` gave `$2-$1`. Several string functions also gave DuckDB's answers instead of Spark's, with no error:
- `left('abc', -1)` was `ab`.
- `chr(321)` was `Ł`.
- `split_part(s, '', 1)` split by character.
- `'a_b' LIKE 'a\_b'` was false.
- `concat_ws(',', array(...))` wrote `[a, NULL, b]`.
- Lengths and positions came back as `bigint`.

After: a pattern written in the query is translated from Java's syntax for RE2 before it runs, and so is one given as a string to the DataFrame API's `F.regexp_replace`, `F.regexp_extract`, `F.split` or `Column.rlike`. What RE2 can't read is refused by name and nothing runs. `regexp_replace`'s replacement is read as Java reads it. The string functions above give Spark's values and types. The cases that can still differ are listed in docs/sql-compatibility.md ("Regular expressions and text on this PC"), and LOC-002 warns wherever a pattern is used.

How: a new `spark_strings` module does two things.
- It tokenizes a Java pattern in one linear pass, rewrites what RE2 reads differently, and counts the capture groups to check replacements and group indexes.
- `sql.spark_fixes` calls its `spark_text_results` after the column names are fixed, so Spark's names stay as written. It applies to Spark SQL and Databricks SQL.

`spark_compat` wraps the DataFrame functions that take a pattern as a string. DuckDB 2.0's own `F.regexp_replace` already reads Java's `$1`, so there the replacement is only checked. The Academy's learner package copies the new module, as it does the other SQL files.

## Release notes

- Regular expressions in Spark SQL and notebook code on this PC read Java's syntax, as Fabric does. A pattern RE2 can't run, such as a lookahead, is refused by name. String functions give Spark's values for edge cases. Preview: not yet compared with a Fabric run.

## Integration

- **Workstream and feature ID:** WR-107 (#2842's new stories)
- **Issue or idea:** #2850
- **Depends on:** none. #2846 (WR-106) touches the same `spark_fixes` and LOC rule area; whichever merges second needs a one-line merge in `sql.py`'s imports.
- **Shared files and contracts touched:** sql.py `spark_fixes`, spark_compat.py `install`, the LOC-002 rule text and the Spark profile's semantic difference (UI copy), academy/learner_pkg.py SOURCES (one new engine file)
- **Stored data:** none. Lengths and positions are now `int`, as in Spark, so a Delta write of them takes Spark's type.
- **Permissions:** none
- **Visual identity:** none

## Tests

- **Added:** tests/test_spark_strings.py has 40 tests:
  - Java patterns, including POSIX classes, `\Q...\E`, `\s` with the vertical tab, `\R`, `\u` and octal escapes, and named groups.
  - Each regex function's values, NULLs and types.
  - String function edges.
  - 25 refusals by name.
  - A replacement taken from the data.
  - The DataFrame API.
  - The Databricks SQL path.
  - A check that each case that still differs is in the docs and gets LOC-002.
- **Run:**
  - `python -m pytest -q -n 8 tests`: 23,456 passed, 181 skipped.
  - After that run I made a type-only refactor and the DuckDB 2.0 fix. The new tests, Spark compat, Academy lab and silent-except tests were then re-run: 146 passed.
  - The Spark and SQL tests (`-k "spark or sql or regex or string or databricks"`) on sqlglot 30.22.0 and 30.27.0: 8,233 passed on each.
  - The same tests on DuckDB 2.0: 8,228 passed and 1 failed, the DataFrame test. That failure was the double translation, which is now fixed, and the strings tests pass on 2.0 (40).
  - ruff, the mypy ratchet (0 new), py_compile: clean.
- **Not tested:** no Fabric run. Every expected value comes from Spark's and Java's documentation, so the results are UNVERIFIED in Fabric.

## Known limitations

- These are listed in the docs and get LOC-002, but aren't fixed:
  - A pattern taken from the data isn't translated.
  - `$` without the `m` flag doesn't match before a final line break.
  - `.` matches `\r` and the Unicode line separators.
  - `(?i)` and `\b` treat letters outside ASCII differently.
  - `split` with a pattern that can match no text has no empty part at the end.
  - `concat_ws` with an array column writes the array as text.
  - `upper('ß')` is `ẞ`.
- In the DataFrame API, `F.split_part` with an empty delimiter and `F.concat` with a NULL keep DuckDB's results. They are listed in the docs, and `F.expr(...)` gives Spark's. The API's other string functions weren't compared.

body:
The current health endpoint stays green when PostgreSQL is unavailable, and browser exceptions have no reporting destination. Add an independent database-readiness endpoint and error-only PostHog reporting so outages and application failures can be diagnosed during preview testing.

Changes:
- Keep /api/v1/health as liveness; add /api/v1/ready with a two-second PostgreSQL ping and documented 503 response. Regenerate OpenAPI and TypeScript contracts.
- Log API requests as JSON with route templates, status, duration and a response correlation ID. Omit raw URLs, identifiers, bodies and credential headers. Rotate API logs in both Compose deployments.
- Capture unhandled browser errors/rejections and React render failures in the authorized EU PostHog project. Disable pageviews, product autocapture, replay, persistence and user identification. An allowlist redacts free text and preserves the SDK routing and JavaScript frame metadata required for ingestion.
- Forward optional browser configuration through source builds and GitHub image publishing. Wire private source-map uploads through a web-only BuildKit secret, and document operational monitoring and rollout.

Validation:
- Backend vet/build and full race tests passed against disposable local PostgreSQL.
- Frontend targeted lint, production build and all 11 unit tests passed.
- Local Chromium verified automatic exception capture, stripping of synthetic private values, no analytics events and no PostHog persistence. EU ingestion created the linked synthetic test issue recorded in docs/observability.md.
- Docker image build and Nginx syntax passed. A browser check of the image without PostHog configuration confirmed the app renders and emits no telemetry. No source maps are served in that configuration.
- Both deployment configuration checks and generated OpenAPI consistency passed.

Rollout: configure the public GitHub Actions variables listed in docs/observability.md, merge, wait for image publishing, then explicitly update the preview's pinned AMD64 tag and redeploy. External uptime monitors and Coolify notification delivery still need operator setup. The PostHog project has been renamed/configured with approval; public preview deployment has not changed.

Limits: private source-map uploads remain pending, so original-source stack resolution is not verified. Redacted error text reduces debugging detail. Vite reports a main bundle above its 500 KB warning threshold (about 810 KB / 249 KB gzip). The complete browser E2E suite and real alert delivery were not run locally.

body:
Android 员工端、会员端加上自动更新。两个 App 在蒲公英分发，但蒲公英的检查更新接口必须带账号 API Key。这个 Key 还能上传、删除应用，接口返回的下载地址里也带着它，所以不能打进 APK。改为由后端代查。

- **后端**：新增 `GET /api/app-update/android/{staff|member}?versionCode=N`，不用登录（`Operations/AppUpdates.cs`）。
  - 用 `Kunlun:Pgyer:ApiKey`、该 App 的 App Key 和已装的 versionCode 调蒲公英 `apiv2/app/check`。只回 `hasUpdate`、`versionName`、`versionCode`、`notes`、`force`、`url`。
  - 蒲公英说有新版、且新版的 versionCode（`buildVersionNo`）大于已装版本时才算有更新，刚装好的版本不会再提示。
  - `url` 取 `appURl`；它不是 HTTPS 的 `www.pgyer.com` / `pgyer.com` 页面时改用短链接 `buildShortcutUrl`，并去掉查询参数。带 Key 的 `downloadURL` 不转给 App，日志只记蒲公英的 code 和 message。
  - 答复按（App，已装版本）缓存 10 分钟，失败只缓存 1 分钟；接口有每分钟 60 次的限流 `app-update`。没配 Key、蒲公英出错或答复不完整时一律回「没有更新」。
  - 两个 App Key 不是机密，写在代码里，可用 `Kunlun:Pgyer:StaffAppKey` / `MemberAppKey` 覆盖。`Kunlun:Pgyer:BaseUrl` 只在本机联调时指向模拟服务。
- **App**（两个 App 各一份 `AppUpdate`、`UpdateChecker`）：
  - 启动时检查一次，之后回到前台时最多每小时一次；检查失败 5 分钟后再试。
  - 弹窗「发现新版本 x.y.z」，显示更新说明和当前版本。「立即更新」用系统浏览器打开蒲公英安装页，只打开 HTTPS 的 pgyer.com 页面。「以后再说」或返回键：这个版本 24 小时内不再提示。强制更新关不掉，回到 App 就再弹出。
  - 版本改为 `versionCode` 2 / `versionName` 1.1.0。1.0.0 没有检查更新，已装 1.0.0 的手机要手动装一次 1.1.0。
- **部署**：API 容器原来只在 `internal: true` 的 `backend` 网络上，不能出网。两套 compose 给它加了只用于出网的 `egress` 网络，并从 `.env` 传入 `KUNLUN_PGYER_API_KEY`（可选，不设置就不提示更新）。数据库仍只在内部网络。

## 测试

- 后端新增 `AppUpdateTests`，用一个模拟的蒲公英测三类情况：没配 Key；有新版、缓存、两个 App Key、各种安装页地址；蒲公英各种失败。另外检查回给 App 的内容里没有 Key 和 `downloadURL`。本机全部 83 个后端测试通过。
- Android 两端新增 `AppUpdateTest`，测解析、只开 pgyer 页面和「以后再说」规则；debug、release 构建、单元测试、lint 通过。
- Android 17 模拟器连本机后端，后端的 `BaseUrl` 指向本机模拟的蒲公英：
  - 两个 App 都弹出更新，后端带各自的 App Key 和 `buildVersion=2` 去查。
  - 「以后再说」后重启不再提示。
  - 强制更新关不掉，点「立即更新」打开 Chrome 访问 `https://www.pgyer.com/…`，回到 App 再次弹出。
  - 已是最新版、后端停掉时都不弹窗。
- al 上桥接网络的容器能访问蒲公英接口（不带 Key 时返回 `code 1001`）。真实蒲公英的完整答复要等服务器配好 Key 后在测试环境核对。

## 请评审留意

- **与 #46 的关系**：#46 也在 `docs/architecture.md` 末尾加了「第 16 节」。后合并的一方会有文档冲突，要把自己那节改成第 17 节。`Program.cs` 的改动位置不重叠，能自动合并。#46 合并后，这里的 `app-update` 限流也按真实客户端 IP 计数。
- **#46 的信任前提**：#46 的注释写着 API 只接在内部网络上，所以只信任 nginx 这一跳。本 PR 给 API 加了 `egress` 网络，但这个网络上只有 API 自己，Docker 默认隔离不同网络，从这里能连到 API 的只有宿主机（宿主机本来就可信）。两个都合并后，那句注释最好顺手改准确。
- **部署前**：服务器 `.env` 要写入 `KUNLUN_PGYER_API_KEY`（由用户在服务器上输入，不经过对话和仓库）。新 compose 第一次 `up` 时会创建 `kunlun_egress` / `kunlun-test_egress` 网络并重建 api 容器。建议先发测试环境，用 `/api/app-update/android/staff?versionCode=1` 核对真实答复，再发生产。

author: chrisromanmiller
body:
## Problem

When current main has no published TauCeti outputs, `warm_host_build_caches` walks main's history and accepts the newest revision the cache has. Right after a Mathlib bump lands, and while CI has not yet published the new main, that is a **pre-bump** revision. Its outputs match almost nothing in current main, because every module's inputs changed. The round starts anyway, and the agent's `lake build` recompiles the whole library locally. Stopping on a miss exists to prevent exactly that.

Observed on a 4-core worker on 2026-11-17. After the Mathlib bump in TauCeti #39404 (2026-11-16 23:48 UTC), a fix round's cache warm-up missed the bump merge and the three revisions after it, then accepted `7cbfff3e`, which was committed 11½ hours before the bump. The agent's `lake build` then ran for over 3 hours, recompiling unrelated parts of the library.

## Fix

Only accept main revisions whose `lake-manifest.json` pins the same Mathlib as current main (`shared_mathlib._manifest_pin`). Skipped revisions are never fetched. If no matching revision is cached, the round stops exactly as it does for a miss. The message now also says how many older revisions were skipped for a different pin.

## Tests

- `tests/host_build_cache.py`: new `stale-main` scenario. Current main is uncached and the only cached main revision predates a Mathlib bump. The round must stop without launching the agent, and the stale revision must never be fetched. The existing rebase fallback is unchanged, because all its revisions share main's pin.
- `tests/host_build_cache.py` and `tests/expanded_cache.py` pass on Linux. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

## Not covered

When the round's HEAD *is* main (for example a fresh authoring round), the first `lake cache get --max-revs=N` lets Lake walk history itself, and it can accept a pre-bump revision the same way. Fixing that means taking over that walk, which changes more behaviour, so I've left it for a separate PR.

body:
<!-- next-upgrade: security; path="." -->

## Summary

Dependency-only security update of Next.js from **16.4.3 to 16.4.6**. The
installed 16.4.3 sits inside the vulnerable range (`>=16.3.0 <=16.4.4`) of
[GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h) —
information disclosure across root params when a `use cache` function is called
through `unstable_cache()` (moderate). The npm advisory service reports 16.4.6
as unaffected; `16.4.5` was skipped in favor of the newest patch on the line.

Draft: a merge to `main` is the release approval under DEC-2026-037 and deploys
to production, so this is for review first.

## Scope

**In**
- `package.json` — `next` pinned to exactly `16.4.6` (the repository already
  pins it), and `package-lock.json` refreshed.
- `next.config.ts` — `experimental.agentUpgrade: "security"`, so build and dev
  upgrade reminders stay limited to published security advisories.
- `scripts/build-worker-config.test.mjs` — the default-shape assertion now
  expects the new `experimental` block.

**Out**
- No application code, route, schema, migration, data contract, pricing,
  eligibility, matching, review, finance, auth, email or configuration
  semantics change. No other dependency changed. This is a same-major update,
  so no codemod and no major-version migration guide applies.

## The config change

`experimental.agentUpgrade` is supported in 16.4.6
(`next/dist/server/config-shared.d.ts`), so nothing was skipped. Adding it
makes the `experimental` block unconditional, where it used to exist only when
`MERCURIUS_BUILD_WORKERS` was set. That opt-in concurrency limit is preserved
and merged into the same block rather than replaced; its validation and its
`cpus` behavior are unchanged, and the existing unit tests for both the
accepted and rejected worker counts still pass untouched.

## Fixes the intermittent build stop

PR #171 reported builds exiting 1 after compiling and generating every page, on
a Next.js CLI notice that 16.4.3 "is affected by a known security
vulnerability", with retries exiting 0 on the same code. That was this
advisory's reminder: per `agentUpgrade.md`, when a coding agent runs
`next build`, the first eligible reminder stops the command and a prompt retry
continues with a warning. Both builds here exited 0 with no such notice, so the
stop is resolved rather than suppressed.

## Verification

Run at `f94e27d` on 2026-11-17, Node 24.17.0, npm 11.13.0, WSL2, in a separate
git worktree based on `origin/main` (`44751a9`).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx next --version` | `Next.js v16.4.6` (exact target) |
| advisory recheck, npm bulk endpoint | `{}` for 16.4.6; GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h for 16.4.3 |
| `npm run typecheck` | No errors |
| `npm run lint` | No findings |
| `npm run scan:secrets` | Passed |
| `npm run test:unit` | 67 files, 973 of 973 |
| `npm run build` (synthetic public values) | Exit 0, twice, no advisory stop |

**Not run:** `npm run test:a11y`, `npm run test:visual`, and the database
tests. No data contract or rendered output changed; CI on this PR is the full
run.

## Things a reviewer should know

1. **Local `main` was stale.** This branch is based on `origin/main`
   (`44751a9`), not the local `main` ref, which was behind at `b7b0d08`.
2. **`NODE_ENV` in the shell.** The session had `NODE_ENV=production` exported,
   which makes a plain `npm install` silently skip devDependencies and leaves
   the verification lanes uninstallable. Installs and checks here ran with it
   unset. Worth knowing for anyone reproducing this locally.
3. **One unit test was edited.** `build-worker-config.test.mjs` asserted
   `toEqual({})` for the unset default, which the new `experimental` block makes
   false. The expectation was updated to the new default shape; no assertion was
   weakened or removed.
4. **No TRACE entry taken.** This is a dependency security patch with no
   behavior change, and Phase 7 work may claim the next number. Say if you want
   one recorded.

author: aaangelmartin
body:
## Why

Review of #282 found three problems with project folders: the oldest project of a name was picked by local row order, so devices could disagree (#324); two different folders with the same last name silently shared one project, and re-adding a folder said "which the space already had" (#325); and the lookup ran before a deferred transaction, so two writers could both create a project of one name (#326).

## What changed

- `project_named` orders by `created_at`, then id, so an older project imported later wins on every device.
- `add_folder` opens its transaction with `TransactionBehavior::Immediate` and makes the lookup inside it.
- `add_folder` records the project a project folder holds in the folder's `project` rule (the project node id), and `folder_project` (used by the service listing, the CLI and the Mac app) reads that record. A renamed project keeps its folder; a deleted one leaves the folder with none.
- Choosing the project for a new folder: its own name (`api`), then that name with its parent folders (`api (b)`, `api (w - b)`), then numbered (`api (w - b) 2`, ...). It joins the first such project no other folder holds, or creates the first name the space does not have, and reports the project of its own name it passed over and the folders holding it. A new folder never shares a project.
- Clients cannot set the `project` rule: `prepare_folder` drops one passed in and keeps the recorded one when a folder changes.
- Folders added before this hold the project of their own name, as they did. The first `add_folder` records that for each of them, as a `system` change, before deciding, so no new folder or project can move them.
- `FolderProject` gains `already_held`, `passed_over` and `shared_with` (service JSON and FFI too).
- `knode folders add` and the Mac Folders screen say "already holds", "named after its parent folder too: the project api already holds the files of ~/w/a/api", the same when the folder joins a parent-named project the space had, and warn about sharing. The Mac confirmation explains the rule.
- CHANGELOG entry for project folders updated.

## Decisions

- Joining rule for #325: a folder joins an existing project of its name only if no other folder holds it (a project an import or a person made, with no folder, is joined). Otherwise it gets a distinct project named with the parent folder, such as `api (b)`; then the grandparent (`api (w - b)`), then a number.
- Which project a folder holds is stored, not derived from the path (review finding: deriving it let `~/x/a/api` move `~/w/a/api` onto `api (a)`). It is stored in the existing `folders.rules` JSON as `project`, so no schema version is needed: readers already keep rule keys they do not know, and an older reader still finds the project by name. Specified in knodemd/format#37.
- Folders without the record keep the old rule (the project of their own name), and are recorded on the first folder add, as a `system` change. Folders that already shared a project keep sharing it; nothing is moved, and re-adding one names the others in `shared_with`.
- A project made by hand with a parent-based name, such as `api (a)`, moves no folder; it is joined only by a new folder whose plain name is taken and that it fits, since it holds no folder.
- Changing a folder by id (such as turning capture off) reads its project and does not report `already_held`; only adding a folder again does.

## Docs

- [ ] Nothing users see changed
- knodemd/docs#79 (CLI and Mac app), knodemd/format#37 (the `project` rule)

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` (`chats::slack::tests::emphasis_stays_linear`, a 5 s timing test in knode-ingest, failed once under the full parallel run and passes alone; not touched here)
- [x] `project_named_returns_the_oldest_by_creation`: an older project imported after a local one wins, and a project folder finds it.
- [x] `a_new_folder_never_moves_another_folder_to_its_project`: the review repro (`~/w/a/api` then `~/x/a/api`: `api` and `api (a)`, the first keeps `api`), same-parent collisions up to a numbered name, and re-adding each says it already holds its project.
- [x] `a_project_made_by_hand_with_a_parent_name_moves_no_folder`.
- [x] `two_folders_with_the_same_name_get_their_own_projects`: removing a folder keeps its project and moves no other folder.
- [x] `folders_added_before_the_record_keep_their_project`: legacy folders keep `api` after `api (a)` is made by hand, are recorded on the next add, and still share it.
- [x] `clients_cannot_set_the_project_of_a_folder`.
- [x] `concurrent_writers_create_one_project_of_a_name`: two threads with their own connections, 8 rounds; with a deferred transaction it fails.
- [x] CLI test: re-add message, `site (Archive)` for a second `site` folder.
- [x] `xcodebuild -scheme Knode -destination 'platform=macOS' build test`

Closes #324
Closes #325
Closes #326

author: echoofdawn
body:
## ELI16

Each machine restarts itself about once a week in the small hours. The owner now has two controls over that:

- **Skip once.** No restart for the next 72 hours. A second tap later moves it 72 hours from that tap. "Unskip" undoes it.
- **Change window.** Pick the night hours the restart may use, for example 01:00 to 04:00. The window must be at least 2 hours long, because the restart sits an hour after the window opens and needs room around it. It applies from the next night. A night already announced keeps its time.

Both are kept in one place per machine, so every agent on that machine follows the same choice. Each change is recorded with who made it and when. Neither control can start a restart: they only make one later or move it.

Today the weekly restart still runs as a rehearsal on paper, so these controls shape the rehearsal. The real scheduled restart will read the same record.

## What changed

- `planner.ts`: `validWindow`, `withControls`, `isSkipped`, `SKIP_MS` (72 h).
- `HostMaintenanceStore`: `readControls()` and `changeControls()` on `~/.instar/host-maintenance/controls.json`, under the host maintenance lock, keeping the last 20 changes.
- `DrainRehearsal`: reads the controls each tick (a new `controls` dep). It opens no night while skipped, and plans from the owner's window. It has `skip()`, `unskip()` and `setWindow()`, and `status().controls`.
- Routes `POST /machine-maintenance/skip`, `/unskip` and `/window` (`{window:{start,end}}` or `{reset:true}`). Each needs a recent dashboard PIN unlock (`X-Instar-Operator-Session`), and each is registered machine-local in `WriteDomainRegistry`.

Not in this slice: the dashboard "Machine care" page that presents these, and agent awareness (which ships with that page, so no agent is told about a control the owner has no surface for). Also not here: the app's device-signed routes, Skip on the final-night question, and Skip closing an episode that is already draining as `rolled`. Today that episode is a paper rehearsal.

## Tests

- Unit (`tests/unit/machine-maintenance-controls.test.ts`, 10): window validity both sides, the owner window against the config, the skip boundary, no night while skipped and the first night after, unskip, a skip during an open night, the next night on a new window, a window changed during an open night keeping its T-0, one host record across two agents with a capped history, and a malformed file.
- Integration (`machine-maintenance-route.test.ts`, 12/12): 401 without a bearer, without a PIN session and with a wrong one (nothing changed), 503 when dark, and skip/unskip/window/bad window/reset through the real route, shown in the status.
- E2E (`machine-maintenance-lifecycle.test.ts`, 5/5): the routes are alive and PIN-gated on the real AgentServer, a skip shows in the status, and server.ts wires the same host store.
- The watch-only guarantee and the planner and rehearsal suite pass (82/82).

Overlap note: #3301, #3298, #3280 and #3236 also touch `WriteDomainRegistry.ts` / `routes.ts` / `server.ts`, for unrelated features (trust approvals, project apps). Each only adds rows, so there is no shared logic.

Constitution counterpart: none: this implements Part F (operator controls) of the approved machine-self-maintenance spec (CMT-1203, first slice). It adds no new principle or standard text.

Side-effects review: `upgrades/side-effects/machine-care-controls.md`.

feat: api-keys command for managing API keys

## Summary

Closes #12

Adds the `api-keys` command group for managing the API keys that
authenticate `/metrics` calls, matching the Kuma 1.23.17
`api-key-socket-handler` events (unchanged on 2.x):

- `api-keys list` prints the pushed `apiKeyList` rows as `[{ id, name,
expires, active, status }]` sorted by id — the stored secret `key` is
never sent, `active` arrives as the BOOLEAN column's 0/1 and prints as a
boolean, `userID` / `createdDate` are pushed but not printed
- `api-keys add --name <n> [--expires <datetime>]` sends `addAPIKey`
with the APIKeyDialog.vue payload `{ name, expires, active: 1 }` and
prints the one-time clear key (`uk<id>_<nanoid(40)>`) with a stderr
warning — the server stores only its hash, so no later command can show
it. `--expires` takes the same offset-free local ISO datetime as the
maintenance flags, is sent in the datepicker's `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`
spelling, refuses dates before the CLI host's today like the UI's
minDate, and omitting it sends `expires: null` ("Don't expire")
- `api-keys enable|disable <id>` sends `enableAPIKey` / `disableAPIKey`;
`api-keys delete <id> --yes` sends `deleteAPIKey` — without `--yes` it
exits 2 before connecting

All three mutations answer ok even when the id matches nothing, and
enable/disable do not even scope by user, so each checks the pushed
`apiKeyList` first and exits 1 on an unknown id instead of trusting
Kuma's answer.

The local-datetime helpers move from maintenance.ts to lib.ts so both
command groups share the offset-free parsing, calendar validation and
field-wise comparison. The fake Kuma answers all five api-key events,
pushes `apiKeyList` after login and models the clear-key/hash split,
the active flag and the computed status. `docs/design/cli.md` documents
the event mappings and command contract; `docs/design/kuma2.md` notes
the handlers are unchanged on 2.x; README lists the command group.

test:integration` — pass locally (78 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, 79 tests);

diff gate pass in CI

body:
Outlook's own window stopped responding while anything watched Titip's status. Measured on the build PC with all processors busy: 90 s without asking Titip, Outlook answered in 22 of 22 looks; 95 s asking the PC page's status, one count of the folders ran 42 s and Outlook's window was hung in 2 of 20 looks. The mailbox has 8 data files and Titip counted the Inbox and Sent of each again every 10 s.

- Counts are kept for five minutes. A send or a saved draft drops them.
- Address and name are asked once per connection to Outlook.

Checked here: 170 unit and server tests (4 new), 73 browser steps.

body:
## Değişiklik ve gerekçe
ML-28 kapsamında kayıt ekranı arayüzü, kayıt doğrulama mantığı ve `POST /api/v1/auth/register` API bağlantısı eklendi; giriş ekranı ile kayıt ekranı arasındaki navigasyon akışı tamamlandı.

- Stitch referansına (`screen_2.png` / `code_2.html`) ve giriş ekranının ortak tasarım diline uygun Java/XML kayıt ekranı (`fragment_register.xml`, `register_strings.xml`, `register_back.xml`, `register_back_button.xml`) eklendi. Backend sözleşmesinde karşılığı bulunmayan Ad Soyad, sosyal giriş (Google/Apple), kullanım koşulları onayı ve 3 bölmeli şifre gücü göstergesi tasarımdan çıkarıldı.
- Ortak e-posta biçimi ve uzunluk kuralları (`AuthInputRules`) tek sınıfa taşındı; şifre doğrulaması 15–128 Unicode karakter (`codePointCount`) kuralına göre `RegisterViewModel` ve `RegisterUiState` içinde kurgulandı. Fragment yalnızca durumu çizer ve kullanıcı olaylarını iletir.
- `RegisterFragment`, `RemoteAuthRepository` üzerinden kayıt isteğini gönderir. `EMAIL_IN_USE` sunucu yanıtı doğrudan e-posta alanının altında gösterilip odaklanır; ağ, 429 ve 503 gibi alana bağlı olmayan hatalar formdaki genel hata satırında gösterilir.
- Backend kayıt işleminde oturum açmadığı için token işlenmez; başarılı kayıtta şifre alanları temizlenir, Activity seviyesinde `Snackbar` bilgi mesajı gösterilir ve `popBackStack()` ile giriş ekranına dönülür.
- `nav_graph.xml` üzerinden giriş ekranına *"Hesabın yok mu? Kayıt ol"* bağlantısı eklendi; giriş isteği sürerken bağlantı kilitlenir. `MainActivity` üzerindeki `isAuthScreen()` yardımcı metoduyla alt menü gizleme ve klavye alt boşluğu kayıt ekranını da kapsayacak şekilde genişletildi.
- Gerçek giriş akışı tamamlandığı için Profil sekmesindeki geçici *"Giriş ekranını önizle"* butonu, `profile_preview_login` metni ve ilgili navigasyon geçişi kaldırıldı.
- Canlı testlerde yakalanan üç arayüz kusuru giderildi: şifre göster/gizle düğmesinin `setTransformationMethod()` tetiklemesiyle doğrulama hatalarını silmesi engellendi, fiziksel klavye Enter tuşunun odağı bir sonraki alana kaydırması tuş bırakma (`ACTION_UP`) olayında gönderim yapılarak çözüldü ve şifre kural notu ile *Şifre (Tekrar)* etiketi arasına `ml_space_sm` boşluğu eklendi.
- `README.md` (ML-07 demo adımı ve mobil uygulama özeti) ve `docs/architecture.md` (doğrulama, hata gösterimi, navigasyon kuralları ve bilinen sınırlar) güncellendi.

## İlgili issue / Trello kartı
- ML-28 — Kayıt ve giriş ekranlarını API ile bağla
- Trello: https://trello.com/c/8UMY2Qxy/17-ml-28-kay%C4%B1t-ve-giri%C5%9F-ekranlar%C4%B1n%C4%B1-api-ile-ba%C4%9Fla

## Doğrulama
- `RegisterViewModelTest`: 17 yeni birim testi eklendi ve geçti.
- `testDebugUnitTest`: Toplam 67 JVM birim testi geçti; hata veya atlama yok.
- `assembleDebug`: Başarılı.
- `lintDebug`: 0 sorun (`warningsAsErrors = true` aktif; 2. commit'te eklenen geçici `tools:ignore="UnusedResources"` işaretleri 3. commit'te kaldırıldıktan sonra da temiz geçti).
- Güncel APK ile emülatörde (`Pixel 7a AVD`) Anılar → Giriş → *"Kayıt ol"* geçişi, her iki auth ekranında alt menünün gizlenmesi ve Profil sekmesinden önizleme butonunun kaldırılması doğrulandı.
- Boş formda üç alanın hata metni, geçersiz e-posta ve 15 karakterden kısa şifre uyarıları, eşleşmeyen şifre hatası, ilk hatalı alana odaklanma (buton, ekran klavyesi "Bitti" ve fiziksel Enter tuşuyla), şifre göster/gizle sırasında hata metninin korunması, backend kapalıyken genel hata satırında ağ hatası görünümü ve geri dönüş (`popBackStack`) akışı emülatörde doğrulandı.

## Bilinen eksikler
- Yerel ortamda Docker Desktop / PostgreSQL servisi çalıştırılmadığı için backend gerektiren 3 uçtan uca senaryo (`EMAIL_IN_USE` sunucu yanıtı, başarılı kayıt sonrası `Snackbar` ve yeni hesapla giriş) canlı sunucu üzerinde henüz doğrulanmadı; ilgili tüm durumlar JVM birim testleriyle kapsanmaktadır.
- Kayıttan sonra girilen e-posta adresi giriş formuna otomatik aktarılmaz.
- Mevcut giriş API koduna dokunmama kararı gereği şifre göster/gizle düğmesinin doğrulama hatasını temizlemesi düzeltmesi yalnızca `RegisterFragment` içine uygulandı; `LoginFragment` üzerinde aynı davranış henüz güncellenmedi.
- Farklı ekran boyutları, büyük yazı tipi ayarı ve ekran döndürme davranışı ayrıca doğrulanmadı.

- [x] Gizli bilgi ve yerel SDK yolu içermiyor.
- [x] İlgili testler çalıştırıldı; çalıştırılamayanlar ve nedenleri yazıldı.
- [x] Kurulum veya mimari değişikliği belgelendi.

author: pjcarriel
body:
Tarea #5 del plan: base del frontend sobre la que cada uno arma su pantalla.

Closes #5

## Cambios
- **Conexión**: `environment.apiURL = 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1'` (+ `environment.development.ts` para `ng serve`).
- **Modelos**: `ActionResponse<T>`, `Rol` (`ADMIN`, `RECEPCIONISTA`), `LoginRequest` / `LoginResponse`.
- **Rutas**: todas las pantallas son hijas de `MenuComponent` (igual que en Facturación), cada una con su título de pestaña.
- **Pantallas**: dashboard, usuarios, tipos-habitacion, habitaciones, huespedes y reservas. Las que aún no existen muestran un aviso "en construcción" con el responsable y la tarea.
- **Menú lateral**: las opciones están en `layout/menu-component/menu-opciones.ts`, con `roles` y `listo`.
- **Indicador de API** en el menú: llama a `GET /api/v1/health` y muestra si el backend responde.
- **Diseño**: estilos globales en `styles.css` (colores, `.tarjeta`, `.btn`, `.etiqueta`) y componentes compartidos `app-icon`, `app-page-header` y `app-en-construccion`. Funciona en escritorio y en celular.

## Para cada uno al hacer su pantalla
1. Reemplazar `<app-en-construccion>` del componente por la tabla y el formulario.
2. Usar `<app-page-header>` para el título y las clases `btn btn-primario` / `tarjeta` para que todo se vea igual.
3. Cambiar `listo: true` en `menu-opciones.ts` para activar la opción del menú.

## Pruebas
- `ng build` (producción) sin advertencias.
- `ng test`: 2/2 (crea la app, renderiza el menú y el dashboard, y llama a `/health`).
- Revisado en Chrome en escritorio y en celular.
- El indicador de API mostrará "sin conexión" hasta que se mergee el PR #37, que agrega `/api/v1/health`.

## Mejoras de diseño (segundo commit)
- Menú lateral contraíble en escritorio y ruta de navegación en la barra superior.
- Dashboard con portada y acciones rápidas, indicadores con color, panel "Movimiento de hoy" y panel "Ocupación".
- Cada pantalla en construcción muestra una vista previa de su tabla con las columnas reales del módulo: sirve de guía para que todas las tablas se vean igual.
- Nuevas clases globales: `.tabla`, `.campo`, `.segmentos`, `.vacio`, `.tarjeta-cabecera` y estados `.estado-exito`, `.estado-peligro`, `.estado-aviso`.
