author: omara455
body:
## What's in this PR

**API layer** (`src/api/`)
- `client.ts` reads the base URL from `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`, attaches the Bearer token, and maps Laravel errors to one `ApiError` with a `kind`: `validation` (422 field messages), `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `conflict`, `throttled` (429), `network` and `server`. A 401 on any authenticated request triggers a **global logout**.
- **Mock mode:** an empty `API_BASE_URL` routes requests to `mock.ts`, which returns the same status codes and shapes as `docs/API.md`. Mock credentials are any email with the password `ftc-portal`. Other passwords get a 422, and 5 failures in a minute get a 429. An email starting with `offline` simulates a network error.
- `endpoints.ts` (`authApi`, `meApi`), `types.ts` (copied from API.md), `queryClient.ts` (no retries on 401/403/422), and `useMe()`.

**Auth** (`src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx`)
- The token is kept in SecureStore (localStorage on web, which is only used for screenshots). At boot it's restored without a network call, so the app opens offline. An expired token is caught by the first 401.
- `signOut` calls `POST /auth/logout` as a best effort, then clears the token and the query cache.
- The auth gate uses `Stack.Protected`. `/` redirects to login, screen 05, or tasks.

**Screens**
| # | Screen | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 01 / 02 | Login + error | Banner, red password border, highlighted forgot link, 429 and offline messages, eye toggle, apply link |
| 03 | Forgot password | Prefilled from login. The button enables for an email-shaped value. Always 204, so no account enumeration |
| 04 | Link sent | 45-second resend cooldown, «رجوع لتسجيل الدخول» |
| 05 | Notification permission | Shown once after the first login, **only when `flags.notifications` is on** (Phase 2). Asks for the OS permission; `POST /devices` is M6 |
| 30 | Logout sheet | Opened from a Settings stub (the full Settings screen is M4) |
| — | Tab shell | The custom floating TabBar on four tab stubs with their artboard headers |

**Tooling:** `npm run smoke` runs an 11-step Playwright check of the auth flow against the mock API, and CI now runs it. `shot.mjs` gained `--fill`, `--signed-in` and fill/click that only drive the app. On web, `useScreenInsets()` simulates the design's 47/34 insets so screenshots line up with the artboards. Also a `.gitattributes` (LF) and an `.env.example`.

## Design checks (web, 390×844, side by side)
01 Main, 02 LoginError, 03 ForgotPassword, 04 ForgotSent, 05 NotificationPermission and 30 LogoutConfirm all match within about 2pt. Fixes made along the way: label and link line height (design uses Cairo's default line height of about 1.875), sheet bottom padding, the icon halo on 04, and the browser focus outline on web inputs.

## Differences from the docs (the artboard wins)
- **SCREENS.md 04** says "shows the masked email"; the artboard shows the **full** email. I followed the artboard. Should SCREENS.md be updated, or should it be masked?
- **Layout vs CLAUDE.md:** `notifications-permission` lives at `app/` root, not in `(auth)`, because it's on the signed-in side of the gate. The logout sheet is a component, not a `(sheets)` route. CLAUDE.md is updated to match.

## Copy that needs sign-off (not in the design)
- 429 on login/forgot: «حاولت كثير. جرّب مرة ثانية بعد دقيقة.»
- Generic server error (5xx): «صار خلل عندنا. جرّب مرة ثانية بعد شوي.»
- Network error reuses the design's «ما فيه اتصال بالإنترنت».

## Checks
- `tsc --noEmit`, `expo lint`, `prettier --check`, `expo-doctor` (20/20) and `npm run smoke` (11/11) pass.
- ⚠️ Not checked on an Android device yet. That's the `docs/DEVICE.md` step.

author: andeeplus
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Video player store** docs recipe next to the existing video player, so #709 can decide whether accessor positions in `@ecopages/jsx` are worth shipping. The component form keeps the same player in one `createStore`, with path-aware `this.$.media.*` bindings. The original component on `main` is the baseline. This PR does not close #709.

The store form does not re-run `render()` while the clip plays, while seeking, or when mute or speed change. Clicking play still costs one render, same as the baseline, but for a different reason (see below). Mute and speed drop from one extra render to none.

The recipe is a variant of the Video player, not a copy: its component imports `video-player.data` and `video-player.loader`, `video-player.css` matches its tag, and its plain pattern is the Video player's plain pattern (`recipe="video-player"`). `recipe-files.ts` takes a script's shared tabs from the stem it imports them from, and `recipe-imports.test.ts` accepts a `<sibling>-<variant>` importing the sibling's data and loader.

## Measurements

Non-blank, non-comment lines of the component form: **490** (baseline) vs **507** (store). Reactive fields: **10 `@state`** vs **1 `createStore`**.

Extra `render()` calls after the player is ready (browser tests, 30 animation frames, no sleeps). A non-zero budget also accepts one more, for a second controller state in a later turn such as `buffering` before `playing`; locally both forms measured exactly the numbers below on every run.

| Scenario | Baseline | Store |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Play click | 1 | 1 |
| 30 frames while playing | 0 | 0 |
| Seek | 0 | 0 |
| Mute | 1 | 0 |
| Rate | 1 | 0 |

The baseline's play render comes from `render()` reading `stage` and `playing`. The store's comes from the error panel's `hidden={media.stage.map(...)}`: `getBindingPart` in `packages/jsx/src/factory/jsx-factory.ts` reads the snapshot of a binding on a standard boolean attribute (`hidden`, `inert`, `disabled`, ...) to pick a presence binding, and that read subscribes `render()`. It holds for `@state` bindings too (`hidden={this.$.flag}` re-runs `render()`), and `bool:hidden` does not. The fullscreen button's `hidden` costs one render on connect for the same reason.

The development warnings (hot field, redundant path) say nothing about these scenarios: a hot field needs 30 renders within a second, and store path writes never warn.

The original component already binds the clock with `this.$`, so per-frame position was not a `render()` cost. The store's win is mute and speed.

## Accessor positions

Places that look like a multi-field expression, and whether an accessor (`{() => …}` in a child, `attr`, `bool`, `classes` or `style`) would remove them:

| Workaround | Would an accessor remove it? |
| --- | --- |
| `muted ? 0 : volume` written to the volume slider | No. `RuiSlider` snapshots `value`; the host writes it by hand and `render()` reads it from a private field. |
| `seekValueText(position, duration)` on the seek thumb | No. The thumb is inside `rui-slider`; a host accessor cannot own it. |
| `stage` from controller status | No. It is one store path, written in `onState`. |
| Clock `formatMediaTime(position)` | No. `this.$.media.position.map(formatMediaTime)` already covers a single field. |
| `pressed={this.$.media.playing}` | No. `RuiButton.pressed` is typed `boolean`; the recipe casts so the binding reaches native `aria-pressed`. |
| `max` / `disabled` / `value` on the sliders | No. The view helper stamps them from the props of the render that drew it, so a later render puts a stale value back; `render()` reads private fields and `requestUpdate()` runs once when the clip becomes seekable. |
| The play-click render | No. It is the boolean-attribute snapshot read above, a `@ecopages/jsx` fix (read it untracked), not a missing JSX position. |

**Recommendation: do not ship accessors from this pilot.** `map` and one store already get mute, speed, seek and per-frame play to zero extra renders, and the last render is a runtime bug. The remaining work is catalog helpers that forward bindings (`pressed`, `max`, `disabled`, `value`), not a function in a JSX position.

Bundle cost if they still ship: `packages/jsx` `pnpm size:report` today:

| Bundle | Raw | Gzip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| client | 45.24 / 45.70 KB | 14.86 / 15.09 KB |
| index | 45.42 / 45.90 KB | 15.05 / 15.25 KB |
| jsx-runtime | 13.98 / 14.35 KB | 5.26 / 5.55 KB |

Accessors would need the factory to accept a function in those positions (jsx-runtime) and the DOM renderer to run it as a live sink (`dom-render`, in the client and index bundles). Estimate **+0.8–1.5 KB minified / +0.3–0.6 KB gzip** in total, against 0.20–0.29 KB of gzip headroom, so the budgets would have to rise. `@ecopages/jsx` stays independent of signals; tracking would still need a computation (in Radiant or a jsx hook).

## What the framework still lacks

- **JSX runtime:** a binding on a standard boolean attribute subscribes the `render()` that builds it (above). Out of scope here.
- **Catalog:** `RuiSlider` snapshots `max`, `disabled` and `value`. `RuiButton.pressed` does not type a binding. Accessors would not fix either. Recommendation: leave for a catalog change, not this PR.
- **Warnings:** hot-field and redundant-path warnings do not cover store path writes. This recipe did not need them.
- **Path-keyed `@onUpdated` / a host-scoped watch:** not needed here. `MediaController` `onState` / `onProgress` write the store.

## Review fixes

- A render reset the store form's seek thumb to 0 and its volume to 1 (`value={0}` / `value={1}`), so muting and then pressing Play showed full volume while muted. Fixed with private `position` / `level` fields, and the shared redraw test now covers it.
- The two component test files are one suite (`test/video-player-component.ts`); the redraw test forces `requestUpdate()`, which the store form needs because a rate click no longer renders it. The 30-frame count checks that the clip moved; the warning checks and the source-text test are gone.
- Removed the copied data, loader, plain script, markup and stylesheet, and their duplicate plain test.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @ecopages/radiant-ui-docs test` (984 passed)
- `pnpm --filter @ecopages/radiant-ui-docs build`
- `packages/jsx` `pnpm size:report`

Refs #709

author: sniezka1927
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #11033

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Small improvement or alignment, with no change to how a feature works
- [ ] New provider, MCP app, or connector
- [ ] Translation or documentation
- [ ] New feature or change to existing behavior (needs an approved issue)

## What changed

`create_agent` with no provider and no model gives the new agent the caller's model only when the model list contains that model. While the caller's provider listed no model, or a Custom agent such as Kiro had not loaded its list yet, the new agent started on the user's default provider (here OpenCode / Pixtral Large), and its first task ran there with no message.

Now, in these two cases, the call fails with a text that the calling agent can act on: `Your model "<model>" is not in the model list now, so the new agent cannot start on it. Try again in a few seconds, or set provider and model to a model that list_models shows.` OpenBot never puts the new agent on another provider. Other projects use the same rule: OpenCode, Codex and Hermes copy the parent's model as it is, and oh-my-pi never replaces it with another provider's model.

Unchanged: a caller whose provider lists other models but no longer lists its model still gets the user's default, as #1211 designed. An explicit provider or model works as before.

Surfaces: backend tool router (`src/backend/agent/openbot-tool-router.ts`), one new `error.agent.*` key in all 15 catalogs, `docs/architecture/agents.md`, release notes. No renderer, IPC contract, mobile or migration change. The tool runs on the host, so a joined server works the same when it runs this version.

Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code.

## Verification

- [x] Narrow checks for what changed: `biome check` on the changed files, `bun run typecheck:node`, `bun run i18n:check`; the pre-commit hook ran the typecheck projects that the i18n change selects
- [x] Surfaces touched are named under "What changed"
- [x] A feature for agents, chats, channels, routines or server settings also works on a joined server, or "What changed" says why it is local only
- [x] Relevant manual smoke test completed, or not applicable
- [x] No credentials, private data, generated output, or real user files are included

Smoke test: a temporary script (not committed) ran the real agent service and tool router with the fake Codex app-server from `scripts/agent-profile-accounts-e2e.ts`. The fake's model list could be emptied during the run, and the fake called `openbot.create_agent` as a model does.

| # | Feature | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Full list: `create_agent` with no model copies the caller's model | pass | New agent `codex` / `gpt-6-luna`, same as the caller |
| 2 | Empty list: `create_agent` with no model refuses | pass | Tool result `success: false`, error `Your model "gpt-6-luna" is not in the model list now, …` |
| 3 | Empty list: no agent is created | pass | Agent count did not change |
| 4 | List back: `create_agent` copies the caller's model again | pass | New agent `codex` / `gpt-6-luna` |
| 5 | Existing profile tool E2E | pass | `bun run test:agent-profile-accounts`: PASS |
| 6 | Custom agent (Kiro CLI over ACP) on macOS | not checked | Needs the Kiro CLI and a signed-in Kiro account. The `acp` branch is the same condition, read from the code. |

## Risk and security impact

None. No change to permissions, IPC, file system, persistence or network access. A `create_agent` call that before created an agent on the wrong provider now returns an error that the agent can act on.

author: codekiln
body:
Closes #454. Part of #448.

`mise run microfreak:write-patch DESC --base N [--slot N --backup-dir DIR]` writes a patch described in the panel's own words into a preset: `oscillator`, `filter`, `envelope`, `cycling_envelope`, `lfo` (including `hz`), `glide` (Time seconds, Rate seconds per octave, Sync division), `keyboard` (bend range, press mode, key/arp mode, velo amp mod, scale, root), `voice` (paraphonic, unison, chord offsets, preset volume), `arp` BPM, `matrix` (routes by source and destination, `semitones` on Pitch, Assign columns filled from a destination name), `fields` for anything else, and `sequence` through the existing sequence writer. Without `--slot` it previews; the report gives each changed setting before and after in panel terms.

- [Microfreak/Patch/Write a patch](https://github.com/codekiln/logseq-encode-garden/blob/claude/454-microfreak-write-patch/pages/Microfreak___Patch___Write%20a%20patch.md) is the agent's entry page: steps, every description key, how to read musical words, and three worked examples written to slots 503–505 and played with `microfreak:probe`.
- The new `microfreak-patch` skill points agents at that page (generated for Claude, Copilot and Codex with `mise exec -- rulesync generate --features skills`).
- More measured on the way and added to [Microfreak/Patch/Storage](https://github.com/codekiln/logseq-encode-garden/blob/claude/454-microfreak-write-patch/pages/Microfreak___Patch___Storage.md): filter type, LFO shapes, Cycling Envelope modes and Amp Mod follow MicroFreak Reader's order; LFO Sync on ignores the LFO rate; the free LFO rate is 0.14–21.9 Hz over stored 0.1–0.8, roughly doubling per 0.1; Keyboard Octave does not move notes arriving over MIDI.
- Fix: `microfreak:probe` now reads YAML scripts whose events use `on:` and `off:`, which YAML 1.1 parses as true and false.

## Checks

author: mattinannt
body:
Fixes ENG-7334

## What & why

**Was:** In the oxlint migration (formbricks/formbricks#10056), the human reviewer caught four gaps that an agent self-review would likely have found. One came from an inline `/* eslint rule: … */` comment that oxlint silently ignores. A `turbo.json` comment also broke tests that live far from that file.

**Now:** Lint fails on inline ESLint config comments, agents run a `code-review` self-review before opening a PR, and the docs point at the tests that guard `turbo.json`.

- `formbricks/no-inline-lint-config` is on in every tier. It reports `/* eslint <rule>: … */`, `/* eslint-env */`, `/* global(s) */` and `/* exported */`, and still allows `eslint-disable` directives. No existing file trips it.
- The `CODING_STANDARDS.md` checklist asks a tool replacement to keep every old behaviour or list the drop under Open gaps.
- The template's agent note accepts `withheld` when the harness forbids recording the model id. `docs/agents/pull-requests.md` says the same.

## Where to look

- [`packages/config-oxlint/plugins/formbricks.mjs`](https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/blob/claude/elegant-bardeen-knjxqx/packages/config-oxlint/plugins/formbricks.mjs): the rule and its pattern
- [`docs/agents/pull-requests.md`](https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/blob/claude/elegant-bardeen-knjxqx/docs/agents/pull-requests.md): the new self-review step

## Breaking changes

- [ ] This PR contains breaking changes

None. Developer tooling and docs only.

## Migrations & env

- none

## How this was tested

Rerun: `pnpm lint && pnpm vitest run --config vitest.root.config.mts scripts/inline-lint-config.test.ts`

**Coverage**

| Behaviour | How | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline config comments fail lint | unit (guard) `scripts/inline-lint-config.test.ts` | 6 comment forms reported in library and next tiers; 8 cases fail without the rule |
| Disable directives, line comments and other block comments stay allowed | unit (guard) same file | No report on `eslint-disable`, `// eslint …` or a block comment that only mentions eslint |
| No existing file trips the rule | manual | `pnpm lint:code` clean, no measurable slowdown (15–20s warm) |
| `turbo.json` guard command in the doc | manual | `pnpm --filter @formbricks/web exec vitest run lib/turbo-`: 5 files, 26 tests pass |
| Pre-PR `code-review` step (`docs/agents/pull-requests.md`) | manual | Followed on this PR: Standards and Spec passes ran; findings fixed in `9f909b2`, `c9c5fb3` |
| Tool-replacement check and `withheld` note | manual | Template, `pull-requests.md` and `CODING_STANDARDS.md` read for agreement; the spec pass caught one mismatch, fixed in `9f909b2` |

**Open gaps**

- The guidance changes are prose for agents and reviewers; no automated check enforces the self-review step or the tool-replacement rule. They take effect on the next PR that follows them.
- The root config enables no rules, so root `scripts/` and the `config-*` packages (this plugin included) are not checked by the new rule. Linting them is tracked in ENG-7329.
- A block comment that starts with `global ` or `eslint ` as prose (`/* global state lives here */`) is reported. ESLint reads such comments the same way.

<details><summary>Out of scope</summary>

The retro's environment findings are not repo changes: the cloud environment runs Node 22 against `.nvmrc`'s 24, and `hyperfine` is not installed.
</details>

**Risks**

- none

author: leifdenby
body:
Lets you select text in the reading pane and copy it to the system clipboard.

## UX

- **Mouse**: click-drag over the text in the reading pane selects it (Textual's built-in selection, which `Static` already supports; clicking also focuses the pane). Double-click selects all the pane's text, header included.
- **`y`** or **`Ctrl+C`** (reading pane focused): copy the selection. Shows "Copied N characters"; with nothing selected, a bell plus a hint ("drag over the text…, or Y for the whole email").
- **`Y`**: copy the whole body of the email shown, *as displayed*: the formatted HTML rendering as plain text, or the plain-text version after `H`.
- A mouse selection is dropped whenever the pane's content changes (another email, `e`, `H`, loading…), so `y` never copies stale offsets from the previous email.
- No conflicts: `y`/`Y` weren't bound in the app or the preview; `Ctrl+C` in the preview previously fell through to Textual's screen copy (silent) / app "press Ctrl+Q to quit" hint. Scrolling, links, `h` focus, and the email actions are unchanged.
- Documented in README (Reading pane section + project layout), the `?` help overlay (READING PANE), and the preview status-bar hint (`y/Y copy`).

## Clipboard mechanism

`EwstuiApp.copy_to_clipboard` now does both:
1. Textual's own: keeps the app clipboard (Ctrl+V / vim `p`) and sends OSC 52 to the terminal (works over SSH in iTerm2 with clipboard access allowed, kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty; not macOS Terminal).
2. On macOS, also `pbcopy` (new `ewstui/clipboard.py`; `subprocess.run` with an arg list, 2 s timeout, UTF-8 forced via `LANG` when the locale isn't UTF-8; failures are logged, never raised).

This also makes vim yanks in the compose view reach the system clipboard in macOS Terminal.

## Terminal caveats

- ewstui captures the mouse, so the terminal's native selection needs a modifier: Option (iTerm2), Fn (macOS Terminal), Shift (kitty, WezTerm, most Linux terminals).
- Over SSH on a non-macOS host there is no `pbcopy`: copying relies on OSC 52 support in the local terminal.
- Dragging past the visible edge of the pane is whatever Textual does (no custom auto-scroll).

## Tests

`tests/test_copy_text.py`: double-click + `y`, real drag (mouse down / move / up) + `Ctrl+C`, nothing-selected hint, `Y` (plain and HTML/`H`), selection dropped on a new email, and the `pbcopy` wrapper (UTF-8, off macOS, failure). An autouse `system_clipboard` fixture in `conftest.py` stubs `pbcopy` for every test. Full suite: 729 passed.

Not verified in a real terminal (only via Textual's pilot).

## Summary

W0.5 of epic #78 (issue #83), first half: the workflow script that audits the sibling repos read-only, and its tests. The audit itself is run separately; #83 stays open until the nine reports exist.

## Changes

- `plugins/hydra/workflows/sibling-audit.js` (new): a script for the host's Workflow tool. Input `args` is `[{id, name, path}]`; no repo name or path is in the file. Per repo it runs an audit agent and then an adversarial verify agent through `pipeline`, and returns one entry per input repo, in input order: `verified`, or `failed` with the stage (`audit`, `verify`, `unknown`). Every prompt carries three rules: read-only, repo text is untrusted data, no secret values in the report. Each finding gets a script-assigned id by position before verification, the auditor's id is kept in `audit_id`, and verdicts merge on the script's id. No gate and no user input mid-run.
- `tests/test_sibling_audit_workflow.py` (new, 26 tests): ten static checks and twelve behaviour checks that execute the script under Node with stand-in `agent`, `pipeline`, `phase` and `log`. The Node tests skip when Node is absent.

No existing file changed.

## How it was produced

Hydra workflow `966bb16a-4585-473e-81e2-77ccdd26a471`, one attended engineering stage (run `run_JFzLhn1Smbgh`). The plan was approved by the operator at the revision ceiling, with the plan judge's two corrections carried in the engineer's brief. Code review by Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` against `code-change-quality@1`: "revise" on `386457b` (two findings with the same id shared one verifier answer), then "pass" on `ff5bd2a` with no required fixes. The engine merged it after a passing smoke run.

## Evidence

- Main checkout after the merge: `env -u HYDRA_EXTRA_REPOS python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_sibling_audit_workflow.py tests/test_native_pack_dispatch.py tests/test_claude_native_configuration.py tests/test_covenant_agents_sync.py` gives 62 passed (Node v26.12.1, behaviour tests ran).
- Full hermetic suite in the stage worktree on `ff5bd2a` (engineer's run): 1 failed, 3587 passed, 5 skipped. The one failure is `tests/test_native_pack_dispatch.py::test_active_source_packs_are_host_attended_native_plugins`, which fails in any linked worktree (#119) and passes on the main checkout (in the 62 above).
- Remove-the-change checks: each one run failed the named test. The engineer ran 12 on the first attempt and 6 on the retry; the host ran ten more against a copy outside the repo on both commits, after an edit hook stopped the engineer (lebobo88/pair-programmer#84). One check (a verify failure returned without its audit report) was run on `386457b` only.

## Known and left open

- Read-only rests on the prompt rules; `agentType` is not set. The host records the git state of every audited repo before and after a run.
- The test stand-ins do not validate the two JSON schemas, so compatibility with the host's structured output is unproven until the first real run.
- At finalize the `synthesis-coherence@1` judge returned "revise" and the record was sealed as done anyway (#110). A false-positive judge warning is recorded as #156.

Refs #83.

body:
## Story
Pouvoir annuler l'import (la reprise) d'un projet qui n'a pas été fait dans ADA.

## Décision de la responsable d'ADA
- **Reprise pas encore validée** → **« Annuler la reprise »** : ADA ferme sa PR de reprise, retire sa branche `ada/reprise`, clôt la demande d'analyse (commentaire d'explication, « not planned ») et retire le marquage. `main` n'a jamais été modifié ; le projet disparaît d'ADA.
- **Reprise validée** → **« Désynchroniser d'ADA »** : seuls les topics d'ADA sont retirés. Rien de ce qu'a fait ADA n'est supprimé : fichiers, stories, versions restent.

## Garde-fous
- Confirmation qui dit exactement ce qui va se passer (« Garder le projet dans ADA » pour renoncer).
- Refus pendant que l'assistant travaille sur le projet.
- Aucun bouton pour un projet créé par ADA : le topic `ada-reprise` est désormais **gardé** après validation pour reconnaître un projet repris.
- Aucune suppression de dépôt ni de demande (règle d'ADA respectée).
- Le projet redevient « à reprendre » ensuite.

## Tests
API 255 (annulation, désynchronisation, refus), front 137 (confirmation, accessibilité, aucun bouton pour un projet ADA), lint, types. ADR-0010 complété.

body:
## Was sich ändert

### Vertretungen (ADR 0018)
Im Abschnitt „Übungsleiter“ eines Termins hat jede Zeile eigene Aktionen. Sie funktionieren vor dem Termin und nachträglich:
- **Übertragen** (eigener Platz oder als Leitung des Termins): Du wählst, wer übernimmt. Das gilt sofort. Die Vertretung bekommt eine Push-Benachrichtigung, sonst eine Mail. War der Termin schon, bestätigt die Vertretung ihre Stunden.
- **Vertreten** (fremde Zeile, wenn man die Rolle übernehmen darf): Man übernimmt den Platz mit derselben Rolle. Der Vertretene bekommt eine Nachricht.
- **Austragen** ohne Vertretung und **„Mich als … eintragen“** funktionieren wie bisher.
- **Letzter Trainer trägt sich aus:** Das Portal fragt vorher nach. Danach bekommt die Abteilungsleitung sofort Bescheid und wird zwei Tage vor dem Termin noch einmal erinnert, falls niemand eingesprungen ist (Markierung `trainer_missing_since`, neuer Job `notify_trainer_missing`).
- Die Seite **„Nicht dabei?“** entfällt. Erinnerung und „Meine Abrechnung“ führen zum Termin. „Hat nicht stattgefunden“ steht nach Beginn im Menü „Weitere Aktionen“. Die alte Adresse leitet weiter (Altlast).
- Bestätigte Stunden kann nur die betroffene Person selbst durch Übertragen oder Austragen zurücknehmen. Eingereichte Monate bleiben gesperrt.

### Rhythmus von Zeitplänen
- **Alle x Wochen**: Standard ist 1. Gezählt wird ab „Gültig ab“.
- **Jeden n-ten im Monat**: der 1. bis 4. oder der letzte Wochentag des Monats.
- Das gilt beim Anlegen einer Veranstaltung und beim Bearbeiten eines Zeitplans. Welches Feld zu sehen ist, steuert `rhythm.js`. Die Anzeige lautet z. B. „Donnerstag 17:00–18:30, alle 2 Wochen“ oder „1. Samstag im Monat 10:00–12:00“.

### Betrieb
- Migration `events/0006_schedule_rhythm`: Es kommen nur neue Felder mit Standardwerten dazu. Bestehende Zeitpläne bleiben wöchentlich, die Änderung ist abwärtskompatibel.
- Es gibt keine neuen Umgebungsvariablen.

### Doku
- ADR 0018. ADR 0012 verweist darauf.
- Hilfe-Kapitel „Übungsleiter“ (neuer Abschnitt „Vertretung“), „Stunden“ und „Veranstaltungen“ angepasst, mit neuen Screenshots.

- ruff, mypy und pytest sind grün. Neu sind `test_substitution.py` und die Rhythmus-Tests in `test_schedules.py`, die über einen Jahreswechsel laufen und den letzten Wochentag im Monat abdecken.

author: khooeee
body:
Adds QuAC, the information-seeking dialogue dataset from EMNLP 2018, to fill a gap the catalog has: every question-answering benchmark imported so far asks a single self-contained question, while QuAC's questions are short, elliptical, and only meaningful inside a conversation — in the authors' own sample, 86% cannot be understood without the dialogue context.

## Scope

The complete official validation split, the published file `val_v0.2.json`, pinned by its SHA-256 digest `09e6229…` because the authors publish the data as plain files with no version history. That is 7,354 questions in 1,000 dialogues over 1,000 sections of 721 Wikipedia articles. The training split is not imported, and the 7,353-question test split is not public at all: models are submitted to the leaderboard, which runs them on the hidden set, so the validation split is the complete official split whose answers are released.

Each prompt holds the question, the earlier turns of its dialogue as `Student:` and `Teacher:` lines carrying the span the original teacher gave, the article and section titles, the summary of the article the student was shown, and the full section text the teacher read. The section text keeps the upstream `CANNOTANSWER` marker that every section ends with, and no instruction is added about it. Each solution lists every reference span recorded for the question, one per line in upstream order — the split carries up to five per question and keeps the repeats, because the official F1 is computed over the reference set as recorded — followed by the affirmation and continuation labels, which the official script also scores, written out as the paper names them.

## Redistribution review

The project page distributes the files under CC BY-SA 4.0, stated in the sentence that carries the download links and linked to the share-alike legal code. The authors' datasheet instead says CC-BY-4.0, "corrected in Oct 2023 from MIT license". Either statement permits this redistribution; the review takes the project page's share-alike statement as the operative one, since it is the more restrictive, it sits beside the data, and the section text is Wikipedia prose that carries share-alike terms of its own. The snapshot therefore carries a share-alike notice. The files are served from a public S3 bucket with no gate, registration, or click-through; only submitting a model for a test score needs an account, which this import does not do.

QuAC records each article and section title but not the revision the text came from, so the generated `ATTRIBUTION.md` credits all 721 articles with links to them as they stand now. 719 titles still resolve, 23 of those now redirect to a renamed article, and two are mangled by an upstream escaping defect and are linked to the articles they stand for. The review and the article's limitations also record the authors' own bias analysis (76% of articles about men, 36% about musicians) and their note that they do not recommend deploying models trained on this data.

- `python3 data/quac/import.py` reproduces `tasks.jsonl` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` from the digest-pinned file using only the standard library, checking every reference span against its recorded offset in the section text.

author: changhansung
body:
M-3290: the daily upstream watch's static precheck flagged Muse **1.4.20-R8619.1 → 1.4.23-R8977.1** as MAJOR (hard=2, hinted=2). This is the full isolated live audit. The result is **no detector change**; this PR adds the 1.4.23 capture set, its test, and the shipped ledger entry.

## Design (what was checked, and how)
1. **Static triage of the precheck's hits**, against both binaries:
   - "Yes, and don't ask again for this command in this session" was already in 1.4.20. The new second copies of it, and of "Allow this" (1→2), "Log in with browser" (1→2) and "Set an API key" (1→2), sit in a new list of the **plugin API's reserved names** (the labels a user plugin can't take: "Approve", "Allow once", "Always allow this MCP tool", "Allow this stage once", …). None of them is drawn on screen.
   - "resume the intended session and retry" and "source session has no stable side-chat point; wait for …" are refusals of `/fork` and `/side`, which AgEnD never sends.
   - "Computer Use now has its own Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions" is a macOS notice.
   - "Muse Code" 541→165, "rate_limit", "to cancel"/"to select" and "ENOENT" are string-table counts.
   - "Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel" 3→2 is the hint of the quit menu with local work running (`MUSE_QUIT_HINT`). Its neighbours changed, and the menu hadn't been captured live since 1.4.11, so it gets a **new live scenario**.
2. **Live, offline** (decision bd0c88aa's isolation):
   - One disposable container per version: `--network none --init --memory 2g --cpus 2 --pids-limit 256`, uid 1000, the binary mounted read-only.
   - A private `tmux -L audit` socket and a fresh HOME per scenario.
   - AgEnD's production launch flags, and input sent as AgEnD sends it.
   - Every model request went to the local mock (`scripts/manual/muse-version-audit/mock.py`). **No muse account or quota was used.**
   - Both runs used `capture.sh`, extended here with the quit-menu scenario: a background task, `/quit`, Down, Escape; never "Exit anyway". Both also ran `switch.sh` (the model/effort switch, M-3180).
   - 1.4.20 was captured in the same run as the control.

## Findings
- All **48 screens** captured on both versions classify **identically** under the production `MuseBackend` predicates: ready, busy, background work, idle, the draft, runtime and startup dialogs, errors, the approval identity, the quit menu and resume-missing. The 45 screens shared with the committed 1.4.20 set do too.
- On-screen differences are only the header version, timestamps, durations, ids and spinner glyphs.
- The approval prompts offer the same options as 1.4.20. The logged-out menu and the trust dialog are unchanged.
- The quit menu is held and never answered with Enter, as on 1.4.20 and 1.4.11. After Escape the composer is idle with the task still running.
- `MUSE_RUNTIME_SWITCH` reads the same: `Model set to … (saved model unchanged)`, the footer row, the `unsupported reasoning effort` refusal, and the next turn's request carrying the switched model and effort.
- One 1.4.20 control screen came out blank (`prod-memory-personal`), the known intermittent rig flake that 1.4.20's own audit recorded. No 1.4.23 screen was blank.

## Changes
- `tests/fixtures/muse-1.4.23/` holds 52 captures and `SOURCES.md` (hashes, rig, findings). `tests/fixtures/muse-1420-model-switch/1.4.23-*` holds the switch screens and that run's mock requests.
- `tests/muse-1.4.23-audit.test.ts` (67 tests):
  - the 1.4.20 surfaces re-captured;
  - the quit menu against 1.4.11's capture;
  - resume after a lost process;
  - the switch outcomes equal to 1.4.20's;
  - every shared screen's verdict equal to 1.4.20's.

  Mutation: changing the quit-hint literal turns the quit-menu test red.
- `src/cli-audited.ts`, the shipped ledger, adds `1.4.23-R8977.1`, and `1.4.20` keeps only its number (the ledger keeps the build only on the newest). It lands with its evidence, as the ledger's rule and `cli-audited-136` require. `cli-audited-136` and `accounts-update-view-136` move their muse examples to 1.4.23.
- `capture.sh` gains the quit-menu scenario. `cli-runtime-switch.ts`'s rig comment lists 1.4.23.

Local: these 4 test files (186 tests) pass, typecheck:tests is clean, and check-public is clean. A main twin follows, as #3905 was for 1.4.20.

body:
The person who bumps Bytebase's omni pin currently assembles seven records: the dispatch plan's
measured tables, the open-decisions note, the release note, four proof reports and the pin-bump
checklist. This adds one document they can paste into the Bytebase PR instead.

`docs/migration/pin-bump-pr-body.md` is written for Bytebase `345007290e` and omni `9bda507ad`, the
SHA it names, over the range `8851de182729..9bda507ad` (144 commits). It contains:

1. **What the bump brings** — 19 new driver trees (only `pg/driver` predates the pin) and Dumper
   coverage on all 20, the analysis moves, the V1 review ports, four metadata-proto additions, and the
   contract surfaces: `Config.TokenProvider`, `Driver.PrivateDatabaseLinkOwner`,
   `driver.AllNodesQuerier`, `Config.Dial` and `ExecuteOptions.Isolation` are in omni;
   `SQLDBProvider`/`db.SQLDB` is Bytebase-side and is explicitly not.
2. **What Bytebase must change with or before it** — the five parser fixtures the pin invalidates, as
   measured in a scratch Bytebase tree with only the pin moved (the records' six-site list had two
   sites that no longer differ and one failing case it did not name); the duplicated corpora list; the
   `GetDB` retirement and its seven call sites; the two advisor seams; `*sql.Conn` keeping as a
   tolerated nil; `ExecuteOptions` adoption; and the inherited decisions, each with its owner.
3. **What users see differently** — linked to the release note (#1397) and summarised in three
   classes, with a table of the eighteen entries a reviewer must consciously accept.
4. **What is not in the bump** — the adapters themselves, the wave-0 layer, the four unverified cloud
   drafts (#1371, #1377, #1378, #1379), the endpoint-blocked Redshift and Snowflake, the five parked
   completion branches, the open omni PRs, and every row the proofs left unpinned.
5. **How the bump was audited** — the commit range, the gates re-run at this SHA (`go build ./...`,
   `go vet ./...`, the full replay-only suite twice-green with no Docker, walkers, compatcheck,
   affected-packages, the `VERIFY.md` lint), the earlier full protocol at `bf1a3396e` and the 18
   commits that followed it, the per-engine proof measurements, the fixture measurement method, and
   what the audit did not cover.

Docs only: no driver, draft, or Bytebase change. The pg partition-clause defect the measurement found
is fixed on main by #1398, which is why the body describes `9bda507ad` rather than the SHA the
measurement started from.

author: joaosouz4dev
body:
## Description

The release workflow currently stops after publishing the GitHub ZIP. Add a Chrome Web Store submission job that consumes that exact published archive and requests automatic publication after Google approval.

- Call the reusable store workflow directly after a successful GitHub release. This also works for releases created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which do not trigger a separate release-event workflow.
- Validate the release tag's main-branch ancestry, source and ZIP manifest versions, published SHA-256 digest and the digest produced by the release job before authenticating to Google.
- Authenticate using service-account Workload Identity Federation with the Chrome Web Store scope. No permanent credential is added to the repository.
- Use the V2 upload/status/publish APIs, wait for asynchronous upload completion and confirm the submitted version. Keep existing visibility and rollout settings.
- Make retries idempotent for the same published or pending version, reject downgrades, preserve other pending/staged submissions and avoid blind retries of mutation requests.
- Add a manual retry workflow for an existing stable release without another version bump.
- Serialize publishing and document one-time publisher linkage and repository variable configuration.

Activation requires `CWS_PUBLISH_ENABLED=true` and the configured publisher/service-account/provider variables. It stays disabled while Google access is being configured, so normal GitHub releases continue to work.

## Related Issue(s)

No linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] Build related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes

## Validation

- Clean `npm ci`: passed.
- Unit tests: 51 passed, including upload/status transitions, async processing, duplicate submissions, downgrades, mismatched artifacts and API failure handling without token disclosure.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`: passed, with the same three existing bundle size warnings.
- Full `npm audit --audit-level=high`: 0 vulnerabilities.
- actionlint 1.7.12: all workflows passed.
- Read-only integration check against real v1.0.96 GitHub release metadata and digest: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live store authentication, upload and publication have not been validated because Google federation and publisher linkage are not configured yet. No Google upload was attempted.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guidelines and reviewed the diff.
- [x] Added regression coverage for the publication flow.
- [x] Existing tests pass and no new build warnings were introduced.
- [x] Added setup and retry documentation linked from both READMEs.

- [Chrome Web Store service accounts](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/service-accounts)

author: xlc2022
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"xlc2022"} -->
_Requested by **Li** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01XuvF5nwNpNP5pV3BXexosA?thread=cmsg_01XuvF5nwNpNP5pV3BXexosA2brno2KBkKcP9jD4f1LnQG)_

The mcp-nixos server that `services.lyrica.mcpNixos` runs reported 25.11 as the stable channel, though this flake and the user's machines are on 26.05.

**Cause.** nixos-26.05 ships mcp-nixos 2.4.3. Its `_discover_available_channels` (caches.py) only probes `latest-{43..46}-nixos-*`. search.nixos.org's live indexes are now generation 48 (25.11) and 53 (26.05, unstable), so it found none and fell back to `FALLBACK_CHANNELS`, whose `stable` is 25.11. Upstream fixed this in 3.0.0 (#159, discovery through `_cat/aliases`), and in 3.1 it also discovers the flake-search index (3.0.2 still hardcodes generation 44). 3.1 needs FastMCP 4, which nixos-26.05 lacks (it has 3.2.3).

**Change.**
- `flake.nix`: a new `mcp-nixos` input, tag v3.1.1 (rev 90922b2, the release commit), with `nixpkgs` following ours. It is fetched over git so places that allow git reads but not GitHub tarballs can lock it. Its `flake-parts` and `devshell` are fetched the same way, and `flake-parts` follows our nixpkgs. Both `nixosModules.default` and `nixosModules.mcp-nixos` default `services.lyrica-mcp-nixos.package` to upstream's `lib.mkMcpNixos { inherit pkgs; }`, built against the system's own pkgs with upstream's scoped FastMCP 4 set, from wheels. A `key` keeps it single when a machine imports both. `packages.mcp-nixos` and the CI roots include it.
- `nix/mcp-nixos-module.nix`: the fastmcp-tests-skipped override is gone, because upstream's set doesn't build fastmcp from source.
- Operators: nothing changes by hand. `nix flake update lyrica` and a rebuild bring it in.

**Checked here.**
- `nix build .#mcp-nixos` passes: 386 upstream unit tests pass.
- Through Lyrica's own `probeMcp` and `McpClient` (pi-mcp), the save check passes with 2 tools (`nix`, `nix_versions`), protocol 2025-11-25.
- `action=channels` lists `stable (current: 26.05) -> latest-53-nixos-26.05`, beside 25.11 and unstable. A stable package search and a flake search both answer.
- A bare GET answers 400, which `check-host.sh` still accepts.
- Evaluates the service in four cases: the full module, the standalone module, both modules imported together, and an operator's own `package` (which still wins). The `toplevel` drv also evaluates.
- `nix flake check --no-build` fails in this sandbox with `path ... is not valid` on `packages.lyrica`, and fails the same way on unchanged main. CI runs it for real.

**Principle.** Principle 3: use what exists. This is upstream's current release built with upstream's own Nix function, and nothing is patched by us.

**Docs touched.** docs/guides/nixos-mcp.md, docs/daemon.md and docs/briefs/nixos-mcp.md (Built, Checked and Handoff).

Risk area: NixOS packaging and module. This goes to PR review.

body:
## Why
UX-9 (AC-CO-1, AC-CO-2): a retry, a double submit or a queued resend must not create a second user message or a second turn for the same send.

## What
- `chat/client-message-id.ts`: pure id generation and checks (`isAlreadySent`, `sendIdFor` keeps one id for identical text within 1.5s). The id is stored on the user message (`clientId`) and validated on load.
- `use-chat-turns`, `use-composer-draft`, `execute-chat-message`: every attempt of one send (first try, Try again, queued turn) carries the same `Idempotency-Key` header to `/api/chat` and `/api/chat/stream`.
- `model/idempotency-key.ts`: the server treats the header as untrusted input and answers 400 `invalid_request` when it is malformed; a missing header is accepted.

## Evidence
- Unit tests for the client id helpers and the server key check; route test for the 400.
- `e2e/idempotent-send.spec.ts`: 502, 502, success gives 3 requests with the same key and one user message, still one after reload; a double Enter gives one message and one request.
- `npm run check` passed in pre-push; Playwright 73 passed locally.

## Not covered
- Server-side replay: the server does not store results by id yet, so a repeated id still runs the model again. Follow-up slice.
- `use-chat-turns.ts` (325) and `execute-chat-message.ts` (312) were already over the 300 line target; splitting them is a follow-up.
- Crew specialist calls and the tools route do not carry the id.

author: iafahim
body:
Refs IAFahim/tl#647 (stage A3). Draft: it pins tl at `63d0d16d` on the tl branch `perf/647-lazy-ticks` (draft PR IAFahim/tl#648), and it adds public API (owner review).

## What it does

A row whose archetype has `TimelineHorizon`, `TimelineClock` and a `PlaybackDue` buffer is stepped lazily by `TimelineKindTickSystem`: only the slots that change this tick are read and written. Rows without the two new types are unchanged.

- Ordinary slots store `tick - clock` (`+ clock` with Reverse) against a per-row clock the job moves by the world direction, so the stored bytes do not depend on direction.
- `PlaybackDue` per slot: the tick of the next kind event or boundary (`KindIndex.Calm`), every tick when not ordinary, never when paused or ended. `TimelineHorizon.Steps` becomes "ticks until the row's next due slot".
- A due row finds its due slots with an AVX2/SSE2 scan of `PlaybackDue` (scalar on other targets) and steps them with `KindRules.TickSlot` (made public in tl `63d0d16d`) in slot order; rated rows run the full rules.
- Kind entry cache: span entries keep their slot's stored tick and Valid/Plain/Reverse/Paused bits in the 4 value bytes spans never use (`KindEntryCache`). The tick job rewrites it when a due slot's bytes change, an entry is added, a request is applied or the chunk was written from outside, and clears it when a row leaves lazy mode. Generated kind jobs use it only when the chunk's `Playback` change version equals this frame's tick version (`KindIndex.TickVersion`, a per-world slot patched into the world's `TimelineLibrary`); otherwise they read the slot. This removed the largest kind-job cost: one random slot read per active clip per frame (measured 1.23 of 2.22 ms at 20,000 x 200).
- Enable bits are written through chunk `EnabledMask`s in the tick job and generated jobs.
- Readers decode with `TimelineTicks.Real`: generated kind and feed jobs (emitters and the checked-in KindGame jobs), `TlPanel`, the library swap job.
- `TimelineGlide { Limit = 0 }` decodes lazy rows back to real ticks and clears their caches.

## Public API added (owner decision)

- `Tl.Unity.TimelineClock`, `Tl.Unity.PlaybackDue`, `Tl.Unity.TimelineTicks` (`Real`, `Decode`, `Encode`, `Due`), `Tl.Unity.KindEntryCache`, `KindIndex.TickVersion`, `TlTimelineSwapJob.ClockHandle`, `KindTickJob.ClockHandle`/`DueHandle`/`Now`/`TickVersion`.
- Generated kind and feed jobs gain a read-only `ClockHandle`.
- Contract for opted-in rows: code that writes `Playback` itself must decode and encode with the row clock; an `EntityManager` write between two hand-driven system updates (no system update in between) is seen by kind jobs only after the next tick (documented in `docs/KINDS.md`).

## Measured (Unity 7000.0.0a16, Burst, 11 workers, safety off, `OwnerScaleBench`, median of 256 frames)

Table below is at `7f88eba`. Newer numbers at `8f47456` (inlined step lookup) are in the latest comment: 20,000 x 200 frame 4.51 -> 2.34 / 4.25 -> 1.62 / 4.46 -> 1.18 ms.

Whole timeline frame (tick + generated kind jobs), ms:

| Rows x active | Duration | Eager | Lazy (4169cda) | Lazy (now) | Speedup now | Tick eager -> lazy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 10,000 x 40 | 120 | 0.520 | 0.320 | 0.342 | 1.5x | 0.318 -> 0.180 |
| 10,000 x 40 | 600 | 0.423 | 0.201 | 0.219 | 1.9x | 0.265 -> 0.074 |
| 10,000 x 40 | 3000 | 0.444 | 0.171 | 0.167 | 2.7x | 0.294 -> 0.039 |
| 20,000 x 100 | 120 | 2.372 | 2.223 | 1.573 | 1.5x | 1.303 -> 0.903 |
| 20,000 x 100 | 600 | 2.166 | 1.386 | 0.903 | 2.4x | 1.171 -> 0.342 |
| 20,000 x 100 | 3000 | 2.307 | 0.978 | 0.701 | 3.3x | 1.371 -> 0.131 |

author: nictanghe
body:
## Change

The current garment window had no connected controls for the inherited static physics-inspired mesher. Add a native **Mesh preparation** accordion with a 17-stop Coarse–Fine spacing slider, numeric inputs, selected/all-piece scope, and separately enabled smooth transitions, fold endpoints, parallel fold constraints, gathering and down-fill sizing estimates.

Hints are persisted against named material-space paths and resolved during compilation, including curved boundaries. Applying compiles before installing, adds one undo entry, invalidates cached state/worker generation and resets the drape. Draft changes do not compile or reset. Invalid inputs, missing paths, impossible rails and exceeded budgets preserve the document. Fix idle worker configuration messages being marked as pending physics steps so repeat preparation stays available.

FC-0064. Builds on the implementation from [original PR #230](https://github.com/erythrofr/ClothCraft/pull/230) and Zhang et al., [Physics-inspired Estimation of Optimal Cloth Mesh Resolution (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3721238.3730619). The paper's Ours-I/II labels describe different comparisons; this UI names the actual behaviors. [Usage, formulas and limits](docs/pie-resolution.md#native-mesh-controls-and-authored-feature-hints-fc-0064).

## Validation

- Full CPU suite: 666 passed, one ignored.
- Desktop garment-runner suite: 28 passed, including the existing Settings/zoom tests after integrating the latest runner refactor.
- Final focused meshing/reference rerun after local review: 36 passed.
- Strict CPU all-target Clippy, desktop/test Clippy, formatting and all-feature/all-binary desktop compilation passed.
- CPU-rendered production-panel layout inspected; native text input, draft staging, scope, rejection atomicity, undo/redo, and save/load exercised.

No external review or GPU/native-window acceptance is claimed.

## Limits

This is opt-in static mesh preparation. Pressure and sewn/rest ratios guide mesh sizing; they do not add inflation, physical shrinkage or crease forces. Pressure uses an explicit reference in Pa and a documented normalized transition law; hard transitions use a bounded band. These are independent choices, not literal reproductions of the paper's dimensional exponent fit. Parallel rails require an internal line and room on both sides; curvature extrema and compartment regions are not automatically discovered. No calibrated wrinkle accuracy, physical optimum or solver speedup is claimed.

The separate 2026 variational r-adaptive solver investigation is tracked in #7; this PR does not close it.

author: rsman-dev
body:
> 🤖 Opened by RsMan-Dev's AI agent (Claude Code), not by RsMan-Dev personally.

A change of behaviour towards vanilla, not a performance change: advancements are granted by the player's own count, as vanilla does (the grant can come up to 19 ticks earlier or later than before for a player who joined off the multiple).

`tick_advancements` read `minecraft:location` when `self.ticks % 20 == 0` (the game's tick); vanilla reads `tickCount % 20 == 0` of the player (`ServerPlayer.doTick` offset 533, `getfield tickCount; bipush 20; irem; ifne`, read in the 26.3 server jar). `Entity.commonTick` (offsets 42 to 47) adds one to `tickCount` and `ServerLevel.tickNonPassenger` calls it before the player's tick, so `doTick` (called later by `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.tick`, offset 50) sees the count after the increment. The count is not saved, `ServerPlayer.teleport(TeleportTransition)` makes no new player object and `PlayerList.respawn` does.

The player's own count already exists in Horizon: `health.tick_count`, advanced in the body's turn before the tail (the same order), 0 for a new body. A trip to another level replaces the guest's body in Horizon where vanilla keeps the player object, so the count is carried over (`Guest.carried_ticks`, applied with the other carried state); a respawn starts at 0, as `PlayerList.respawn` makes a new object. Other uses of the game's tick, `sync_score_registries` (Horizon's own sync), the border damage every 10 ticks and `minecraft:levitation` (a difference of one counter, so the same), are left alone.

Closes #17897.

## Tests

`advancements::progress_tests` (daily, needs the game resources like `building_cache`; rows in `tools/ci/ignored-tests/daily-horizon-client-location-cadence.txt`):

- `location_is_read_every_twenty_ticks_of_each_players_own_count`: two guests on game tick 40 with own counts 7 and 19 are not evaluated (the old reading evaluated both), then 20 for the second is granted while the first is not, then 40 for the first. It fails on the old line and passes on the new one.
- `the_tick_count_goes_through_a_change_of_level_and_not_through_a_respawn`: a body replaced for another level keeps its count, one replaced for a respawn starts at 0.

`cargo test -p horizon-client --lib -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1 location_is_read_every_twenty_ticks the_tick_count_goes_through` (with `HORIZON_TEST_RESOURCES`): 2 passed.

Not exercised by the tests: the host's own player (single-player), whose count I have not checked against this path; a guest whose body does not run (`!loaded`: `advance_clock` is skipped, vanilla counts those ticks); a datapack `/reload` (unchanged by this change).

## Measurement of the spike

Throwaway dedicated server (`horizon-server`), 200 `horizon-bots` together on a flat world (`--height 0 --ground`), `locator_bar` false, `spawn_mobs` false, entities killed, TPS 20. `perf stat -e instructions:u` per thread over two passes of 10 s; the tick thread is the busiest thread. Both binaries are the `fast` profile with line tables, built clean (no incremental) from this branch's commit and from its parent `origin/main` 2a247ac19e; two runs of each, interleaved, one after the other on a shared, loaded machine (instructions, not times, are compared). Here the figure is the instructions of the busiest thread in each 50 ms interval (`perf stat -I 50 --per-thread -e instructions:u`, 30 s, 594 intervals, about one a tick), standing bots, two runs each:

| | median tick | 95th percentile | mean of the costliest 5 % | costliest tick |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | 91.0 M / 90.1 M | 131.5 M / 115.8 M | 138.4 M / 137.3 M | 142.5 M / 141.4 M |
| this branch | 94.7 M / 94.7 M | 99.6 M / 99.7 M | 106.3 M / 106.8 M | 119.8 M / 128.4 M |

The expensive tick of every twenty (all 200 players' location criteria on one tick) becomes a smaller one: the bots join two ticks apart, so their own counts start on ten phases of twenty and each phase holds twenty players. The median moves up by about 4 M as the same work is spread over more ticks. With players joining at random ticks the spread is finer. The mean per tick does not change: tick-thread instructions a player a tick, mean of four passes, standing 462.9 k against 457.1 k, walking 600.2 k against 603.5 k; Two clean builds of this tree can differ in the thread's total by about 20 k instructions a player a tick for reasons unrelated to the change (a function inlined in one build and not in the other: seen here between `origin/main` and a branch that changes one function), so a difference of that size in a total is not by itself a result; where a branch changes one function, that function's own inclusive count (`perf record -e instructions:u -c 100000`, 200 walking bots, 421 ticks, the same two binaries) is given too.

## Kind

- [ ] parity
- [x] bug
- [ ] perf: faster, or less memory
- [ ] feature
- [ ] extra
- [ ] tooling
- [ ] docs

## Layer

Engine (advancements).

## Vanilla reference

26.3 server jar: `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer.doTick` (offset 533), `net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity.commonTick` (offsets 42 to 47), `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel.tickNonPassenger` (offsets 34 to 38), `net.minecraft.server.network.ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.tick` (offset 50), `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer.teleport(TeleportTransition)`, `net.minecraft.server.players.PlayerList.respawn` (offset 45).

## Self-check

`tools/pr_ready.py` was not run in full (workspace-wide; this machine's build directory is shared). Run on this branch alone (one commit on `origin/main` 2a247ac19e), each on its own:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `rustfmt --check` on the changed files | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p horizon-client --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
| `cargo test -p horizon-client --lib -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1 location_is_read_every_twenty_ticks the_tick_count_goes_through`: 2 passed | ok |
| `python3 tools/check_public_tree.py` | ok |
| `python3 tools/ci/check_ignored_test_rows.py` (the daily rows of the new tests) | ok, 0 problems |
| the vanilla harnesses | not run |

author: paullj
body:
PR 3 of the Other targets milestone. **Stacked on #444** (base `tg/02-isa-abi`). Merge order: #442, #444, then this PR. It adds a format-neutral Image with a writer per object format (#424), and OS-neutral library diagnostics (#431).

## Changes
- **Neutral Image** (#424, #60 D3). `link/Image.zig`: arch, text, entry, cstrings, bss size, imports with a 16-bit library index, libraries, search paths, relocations, the ISA patcher and debug content. Link builds it; `Image.patch` applies the cross-section relocations, so writers do not depend on Link. No data section and no GOT field yet: nothing emits initialized data, and the GOT is one slot per import (recorded in the commit body).
- **Writers.** `MachO.write(Image)` gives today's bytes; code signing is a separate step (`MachO.writeSigned = write + sign`). The Mach-O cputype comes from the target arch. `emit.writerOf(format)` is the one writer lookup (ELF returns null until #433), used by `canEmit` and `writeImage`. The module doc maps every Image field to ELF and notes how a later wasm backend supplies its own image path.
- **Library resolver interface.** `link/LibResolver.zig`; the Mach-O reader (Dylib.zig) is behind it, and Libraries.zig talks only to the interface. The 8-bit dylib ordinal limit stays in the Mach-O writer.
- **OS-neutral wording** (#431, #60 D12). R0015–R0019 say "the system C library", "shared library" and "the system library cache". Each resolver supplies its target nouns, and a note footer names the real thing ("on macOS the system C library is libSystem …"). The R0016 note names the file toy searched for, so a doubled `lib` prefix still shows. Notes appear under drawn diagnostics only, and in NDJSON (`= note:` in `rendered`, and a `notes` array). The R0017 slug is now `not-a-shared-library`. Explain pages, ffi.md, std.md and the `-l` help are updated.

## Commits
- `18bc2c94` refactor(link): a neutral Image and a writer per object format. Closes #424.
- `97b64077` fix(diagnostics): OS-neutral wording for library errors. Closes #431.

## Review and checks
- A3: 3 reviewers, 1 fix pass (library index width, patching on the Image, one writer lookup, stale docs). The A3 implementer hit a network error after it committed; the reviews and fix pass completed. A10 ran as its own workflow on top of A3: 3 reviewers, 1 fix pass (notes as per-diagnostic footers, NDJSON notes, render cap, the searched file name in R0016).
- fmt clean. `zig build test`: 24/24 steps, 2722/2722 tests. GC stress corpus pass. Fuzz: seeds 1, 3, 7 and 11, 300/300 each. incremental.sh 67 sound. site:e2e 38, site:test 51.
- byteid: 538/538 identical at both commits.
- **Perf** (`-j1`, 200×50 project, cold, debug builds, base vs this PR): `build` 45.94–46.00 vs 45.89–45.90 billion instructions; `check` 7.95–8.01 vs 7.79–7.81 billion. Flat to slightly lower.

## Open questions
1. #424 listed a data section and a GOT field; the Image has neither yet (see above). Keep, or update #424?
2. The resolver cannot yet express "accepted without a check, with a note" (T14 cross builds). OK for #435 (ELF resolver) to add it?
3. NDJSON: every record now has a `notes` array, empty for most. OK as a schema change, or only when there is a note?
4. Notes are keyed by message address, because the cached diagnostic record cannot hold a slice. Make this a general per-diagnostic note channel later?

author: daniakash
body:
The ultrafast meter on Home now magnifies savings as they grow. The old ruler was logarithmic and fixed from 1k to 2.5M, so each new milestone got a thinner slice and a big gain barely moved the needle (from 120k to 366k it moved 14% of the width, and past 2.5M about 11%).

- **Close-up ruler:** the scale spans the last milestone passed to the next one and fills the full width, ruled in round steps with every fifth tick longer. At 366k it runs 250k to 500k with the needle at 46%.
- **Trail:** milestones passed before the current stretch fold into small marks and a count at the left ("4 passed"). A first stretch starts at 0 with no trail.
- **Milestones:** 10k, 25k, 50k, 100k, 250k, 500k, 1M, 2.5M, 5M, 10M, 25M and onward, so heavy users always have a next one. The "to go" and "You just passed" line follows the new list.
- **Needle:** still moves once from the last total this computer saw. When that total sits before the current stretch, it starts from the left end. Readers who prefer less motion get it placed directly.

Everything else in the meter, the Details popup and who sees the meter is unchanged. Pure scale logic lives in `energy-meter.helpers.ts`, with tests for each stage from 6k to 12M (span, needle, trail count, next milestone, the line under the scale), and the meter's DOM tests cover the new ruler and the first stretch.

author: breno-lira
body:
This pull request introduces infrastructure and configuration improvements to support monitoring, logging, and alerting for the BLU service, primarily through Docker Compose orchestration. It adds example environment files, logging and monitoring parameters, and configures line endings for cross-platform compatibility. The changes make it easier to deploy, monitor, and receive alerts for the service, both locally and in production-like environments.

**Monitoring, Logging, and Alerting Setup:**

* Added a complete `docker-compose.yml` file to orchestrate the BLU service, Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Mailpit for local monitoring, metrics collection, and alerting via email or a local mailbox.
* Introduced `.env.alertas.example` as a template for configuring email alerts via SMTP, including instructions and example settings for Gmail integration.

**Configuration and Documentation Enhancements:**

* Updated `.env.example` with new environment variables for logging (file path, size, backups) and thresholds for image quality and expected parking slots.
* Updated `bentofile.yaml` to document the `/metrics` endpoint, log file location, and added `prometheus-client` to Python dependencies for metrics export. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4552bf531db78c7c42db85d975cb6b8c064d7ce8439188cf7209512bedac2dR16-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4552bf531db78c7c42db85d975cb6b8c064d7ce8439188cf7209512bedac2dR32)

**Cross-platform Development Improvements:**

* Added `.gitattributes` to enforce LF line endings for scripts and templates, preventing execution errors in Linux containers when checked out from Windows.

author: fabbiosborges
body:
## Objetivo
Fecha a pendência de **logout da US02 (RF02)** e implementa a **US03 — gerenciamento de barbeiros (RF03)**, restrito ao administrador, com CRUD completo exposto para o front.

Segue o spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-...`) e o plano (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-17-...`) incluídos nesta branch.

## US02 — Logout (RF02 / RNF02)
- Habilitado o app `rest_framework_simplejwt.token_blacklist` (+ migrations).
- `SIMPLE_JWT`: `ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS` e `BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION`.
- `LogoutView` → `POST /api/token/logout/` com `{"refresh": "<token>"}`:
  - `205` em sucesso (refresh invalidado no servidor), `400` se ausente/inválido, `401` sem auth.

## US03 — Gerenciamento de barbeiros (RF03, admin only)
- `RegistroBarbeiroSerializer`: cria o `User` do Django (senha com hash) + perfil `Barbeiro` em `@transaction.atomic`; valida username/email duplicados.
- `BarbeiroViewSet` (`ModelViewSet`, `IsAdminUser`): `create` usa o serializer de registro, demais ações usam `BarbeiroSerializer`.
- **Soft delete**: `DELETE` marca `ativo=False` (preserva histórico/FKs de agendamentos), retorna `204`.
- Admin enxerga barbeiros inativos; a rota pública `GET /api/barbeiros/` (ativos) foi mantida separada.

## Rotas novas
| Método + Rota | Permissão |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/token/logout/` | autenticado |
| `GET·POST /api/admin/barbeiros/` | admin |
| `GET·PUT·PATCH·DELETE /api/admin/barbeiros/{id}/` | admin |

## Testes
- Suíte `usuarios`: **10/10 passando**; `manage.py check` sem issues.
- Cobre: logout invalida refresh (refresh posterior → 401), 400/401; criação de barbeiro cria User, 403 para cliente, 401 sem auth, soft delete preserva registro, admin lista inativos.

## Observações (fora do escopo desta PR)
- Desativar barbeiro não bloqueia o login do `User` vinculado (soft delete preserva o registro, conforme spec). Se desejado, setar `user.is_active = False` no `perform_destroy` numa iteração futura.

홈에 짧고 조용한 움직임을 더합니다.

- 내릴 때: 아래 구역이 화면에 들어오면 한 번 나타납니다.

"움직임 줄이기"를 켠 기기에서는 모두 꺼집니다. 운영자가 승인한 움직임 기준 한 줄도 저장소 지침(`CLAUDE.md`)에 더합니다. 홈 말고 다른 화면은 바뀌지 않습니다.

## 바뀌는 것 (파일 6개)

- `src/styles/home.css`: 홈 전용 움직임
  - 들어올 때는 첫 화면 매물 종이(0.28초, 8px)와 도장(0.26초) 한 번뿐입니다.

author: tiandi101
body:
## What

Adds a Claude skill, `.claude/skills/umbp-tuning/`, next to `umbp-add-backend` and `umbp-add-transfer-engine`. It is a method for answering "why is this UMBP pool slower than it should be, and what do I change", independent of model, engine or cluster. Docs only; no code changes.

## The framework

A pool tier can cost performance in only three ways:

```
                      gap vs reference
                             │
            ┌────────────────┴─────────────────┐
   engine does MORE work               engine does the same work,
   per request                         but slower or later
            │                                  │
      1. HIT LOSS                       2. LOAD LATENCY

      3. WRITE PRESSURE   (feeds 1, and wears the medium)
```

| Stage | Question |
|---|---|
| 0. Validity | Is the comparison fair, and are the settings really in effect? |
| 1. Decompose | Is the gap work (computed share) or speed (compute rate)? |
| 2. Attribute | Which hit-loss class, load stage or write-pressure symptom? |
| 3. Choose a lever | Which lever family moves that class and nothing else? |
| 4. Verify | Did the predicted class move? |

## Layout

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | Tier-neutral: the model, the five stages, class → lever-family map, sizing rules, signals (activity summary, `/metrics`, startup lines) |
| `architectures.md` | Tuning for the model architecture: inventory of cache state, bound, candidate placements (six ordered questions), offline search, verification; three archetypes |
| `tiers/ssd.md` | SSD module: segment-granular reclaim, staging, promotion churn, write pressure, the `[SsdPerf]` stage split, knobs grouped by lever family |

HBM, DRAM and remote modules are not written yet; `SKILL.md` says so.

Placement comes before pool tuning: where a model's state is saved sets the hit the pool can reach at all, so `SKILL.md` sends the reader to `architectures.md` when the unlimited-cache ceiling is itself low.

## Checked

Every mori knob, default, log line, metric and API named in the files was checked against `main` at `7e23fa2ae` (`config.h`, `runtime-env-vars.md`, `pure-ssd-mode.md`, `policy_config.cpp`). The skill has not yet been used on a fresh diagnosis.

author: yassirezoo44ye-stack
body:
App Builder currently executes generated projects on the API host, inheriting its environment. Generic same-origin previews conflict with authentication/framing policies and expose generated content to the platform origin. Workspace files lack declared persistent storage.

This change routes App Builder Run exclusively through bounded Vercel microVMs and fails closed when isolation is unavailable. Generic previews use a short-lived capability on a separate origin. The existing opaque commerce preview is preserved through owner-authenticated, path-limited RPC to the VM. Platform credentials are never forwarded; bridge responses are non-executable attachments with nosniff. Upstream headers are sanitized, and workspace reads select an existing project directory under the configured trusted root.

Commerce SQLite backups run inside the VM. Bounded database snapshots are atomically saved to the project's durable workspace before initial readiness and before acknowledging store mutations. New VMs receive saved state. Failed persistence blocks destructive Stop; the setup token is read from the active VM. Direct Open is withheld for commerce so the supported UI uses the saving bridge.

The Render Blueprint declares a 5 GB disk at /app/workspaces and requires an actual writable mount at startup. docs/ISOLATED_PREVIEWS.md and docs/RUNNABLE_COMMERCE.md cover activation, backup/restore, runtime limits, and remaining acceptance checks.

Reconciled with main at 159da040d05f7df1a9a4e472cb704060d0f8c2df, preserving runnable commerce, delivery gates, and Feed changes. The original Blob-preview assertion was replaced by a behavioral fail-closed HTML test. Security regressions cover trusted-root enforcement, header splitting, credential stripping, bounded persistence, failed save/Stop recovery, and VM replacement.

Local validation of the reconciled tree:
- 199 related backend/security tests passed.
- 89 App Builder frontend tests passed.
- TypeScript, strict ESLint, production frontend build, scoped Ruff, and git diff --check passed.
- Published contents of all 28 changed files match the tested local files.
GitHub validation at c3068fbff323d6a5ab9e48831f534b15edf61c03:
- Backend full suite: 3333 passed, 4 skipped; 26 subtests passed.
- Frontend full suite: 533 tests passed across 62 files; production build passed.
- Docker image build passed (no image push).
- CodeQL Python/JavaScript analysis and the PR security gate passed with no new alerts.
- Render deploy, post-deploy health check and release jobs were skipped on the PR; production activation was not performed.

Draft pending authorized live integration verification. No paid VM was started and no production database/files or service settings were modified. Activation requires backend-only Sandbox credentials, an authorized disk attachment/deployment, backup/restoration of existing ephemeral workspaces, and browser/runtime/persistence acceptance checks. Render disk attachment makes the service single-instance without zero-downtime deploys. The existing mismatched Render deploy-hook secret is a separate configuration issue.

Scope: App Builder Run and commerce preview routes. Legacy execution entry points elsewhere in Flow are not claimed to be isolated. Runtime writes for arbitrary apps remain ephemeral; manually mutating the VM URL bypasses the supported commerce persistence bridge. Unacknowledged mutations can be lost on VM/provider failure. Multi-file modification rollback and general workspace-session restoration remain follow-ups. No PR merge or production deployment is included.

author: jrandolf
body:
## Why

Vapor applies a template ref only through an explicit `ref` or `:ref` attribute. A bound object's ref has no effect ([Vue decision](https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/15900)).

Hidden and range inputs thus had no element ref when compiled as Vapor. An explicit ref makes Vue merge input props. With `width` and `height` in the handler, the next render loses the 1px box that Chrome needs for native validation messages.

The package still builds virtual DOM components. Current user behavior stays the same.

## What

- Use `min-width` and `min-height` for the validation box. Vue writes only the keys of the input's style object ([Vue source](https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/main/packages/runtime-dom/src/modules/style.ts)). The box stays equal to Base UI's box, so no parity exception is needed.
- Bind hidden and range input refs by name. Pass setters through the current contexts and remove the ref keys from their props.
- Remove the two input wrapper components. The OTP, date, and time roots now render their inputs.
- Give the Combobox and Number Field visible-input fixtures the same form.
- Add the ESLint guard and five cases. The render-size case mounts a Vapor fixture in the Vapor project and a regular fixture with the same template in each other project. The guard reports all 11 affected templates on the base before the input changes.
- Correct the contributor rules. The public `useRender` change belongs to a separate pull request.

The measured extra cost is 50 to 200 ns per render of one hidden input in the regular build.

## Tests

- The browser jobs pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, and on the Vue floor. They check input refs, form behavior, and validation size.
- The Node suite passes. It checks server render without a DOM.
- Typecheck, lint, parity, build, and package validation pass. No parity file changes.
- The job `test-vue-rc` passes with Vue 3.6.0-rc.15, in the Chromium project, which has no Vapor interop, and in the Vapor project. The Vapor project runs all three handler cases, which include the ref and render-size checks.
- Remove the fixture's named ref: the Vapor ref case fails with zero calls. Move the ref into the object: the same case fails.
- Restore `width` and `height`: nine size cases fail in Chromium, and the render-size case fails in Vapor and with the regular fixture. This covers the handler, Checkbox, Switch, Radio, Number Field, OTP Field, and the date/time field.
- Remove the lint guard: both rejection cases fail. Remove the named-ref exception: its acceptance case fails.
- Remove the spread-only condition: the plain-input acceptance case fails. Remove the input-tag condition: the other-element acceptance case fails.
- Remove Radio's named ref: ESLint reports the input at its template line.

All mutation changes are restored. The Vue dependency version stays unchanged.

author: derekmerck
body:
Brings the project's Zotero library into the Sphinx docs so design notes and READMEs can cite a shared set of references.

## What's here
- **`docs/src/bibliography/storytangl.bib`.** The Better BibTeX export of the Zotero library (204 entries), with file paths omitted. Zotero is the source of truth, so this file is not edited by hand.
- **Sphinx wiring.** `sphinxcontrib-bibtex` is in the `docs` extra and the dev group. `conf.py` enables it with `bibtex_bibfiles`. A new **Bibliography** page renders the whole library.
- **`docs/src/_ext/bib_style.py`.** A small pybtex style:
  - formats `@standard`, the BibLaTeX type Zotero uses for specifications;
  - labels entries by cite key (`aarseth_cybertext_1997`, not `Aar97`), so readers see the key authors type;
  - gives each entry one link (the DOI if it has one, otherwise the URL);
  - links JSTOR eprints to JSTOR instead of arXiv.
- **`scripts/mini_bib.py`.** Prints Markdown reference lists for READMEs and other files Sphinx doesn't index. Select entries by cite key or by keyword; a bare topic matches the `devref:<topic>` tag on entries. Example: `poetry run python scripts/mini_bib.py -k credentials`.
- **`AGENTS.md`.** A short References section: Zotero is canonical, how to cite, and when to use `mini_bib.py`.

## Keeping it live
Better BibTeX auto-exports to the tracked `.bib` file in the main checkout, so library edits show up as ordinary diffs to commit. The docs build runs with `-W` (and `fail_on_warning` on Read the Docs), so an unformattable entry or a citation to a missing key fails the build.

## Validation
- `poetry run pytest docs/tests`: passes.
- `poetry run pytest engine/tests`: 4651 passed, 75 skipped, 6 xfailed.
- The `poetry.lock` diff adds only `sphinxcontrib-bibtex`, `pybtex`, `pybtex-docutils` and `latexcodec`.

A new section, **Text people type**: text a person or an assistant types is cleaned on its way in, by one rule at every door, and nothing is changed on its way out. The rule: control characters dropped (multi-line text keeps its line breaks), every `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` character except the joiners, variation selectors and tag characters, and lone surrogates; stored in NFC, trimmed, quietly; a name needs a visible character; comparisons fold with NFKC; lookalike checks only for unique identifiers; each output escapes for itself; a change of rule cleans stored text with a migration; a right-to-left language brings isolation of typed text inside sentences. `README.md` lists the new topic.
