author: aburan28
body:
## Prime31 B8 public RR9 Macaulay: degree-six frozen experiment — complete bounded null result [pcc:unverified]

The separate prospective follow-up to #4548 reuses the **original Rust prime31 arithmetic** and the same public-only seven-coefficient RR9 equations on the actual ordinary cofactor-one curve `p=2^31-1, n=2147446831`. No signed supports or hidden scalar enter the candidate. Source-specific pinned Rust 1.100.0 **[Actions #44093411239 PASS](https://github.com/isogeny-labs/crypto/actions/runs/44093411239)** on code `23bc7919`: 40/40 original library tests, 2/2 example tests, raw JSON and fixture checks.

**[Raw fixed-case JSON artifact #14333365564](https://github.com/isogeny-labs/crypto/actions/runs/44093411239/artifacts/14333365564)**, independently matched SHA256 `7940677f74135e2d9b8d67e466828118d86eea4f088f4c72ca9d57f10b830737`.

| Frozen public residual | Chart status (test oracle only) | D6 rank | Charged Macaulay wall | Unit certificate | Unique chart |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| (1911579686,548820096) | positive | 1688/1716 | 346.920 ms | no | no |
| (625037715,2100627251) | negative | 1688/1716 | 329.113 ms | no | no |
| (1923055775,307731458) | negative | 1688/1716 | 328.519 ms | no | no |

All cases: 2,640 rows, 284,111,722 field multiplications, 502,205 reductions, 1,688 inversions, 23,172,864-byte dense pivot upper storage metric. **Both true negatives are still inconclusive; the positive chart coefficients are unrecovered**. No new complete ECDLP solves or speedup.

### Mathematical contribution: exact generic Hilbert-function match

Homogenizing eight affine quadrics in seven variables gives eight homogeneous quadrics in eight variables. For a generic regular sequence the Koszul Hilbert series is `(1+t)^8`. The maximal-rank degree-5/6 predictions are thus **792−C(8,5)=736** and **1716−C(8,6)=1688**, exactly matching #4548 and this experiment. These measurements show no **extra** low-degree rank deficiency; they do *not* prove that the structured RR9 equations are globally regular or that larger-degree elimination succeeds. The natural next step is to stop blindly growing dense Macaulay matrices and investigate a public-only sparse factor-base-aware B31 algebraic extractor.

### Provenance / decisions

author: spikeon
body:
## Problem

With IBus, the number inputs of Bambu Studio do not accept keys. IBus is the default input method framework on GNOME, so most Ubuntu and Fedora users have this problem. Also, when a long-running Bambu Studio window closes, `ibus-daemon` can lock up at 100% CPU. Then the keyboard stops for all software until you start IBus again.

Upstream issue: https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/13201

PrusaSlicer had the same problem with IBus in its input fields: https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/issues/1943. Bambu Studio comes from PrusaSlicer, and both use wxWidgets.

## Change

The `entrypoint` script sets `GTK_IM_MODULE=gtk-im-context-simple` before it starts Bambu Studio. `XMODIFIERS` does not change, because a test showed that only `GTK_IM_MODULE` is necessary. This is the same type of work-around as the two other work-arounds in `entrypoint`.

Users who must have the input method of the host, for example for CJK input, can keep it with one command:

```
flatpak override --user --env=BAMBU_STUDIO_USE_HOST_IM=1 com.bambulab.BambuStudio
```

## Test

- Ubuntu 26.04.1, GNOME Shell 50.1, IBus 1.5.34, Bambu Studio 2.8.2.61 from Flathub.
- Without the change, the number inputs did not accept keys. With `GTK_IM_MODULE=gtk-im-context-simple` set through `flatpak override`, the number inputs work. `XMODIFIERS` stayed `@im=ibus`.
- The script sets the variable if `BAMBU_STUDIO_USE_HOST_IM` is not set. If `BAMBU_STUDIO_USE_HOST_IM=1`, the script keeps the value of the host.

body:
This PR formalizes the divided power filtration (`DividedPowers.pdFiltration`), PD-nilpotent divided power ideals (`DividedPowers.IsPDNilpotent`), the factorial nilpotence bound and nilradical criterion (Stacks Project Lemma 23.2.6 / Tag 07GR), and the complete `p`-adic and `ZMod (p ^ e)` filtration and PD-nilpotence classification (including the separating counterexample `(2) ⊂ ZMod 4`).

This completes section PD.4 (*The divided power filtration and PD nilpotence*) of the `DerivedDeRhamCohomology` roadmap as an explicit upstream prerequisite for `CrystallineCohomology` Layer CR.1 (`CR.1.1`). Specifically, `CR.1.1` consumes §PD.4 in two places:
- *Schemes with a quasi-coherent PD ideal* consumes §PD.4 *PD-nilpotent divided power ideals and ordinary nilpotence* (`DividedPowers.le_nilradical_iff_isNilpotent_of_quotient` / `DividedPowers.le_nilradical_iff_isNilpotent_natCast`) to prove that on a PD scheme `(T, J, γ)` over `ℤ_(p)` with `p` locally nilpotent on `U = V(J)`, `U → T` is a thickening if and only if `p` is locally nilpotent on `T`.
- *Structure, quotient and PD-ideal sheaves* consumes §PD.4 *Divided power filtration* (`DividedPowers.pdFiltration`, `pdFiltration_zero`, `pdFiltration_one`, `pdFiltration_mul_le`, `IsDPMorphism.map_pdFiltration_eq`) to define the PD-power sheaf of ideals `J_crys^{[r]} ⊂ O_crys` on the crystalline site.

What remains after this PR: on `DerivedDeRhamCohomology`, §PD.5 (canonical divided powers on `(p)`, compatibility with a base, and square-zero/second-order thickenings) and §PD.6 (pushouts of divided power rings); on `CrystallineCohomology`, combining the in-flight §§PD.1–PD.2 PRs (`#42996`, `#43302`, `#43371`), §PD.4 from this PR, and §PD.6 to assemble `CR.1.1` PD schemes and crystalline sites.

Roadmap: DerivedDeRhamCohomology
Consumer roadmap: CrystallineCohomology
<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"DerivedDeRhamCohomology","id":"divided-power-filtration-pd-nilpotence"}-->

Files added (1,360 lines total, all well under 1,000 lines per file, strictly under `TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/`):

- `TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/PDFiltration.lean` (606 lines, `namespace DividedPowers`, over `[CommSemiring R]`): defines `pdFiltration` (`Fⁿ_γ I` / `I^[n]`) with unfolding lemma `pdFiltration_def`, universal containment criterion `pdFiltration_le_iff`, `pdFiltration_antitone`, `@[simp] pdFiltration_zero` (`F⁰ = ⊤`), `@[simp] pdFiltration_one` (`F¹ = I`), `pdFiltration_le_self`, `pdFiltration_mul_le`, `prod_dpow_mem_pdFiltration`, `pdFiltration_pow_le`, `pow_le_pdFiltration`, stability `dpow_mem_pdFiltration_mul` (`n ≠ 0 → x ∈ Fⁿ → γₘ(x) ∈ Fᵐⁿ`), and `isSubDPIdeal_pdFiltration`. Proves generator descriptions for arbitrary generating sets (`pdFiltration_eq_span_of_eq_span`, `pdFiltration_le_iff_of_eq_span`) and principal ideals (`pdFiltration_eq_span_of_eq_span_singleton`, `pdFiltration_le_iff_of_eq_span_singleton`), functoriality under divided power morphisms (`IsDPMorphism.map_pdFiltration_le`, `IsDPMorphism.map_pdFiltration_eq` requiring `I.map f = J` with no surjectivity assumption, and `pdFiltration_ofRingEquiv`). Proves the sharp equivalence `pdFiltration_eq_pow_iff` (`(∀ n, Fⁿ = I ^ n) ↔ ∀ m ≥ 2, ∀ x ∈ I, γₘ(x) ∈ I ^ m`) and derives `pdFiltration_bot`, `@[simp] pdFiltration_bot_of_ne_zero`, `pdFiltration_eq_pow` (`[Algebra ℚ R]`), `OfInvertibleFactorial.pdFiltration_eq_pow`, `OfInvertibleFactorial.pdFiltration_eq_bot`, `OfSquareZero.pdFiltration_eq_pow`, `OfSquareZero.pdFiltration_eq_bot`, `IsNilpotent.pdFiltration_eq_pow`, and `CharP.pdFiltration_eq_pow`.
- `TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/Nilpotent.lean` (297 lines, `namespace DividedPowers`, over `[CommSemiring R]` except the quotient form requiring `[CommRing A]`): defines `IsPDNilpotent` (`∃ n, 0 < n ∧ hI.pdFiltration n = ⊥`) with `isPDNilpotent_iff`, `isPDNilpotent_iff_exists_eq_bot`, `pow_eq_bot_of_pdFiltration_eq_bot`, `IsPDNilpotent.isNilpotent`, `IsPDNilpotent.le_nilradical`, `@[simp] isPDNilpotent_of_subsingleton`, `isPDNilpotent_of_eq_bot`, `@[simp] isPDNilpotent_bot`, and `isPDNilpotent_iff_eq_bot` (over `[IsReduced R]`). Proves functoriality (`IsPDNilpotent.map` with no surjectivity needed, `IsDPMorphism.isPDNilpotent_iff_of_injective`, and `isPDNilpotent_ofRingEquiv`), equivalence with `IsNilpotent I` via `isPDNilpotent_iff_isNilpotent_of_pdFiltration_eq_pow`, `isPDNilpotent_iff_isNilpotent_of_dpow_mem_pow`, and `isPDNilpotent_iff_isNilpotent` (`[Algebra ℚ R]`), plus PD-nilpotence of `OfInvertibleFactorial`, `OfSquareZero`, `DividedPowers.IsNilpotent`, and `DividedPowers.CharP`. Proves the factorial nilpotence bound `pow_eq_zero_of_factorial_eq_zero` (for all `n : ℕ`, strengthening Mathlib's `nilpotent_of_mem_dpIdeal`), `pow_eq_zero_of_natCast_pow_eq_zero` (for any nonzero `m : ℕ`, no primality needed, using `Nat.prod_factorial_dvd_factorial_sum`), `le_nilradical_of_isNilpotent_natCast`, `le_nilradical_iff_isNilpotent_natCast`, and `le_nilradical_iff_isNilpotent_of_quotient` (Stacks Tag 07GR).
- `TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/Padic.lean` (457 lines, `namespace PadicInt` and `namespace ZMod`): computes `valuation_dpow_p`, `dpow_p_mem_span_pow_iff`, and the Legendre valuation identity `sub_one_mul_valuation_dpow_p` (`(p - 1) * v_p(γₙ(p)) = (p - 2) * n + s_p(n)`), deducing `isSubDPIdeal_span_pow`, `isSubDPIdeal_ker_toZModPow_inf`, `pdFiltration_le_span_pow`, `pdFiltration_two_mul_le_span_pow`, and `not_isPDNilpotent_dividedPowers` for all primes `p`. For `p = 2`, proves `valuation_dpow_two` (`v₂(γₙ(2)) = (Nat.digits 2 n).sum`), `valuation_dpow_two_pow` (`v₂(γ_(2^a)(2)) = 1`), `dpow_two_two`, `exists_unit_mul_two_eq_dpow_two_pow`, `pdFiltration_two_eq` (`n ≠ 0 → Fⁿ = (2)`), and `span_two_sq_lt_pdFiltration_two`. Constructs the canonical quotient divided power structure `ZMod.dividedPowers p e` on `(p) ⊂ ZMod (p ^ e)` via `DividedPowers.Quotient.OfSurjective.dividedPowers` along `PadicInt.toZModPow e` with uniqueness (`dividedPowers_unique`), compatibility (`toZModPow_isDPMorphism`, `dividedPowers_dpow_toZModPow`), filtration transfer (`pdFiltration_dividedPowers`, `pdFiltration_dividedPowers_eq_bot_iff`, `pdFiltration_dividedPowers_eq_bot`, `pdFiltration_dividedPowers_two`), the complete classification `ZMod.isPDNilpotent_dividedPowers_iff` (`(ZMod.dividedPowers p e).IsPDNilpotent ↔ p ≠ 2 ∨ e ≤ 1`), general nilpotence (`ZMod.span_pow_eq_zero`, `ZMod.isNilpotent_span_natCast`), `ZMod.not_isPDNilpotent_dividedPowers_two`, and `ZMod.dividedPowers_two_two_ne_ofSquareZero` separating the two divided power structures on `(2) ⊂ ZMod 4`.

Attribution: Builds on Mathlib's `DividedPowers` formalization by A. Chambert-Loir and M. I. de Frutos-Fernández. Mathematical sources: Stacks Project, Crystalline Cohomology Section 60.5 (Tag 07HL, Definition 60.5.2 Tag 07HM), Section 60.6 (Tag 07HQ, paragraph between Lemmas 60.6.2 Tag 07HS and 60.6.3 Tag 07HT), Section 60.7 (Tag 07I1, observation before Situation 60.7.5 Tag 07MF); Divided Power Algebra Section 23.2 (Lemma 23.2.6, Tag 07GR), Section 23.3 (Remark 23.3.6), and Section 23.5 (Lemma 23.5.3); P. author: kaloyantanev
body:
Publishes the signed proposer config revisions to the Obol API and fetches them from it, the last follow-up of #4692. One use is recovery: a lost `proposer-config.json` otherwise takes a new edit ceremony.

- `--publish` on `charon alpha proposer edit` publishes the new revision once the ceremony is over; `charon dkg`, `charon create cluster` and the lock edit commands publish revision 1 after the lock. Opt-in and best effort, as for the lock.
- `charon alpha proposer publish` publishes the revision of an existing file. Revision 0 is unsigned and is not published.
- `charon alpha proposer fetch [--revision=N]` fetches it into the node's file: the request is signed with the node's ENR key, as only the cluster's operators may read builder URLs, and the response is verified against the lock before anything is written.

The Obol API does not serve these endpoints yet (`POST /proposer_config/{lock_hash}`, `GET /proposer_config/{lock_hash}/{share_index}?revision=N`), so this is tested against `obolapimock` only.

author: zenyoda3
body:
92 tests and wiring modules each carried a hand-copied regex to slice one service out of `docker-compose.apps.yml`, `/^  svc-x:\n(?:.*\n)*?(?=^  [a-z]|\Z)/m`. JavaScript has no `\Z`: it matches a literal capital `Z`, so the "end of file" branch of every copy never worked and a last service never ended. Separately, five lint rules each said "use the shared helper".

Now there is one reader, `composeServiceBlock(composeText, service)` in `@intafaced/config/compose`. A block ends at the first line at or above the services' indent (the next service, an indent-2 comment, a top-level key such as `volumes:`), or at the end of the text. Every copy calls it. One rule, `garden/use-shared-helper`, replaces `no-local-helper`, `no-local-scale`, `no-hand-decimal-parse`, `no-hand-trpc-unwrap` and `no-fetch-without-timeout`, and adds a `compose-slice` kind that refuses a new hand-written slice (in tests and apps too) with the fix in its message. Each message starts with its `[kind]`, and the lint ratchet counts each kind on its own (`ruleOf`), so removing one kind's copy never pays for adding another's, money scale and decimal parse included.

Weed: project-state#2761.

## Proof

- **The fault on today's main:** `packages/config/src/compose.test.ts` "the hand-written \Z slice it replaces never ended a last service" runs the copied pattern on a compose text whose last service is `svc-z`. It returns `null`. The shared reader returns the block.
- **The rule fails on the old code and passes on the new:** with this branch's `.oxlintrc.json` and plugin, oxlint over main's `services packages apps` finds **97** `compose-slice` findings. Over this head it finds **0**.
- **Nothing else moved:** on main, the five old rules report 139 findings in total. On this head, `garden/use-shared-helper` reports the same 139.
- **The ratchet still counts per kind:** the new test in `tooling/ci/lint-ratchet.test.mjs` runs a planted PR that removes a `fetch` copy and adds a `10n ** 18n` in the same file. It fails with `garden/use-shared-helper[local-scale] rose from 0 to 1`. With the per-kind key taken out of `ruleOf`, the same test passes the fault (checked locally, then restored). The known-good case (same kind removed and re-added) passes.
- `node --test tooling/lint/oxlint-plugin-garden/*.test.mjs`: 36/36. `node --test tooling/ci/lint-ratchet.test.mjs`: 10/10.
- vitest on every changed test file and every test that imports a changed module, across all 21 touched packages: all pass. The largest are svc-bank 64, svc-trade 58, svc-indexer 52, svc-academy 40, svc-pay 38 and svc-protocol 32.
- `turbo run typecheck` on the 22 touched packages: 47/47 tasks.

## What guards what it moved

- Money (`local-scale`, `hand-decimal-parse`): the same patterns, the same scope, error level, and counted per kind by the ratchet as before, under `garden/use-shared-helper[...]`.
- The compose pin tests (money, custody and sign-in env pins in svc-bank, svc-ledger, svc-identity, svc-pay and others): every assertion is unchanged. Only the slice they read comes from the shared reader. The reader drops trailing blank lines and lines after a column-0 key. No fixture in the real compose file depends on those.
- Four fixture tests (svc-execution, svc-indexer, svc-notify, svc-support) planted a column-0 `Z…` line *inside* a service to prove the old copies did not stop at `Z`. A column-0 line is a top-level YAML key, so it ends a service. Those fixtures now plant the `Z` line as a nested key, which keeps their point: a line starting with Z stays in the block. The column-0 case is covered in `compose.test.ts`.
- svc-tax and svc-ops checked the slice with `expect(match).toBeTruthy()`. Each now asserts that the block starts with its own service line instead (the Doctrine gates test-diff guard, net +0).
- `apps/admin` `adminComposeBlock` lost its fallback to "200 characters after `ADMIN_BFF_SHARED_SECRET`" when the admin block was missing. Now a missing block throws.

Decisions:
- The reader lives in `@intafaced/config` because 19 of the 21 callers already depend on it. `execution-arb` and `execution-mm` gain the workspace dependency (lockfile change).
- The reader is pure text in, text out. Callers keep reading the file themselves, as `config` does no I/O.
- The kind tag goes in the message, and `ruleOf` keys on it, so per-kind ratcheting survives the merge into one rule without a new config.
- The copied-helper rule for journey spec files stays a separate issue, as the weed says.

Revert: revert this squash commit. Nothing else depends on it yet.

## Handover
Head: e2d4cb45a9
Done: shared reader, 92 callers moved, one rule, per-kind ratchet, local proof above.
Not checked: CI on this head (pending).
Next: CI green, then ready and auto-merge.
Blocked: nothing.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Tests-only change to strengthen `tests/test_types.py` for **`src/srf/types.py`**.

## What the new tests check
- `SlipRate.sum()` with no axis adds in double precision and returns an `np.float64`: `[[2**24], [1]]` sums to `2**24 + 1`, which float32 can't represent.
- `SlipRate.from_pulses` converts each pulse to float32 on its own. Mixed `int64`/`uint64` pulses don't go through float64 first, because that rounds twice: `2**54 + 2**30 + 1` must become `2**54 + 2**31`, not `2**54`.
- The check that columns strictly increase along a row uses exact integers. Columns `2**53` and `2**53 + 1` are accepted, and `samples` is `2**53 + 2`.
- `SlipRate.delay` adds very large delays exactly. A delay of `2**53 + 1` gives columns `[2**53 + 1, 2**53 + 2]`.
- Indexing with a scalar raises the full `IndexError` message, checked with an anchored regex.

## Coverage of `src/srf/types.py`
100% before and 100% after (175 statements, none missed).

## Mutants
I applied each mutant by hand and ran the suite.

Killed:
- `__post_init____mutmut_64`: `columns.astype(None)`
- `from_pulses__mutmut_4`: `_column("pulse", pulse, None)`
- `sum__mutmut_2`: `values.sum(dtype=None)`
- `delay__mutmut_16`: `delays.astype(None)`
- `_take__mutmut_12`: the error message changed to `XX…XX`

Judged equivalent:
- `_column__mutmut_10`: setting `writeable = None` makes NumPy treat it as `False`, so the view is still read-only.
- `__post_init____mutmut_27`: checking offsets in float64 is exact, because valid offsets are bounded by `values.size`, which is far below `2**53`.
- `__post_init____mutmut_80`: assigning `None` into a bool array stores `False`.
- `from_pulses__mutmut_25` and `_27`: the empty `values` array is float64, but the constructor converts it to float32 anyway.
- `_stored_columns__mutmut_13` and `_15`: `np.arange`'s default integer type is `int64` on the 64-bit platforms this package targets.

I filed no issues, because none of these tests found a bug.

author: maasanto
body:
Fixes https://github.com/maasanto/blimey/issues/51

The song's playback now lives outside the timeline component, one per song, so leaving the timeline no longer closes it. Back on the timeline, the playhead and the Pause button pick it up again, and the audio carries on without reloading. The MIDI sender moved into the playback too, so messages stay in order across a remount. A send that fails while you are away still stops playback, and the timeline shows why when you come back.

## Decisions

- "Tabs" read as the app's own tabs (Monitor, Builder, Patch, Front view) and the Builder's screens, not browser tabs: those unmount the timeline, and that is what stopped playback.
- Playback also goes on on the scenes home: same root cause, and stopping there would need a rule the issue doesn't give.
- Opening a scene's editor pauses playback: each scene note-on the song sends clears the editor's look preview (docs/api.md, `POST /api/midi`), so both can't run together.
- An audition of another song pauses playback: its Program Change would otherwise make the playing song fire its notes into that song.
- Opening another song's timeline stops the first one's playback, as before: only one song plays at a time.
- No Pause control outside the timeline: the issue only asks for playback to go on, and the user returns to the timeline to stop it.
- Expect a conflict with the fix for #50 (the audience view not showing the active scene during playback), which likely touches the same playback state in `Timeline.svelte` and `playback.svelte.js`.

Playing, then on Monitor: scene 37 fires on time with the Builder unmounted. Back on the timeline, it is still playing at bar 3.

![Monitor while playing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maasanto/blimey/557ad8ed8086aef1f98e8427ea2e5352f38a8f93/51/2-monitor-while-playing.png)

author: stefanofa
body:
## Why

Stargrep launches on Show HN soon, and its landing page has to load fast. The landing JS budget is 130,000 B gzipped. Main sat at 129,727 B, so #136 (the footer) measured 320 B over, and every later landing change would hit the same wall. This PR frees about 5.7 KB without raising the budget or changing what a visitor sees.

## What changed

Base UI (the UI kit's primitives, about 4 KB gzipped with its helpers) shipped in the landing entry, though a signed-out first paint uses none of it. Three things pulled it in.

- The root error and not-found pages imported `Button`. They now load from the engine chunk through `lazyRouteComponent`, the same way `/privacy` and `/developers` do in #136. The router loads an error or not-found component only when a match ends in that state, on the server and in the browser, so the landing never waits on it.
- The sign-in problem tile (`?error=...` after a failed GitHub sign-in) rendered `SignInButton`. It moves to `sign-in-problem.tsx` and renders as an engine part inside the stars page's existing Suspense boundary. The server preloads the engine, so it paints the tile as before, and hydration keeps the server's HTML until the engine lands.
- `buttonVariants` lived in `button.tsx` beside `Button`. The landing's star link only needs the variants, but the bundler places a module and its imports in every chunk that reaches it, so Base UI followed. `buttonVariants` now has its own module.

The landing budget now forbids `@base-ui/` in landing chunks, so a later import fails `bun run check` instead of quietly costing 4 KB.

## Measurements

`bun run --cwd apps/web budget`, gzip level 9, on this branch's base `65788e39a`.

| Step | Landing JS | Engine JS with deps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 129,727 | 339,480 |
| this PR | 124,281 | 338,875 |

Each step measured on top of #136's head (`4a49269f2`), where the landing started at 130,320 B:

| Step | Landing JS | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #136 head | 130,320 | |
| error pages into the engine | 129,255 | -1,065 |
| sign-in problem tile into the engine | 128,561 | -694 |
| `buttonVariants` in its own module | 124,629 | -3,932 |

The split alone measured 130,320 B (no change), because the error pages and the tile still imported `Button` directly. All three are needed.

## Testing

- `bun run check` and `bun test --parallel` pass locally (1,887 tests).
- New server-page test renders `/?error=access_denied` on the server, hydrates it, and checks the tile and its button with no hydration errors. The existing tests for the 404 page and both error pages cover the lazy error components on the server.

author: aguiddir
body:
## Why

The [Herdr Annotate](https://plannotator.ai/tui-annotate/) plugin only loads in classic Herdr. The app runs on herdr-core, which has no plugin system, so Plannotator fell back to its web page in the system browser. The app cannot embed a web view, but `plannotator-tui` runs in one of its terminals.

## What

`bin/annotate.sh` opens `plannotator-tui` in a pane right of the terminal and sends the notes to the tab's agent when the review quits.

| Key | Opens |
|---|---|
| `ctrl-shift-r` | the terminal's folder: pick a Markdown file and annotate it |
| `ctrl-shift-y` | the agent's last reply |

- The notes go to the agent the app focused last in that tab, else the first one. `ANNOTATE_TO` overrides it.
- Nothing is sent when no note changed.
- `install.sh` checks for `plannotator-tui` (on the PATH, or the one the classic plugin ships) and `jq`.

## Tested

- A note written on a test document reached a stand-in terminal on quit.
- The last-reply mode opens on a live Claude session.
- The key's action, run by command, opens the review in the right folder and the pane closes on quit.

## Not confirmed

- **Agent choice in a tab with several agents**: I could not check that the app still reports the last focused agent once the review pane has the focus. Press `ctrl-shift-r` in such a tab and see which agent gets the notes.
- The keys were only run through `herdr-app do`, never pressed.

## Limits

- No Send button inside the review: the TUI's own needs classic Herdr's CLI, so sending happens on quit.
- When a file's notes changed, all of them are sent again, earlier ones included. "Finish review" in the `m` menu archives them.
- Annotating a terminal selection (the plugin's `prefix+a`) is not ported.
- Plan approval on leaving plan mode, code review and the Inbox stay in the browser.

author: mhwang285
body:
Add a new subgenerator ID specifically for hard process/signal events in JJ and GJ MCs, so that JJ/GJ events can be unambiguously identified relative to MB events. 

From this definition of [MCGenIdEncoding](https://github.com/AliceO2Group/AliceO2/blob/dev/DataFormats/simulation/include/SimulationDataFormat/MCGenProperties.h#L25-L37), the last 5 LSBs of the encoding are the subgenerator ID, and requesting it with `.getSubGeneratorId()` [returns 1 minus this value](https://github.com/AliceO2Group/AliceO2/blob/dev/DataFormats/simulation/include/SimulationDataFormat/MCGenProperties.h#L123-L126). So:

True MB events from MB MC: encoding = 127 = 00000 0000 1111111
	`subGeneratorId` = 0, so `.getSubGeneratorId` returns -1
MB gap events in JJ and GJ MC: encoding = 2175 = 00001 0000 1111111
	`subGeneratorId` = 1, so `.getSubGeneratorId` returns 0
GJ and JJ sig events in JJ MC: encoding = 4223 = 00010 0000 1111111
	`subGeneratorId` = 2, so `.getSubGeneratorId` returns 1

author: pch
body:
Part of #998 (PR 8 of 8), stacked on #1144: **Read Smart Collections from Lightroom Catalog…** for catalogs imported before smart collections were imported.

## What changes for the user

A catalog imported from Lightroom by an earlier release has its smart collections, but without their rules (they list no photos, saying why). It also has no collection sorts, no target collection, and no keyword synonyms (the notice says so). **Catalog › Read Smart Collections from Lightroom Catalog…** fixes that:

- It asks for the `.lrcat`, starting where the catalog was imported from. It reads a copy of it, as an import does, and refuses a catalog Lightroom has open.
- It **only fills in what is missing**: rules of smart collections that have none, sorts of collections that have none, the target collection when none was chosen here, and synonyms of keywords that have none. Rules or sorts changed here, and a target chosen here, are never replaced. Reading the same catalog again changes nothing.
- A collection counts as that Lightroom catalog's only when its id, name, set and kind are the same; a keyword when its id and name are. Anything else (renamed or moved here, or from another catalog) is left alone and listed: a short summary on the status line, every item in its detail.
- Keyword synonyms become complete, and the notice goes, only when every keyword of the catalog, used or not, is that Lightroom catalog's. Otherwise they stay incomplete and the summary says so.
- Like an import, it can't be undone, and the file picker's title says so.

## How

`Catalog::read_smart_collections` (`catalog/lightroom/recover.rs`) works on a snapshot, in one transaction, with the import's checks, and returns `SmartRecovery`. The app runs it on a worker with its own connection, then opens the catalog again, so smart collections are worked out afresh. The summary is `library::smart::smart_read_line`.

## Testing

- `make check` passed locally on 2e7db026b.
- New tests:
  - a catalog imported "the earlier way" gets back rules, sorts, target and synonyms;
  - rules and sorts changed here are kept;
  - a second run changes nothing;
  - renamed collections and keywords, and a nameless root keyword that doesn't match, are listed and left as they are, and synonyms stay missing;
  - a Quick Collection target;
  - the summary text, with every item in its detail.
- Not run here: a real Lightroom catalog (synthetic `.lrcat` with the measured row shapes only), and the file picker (UI).

## Local Codex review

- Round 1 (Codex `gpt-6-astra` medium) on 1488dfd96: NOT OK, two reporting defects, both fixed:
  1. A nameless root keyword could block completion without being listed, while the summary said "nothing was missing".
  2. Only the first three mismatches were kept.
- Round 2 on 2e7db026b: **OK**.

body:
Chainguard Team includes every application, base, and AI catalog image at its latest build, on top of the 5 picks. The docs don't say so, and nothing documents how to add one of these images. This PR adds both. It was held out of the launch docs until the registry fix that makes these pulls work reached production; it was verified there on Nov 17.

## Changes

- `plans.md`: the Team **Catalog images** row, and a paragraph on what Team gets for images outside the picks.
- `upgrade-team.md`: a bullet under "What changes when you upgrade," and a new "Add a catalog image outside your picks" procedure with the refusal message.

## Verified in production on Nov 17, in a Team test organization

- Adding a non-pick image with `chainctl images repos create --source` uses no pick.
- Its `latest` and `latest-dev` builds pull on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, with `crane pull` and `docker pull`.
- Version tags such as `python:3.12` are refused with the Team plan message, even when they point to the newest 3.12 build. Engineering confirmed this is intended: for an image outside the picks, only the newest build of its highest version counts.

Not verified: the 14-day window for a replaced build comes from the design doc.

## Testing

- `hugo --gc --minify` builds cleanly, and the new section's anchor and both links to it resolve.
- `check-related-pages` found no other page that describes Team's catalog access.

## Summary

When a strongly-typed variation method (for example `boolVariation` on a string flag) returns the default value with a `WRONG_TYPE` reason, the analytics events must describe that same result. The evaluation algorithm spec says to treat a wrong-type result as if the variation index were undefined, with an `ERROR` / `WRONG_TYPE` reason, and to use the default value in any analytics events. The existing wrong-type tests check only the returned value and reason, so an SDK can return the default while it reports the flag's value and variation in its events.

This adds a "wrong type evaluation events" test group under events, for server-side and client-side SDKs that have the `strongly-typed` capability. Each test evaluates a tracked flag with a typed method of the wrong type (bool, int, double and string, against bool, number and string flags), with and without reasons. It checks that:

- the feature event has the default value, no variation, the flag version, and a `WRONG_TYPE` reason when reasons are included;
- the summary counter has the default value, the flag version, and no variation.

Numeric flags are not tested with the int and double methods, because SDKs differ in how they convert between those two types.

Results from running the new tests locally:

- Pass: Go, Java, .NET server, Node server.
- Fail: Rust, C++ server and client, Lua, Haskell, .NET client, Node client. The js-core browser SDKs share the Node client code. Android and iOS were not run here, but their code has the same problem. Fixes for each are in progress.
- Skipped (no typed variation methods): Python, Ruby, PHP, Erlang.

The same tests for the other harness version: #653 (v2).
<!-- TERMAG_PR_BODY_END -->

https://claude.ai/code/session_01M2LziV9hBUh3o3xEFTpAwE

## What

- **`uart_rx_port`** is a receive-only FerroHAL `Uart` on an `RxWiring`, served from two vectors by its own members, `on_rx_uart` and `on_rx_stream`.
  - Each member serves the UART and reads the firmware's monotonic inside the interrupt.
  - It spawns `events(events, at_us)` with the arrival time in microseconds.
  - A wake dropped while the reader is queued leaves the queued wake's earlier stamp, so data never looks newer than it is.
  - Requirements: PORT-101 and PORT-102.
- **New dependencies:** `rtic-monotonics =2.2.1` and `fugit =0.3.9`, which a `monotonic = Mono` member needs.
- **`port-contract.md`** gains these rules:
  - A receive-only port is its own group.
  - A port carries no protocol: decoders live in the application or a protocol crate.
  - The receive constraints, promoted from FerroForge's retired prototype text.
- **Removed during the work:**
  - `sbus_rx`, because protocols are not hardware.
  - `tick`, because a real firmware runs its periodic work inside the timer's interrupt, where a group's spawn hop only adds latency.
- No application specifics appear in code, docs, requirements or the bench.

## Bench

`hil/nucleo-f401re-rx-ports` uses the existing J1 and J2 links. It drives PA9 and PA11 as GPIO, because a receive-only port has no transmitter of its own.
- Two `uart_rx_port`s: USART6 at 8N1 and USART1 at 8E2.
- SysTick at 1 kHz is the monotonic.
- It checks bytes in order, idle-line wakes, and stamp ordering.

## Evidence

- **F401 bench:** run on the rig at ecff97e through `tools/rig_run.py`. 6 of 6 checks passed, exit 0. Recorded with `reqtool record` in 26d760c.
- **Host tests:** recorded with `reqtool test`.
- **Requirements:** `reqtool check` shows PORT-001 to 003, 101 and 102 verified.
- **Checks:** `checks/run.sh` passes.
- **Record history:**
  - Records from earlier iterations of this branch remain as history.
  - 946a5a0 drops one record that was made with a relative `--repository .`, which left the library files out of its configuration. It is the same run, recorded again.

author: nimbleengineer21
body:
## What

Adds `cmd/loadgen`, a load generator that sends concurrent `POST /v1/messages` requests (stream or non-stream) to one or more gateways and reports outcomes, token counts, and TTFT/latency quantiles, as text or `-json`. Docs in `docs/loadgen.md`.

## Why

The demo and the coming multi-replica overspend test need a way to drive a team past its budget across both replicas and count what happened: `ok`, `http_429`, `stream_rate_limit_error` (cut mid-stream), `stream_truncated`, `transport`, `canceled`.

Design notes:
- The gateway key comes from `TW_GATEWAY_KEY` only, never a flag (argv leaks), same rule as the gateway's upstream key.
- `-url` takes a comma-separated list; request n goes to URL n mod len, so one run loads both replicas.
- `-duration` stops new requests; requests in flight run to completion, so the end of the run does not add fake failures.
- Each prompt starts with its request number, so the seeded mock does not send one reply to every request.
- Quantiles are nearest-rank in integer math (no float rounding moves the rank).
- Token counts are the usage that replies report; input = input + cache creation + cache read, the same sum the gateway charges.

No new dependency (stdlib + `internal/anthropic` SSE reader). No DB code.

## How tested

- `make check` (lint, `test -race`, build, tidy, govulncheck, gitleaks): green.
- Tests beside source: config errors, flag-table parity with `docs/loadgen.md`, a full run against `internal/mock` (stream and non-stream), request shape and unique prompts, each outcome class (`ok`, error event, missing `message_stop`, bad data, 429/403/503, transport, timeout), request count + round-robin, duration stop, canceled run, quantiles, text report.
- Mutation check: 19/19 mutants killed (request limit, duration stop, canceled override, usage merges, round-robin index, error type, outcome classes, cache-token sum, latency filter, TTFT filter, rank rounding, max).
- Manual, Compose stack: `TW_GATEWAY_KEY=tw_test_red_alice loadgen -url http://127.0.0.1:8080,http://127.0.0.1:8082 -requests 200 -concurrency 50` → `ok=200`; team blue (600 tokens/min) `-requests 6` → `http_429=4 ok=2`. The docs example is that real output.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title is a Conventional Commit
- [x] `make check` passes
- [x] New dependencies are explained above
- [x] Docs or ADRs are updated if behavior or design changed

author: mmd30na-sketch
body:
## Why
Live `carla-crm` logs showed repeated `Gemini OCR failed key#1 gemini-2.5-flash` with `relay: upstream timeout`. The Iran `gemini-relay` (SOCKS to Google) can wait 120s, but OCR’s budget is 25–50s and `generateContent` had no per-attempt timeout, so later Gemini models/keys were never tried. Cloud Vision is optional and not configured on the server.

Gemini is reachable from Iran through the existing SOCKS relay; the failure is hang/timeout (and occasional 503), not a hard block.

## What
- `ocrProviders.ts`: per-attempt `AbortSignal` + timeout (default 12s, `GEMINI_OCR_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS`), then an OpenAI-compatible vision fallback (`OCR_VISION_*`, otherwise `COPILOT_API_URL` / `COPILOT_API_KEY`).
- `server.ts` `/api/ocr` tries Gemini, then the free vision fallback; Cloud Vision path is unchanged.
- Tests: `npm run test:ocr-providers` (timeout/abort, 429 key rotation, vision 500→200, no API key in logs). `npm run test:ocr` still passes.

User authorized merge and deploy to the Iran server.

author: blancamunizaga
body:
Parte de #118 (GC-2 de la orquestación #116).

## Qué cambia

- **Rutas nuevas del admin para categorías**, limitadas al país de la sesión:
  - `GET /admin/categories`: todas las categorías del país, habilitadas o no. Cada una trae su umbral propio (`null` = global), `layerCount` y `publishedLayerCount`. La respuesta también trae `readable` y `errors` de `categories.json`.
  - `POST /admin/categories`: crea una categoría habilitada con un `id` que elige el admin. Un id ya usado, incluso por una entrada rechazada, y `deforestation` responden 409.
  - `PUT /admin/categories/{id}`: reemplaza los campos editables. Editar `deforestation` la guarda primera en el archivo, y editar una entrada rechazada la repara.
  - `PATCH /admin/categories/{id}`: habilita o deshabilita.
  - No hay borrado, y los ids nunca se reutilizan.
- **El significado de una capa publicada no cambia en el lugar.** Estos casos responden 400 con las capas que hay que ocultar primero:
  - deshabilitar una categoría con capas publicadas;
  - cambiar la polaridad de una categoría con capas publicadas;
  - cambiar `temporal` de una categoría que tiene alguna capa;
  - reparar una entrada rechazada que tiene capas publicadas;
  - publicar una capa cuya categoría está deshabilitada o no se resuelve;
  - mover una capa publicada a otra categoría;
  - reparar una entrada rechazada, o crear una categoría cuyo id ya usan capas del índice, mientras alguna de esas capas esté publicada o tenga años que no calzan con el `temporal` (agregado por los reviews);
  - publicar una capa cuyos años no calzan con su categoría: una categoría temporal exige los dos años y las demás ninguno (agregado por los reviews).
  - habilitar o deshabilitar una categoría que tiene capas publicadas (agregado por los reviews).
- **Invariante en la lectura (agregado por los reviews):** `GET /maps` y `GET /countries` solo ofrecen una capa habilitada, con su categoría resuelta y habilitada, con años que calzan con la categoría y con su raster en disco. Vale para cualquier cosa que haya editado el share. Si una capa no cumple, se oculta, se registra en el log una vez, y el admin la muestra con `category_issue` o con `layer_issue` (`years_mismatch`, `missing_raster`). El análisis, los tiles y las imágenes la siguen resolviendo por id, como decidió GC-1.
- **`LayerInput` exige `category_id`**, que tiene que ser una categoría habilitada del país. Al editar, una capa puede quedarse en su categoría actual aunque esté deshabilitada.
  - Los años son obligatorios en las categorías `temporal` y van en `null` en las demás.
  - Las dos claves de año siempre se escriben, que es la regla de rollback de GC-1.
- **`AdminLayer` devuelve `category_id`, `category_issue` y `category_enabled`**, así el admin ve por qué una capa no es pública (D14).
- **`LayerStore.put_category`** cambia una sola entrada de `categories.json` y deja las demás tal como están guardadas, incluidas las rechazadas: nada se pierde. Si el archivo no se puede leer, responde 409 y no lo sobrescribe.
- **Contrato regenerado** (`openapi.json` y `schema.d.ts`).
- **Puente web:** el formulario del admin envía el `category_id` de la capa (`deforestation` si es nueva) hasta que GC-5 agregue el selector. No agrega UI ni claves de i18n.
- **Docs:** `docs/maps.md` (nueva sección "Managing categories in the admin"), `docs/architecture.md` y `docs/onboarding.md`.

**Cambios por el review** ([review](https://github.com/undp/monbo/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5942566823), commit `4943b2d`):
- Bloqueante: reparar una categoría rechazada ya no puede cambiar `temporal` por debajo de los años de sus capas, y publicar una capa vuelve a revisar sus años contra la categoría. Esto último también cubre las ediciones a mano del share.
- Reparar una entrada rechazada conserva su `enabled` guardado: `PUT` nunca cambia si una categoría es pública.
- El docstring de `models.py` quedó en 88 columnas.

**Cambios por la re-revisión** ([review](https://github.com/undp/monbo/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5943523241), commit `2b55890`):
- Bloqueante: `POST /admin/categories` ya no publica capas huérfanas. Si capas del índice ya apuntan al id (`unknown_category`, por una edición a mano), aplica la misma regla que la reparación: tienen que estar ocultas y sus años tienen que calzar con `temporal`. Si no, responde 400 y nombra las capas. Esas capas solo se vuelven públicas con `PATCH`.
- `years_fit` exige los dos años en una categoría temporal y ninguno en las demás. Una capa con un solo año ya no pasa ni la publicación ni la reparación.

**Cambios por la segunda re-revisión** ([review](https://github.com/undp/monbo/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5944222959), commit `2b59ae9`):
- Bloqueante: `PATCH /admin/categories/{id}` responde 400 si la categoría tiene capas publicadas, tanto al habilitarla como al deshabilitarla. Sus capas solo se publican una por una con `PATCH /admin/layers/{id}`.
- Red de seguridad: el invariante en la lectura descrito arriba (`LayersRoot.is_public`, que reemplaza el `is_public_layer` de GC-1).
  - Los años se revisan como tag, sin I/O.
  - El raster se revisa solo en los listados, así los tiles no pagan un `stat` por capa.
  - Un año ilegible ya no da 500 en `GET /maps`: la capa se oculta. `GET /admin/layers` sigue dando 500 en ese caso, como antes de esta PR.
  - La spec `layer-storage` suma el invariante, y los fixtures de tests que listan capas ahora escriben su raster.

**Cambios por la tercera re-revisión** ([review](https://github.com/undp/monbo/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5945062122), commit `639f718`; solo nits):
- `years_fit` aplica las reglas de `LayerInput` con el mismo código: `YEAR_MIN`, `YEAR_MAX` y `years_problem` pasaron a `layers/categories.py`, y `LayerInput` los usa desde ahí. Ya no pasan años invertidos, fuera de rango ni booleanos.
- `enabled` solo cuenta como publicado si es el booleano `true` (`is_enabled`). Lo leen igual el listado público, `AdminLayer`, los guards y `PATCH /admin/layers/{id}`. Esto también cierra un caso que encontré: con `"enabled": "true"` como string, el `PATCH` se saltaba los chequeos de categoría.
- `GET /maps` filtra por país antes de `is_public`, así solo hace `stat` a los rasters que puede listar.
- `GET /admin/layers` muestra un año ilegible como `null`, con `layer_issue: "years_mismatch"`, en vez de responder 500 para todo el país.
- El fixture de EC tiene una capa pública de verdad, y el test de aceptación revisa la lista de EC.
- Dos frases de `docs/maps.md` y del design volvieron a su párrafo.

author: zhongkechen
body:
## Problem

The get_message cache has no TTL and retains an old Telegram file reference. A FileReferenceExpired error from file retrieval does not cause the message to be fetched again; replaying the same video reuses the old reference and fails again.

This PR adds an issue description and an independently executable offline reproduction case, with review priority **P2**.

## Preconditions

A video message has been cached. The mocked Telegram file RPC returns the real FileReferenceExpired exception type on subsequent reads. A successful message response with a fresh reference is prepared as the next fetch response.

## Expected and observed behavior

- Expected: after a file reference expires, replay should not continue reusing that invalid reference.
- Observed: both replay attempts raise FileReferenceExpired, and both file requests contain the old reference. GetMessages runs only once; the prepared fresh reference is never fetched.

## Source locations

- [castbot/client.py:51](https://github.com/zhongkechen/castbot/blob/dfba532498d7630a3bb15b0546dc5847f5482ee9/castbot/client.py#L51)
- [castbot/client.py:83](https://github.com/zhongkechen/castbot/blob/dfba532498d7630a3bb15b0546dc5847f5482ee9/castbot/client.py#L83)
- [castbot/client.py:92](https://github.com/zhongkechen/castbot/blob/dfba532498d7630a3bb15b0546dc5847f5482ee9/castbot/client.py#L92)

## Reproduction

From the repository root, in an environment with the project's locked dependencies installed, run:

```bash
poetry run python -m unittest discover -s tests/repro_cases -p test_13_expired_file_reference.py -v
```

The case constructs real RawMessage and Document objects and replaces Telegram RPCs with local AsyncMock objects. It executes the real get_message → get_block sequence twice and checks caching, request references, and RPC call counts.

**PASS confirms the currently observed defect, not remediation.** The case asserts existing erroneous behavior; update or replace these assertions when that behavior changes.

## Validation and limitations

Offline Python 3.14 verification: **1 test passed**.

- No Telegram connection was made, and the server's actual reference-expiration interval was not measured.
- The RPC boundary simulates a known file-reference-expiration error. All document identifiers, references, and account data are fictional.

author: caikun-pjlab
body:
## Motivation

Health checks and Prometheus scrapes share the inference API event loop. Synchronous preprocessing of long prompts can delay `/health` and `/metrics`, making monitoring less responsive under load.

This change introduces an optional dedicated monitoring listener to improve response latency while keeping the scope focused on monitoring.

## Changes

- Add `--monitoring-port` to serve `/health` and `/metrics` in a dedicated thread with its own event loop.
- Read thread-safe health snapshots and reuse the existing Prometheus registry.
- Expose health snapshot age and scheduler update timestamps to make data freshness observable.
- Allocate consecutive monitoring ports for local DP replicas.
- Preserve the existing endpoints on the API port. No additional listener starts unless configured.

Backend health probes and metric updates retain their existing scheduling. The dedicated listener improves response handling; it does not increase data update frequency.

## Test results

**Regression tests:** 3,174 passed, 12 skipped, and 40 deselected in both the local environment and the test container. The deselected tests require model weights and GPU backend integration.

**Live benchmark:** compared API ports `9200–9207` with monitoring ports `9300–9307` simultaneously on an eight-DP deployment.

| Input length | Total service concurrency | Duration |
|---|---:|---:|
| ~32K tokens | 8 | 60 seconds |
| ~128K tokens | 16 | 90 seconds |
| ~256K tokens | 16 | 90 seconds |

Requests used a repeated prefix with prefix caching and generated one output token. Each monitoring endpoint was sampled once per second.

Aggregated results across all eight DP replicas and the three load stages, with **1,920 samples per endpoint and port group**:

| Endpoint | API-port p99 | Monitoring-port p99 | p99 reduction | Responses >500 ms, API → monitoring |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `/health` | 714.57 ms | 112.17 ms | **84.3%** | 209 → **0** |
| `/metrics` | 686.02 ms | 174.25 ms | **74.6%** | 126 → **0** |

Including baseline, warmup, and cooldown, all **2,672 inference requests** and **10,452 monitoring requests** succeeded. Scheduler metrics continued updating, and final request/token counters matched between both listeners for every DP replica.

Neither port group exceeded five seconds during the measured load stages, and no router unhealthy transition was observed. These results demonstrate improved monitoring latency under the tested long-text workload; they do not establish a reduction in router health-check failures.

author: andyrub18
body:
Main's CI failed right after #116: two tests of `BudgetLimitTests` refused with `IllegalStateException` ("Dispatchers.Main is used concurrently with setting it"). Nothing is wrong in the app; this is a timing race in the test harness, and one event failed both tests.

## What happened

- A view model's coroutines are its own, not the test's. A test that has seen what it came for returns while the view model may still be waiting for the mock server's answer.
- The answer comes back a moment later on the HTTP engine's thread and takes the coroutine to Main, at the moment `@AfterTest` gives Main back.
- kotlinx-coroutines-test refuses that change, and keeps the refusal for the next test's setup too.
- All 15 view model test classes were exposed. The PR's run and main's were the same code; main's was the unlucky one.

## Reproduced

A loop of the failing test's shape, 400 rounds, four times (also with the processor kept busy): 8 to 11 refusals each time before, none in 1,600 rounds after.

## The fix

- `TestMain` (commonTest): what `@BeforeTest` and `@AfterTest` call. A refused change waits for that moment to pass and is made again; one that still refuses after two seconds is shown.
- The 15 test classes use it.
- `TestMainUseTest` fails on a test that changes Main directly, and names the file.

## What it does not do

It does not make each test wait for its view model to finish. That would mean running the mock server on the test's own thread in every test file's server setup, which is more change than this fault is worth now.

## Checked

- The app's tests three times from scratch (495).
- The new check failing on an offender.
- The client job's whole command (common Kotlin, tests, desktop and Android builds).

No app code changes. Docs: ROADMAP (bugs table), CLAUDE.md.

author: arpan404
body:
## Cause

On one person's Mac (ace 0.0.23), agent control failed at every start with `Missing engine state`. Machines, transfers and external MCP went down with it. A parent thread had been deleted and later purged by storage cleanup: its `threads` row stayed as a tombstone, but its `thread_state` was gone. Two of its delegations were settled while their children were still `limited`, so `journal.revived()` returned them, and `ChildSync.reconcile` called `engine.updateChild(parent)`, which threw. Nothing caught it. The same gap made the machine-children poll fail once a second for 26 hours: settled children of that parent were re-read, `machineChild` threw, and the read counted as unapplied.

"Thread is gone" had no owner. Four paths wrote the tombstone, and only the person's delete ran the deletion policy (`cancelDescendants`). Purging left every row in other tables that names the thread. Readers assumed the thread was still there.

The notification warmup error, `Missing notification thread`, is the same class of bug. A purge deletes a thread's whole event log, `thread.created` included, so any later write to that thread leaves an orphan event, and notification replay threw on it at every start.

## Fix (ADR 0183)

- `thread-gone.ts` owns it:
  - `retireThread` runs the deletion policy and writes the tombstone in one transaction.
  - `purgeThread` purges the data and records the purge in one transaction; it also removes the thread's engine session, selection and queue rows.
  - `threadGone` is the read rule: deleted, or no engine state.
- All tombstone writers go through it: the thread lifecycle, project removal, the removed-project sweep and storage cleanup. The last three skipped the policy before.
- **Agent control:**
  - Deleting a thread settles its open child edges as cancelled, with wakes suppressed.
  - A settled edge is never revived for a gone parent.
  - Recovery settles or skips edges and queued launches whose parent is gone, and reports once when a parent that was never deleted lost its state.
  - The wake loop discards results owed to a gone parent.
  - A reservation row this build can't read is kept, reported once and skipped.
- **Machine children:** the engine is reached only for a parent that is still there.
  - Settled children of a gone parent leave the re-check.
  - An open one is stopped; if its machine is unpaired, it stops being tracked.
  - The stop/lease check and each machine's planning now fail on their own, so one failure no longer skips the rest of the poll.
- **Readers:** model-default migration, transfer hold and adoption, messages to a child of a gone parent, delegated machine threads, and notification ingest all treat a gone thread as gone.
- Children are never shown done for a gone parent: running ones are cancelled by the deletion policy, and limited ones are left as they are.
- Merges origin/main, including #2228, and keeps its guards. `machines/parent-gone.ts` now uses `threadGone`.

## Review fixes

- **A child of a gone parent can be carried on.** Deleting a delegated thread records a subtree stop on it, and the command policy applied that ancestor fence before checking whether the parent was gone. A limited grandchild of a deleted middle thread therefore refused every Resume and message from the person as `cancelled`. The policy now recognizes a gone parent first: the person's explicit work continues the child on its own, its edge stays settled, and nothing is delivered to the gone parent. Work still being cancelled from the deletion stays cancelled, and automatic work stays fenced. Test: `deleted-parent.process.test.ts`, "the person can carry on a limited child of a deleted, purged middle thread on its own".
- **A purge goes a batch at a time and resumes.** The tombstone stays the visibility fence. The purge is recorded in `thread_purges`, and the transcript is deleted in writes of at most 512 rows, each followed by a turn of the event loop (WITHOUT ROWID tables are deleted by primary key). A last small transaction removes the engine state and the engine's own rows, records the deletion and marks the thread purged. A purge cut short by a stop or a restart is finished in the background at the next start. Tests: `thread-purge.process.test.ts`:
  - other writers get in between batches, and the thread reads as gone throughout;
  - a purge cut short finishes after a restart.

### Measurement: one synthetic deleted thread, 20,000 items (20,002 events)

| | Writes | Longest single write | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before: one transaction | 1 | 256 ms | 256 ms |
| After: batches of 512 | 123 | 7.9 ms | 312 ms |

## Re-review fixes

- **Only the person carries on a child whose parent is gone.** The exception skips the deleted thread's ancestor fence, and it now applies only to the person's own commands. It does not apply to `parent_agent` sends, to anything sent while an agent's tool is running, to ace's agent or automation devices, or to outside grants. Test: in "the person can carry on a limited child of a deleted, purged middle thread on its own", an ancestor agent's message and resume are refused as `cancelled`.
- **Every purge write is bounded, cascades included.**
  - Rows owned through a cascading key (output, blob and streamed-blob chunks, item text, source chunks, history revisions) are found from the schema and deleted by key, in batches, before their owners.
  - Item text streams, the history index tables, view windows and the `long_`/`client_` read models are now purged.
  - The two tables with no `thread_id` index are reached through items and streams.
  - Finished intents are batched with the transcript, and the purge resumes from the step it reached.
  - Each write reports every row it changed. Completion only removes engine state and rows and records the purge.
- **Test:** `thread-purge.process.test.ts`, "a thread with one very large stream, long item text and many finished intents is purged in bounded writes". Before the fix:
  - a single write changed 6,001 rows;
  - completion changed 3,005 rows;
  - 3,000 source chunks and 2 text streams were left behind.

  After the fix, no write changes more than 200 rows (the batch size), completion stays under 50 rows, and nothing is left.

## Tests (each fails on origin/main)

- `thread-gone.process.test.ts` (invariant): one tree per deletion path (delete, project removal, storage cleanup), each with a limited child, a running child and a re-checked remote child. Each is retired, purged and restarted. Agent control, machines, transfers, external MCP and notifications come up; no open edge, wake, launch, engine row or tracked machine child names a gone parent; delegation still works.
- `agent-control/deleted-parent.process.test.ts`:
  - the real case (revived path);
  - an open edge whose parent was purged while agent control was down (active path);
  - deletion settling open edges at the source;
  - a queued launch whose parent was purged.
- `agent-control/recovery.process.test.ts`: an unreadable reservation row.
- `machines/children-gone-parent.process.test.ts`:
  - settled children are not re-read every poll;
  - a working child is stopped;
  - an unpaired working child stops being tracked.
- `machines/settlement-delivery.process.test.ts`: a failing stop check doesn't hold back results owed in the same poll.
- `packages/notify/src/purged-thread.test.ts`: replay passes over an orphan event.

`bun run fmt`, `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` pass. Only the added and changed test files were run.

body:
## Summary
After a jump to a comment that isn't on screen yet, the files that mount around it keep resizing for a few frames. Pierre holds the top of the viewport still while they do, which pushes the card about 70px down. The align loop stopped after 12 frames, so the card was left off-center. Locally a second click put it back, but on Windows CI the resize landed even later, so `lazy-comments.perf.spec.ts` kept failing on `e2e-windows (2)` on unrelated PRs (#1177, #1192).

- The alignment keeps going until the card is centered and the list has been still for 300ms, up to 2s. When the card can't be centered because the list is at its top or end, it accepts the nearest position.
- Any input from the reader cancels it: wheel, touch, pointer down (clicks and scrollbar drags) or any key. It never pulls the list back against the reader. Listeners are removed on every exit.
- Pierre's pending scroll target is cleared before each correction, so Pierre doesn't fight the alignment.

- `lazy-comments.perf.spec.ts` now measures from the first click and checks three repeat clicks, reading positions only once the card has stopped moving.
  - On the old code it fails every time (`Received: 70`, the Windows CI failure).

author: dillan-03
body:
Closes #108

Five new item kinds sit in existing categories, so ⌘1–⌘9 stay as they are: output styles, the status line and keybindings go under **Settings**, and LSP servers and monitors under **Plugins**. Every rule below comes from the verbatim Claude Code docs. Sources are in `docs/configuration-resolution.md`.

## Output styles
- **Sources:** `output-styles/` in `~/.claude`, the repo's `.claude`, managed settings, and enabled plugins. The name comes from the frontmatter `name`, or the file name.
- **Which applies:** the highest-precedence `outputStyle` selects one, and a plugin style with `force-for-plugin` overrides it.
  - The selected style is **Applies**. Others are **Inactive** (available).
  - Built-ins such as Explanatory leave every custom style inactive.
- **New issue:** `outputStyle` that doesn't match a style exactly. Names are case-sensitive, so "explanatory" silently gives Default.
- **Same name in two folders:** **Unknown**, because the docs don't say which wins.
- **Edits:** need a restart.

## Status line
- **Which runs:** the highest-precedence `statusLine` wins and is **Conditional**, because it stays blank until the folder is trusted. Lower-precedence copies are **Overridden**.

author: jamesonlin
body:
Part of YIV-530. Real issuance on staging is in YIV-646, and what needs WE BUILD itself is in YIV-654.

## What changes

- Vendors the WE BUILD SD-JWT VC schemas and samples for EUCC, EU-PoA, VAT-ID and UBO (Apache 2.0) at a pinned upstream commit. A test checks the files against their sha256.
- LEI has no published JSON schema upstream, so `lei-sd-jwt.json` is written from the `rb-lei` rulebook. Like the upstream EUCC, EU-PoA and UBO schemas, it refuses claims the rulebook does not define.
- An organization can import a rulebook as a schema (`POST /orgs/{slug}/attestations/rulebooks/{id}/import`). Its vct, subject type and attributes are fixed.
- A rulebook's vct is only available through that import. Creating a normal schema with it is refused (`vct_rulebook`).
- Issuing from a rulebook template takes JSON claims, checked against the rulebook schema (`invalid_claims`). Organization-defined schemas still take strings only.
- The held credential view shows nested claims and whether a rulebook-type credential matches its rulebook.
- The issuer bundle lists every nested claim path. LEI claims are `sd: never`, as its rulebook says.
- Rulebook templates can't join the onboarding auto-issue set.
- The seed imports all five rulebooks into the demo org.
- Migration: `attestation_schemas.rulebook` (nullable).

### Issuer side of an offer to an organization

Found while testing. Both also affected offers on `main`.

- **Accepted:** the Issued list now asks the issuer about each open offer, so an offer the receiving organization accepted shows as claimed. The stub issuer keeps an offer to an organization pending until the stub holder redeems it.
- **Declined:** declining sends a QERDS message back to the issuer, which marks the offer `declined`. The message carries the offer's SHA-256, not the offer link. Migration: `declined` added to the issued status check.

## Not in this PR

- **YIV-646** (no WE BUILD access needed): release to staging, the `we-build-*` credential configs on the hosted Veramo issuer in `openid4vc-poc-ops`, a real round trip, nested selective disclosure in irmago, and revocation reaching the receiver.
- **YIV-654** (needs WE BUILD): which `status` claim shape is meant, and exchanging rulebook attestations with other WE BUILD parties. EUCC, EU-PoA, UBO and LEI define a different shape than the Token Status List our issuer emits, so validation accepts any shape until then.
- New offers and status changes only show after a page refresh, because nothing is pushed to the page. That is a separate issue.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the rulebook package (samples validate, invalid and extra claims are rejected, nested claim paths), the import/issue validation, the refused rulebook vct and the issuer config.
- Integration tests for import, issuing with nested claims, the onboarding refusal, an organization offer going from offered to claimed, and a decline marking the offer declined.
- Tested by hand locally with the stub issuer and holder: import, issue with JSON claims and the claims check, accept and decline between two organizations, the mismatch warning on a held credential, onboarding, the locked schema form and the received EUCC values.

author: bjorn-ali-goransson
body:
GPU G2, step 3: Direct3D 11 runs, and its frame reaches the desktop.

`d3d11_test` makes a D3D11 device and a DXGI swap chain on a window,
clears the back buffer, copies a second render target into it, reads the
frame back and presents it; the screen check finds it on the desktop.
DXVK 3.1.1 (PREBUILT, shipped beside the program -- System32's
`dxgi.dll` stays gala's, the one the Vulkan loader calls) sits on the
Vulkan stack `vk_test` already uses: Mesa's lavapipe through the Khronos
loader. No shader, so no HLSL compiler yet.

## The blocker this turned up

`Present` returned `S_OK` and nothing appeared. gala presents a window
when the window's **own** thread's message queue empties -- and DXVK
blits each frame from a presenter thread of its own while the program's
thread sits in `GetMessage`, which it never leaves again.

The fix keys on the window's thread, not on the DC's lifetime:

- `client_dc` tells gdi32 which thread each window DC was handed out for
  (`GalaSetDcThread`), and user32 registers what to call when another
  thread draws on one (`GalaSetPresentHook`).
- gdi32 fires that hook from `with_dc`, outside its object table's lock,
  and user32 copies the window's area to the desktop then and there.
- The window's own thread keeps today's 50 ms batching, which a repaint
  storm needs (FileZilla's resize). Cross-*process* DCs are untouched:
  their thread stays 0, so `windows_across_test` and Chromium keep
  today's ReleaseDC behaviour.

This is what Windows does -- GDI drawing on a window DC reaches the
device as it is drawn.

`paint_thread_test` is the test that drove it, written first and seen to
fail for the right reason (the client blue on screen, the second
thread's square absent): a window whose thread waits for a message while
a second thread draws a square on its DC and never releases it, as
Mesa's WSI keeps its swapchain DC.

## Also on the way

- msvcrt/ucrt: `mbsrtowcs`, `wctype` and the rest of DXVK's import
  table, each with a `ucrt_test` case.
- gdi32: the entries DXVK's WSI asks for and does not get, named in the
  absent table so the ledger says so instead of a silent load failure.

## Known stopgap

Red and blue arrive swapped. DXVK asks for a `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM`
swapchain whatever the back buffer's format is, Mesa's Win32 WSI
advertises that format, and its GDI present path -- the only one a
software driver is given -- copies into a `BI_RGB` (so BGRA) DIB without
swizzling. The window path itself is sound: `vk_test`, which asks for
BGRA, gets its colours right through it. The screen check expects the
swapped colours for now, named as a stopgap in ROADMAP "Known issues and
stopgaps".

## Tests

- `d3d11_test` and `paint_thread_test` pass from boot.
- The full suite: 3 of 674 failed (`chromium_host`, `lx_gimp_batch`,
  `arm_taskmgr`), all three pass on re-run and all three are on the
  flaky list for reasons unrelated to presenting.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo xtask lint --full` (clean), `cargo xtask
  export-tests`.

After #43 the owner compared the app with the agreed mock-up v3 and it was not identical. This PR rebuilds the mocked screens one to one. It also carries the fix for `main`'s broken `mobile-perf` check.

## Commits

1. **a59795d — the fix for `main`.** #43 faded every block in from opacity 0. Chrome does not count such paints for LCP. With a live quote, which CI's `client-mobile` leaves behind, the Exchange's warm LCP went 448 → 1964 ms, over the 1500 ms budget. The heading and the first block now only move (a transform-only `rise`), and later blocks still fade.
2. **2f84c34 — mock-up v3, screen for screen.**
   - **Exchange:** the request sheet on the left and the quote stage on the right. The heading names the deal ("Sell 10,000 USDT"). Recent trades are a table that shows where each trade landed (`clientHistory withLanding`).
   - **Trade:**
     - the deal rail has the client's initial, "SENT 14:41 · FINAL", the payment rail, and where the rupees go to and come from;
     - figures are set as statements;
     - the cap has a halo and a ring that empties;
     - the claim shows the bank's tile, and "Release 8,000 USDT" is a size larger;
     - the chat header is one line with Support, and its rule sits at the top of the thread.
   - **Trade on a phone:** its own bar (back, reference, chat, support). The move comes first, the timer is a visor pill, and the release is docked with "Not yet".
   - **Trader home:**
     - no side column;
     - an online switch pill in the heading;
     - the move field beside the balances (with meters);
     - three lanes, each card with its time at the corner and a foot line;
     - along the foot, prices (one Edit opens both sides), the reserve and settlement.
   - **Trader home on a phone:** the lanes become one switch, and the tab bar adds Orders and Reserve.
   - **Bar:** a market ticker with a 24-hour sparkline. The new `marketTrail` in `@inrp2p/pricing` returns the reference mid, hour by hour, from `rate_snapshot`; `/api/market-rate` serves it as `trail`. Search shows the glass icon and ⌘K only.

## Tests

- Typecheck, eslint, unit tests (1818) and the integration tests `auto-pricing` and `live-deal` pass. `auto-pricing` now also checks `marketTrail`.

## Not as in the mock-up, on purpose

- The Exchange heading stays on phones. Hiding it moves LCP onto the animated digits.
- Lane footers say what is known ("From your own account", "TRC20"). The order summary carries no payee rail or account.

body:
## What

The back button scrolled out of view on long pages. The page header now stays pinned directly under the navbar and, once content passes under it, morphs into a compact translucent bar.

- Resting: unchanged.
- Scrolled: 70% background opacity with a 12px blur, a ring outline and a shadow. The back button (48px to 40px) and the title shrink, and the description collapses. The page action (for example the year select on payment details) stays on the right. On narrow screens the stuck bar is a single row with a truncated title.
- The header keeps its resting height while the bar compacts, so the content below does not jump (layout shift about 0.0002 on desktop, 0.04 on mobile).
- Transitions are skipped for reduced motion.

## How

- `StickyHeader` (client) wraps the header in `PageHeader`; `useHeaderStuck` detects the stuck state with an `IntersectionObserver` sentinel and remembers the resting height.
- The charges and payment detail headers pass the fade-in class to `PageHeader` instead of wrapping it, because a short wrapper would stop the header from sticking.
- `openspec/specs/visual-design` gains a "Sticky Page Header" requirement and `openspec/specs/testing` a scenario for the pinned-header snapshot.

## Testing

author: hervehenault-hub
body:
## En bref

Cette PR crée **toute la base de données** d'Alt. : les lieux, leurs horaires, les profils, les contributions, le parcours, l'entraide entre voisins et la mesure d'audience. Pour chaque table, elle règle **qui a le droit de lire et d'écrire**. Tout est vérifié par **472 tests automatiques**.

## Ce qui est fait

| Tâche | En clair |
| --- | --- |
| T2.1 | Une recherche en français qui ignore les accents et les tirets (« reparation » trouve « réparation ») |
| T2.2 | Bordeaux, les 3 domaines, les 6 catégories et **26 besoins** du quotidien. Taper « grille pain » renvoie la catégorie *réparation* |
| T2.3 | Les lieux. Une date de vérification est obligatoire, et un lieu n'est visible du public qu'une fois publié |
| T2.4 | Les horaires et le calcul « ouvert maintenant ? » en heure de Paris : pause de midi, créneau après minuit, changement d'heure. 15 cas testés |
| T2.5 | Les profils, créés à l'inscription. Un utilisateur ne peut **jamais** changer son propre rôle |
| T2.6 | Propositions de lieux, signalements et confirmations. Chacun ne voit que les siens, l'admin voit tout. Un signalement fait passer le lieu en « à revérifier ». Au bout de 3 confirmations, le lieu devient « confirmé par plusieurs personnes » |
| T2.7 | Seul un admin relie un commerçant à son lieu. Le commerçant peut alors mettre sa fiche à jour, mais il ne peut pas la publier lui-même |
| T2.8 | Facteurs d'impact et équivalences au format de `content/`. Une source (lien https) est obligatoire |
| T2.9 | Le parcours. Chacun ne voit que son historique, l'admin non plus. Une action ponctuelle ne compte qu'une fois, une habitude peut se répéter |
| T2.10 | L'entraide : aucune adresse exacte (le quartier seulement), règles à accepter avant de publier ou d'écrire, blocage, conversations lisibles par les 2 participants seulement, annonces de 30 jours maximum |
| T2.11 | La mesure d'audience : tout le monde peut envoyer un événement, personne ne peut les relire depuis l'app. Les événements des personnes qui l'ont refusée sont ignorés |
| T2.12 | Une **matrice d'audit** qui vérifie chaque table pour 4 profils (anonyme, utilisateur, commerçant, admin), en lecture et en écriture. Le tableau récapitulatif est dans `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` |
| T2.15 | Données de test locales : la ville fictive « Testville », 3 quartiers, 40 lieux, 5 comptes de test (`@alt.test`) |

Les types TypeScript ont aussi été régénérés (`pnpm db:types`).

## Ce que vous devez faire

1. Attendre que les vérifications automatiques en bas de cette page soient **toutes en coche verte ✅**.
2. Cliquer sur **« Merge pull request »**.

C'est tout. Aucun compte externe n'a été créé et aucune clé secrète n'a été ajoutée. Le mot de passe des comptes de test ne sert que sur un ordinateur de développement.

## Pour la suite (pas bloquant)

- Charger le contenu de `content/actions.json` et `content/impact-factors.json` dans les tables `actions`, `impact_factors` et `equivalences` (prévu pour une prochaine tâche).
- Brancher l'import OpenStreetMap (T2.13, déjà fusionné) sur la table `places`. Le format est compatible.

## Notes techniques

- 12 migrations créées avec `supabase migration new`. Aucune migration déjà fusionnée n'a été modifiée.
- Vérifié en local après rebase sur `main` : `db:reset`, `test:db` (472 tests), `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `format:check` et `check:secrets` passent.
- Les outils de test partagés sont dans `supabase/tests/_lib/helpers.psql`.

author: cchangyeol
body:
## 왜
맥(시뮬레이터)에서 가입하고 설정을 마친 계정으로 아이폰에서 로그인하자, 이름 · 학습자 유형 설정과 처음 안내를 **다시** 했습니다.
두 완료 여부를 기기 저장소(`notelink.onboarded` · `notelink.toured`)에만 적고 있어서, 처음 쓰는 기기에서는 매번 새 계정처럼 보였습니다.

## 무엇을
**서버(계정 기준)**
- `toAppUser`가 `onboarded` · `toured`를 함께 내려줍니다.
  - `onboarded`: 필수 약관(service · privacy)에 동의했고 학습자 유형을 직접 골랐으면 true입니다. 학습자 유형은 가입 직후 null이고 프로필 설정에서만 채워지므로, 새 필드 없이 기존 기록으로 계산합니다.
  - `toured`: `touredAt`이 있으면 true입니다. **필드 자체가 없는 예전 계정**은 설정을 마쳤으면 본 것으로 칩니다(설정을 마치면 바로 안내가 열렸기 때문).
- `User.touredAt`(기본값 없음)을 추가하고, `PATCH /users/me`에 `toured: boolean`을 받습니다. true면 지금 시각을, false면 null(안내 전)을 적습니다.

**앱**
- `signIn`: 서버가 `onboarded: true`를 주면 처음 쓰는 기기여도 설정을 건너뜁니다. `setUser`도 같은 계정이면 따라갑니다.
- 프로필 설정 저장 때 `toured: false`를 함께 보내 새 계정을 「안내 전」으로 적습니다.
- 안내를 마치거나 건너뛰면 기기 기록과 함께 `toured: true`를 계정에 적습니다. 실패해도(오프라인 등) 기기 기록은 남깁니다.
- `useTourOnce`: 계정에 `toured: true`가 있으면 열지 않습니다.
- 공용 `User`에 `onboarded?` · `toured?`(선택)를 추가했습니다.

## 시험
- API: 계산 규칙(약관 누락 · 미동의 · 학습자 유형 없음 · `touredAt` 있음/null/없음), `PATCH toured` 저장 · 400 검증
- 앱: 서버 기록으로 설정 건너뛰기, 다른 계정 정보는 무시, 서버 기록으로 안내 열지 않기, 가입 시 `toured: false`
- API 2992 · 앱 1063 · 공용 34 모두 통과, `tsc` · `eslint` 통과

author: pipemora1324
body:
El despliegue en Render falló al compilar `agrovet-api`:

```
error: invalid local: resolve : lstat /opt/render/project/src/backend/backend: no such file or directory
```

Con `rootDir: backend`, Render cuenta `dockerfilePath` y `dockerContext` desde esa carpeta, así que `./backend` quedaba duplicado. La guía de monorepos de Render dice que esas rutas son relativas al root directory, aunque la referencia del Blueprint dice que son relativas a la raíz.

## Cambio
- `render.yaml`: se quita `rootDir`. Quedan `dockerfilePath: ./backend/Dockerfile` y `dockerContext: ./backend`, contadas desde la raíz, y se corrige el comentario.
- `docs/DEPLOY_RENDER.md`: la fila de `render.yaml` explica por qué no lleva `rootDir`.
- `backend/Dockerfile` no cambia.

`rootDir` solo filtraba qué commits disparan un despliegue automático, y aquí está apagado (`autoDeployTrigger: "off"`), así que quitarlo no cambia nada más.

## Probado
- `render.yaml` leído con yq: `rootDir: null`, `dockerfilePath: ./backend/Dockerfile`, `dockerContext: ./backend`.
- `docker build -f ./backend/Dockerfile ./backend` desde la raíz del repositorio (mismo contexto que usará Render): compila.

Después de integrar: en Render, Blueprint → **Manual sync** y luego un deploy de `agrovet-api`.
