author: zhongkechen
body:
# [P2] Health checks report HTTP 500 as healthy

## Problem

When the Telegram session is disconnected, the real `/healthcheck` handler returns HTTP 500. The CLI health_check function only observes whether the request raises an exception; it does not check the response status and returns exit code 0. Docker HEALTHCHECK therefore cannot distinguish a healthy bot from this disconnected state.

## Expected and observed behavior

- Expected: HTTP 500 produces a nonzero result, while HTTP 200 produces 0.
- Observed: HTTP 500 and HTTP 200 responses from the real server handler both produce 0 when supplied to the real CLI through a mocked HTTP transport boundary.

Sources: [CLI check](https://github.com/zhongkechen/castbot/blob/dfba532498d7630a3bb15b0546dc5847f5482ee9/castbot/__main__.py#L49), [Server response](https://github.com/zhongkechen/castbot/blob/dfba532498d7630a3bb15b0546dc5847f5482ee9/castbot/http.py#L162).

## Reproduction

Run from the repository root:

```bash
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python -m unittest discover -s tests/repro_cases -p test_14_healthcheck_http_status.py -v
```

The independent case instantiates the real Http class, simulates a Telegram session check raising ConnectionError, and obtains the real HTTP 500 Response. A fake ClientSession passes that response to the real CLI check. A separate HTTP 200 control is included.

The test asserts the current defect: **PASS confirms reproduction, not remediation**. This PR adds only the description and reproduction case; update or replace these assertions when the behavior changes.

## Validation boundaries

Telegram session state and HTTP transport are mocked. The case does not connect to Telegram or start an HTTP service or Docker container. There are two automated cases, with no dependency on other reproduction PRs.

author: ganten1998
body:
Templates for 2.2: a PDF in `grimoire/templates` gives one template tile a page, each page drawn once by the sandboxed PDF worker into the form a picture template already has (#172).

## What it does

- **A tile a page.** A PDF copied into `grimoire/templates` (over USB, or by Use as template in Files) shows on the Templates sheet (Paper > More layouts..., and New notebook's More layouts...). Until its job has counted the pages it is one waiting tile under the file's name; then the folder is read again (as after a copy, never under a contact: after the lift) and its pages take its place, "Planner p. 1", "Planner p. 2" and on, each filling in as its picture is made. A long file name is cut short before " p. N", so the page's number stays in view. The tile the sheet's page in view was anchored on stays in view when a PDF before it becomes its pages.
- **A page is a picture template.** A page tapped goes onto the page (or the new notebook) as any picture template does: `template_install` takes the page's key and the picture worker fits the page's stored picture to the notebook's page size. Picking a page, drawing it and opening a notebook on it never read the PDF again; the PDF can be deleted afterwards, and a notebook keeps its own copy. Colour follows a picture template's (a page with colour stays colour; previews are gray).
- **Use as template on a PDF's card in Files**, after Import as notebook: the pictures' copy job (#152) and its 16 MB limit ("Too big (over 16 MB)."). Not offered in the pickers, for a PDF already in the templates folder, or out of Grimoire's PDF copies. The Templates sheet's From a file... still picks pictures only.
- **What the sheet cannot use stays visible.** A PDF's tile the sheet cannot use (a refused PDF, one past the cap of tiles, a page left out) keeps its place crossed out at every opening, with its name, so a refused planner is seen even beside other templates; with no template to offer, the sheet counts them among the files it cannot use, as for pictures. A picture it cannot use is still left out, as on main.
- **A folder with no PDF** gives the same tiles, jobs and refreshes as on main. One thing is new there: each look at the templates folder now lists its cache, `templates/.cache`, once, also for users with no PDF. That is one directory read a look; it queues nothing unless the cache holds the page count of a PDF that is gone.

## How a page is drawn and stored

- **Only the sandboxed worker parses the PDF.** The pages are drawn by the PDF import's own worker: the same exec, seccomp filter, address space and CPU limits, page watchdog, band mode under little memory, and record grammar, each record checked by the same `Session`. The writer and the UI never parse PDF syntax: the UI only stats files and reads a 16-byte page count; the job opens the PDF once with no link followed, as a plain file directly in `grimoire/templates`, and that open file is what every worker of the slice reads. With no worker to be had, nothing is drawn or marked and the tile waits.
- **The job** is `BgKind::Template` with no notebook and the PDF's path, queued by the look at the folder (at most 8 a look), ranked behind imports and font checks with Files' previews, and run in an import's slices (25 pages or 20 s): a slice that leaves pages ends with status 3 and is queued again behind whatever ranks higher, so a picture picked meanwhile waits one slice at most. A sandbox step refused ends it with status 4, which marks the UI's session broken, as an import's and a font check's do. Jobs still queued at exit are dropped; the next look goes on from the pages made.
- **The stored pages are Grimoire's own picture-template form**, in `templates/.cache` beside the pictures' previews and under the key theirs have (the hash of the PDF's name, size and time): `<hash>.pages` (the count), and for each page `<hash>-p<nnnn>.png` (the page at the Kindle's page size, gray or RGB as the import keeps them), `.key` (the hash of that PNG's bytes and its size, a template's key) and `.pgm` (its preview), written in that order through the existing writers (a temporary name, fsync, rename, never through a link), or `.bad`. A page's tile path is its PNG, so the template code works on it unchanged. docs/FORMAT.md, "Template PDFs", has the files.
- **Guards**: the cache reached with no link on the way; the free-space floor before the count, before each page's worker is asked, and with the page's real size before it is kept; the open file checked unchanged and still at its name (device, inode, size, time to the nanosecond) before the count is kept and before each page is kept, so nothing of a file swapped or written over is kept and nothing is marked. A PDF itself is never a picture: whatever the cache holds under its own name it has no preview or key of its own, `template_install` refuses it, and a notebook's picture job refuses a PDF. Removals of cache entries look for a link again right before they list the cache. A look that finds a removed PDF's count in the cache has its entries swept.
- **Never imported by itself.** The import watch reads `grimoire/import` alone, and the template job makes no notebook and queues no import. Import as notebook on the PDF's card in Files still imports it when the user taps it.

## Limits and refusals

| cause | what happens |
|---|---|
| more than 50 pages (`TEMPLATE_PDF_MAX_PAGES`) | no template as a whole, never its first 50: `<hash>.bad`, its tile crossed out, the count in grimoire.log |
| over 16 MB (`TEMPLATE_MAX_BYTES`, a picture's), or empty | marked before any worker starts |
| no PDF the worker reads, a password, no page | marked as a whole |
| its worker lies, ends or stalls twice while opening it, or no page draws | marked as a whole |
| a page the worker cannot draw | that page alone is marked and crossed out |
| a page whose worker ends or stalls twice (a fresh worker tries once more) | that page alone is marked (`died`); two such pages mark the whole PDF |
| more than 200 tiles of PDF pages in all (`TEMPLATE_PDF_TILES_MAX`) | PDFs taken in name order; one past the cap is left out whole: one crossed-out tile, no job, the count in the log |
| no worker starts, or one without the sandbox's steps where the sandbox is required | nothing marked; the next look tries again |
| a sandbox step refused | nothing marked; the session is marked broken, so no look queues the job until Grimoire starts again |
| no room above the floor, the writer out of memory for a page, a write that failed | nothing marked; the next look tries again |
| the file changed while its pages are made | what was made of it goes, nothing marked; the next look draws the file as it is |

## Strings

None new. Reused, each with a translator note: "p. %d" for the page tiles (Spanish "p. %d") and "Use as template" on the PDF card (Spanish "Usar como plantilla"); the crossed-out tile and the empty sheet's "Grimoire cannot use %d file(s) there (see %s)." are main's. Japanese is untouched: `make l10n` changed only `#.` notes and `#:` references in po/ja.po.

## Tests

Unit and integration: `rust/tests/test_template_pdfs.rs` (sim; the worker is a fresh exec of the headless runner, as in the app), `bgwork_tplpdf.rs`'s unit tests (the count read strictly, a long name's page part), `browser.rs`'s `a_pdfs_card_in_files_offers_its_copy_into_templates`, and pins in `test_sec_invariants.rs` (`pdfs_as_templates_are_told_as_they_are`) holding DESIGN.md's safety sentences to the lines that make them true. Scenarios: `z_tpl_h_pdf_pages`, `z_tpl_i_pdf_refused`, `z_tpl_j_pdf_cap`, `z_tpl_k_pdf_use_as`, and `files_5_cards` (changed).

How each was shown to fail: every guarded line below was taken out (or put back as it was) on its own, the test run and failing, then the line restored byte for byte.

- The page cap, `same()` before a page is kept, the two-dead-pages rule and the floor's function: `test_template_pdfs` failed in the cap, hostile, swap and room checks. The sheet's re

author: kinetic639
body:
## What changed

**Site theme**
- A night theme on the same CSS tokens. Day is the default, whatever the system says.
- The choice is kept in the browser and applied by a tiny inline script before the first paint, so a returning night visitor never sees a flash of day.
- The switch (sun/moon, `role="switch"`) is in the page header and in the world beside the map.
- Colours ease over 2 s while it switches. In the world, only the world's controls ease; the hidden page under it does not.
- The world's HUD (perf badge, icon buttons) moved from hard-coded colours to the tokens.

**Day and night in the world** (`lib/engine/day-night.ts`, `environment.ts`, `sky-discs.ts`)
- One number, 0 for day and 1 for night, drives everything, so a switch is an animation of that number: 2 s, with the entry's cinematic ease.
- **The sky's movement:**
  - The sun and the moon move on daily circles about a polar axis tilted for about 50° north. The sun's circle passes through the map's own sun position, so day is exactly as set in the editor.
  - Day to night: the sun goes on west and sets (here west-north-west), its light warming and fading, then the full moon rises in the east and climbs.
  - Night to day: time runs on. The moon sets in the west, then the sun rises in the east and climbs back to its place.
  - Shadows turn as they lengthen.
- **One light:** the scene's single directional light is the sun and then the moon. The hand-over happens at the horizon, where its intensity is zero, so no light is added or removed.
- **What follows the sky:**
  - sky light, background and shadow strength;
  - the terrain, which keeps the original's own light, now multiplied by a tint and with its glow as uniforms (identical by day);
  - the unlit placeholder buildings, recoloured by the same tint.
- **Discs:** the sun and the moon are sprites far beyond the map in the light's direction, hidden by the terrain like a horizon. They show only where the sky is in frame (the closest, lowest views), travelling along their arcs during a switch.
- **Cost:** only uniform values change, so nothing compiles. On the landing page (world not shown) the switch is instant. With reduced motion it is instant everywhere.
- **Loader view at night:** the world's controls are kept rasterized at 1 % opacity, and light text on a dark page showed through at that level. At night they use about 1/255.

## Verification
- **Unit tests:** 215 pass. New ones:
  - day equals the map's lighting from both directions;
  - the sun sets in the west and the moon rises in the east, with the light's bearing turning;
  - no jumps in light intensity or direction.
- **End-to-end:**
  - theme default, persistence and colours on the page;
  - the switch in the world, which reaches night with no new shader programs;
  - site suite: 33 passed.
- **`pnpm perf`** (production build) passes every budget, including the new `dayNight.*`:
  - p95 16.8 ms, worst frame 33.4 ms;
  - 0 long tasks, 0 programs compiled.

author: dykamino-coder
body:
## Task
INC-2026-0098: thinking blocks reach the chat without text, so a real answer shows no thinking at all. The CLI asks the API for the `updates` thinking display by default, and that display returns most reasoning as a signature without text. The lead chose options 2 and 3 from the card. Bridge starts Claude with `--thinking-display summarized` as a per-chat setting that is on by default. A block that still has only a signature draws a "thought N s" marker. The KaminIDE chat and the Bridge web client render through the same webview code. Change PR: server, webview, rebuilt webview bundles, and the card.

## Summary
- Server (`session-env.ts`): `buildClaudeArgs` adds `--thinking-display summarized` unless one of these applies:
  - the chat asked for `thinkingDisplay: 'updates'` (the CLI's own display) in `session:create` or `session:resume`;
  - the server sets `CLAUDE_BRIDGE_THINKING_DISPLAY=updates`;
  - the session's extra CLI flags already name a display.
- `SessionConfig.thinkingDisplay` rides in the launch config, so restarts keep the choice. Values other than `summarized` and `updates` are ignored.
- Webview (`ThinkingBlock.tsx`): an empty, non-streaming thinking block draws one quiet line with the lightbulb and "thought N s". The duration comes from the row's `thinkingDurationMs`, and the line reads plain "thought" when no duration is recorded. A block that is still streaming draws nothing, because its text may not have arrived yet.
- Only the thinking row carries `thinkingDurationMs`. Both message merges (`mergeAssistantEntry` and `mergeAssistantEntriesByMessageId`) now copy it onto that row's thinking blocks through `contentWithThinkingDuration`, as render copies without mutating the store. Otherwise a merged bubble would lose it to the last row's fields.
- Entry-level visibility is unchanged. A signature-only thinking turn that has nothing else to show, or one that joins a tool group, still draws no extra line.
- `builtin-extensions/claude-bridge/{chat,tools,customize}.html` rebuilt with `npm run build` in `webview`. `extension.js` is unchanged by the build.

## Validation
- New tests fail on the base and pass with the fix:
  - `session-env.model.test.ts`: the default, resume, a per-chat `updates`, own flags, and the server override.
  - `ThinkingBlock.test.tsx`: the marker, the label without a duration, streaming, and the duration carried through both merges without mutating the source row.
- `npm run typecheck` in server and webview. Webview `vitest run`: 95 files, 670 passed. Server `vitest run src/core/pty src/core/server`: 88 files passed, 1 skipped.
- Live check: on the candidate before merge. The acceptance stand was recreated on the published 6.3.190 image plus this branch's server files (and those of #1022), with the same volumes, then returned to the published image (`/health` 6.3.190). A KaminIDE 1.0.113 copy on its own profile, with the candidate chat bundle and driven by commands, ran one turn that asked for step-by-step thinking. The chat showed the summarized thinking text under the lightbulb, then the answer. No signature-only block occurred, so the marker is covered by the render tests only.

## Risks and limitations
- `summarized` asks the API for thinking summaries. INC-2026-0063 narration notes come from the `updates` display, so they may stop appearing; a chat can choose `updates` per session.
- Per-chat choice: the server accepts `thinkingDisplay`, but no client UI sends it yet, so every chat uses the default unless the server override is set.

author: sloraris
body:
## What changes

**Named API tokens.** The hub gets a **Settings** page (new nav item) with an **API tokens** section: create a token with a name and a scope (`read` or `write`), see when each was created and last used, revoke it. The secret is shown once (the page is rendered, not redirected, so it never sits in a URL). The hub keeps only its SHA-256 hash in `STATE_DIR/tokens.json`, written atomically with mode 600. Last use is written at most once a minute per token. Headless setups get the same thing on the command line:

```bash
docker exec backtrack backtrack token create dashboard --scope read   # prints the token once
docker exec backtrack backtrack token list
docker exec backtrack backtrack token revoke dashboard                 # by name or id
```

The bearer check accepts these alongside `READ_TOKEN` / `WRITE_TOKEN` from the environment, which keep working unchanged. All comparisons are constant time. A token can't reach the UI, so it can't mint more tokens. The server re-reads the file when its mtime changes, so CLI changes apply without a restart.

**New read endpoints** (read scope):

- `GET /api/v1/jobs?limit=&machine=&stack=&state=`: recent jobs across online agents, newest first. `limit` is 1–200 (default 50), `state` is `queued|running|ok|failed`. Each job has `machine`, `id`, `kind`, `stack`, `trigger` (`manual`, `pre-migrate`, `nightly` or `schedule`), `state`, `created`, `started`, `finished`, `error`. `unreachable` lists agents that didn't answer. With a stack or state filter the hub reads each agent's full history, so the filter still finds `limit` matches. The agent's signed `/v1/jobs` now takes `?limit=` (older agents ignore it and return 50).
- `GET /api/v1/stacks/{stack}`: the stack as its agent reports it, plus `machine`, `agent_online`, `also_on` (other agents that report the same name) and `prerestore` (its set-aside folders).

README and `docs/design.md` now have an endpoint table with the scope each one needs.

## What an integration should use

- Create a **named read token** for it (Settings → API tokens, or `backtrack token create <name>`), one per tool, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Leave `READ_TOKEN`/`WRITE_TOKEN` for simple setups.
- Check: `GET /api/v1/status` (fleet summary and warnings). `/healthz` needs no token but says nothing about auth.
- Overview: `/api/v1/status` and `/api/v1/stacks` (each stack's last backup and state).
- What failed and why: `/api/v1/jobs?state=failed&limit=20`, then `/api/v1/jobs/{machine}/{id}` for the log.
- One stack: `/api/v1/stacks/{stack}` and `/api/v1/stacks/{stack}/snapshots`.
- Use a write token only if the tool should start backups or restores.

## Testing

- New `tests/test_tokens.py`: hash-only storage and file mode, validation, revoke by id or name, the last-used throttle, a second store (the CLI) seeing changes, CLI create/list/revoke, named tokens on the API (read vs write scope, env tokens still working, a revoked token refused), the Settings page minting (shown once) and revoking, CSRF required, and a bearer token not getting into the UI.
- `tests/test_server.py`: the job list with each filter and bad input, and stack detail.
- Full suite: 105 passed, 1 skipped (the root-only ownership test), about 6 minutes.
- Checked the Settings page by hand in a browser against a local hub: list, create (token shown once), env tokens shown as not revocable.

Version left at 0.2.1.

First fix out of the prime grader's 2026-11-17 scorecard (Kent: "The gross ones"). Built and **flipped ON in this PR: Kent, shown original | before | after for both designs it moves, "Flip ON (Recommended)".**

## The fault

Precision Drone, graded Bad: "no blue thread anywhere". Traced by eye through the stage dumps: the blue water is present at stage 2 and gone after the colour cap. `enforce_color_cap` keeps the N threads with the most sewn area, which on the Drone at the Studio's 6 is black, orange and four greys; the 34 mm2 of blue is the smallest and sews in the nearest grey.

## The flag (`color_cap_least_loss`, now default ON)

author: qthans
body:
Refs #571

Second step of scheduled tasks: the tables, the contracts and the time math. Nothing in this PR is reachable by a user: there is no route, no dispatcher and no adapter registered with the scheduler.

## Summary

**Database (`0079_agent_tasks`)**

- New table `agent_tasks`: the task definition (owner, name, prompt, request snapshot, status and reason, failure counter, notification switches, version, soft delete). A name is unique per owner and workspace, ignoring case, among tasks that are not archived.
- `task_schedules`: new `agent_task_id` with a composite foreign key to the task's id, workspace, team and owner, and a unique index (one schedule per task). The target CHECK now requires `agent_task_id` (and no connector) on every `agent_task` schedule, and no task on a connector schedule.
- `schedule_occurrences`: `team_id` and `workspace_id` (backfilled from the schedule, nullable for now, with the workspace/team foreign key), `chat_run_id`, `thread_id`, `trigger_kind`, `skip_reason`, `task_version`, `is_catch_up`; CHECKs for `status` (adds `blocked` and `cancelled`), `trigger_kind` and `skip_reason`.
- `threads.origin` accepts `scheduled`.

**Contracts** (`@sourceweft/contracts/scheduled-tasks`): task record, the closed request snapshot, the time-rule union (`manual`, `daily`, `weekly`, `weekdays`, `cron`, `once`), run record, and the create / update / run-now / list / preview shapes the API will use. The database CHECKs are generated from these enums.

**Time evaluation** (`modules/schedules/rules.ts`, `wall-time.ts`): next fire times for every rule kind in an IANA time zone, rule validation (parseable five-field cron, minimum interval, one-time rule in the future, a rule that can never fire), and `planDueSlot`, which decides what an overdue schedule does: run the newest elapsed slot if it is younger than one period (at most 24 hours), report older ones as missed. `croner` 10.0.1 (MIT, no dependencies, pinned) iterates the cron pattern; daylight saving is decided in our own code: a wall time the clock repeats fires once, a wall time the clock skips fires at the jump.

**Task-specific pieces** (`modules/agent-tasks/schedule.ts`): the one-hour minimum interval, the fixed per-task offset (up to five minutes), the five-time preview, and the schedule-row time columns for a saved rule.

**Plan limits**: `BillingRuntime.getScheduledTaskLimits` (read only). Commercial: 3 / 10 / 15 per member by plan, 25 for the tiers above the team plan. Core: a fixed 25.

The engine now writes `team_id` and `workspace_id` on the occurrences it materializes. No other engine or connector behaviour changes.

## Hand-written SQL and the one changed existing test

`0079_agent_tasks.sql` is generator output except for one statement, line 36, which fills the two new occurrence columns from the schedule:

```sql
UPDATE "schedule_occurrences" AS o SET "team_id" = s."team_id", "workspace_id" = s."workspace_id" FROM "task_schedules" AS s WHERE s."id" = o."schedule_id";
```

The journal and the snapshot are untouched generator output.

One existing test changes: `reserved user-owned task schedules are never dispatched by the connector scheduler` in `connectors/repository/schedule.database.test.ts` now inserts the `agent_tasks` row its schedule points at, because a task schedule without a task is no longer storable. What it asserts is unchanged: the connector scheduler materializes nothing for that schedule. No other connector or schedule test is modified.

## Verification

Local (Node 24.18.0), after rebasing onto main; backend commands run from `apps/backend`:

- `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`: passes (3 low).
- `vitest run --config vitest.database.config.ts src/modules/connectors src/modules/schedules src/modules/agent-tasks`: 10 files, 86 passed, with the migrate helper unmodified.
- `pnpm --filter @sourceweft/contracts test`: 245 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @sourceweft/billing test`: 359 passed.
- `vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/modules/schedules src/modules/agent-tasks src/billing-host`: 11 files, 68 passed.
- `pnpm lint`: 5 of 5 tasks. `pnpm check-types`: 51 of 51 tasks.
- Before the follow-up commit, the whole backend unit lane: 4916 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed; both failures are `connectors/extracted-file.test.ts` cases that need the AnyDoc native binding, which is not built in this checkout.

Covered by the new tests: every rule kind; spring-forward and fall-back in New York and Berlin, a half-hour jump on Lord Howe Island; month ends and leap days; a one-time rule in the past; minimum-interval rejection; cron parse errors; offset stability and spread; catch-up, expiry and missed-slot reporting; the migration applied over existing connector schedules and occurrences; an occurrence written without the tenant columns (the shape an older scheduler writes) and with them.

## Rollout risks

- The migration rewrites CHECK constraints on `task_schedules` and `threads` and adds CHECKs to `schedule_occurrences`; each takes a short exclusive lock and scans the table. `schedule_occurrences` is also updated in full once for the backfill.
- The tightened target CHECK fails the migration if an `agent_task` schedule without a task already exists. No shipped code has ever written one.
- The new `status` CHECK on `schedule_occurrences` fails the migration if a row holds a status outside the eight listed. The code has only ever written six of them.
- `schedule_occurrences.team_id` and `workspace_id` are nullable in this migration on purpose: a scheduler or worker from the previous release, still running during the deploy, keeps inserting occurrences without them. The new engine always writes them. The next PR of this feature sets them NOT NULL after backfilling any rows written in that window.
- New runtime dependency `croner` (exact pin).

author: bahaamattar
body:
A `<th>` with `scope="col"` or `"colgroup"` is now a column header, and one with `scope="row"` or `"rowgroup"` is a row header, as the HTML Standard defines for the th element. Before, `parse_table_data` set the flags only from the other cells in the row: any `<td>` in the row, even an empty corner cell, made every `<th>` in that row a row header. In the W3C WAI "two headers" table, Monday and Tuesday were row headers, and `export_to_dataframe()` returned columns `0, 1, 2` with the days as data row 0.

**Issue resolved by this Pull Request:**
Resolves #5445

### Change

- New helper `HTMLDocumentBackend._get_cell_header_flags()`. For a `<th>` with a `col`, `colgroup`, `row` or `rowgroup` scope (case-insensitive), it returns the flags of that scope. For all other cells, it returns the same row-based flags as before.
- Both cell paths in `parse_table_data` (`TableCell` and `RichTableCell`) use it. The table layout is unchanged, including the row-header rows from #4216.
- A `<th>` without `scope` (or with an unknown value) and `scope` on a `<td>` (obsolete in HTML5) keep the row-based flags.

**Checklist:**

- [x] Documentation has been updated, if necessary. (Not needed: no docs page describes how HTML header cells are detected.)
- [x] Examples have been added, if necessary. (Not needed.)
- [x] Tests have been added, if necessary.

**Review evidence:**

Source: the W3C "two headers" table (empty `<td>` corner, `<th scope="col">` days, `<th scope="row">` times), as plain rows and with the first row in `<thead>`.

- Document tree:
  - Before: Monday and Tuesday `column_header=False, row_header=True`.
  - After: `column_header=True, row_header=False`.
  - The time labels stay `row_header=True`. Data cells and the corner cell are unchanged.
- `export_to_dataframe()`:
  - Before: columns `[0, 1, 2]` with Monday/Tuesday as row 0.
  - After: columns `['', 'Monday', 'Tuesday']`, and row 0 is `['09:00 - 11:00', 'Closed', 'Open']`.
- `export_to_markdown()` and `TableItem.export_to_html()` give the same output before and after for this table.
- Reference data: no changes. `wiki_duck.html` is the only fixture with `scope`. It uses `scope="col"` in a row of only `<th>` cells and `scope="row"` next to a `<td>`, which already got these flags.

Tests:

- `pytest tests/test_backend_html.py -k scope`: 5 passed. On main, the 4 `test_table_th_scope_sets_the_header_flags` cases (plain, thead, colgroup/rowgroup in mixed case, rich header cell) fail, and the no-scope test passes.
- `pytest tests/test_backend_html.py`: 166 passed, 1 skipped (the Playwright render test; Playwright is not installed locally).
- `pytest tests/test_backend_markdown.py tests/test_backend_mhtml.py tests/test_backend_epub.py tests/test_backend_email.py`: all pass (93, 41, 24, 42).
- `prek run --files docling/backend/html_backend.py tests/test_backend_html.py`: all hooks pass (ruff, ruff format, ty, tach, max lines, license header).
- Not run: the full test suite and the Playwright-rendered HTML test.

author: sgoil2019
body:
Phase 4 slice 5: upload sharing (spec FR-17a). Off by default; nothing changes unless `AGENCY_UPLOAD_SHARING=workspace` is set.

**What**
- The owner can share one of their upload records into the Workspace it was made in (`POST /uploads/{id}/share`), and take it back. An upload made with no Workspace goes to `all-data` when the stack has that Workspace; otherwise it cannot be shared.
- **Who sees it is decided by the Server, not the layer:** other users get it, read-only, only when *their own* Server session lists that Workspace (`/app/namespaces`). The owner must themselves be able to use the Workspace, so sharing never widens access. Losing the Workspace, or turning the setting off, hides the record again.
- Shared views show who shared it and when, and drop any GPS position and its note. Sharing does not extend the expiry. Viewing needs no grant; uploading still needs `canUploadFiles`.
- Admins: `AGENCY_UPLOAD_ADMINS` (comma-separated Server usernames) may unshare or delete a shared record and see all shared records; they cannot read a private one or share for someone else.
- UI: share control with a confirmation that says who will see it, "Stop sharing", a "Shared with you" list (read-only, shows who and when), and a "Check for uploads shared with you" refresh.
- Compose passes both settings through.

**Tests**
- 8 new layer tests (31 total): off by default; shared is read-only, redacted and limited to the Workspace; losing the Workspace or turning it off hides it; cannot share into a Workspace you cannot use / with no Workspace / bad body; sharing grants no upload; all-data default; admin rules; expiry unchanged; CSRF header on share. The fake Server now has three users with their own Workspace lists.
- Live (treasury stack, two users, Workspaces `treasury` and `all-data` loaded): a JPEG with GPS uploaded by `demo`, shared; `demo2` (no upload grant) saw it, read-only, GPS hidden, delete refused; in the browser `demo2` saw the card with no buttons, and `demo` got the confirmation, stop and re-share. Stack torn down.

**Not done / limits**
- Not tested live that a user *outside* the Workspace is excluded (the stack had only one Workspace rule I could set; covered by unit tests with a fake Server). 
- Records and shares are in the layer's memory: a restart loses them. Admin names and the on/off setting are environment settings, not an Admin console screen.
- "Who can see" is every member of the Workspace: no per-person sharing. A shared record's preview (rows, text) is visible to them, which the confirmation says.
- The layer cannot tell who counts as a "member" except by asking the Server per viewer; with many Workspaces and users this is one extra Server call per list request.
- Admin delete has no UI, only the API.

## Defect

`Stratex/rigorous_backtest/rd19/run_xsrev.py`'s panel-verification loop read `exp["missing"]`, but the S-RD1 provenance manifest — the runner's own default `--expected-provenance` — keys the field `missing_bars`. Any real declared run would raise `KeyError: 'missing'` on the first symbol, before any simulation.

Found by RD-019 run-prep (runprep-rd019 READINESS, BLOCKER 1), which executed the runner's literal comparison block against the real manifest + verified panel: KeyError on 30/30 symbols.

## The change (one defect, two sites)

- Line 338 (the comparison): `exp["missing"]` -> `exp["missing_bars"]`
- Line 340 (the mismatch message): `exp['missing']` -> `exp['missing_bars']` — the same wrong key read again while formatting the ABORT message; with only line 338 fixed, a genuine mismatch would KeyError while reporting itself. body:
## What

The assistant server counts every signed-in `POST /interview` against the caller's quota, a day and a month (UTC), in SQLite (standard library) on a Docker volume, out of every client's reach. Over either limit it refuses with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (HTTP 429) and `details.resetsAt`, before the model. The app reads `resetsAt` and the interview says which day the assistant is back, in all four languages.

Closes #67

- Limits are configuration: `ASSISTANT_DAILY_QUOTA` (50), `ASSISTANT_MONTHLY_QUOTA` (500), `QUOTA_DB`. Per-plan limits come with #120.
- A refused call does not count; a call the model then fails still does. A caller without a valid token is never counted.
- [x] `Actual` logged: 0.1 h

## How to test

- `cd server && pytest --cov`: `tests/test_quota.py` covers the counting, both limits, the resets (day, month, year), restarts and the HTTP refusal.
- App: `InterviewMapperTest` and `InterviewViewModelTest` cover reading `resetsAt` and the day shown.
- On the server: set `ASSISTANT_DAILY_QUOTA=1` in the stack, recreate it, run two interview steps: the second says when the assistant is back.

## Reviewer notes

- Android build, iOS compile, host and iOS simulator tests pass locally. End-to-end against the deployed server is not verified yet: it needs the stack redeployed with the new `quota` volume.

body:
## Summary

Implements Step 49 Personio monitoring, bilingual XML merge and conditional ETag handling, .com/.de URL normalization, direct board routing, and discovery registration. This PR is stacked on PR #48 and contains only the Step 49 implementation.

## Key Changes

- Added strict Personio XML parsing and a board adapter with bounded streaming, anti-XXE checks, numeric unique IDs, validation, and fail-closed incomplete-snapshot handling.
- Added bilingual description handling. English descriptions take priority; default-feed descriptions fill missing English descriptions. Empty English feeds are checked against the default feed, and mismatched position ID sets fail closed.
- Added composite ETag state for English and default feeds, including the conditional request transitions and refetch behavior needed to avoid stale fallback descriptions.
- Corrected Personio employment mapping: permanent employment alone never implies full-time. Explicit full-time and part-time schedules are classified; ambiguous or missing schedules remain unknown. Extraction does not re-infer a classification from free text.
- Added .com/.de board parsing and posting URL normalization, registry promotion, search discovery registration, HTML enrichment support, and direct routing.
- Added eight captured XML fixtures with provenance metadata and offline regression tests.

## Verification

- Personio tests: 71 passed, 0 failed.
- Combined focused regression suites: 227 passed, 0 failed.
- Database safety checker: passed, 0 unsafe patterns.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 verification script: 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- GitHub Actions on this exact commit: backend-and-db-safety, windows-safety, frontend-checks, and GitGuardian Security Checks all succeeded.
- All eight Personio fixtures matched their recorded byte counts, SHA-256 hashes, position counts, and empty-description counts.
- Protected operational database, sidecars, backups, and forensic staging assets were reported byte-for-byte identical before and after local verification. No monitoring run, Serper search, database migration, repair, or deployment was performed.

## PR Relationship

- Base: step/48-personio-monitoring-investigation (PR #48)
- This PR remains a draft and is intentionally unmerged.
- PR #48 remains a separate documentation-only draft targeting main.

## Known Boundaries

- If a position has no description in either language feed, its description remains unknown; this step does not add per-job detail-page requests.
- Personio's language-feed behavior and the observed ID parity are documented in the Step 48 investigation. The adapter verifies both feeds whenever fallback is required and fails closed on inconsistencies.

sacredtrees
body:
The OpenMakeWorkshop command, `openmake-workshop`:

    openmake-workshop new <drawer> [name=]
    openmake-workshop list <drawer>
    openmake-workshop add <drawer> kind= file= [name=] [from=] [settings=]

`new` makes the drawer, the kind subdrawers and a `project.om`. `list` prints the product's name, notes and items. `add` copies a known suite file into the matching subdrawer, or references a KiCad project (and an unknown kind) in place, then writes the manifest.

A relative `file=` is taken from the current directory, not from inside the project drawer. An unknown kind (the tests use `render`) is kept, so a later kind can be added without a format bump. An unknown key is refused.

Host tests in `make test` cover new, list, add, a refused unknown key, and a missing file. The window comes next.

Solo documentazione: la procedura del filesystem dedicato in `docs/setup-vm-hermes.md` §6.

## Il difetto

La riga di `fstab` non aveva `nofail`. Un montaggio che fallisce all'avvio (immagine spostata, riga scritta male) avrebbe fermato la VM in modalità di emergenza, e una VM che non parte non si ripara via SSH.

## Cosa cambia

- `nofail` fra le opzioni. Se il montaggio fallisce la VM parte lo stesso, e il preflight lo segnala perché la directory torna a non essere dedicata.
- `findmnt --verify` prima del montaggio, per controllare la riga quando un errore costa poco.
- Due controlli prima di creare l'immagine: lo spazio libero, e che la directory sia vuota (un filesystem montato sopra nasconde gli esiti che c'erano).
- La verifica finale guarda le opzioni del montaggio con `findmnt`, non solo che ci sia.

Il test che vieta riferimenti a un laboratorio specifico passa.

author: galaktischegurke
body:
The live score line under the composer (added in M8) now comes from the fast model, not from the local word rules. Frontend only.

## Why

The line showed the word rules' label and how sure they are. For "I will do nothing myself" that is "delegating, 50% sure" and "you 25 · ai 75", and typing more barely changes it, because no further rule matches. It read like a model's rating that does not react. The fast model rates the same sentence 0 % and follows a sentence while it grows ("I think" 41, "I think the seasons happen because" 54, the finished claim 75).

## What

- `src/lib/draftScore.ts`: after a typing pause of 600 ms the draft is rated with the same question the turn uses on send (`Provider.score`, thinking scale). A keystroke aborts the call in flight, an answer for an older text is dropped, a call over 5 s is given up quietly, the same text is never rated twice in a row, and after 2 failed calls in a row it stops asking for the visit.
- The gauge takes label, bar and split from the model rating. While newer words wait for their rating the old one stays, dimmed. Before any rating, and when the model is not available, the line shows the word rules as before. The hover says which of the two the number comes from.
- On send, a rating for exactly the sent text decides the veil and is handed to the turn, so the score is not asked twice and the message shows its percent at once.
- Demo mode and providers without scores make no call and look as before. ASCII design only.

## Cost

One small call per typing pause: about 250 input tokens without context, up to about 650 with four earlier messages, 1 output token. A prompt typed in one go causes 1 call.

## Needs

The group backend must have the fast model's key (`FAST_API_KEY`). Without it the line stays on the word rules and says the model rating is not available.

## Tested

- `npm test`: 314 passed (297 on main). `parity.test.ts` unchanged.
- `npm run build`
- In a browser against a local backend with the real models: "I will do nothing myself" goes to "you 0 · ai 100"; adding an own claim moves it to "you 87 · ai 13"; typing without pauses causes exactly one call; a rated draft is sent without a second score call; a delegating draft rated by the model is veiled; demo mode makes no backend call.
- Known limit: about 1 fast-model call in 5 takes longer than 1.5 s and about 1 in 10 longer than 5 s (measured on `zai.glm-4.7`, 30 calls). The line then keeps the old value dimmed until the next pause.

## AI use

Written with Claude Code (Anthropic) at Salomon's request.

author: arbobendik
body:
Continues #148, which GitHub closed when its base branch was deleted; ws4 passed e990d675 by reading there. Rebased onto main d216dfe0.

**OptiX only (Bendik's decision).** On Vulkan a panoramic camera is refused at export with `Flex: panoramic cameras render on OptiX only, not on Vulkan`, the only message: no scene is piped and nothing is traced. The Vulkan descent hangs NVIDIA's driver 620.70.06, and no bounded fix passed both gates. renderer.slang carries only the record's Projection fields (stride 800). Hold at e990d675: the OptiX panorama rows, the Vulkan refusal row and main's fog cube on Vulkan, cold, all pass with no Xid.

Panoramic cameras, first part: the equirectangular and the central cylindrical panorama render, in final renders and in a viewport looking through the scene camera.

Before this, a panoramic or custom camera silently rendered as a perspective camera at its lens. Now:
- A custom camera raises "Flex: custom cameras need OSL, which Flex does not run".
- The five panoramas still to come (equiangular cubemap face, mirror ball, and fisheye equidistant, equisolid and lens polynomial) each raise "Flex: the <name> panorama is not supported". Each later PR of this stack removes the raise of the type it implements.

Directions follow Blender's definitions of the two types:
- **Equirectangular:** u is the longitude to the right over [longitude min, longitude max], v the latitude over [latitude min, latitude max].
- **Central cylindrical:** u is the angle to the right over [u min, u max], v the height at which the ray crosses a cylinder of the radius, over [v min, v max].
- **Both:** the camera's shift offsets u and v. Rays start at the clip start along each ray.

## Commits

1. `feat(camera)`: carry a panorama beside each camera in the scene record, none yet. +22/−12.
   - A `Projection` record follows Scene's last field, three copies for the camera, the previous and the denoised camera, so every existing offset stays.
   - The host fills and compares them alongside each camera.
   - The exporter sends none.
2. `feat(camera)`: hand each camera's panorama with it to ray generation and projection, unread yet. +49/−32.
   - In the extended kernels, `pixelDomain`, `shift` and `project` take the panorama beside the camera (`VIEW`, `VIEWING`).
   - In the base kernels the macros expand to the camera alone, as on main.
3. `feat(camera)`: mark a panoramic camera's scene for the extended kernels, raising for custom cameras and each panorama. +37/−21.
   - The step `PANORAMA`, after `TOON`, marks a scene whose camera is panoramic, and selects the extended module as varying media and strands do.
   - The base kernels fold it out.
   - Switching the scene camera's type to panoramic exports the scene anew.
4. `feat(camera)`: render an equirectangular panorama, projecting positions back through it for reuse. +100/−8.
   - Each ray takes its direction at the pixel's u and v, with the clip measured along the ray.
   - The cone spreads by the pixel's span: the longer chord to the next pixel's direction across and down, so rows near a pole don't alias.
   - `project` maps a position back to its pixel, for the temporal neighbor and the denoiser's flow.
   - The denoiser trusts a previous pixel without the perspective's in-front test, as a panorama sees all around.
5. `feat(camera)`: render a central cylindrical panorama. +16/−1.
6. `feat(camera)`: read a panorama's window coordinates as its u and v. +13.
7. `chore(test)`: rows, below. +59/−1.

The first three were one commit of 159 changed lines; split, each builds and stands alone.

## Cost for perspective and orthographic cameras

Scenes without a panoramic camera run the base kernels.

**OptiX.** The base PTX (shaders and stand-in) at the tip against its base c9704eeb: every function is identical but `__raygen__temporal`, where one line differs: `add.s64 %rd175, %rd13, -1376` becomes `-1536`, the step back by two records, `RECORD_STRIDE`.

**Vulkan.** The base SPIR-V against the base's, with ids stripped and whitespace normalised. Every function body is identical. Only these lines differ:

```
< OpDecorate % ArrayStride 680              > OpDecorate % ArrayStride 768
< OpDecorate % ArrayStride 648              > OpDecorate % ArrayStride 736
< % = OpConstant % 1376                     > % = OpConstant % 1536
< % = OpTypeStruct (Scene, 53 members)      > % = OpTypeStruct (Scene, 56 members)
> % = OpTypeStruct (Projection: type, range, shift)
> % = OpTypeStruct % ; % = OpTypeArray % %  (the float[2] array type)
> OpName "fcpt.Projection_natural", OpName "_Array_natural_float2"
> OpMemberName 53 "cameraProjection", 54 "previousCameraProjection", 55 "denoisedCameraProjection"
> OpMemberName 0 "type", 1 "range", 2 "shift", 0 "data"
> OpMemberDecorate 53 Offset 648, 54 Offset 676, 55 Offset 704
> OpMemberDecorate 0 Offset 0 (twice), 1 Offset 4, 2 Offset 20; OpDecorate ArrayStride 4
```

**`RECORD_STRIDE`** is the size of one shader binding table record: OptiX's header and a copy of the scene. It strides over the table's 12 records (the anchor's, the 8 passes', and the 3 walk callables'), not over frames or pixels. The scene grows by its three panoramas, 84 bytes, so a record grows from 688 to 768 bytes and the table from 8256 to 9216. That is 960 bytes more device memory, allocated once, and 960 bytes more copied from the host once per frame. Nothing per pixel; at 1280 × 720 the per-pixel arrays are unchanged.

## Tests

New rows, on both backends:
- **A panoramic camera sees each direction at its u and v.** A sphere of radius 0.5 glows 10 units off under a white world of 1, the camera at 128 × 64.
  - Equirectangular over longitudes −90° to 180° and latitudes −45° to 90°, the sphere at longitude 40° and latitude 20°: u = (40 + 90) / 270 and v = (20 + 45) / 135.
  - Central cylindrical over angles −2 to 2 and heights −0.5 to 1 at radius 2, the sphere at angle 1 and height ratio 0.15, so height 0.3: u = 3 / 4 and v = 0.8 / 1.5.
  - Each sphere's light has its centroid within half a pixel of u and v, and every pixel more than 6 away reads 1 within 1e-5. The central cylindrical sphere reaches 4.4 pixels above and below its center: its 0.05 rad radius at 0.0117 of height ratio per pixel.
- **An animation's frame reusing the last one's reservoirs reprojects them through its panorama.** An equirectangular camera turned 5° between two frames renders the second, reusing 192 samples, within 1% of that frame rendered alone at 256.

Readings so far, on a build of the code before the rebase onto the stack (faee7a03):
- **Equirectangular on OptiX:** centroid (61.700, 30.756) against (61.630, 30.815), 0.09 px off.
- **Vulkan:** the renderer stopped on the first panoramic render, after 3.5 minutes, with the GPU reporting a context-switch timeout. Being diagnosed; this PR is not ready to verify until it renders.
- **CPU checks:**
  - Each type's exported record matches its derivation.
  - A dry run of the rows' export sends every request well formed.
  - The extended and base SPIR-V pass spirv-val.
  - Base and extended kernels compile at every commit of the rebased branch.

body: This is stage 2 of the dangling-host-throw work: the entry domain, a validated aliasing fixture, and the reverse inclusion **on the legal part only**. **The reverse direction for dangling throws remains OPEN**, so #988 together with this PR is **not** an equivalence when there are imports. Nothing about `core3SemD` follows: since #995, `core3SemD` never feeds host throws to instances, so this concerns the raw `instSession` on `ssig` only. **1. Entry domain** (`Wasm/Cfg/DanglingTyped`) - **The lemma "checker acceptance ⇒ `FuncsSupp`" is false.** The checker skips code after a non-fallthrough instruction. - Validated counterexample `ExampleAlias.dcMod`, with body `unreachable; ref.test anyref; drop`. - Proved: `dc_instDom : InstDom dcI dcStore` (accepted via `storeChkEB`), `dc_not_funcsSupp`, `dc_not_supported`. - **What holds:** `funcsSupp_of_storeSupported (hs : StoreOk s) (hsup : StoreSupported s.funcs) : FuncsSupp s`. The entry domain is therefore `StoreSupported` (#972's computable profile), not `InstDom`. - **Entry theorems** (every profile `P`): - `configOkD_invoke_of_storeOk (hs : StoreOk s) (hF : FuncsSupp s) (hok : InvokeOk s a vs) : ConfigOkD (invoke s a vs)`; - `configOkD_of_supported (hw : I.WellFormed s) (hsup : StoreSupported s.funcs) a`. - **`FuncsSupp` narrowed** to Wasm functions. Host functions run no frame, and the clause was only used at Wasm calls. - **Witness-store boundary unchanged.** The witness is used for typing only. The `ASupp` profile excludes `ref.test`, `br_on_cast*`, aggregates and abstract `ref.cast`, which are exactly where the real store and the witness could differ. No theorem claims operational commutation there. **2. Validated aliasing fixture** (`Wasm/Cfg/ExampleAlias`) - **Module `alMod`:** host `h : [] → []`, tag `$t : [exnref]`. - `grab` = `try_table (result exnref) (catch_all_ref 0) (call h; unreachable)`. - `run` = `call grab; throw $t`. - **Validation:** `al_specInstance`, `al_storeOk`, `al_chk`, `al_supported`, `al_instDom`, `al_funcsSupp`, `al_storeOkD`. - **The run.** `h()` is answered by a dangling `throw 0`, an `instHostU` answer (`al_instHostU_throw`). - Natively: `run_round : ([alAns], .ret (.inl (.inr 0)) alEnd) ∈ cfgSessionTripleC.1 alStore (1, [])`. - In Core, every profile `P`: `run_core_U : EvRun P (instHostU alI) (invoke alStore 1 []) [alAns] ⟨alEnd, {}, throwing 0⟩`. Same log and end, via #988's `fin_sub`. - `run_throw_core`/`run_throw_native` instantiate the allocation step on both sides. - **The end store** `alEnd = alStore.addExn ⟨0, [ref.exn 0]⟩` holds a self-referencing exception: `alEnd_not_storeOk` and `alEnd_storeOkD`. **3. Reverse inclusion** (`Wasm/Cfg/DanglingRev`; on `InstDom`, deterministic `profile o`) - `cfgInstTripleL_sub_U`: the legal CFG triple is contained in `cfgInstTripleU`. - `instTripleL_sub_cfgInstTripleU`: per question and componentwise, `instTripleL I (profile o) ⊆ cfgInstTripleU I ⊆ instTripleS I (profile o)`. The second inclusion is #988's. - `instTripleS_agree_cfgInstTripleU_of_nil`: with no imports, full agreement. This one is trivial. **Open** - **The reverse inclusion for behaviours that contain a dangling host throw**, for every observation. No counterexample is known: within the checker profile only handler rules read an exception instance, and they agree (`catchMatches_gst_iff`). The obstacle is size: `back_all`, `HostClosingInfXPBack` and `HostEval` carry `Interp.TypedP` (`Sim.ContextTyped` on the real store), with about 68 uses of `ContextTyped.steps_typed`, plus native progress. The recorded route is to restate `TypedP` over `ConfigOkD`, derive the context lemmas from the witness, and transfer progress, since `evalFlat` in the profile reads no tag or exception. - **Stage 3:** sessions on a `StoreOkD`/`StoreSupported` domain. No new CFG-built definitions, so no audit roots; the `trustedOpaque` allowlist is unchanged. **Checks** - Local, independently re-run after rebasing on `60a082e8`: `lake build --wfail` on all changed modules and `CfgClosureAudit` passes, and `scripts/check-layout.sh` passes. - Axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. - CI pending. author: ff225
body:
Phase 4.4, step 1 (open since phase 3.9): with the link saturated for more than 60 s, or since the device connected, the latency (half the minimum ping RTT of the last 60 s) included the queue, and `UploadMS` added it to every transfer.

## Change
- A ping is **clean** when no message finished after it was sent (`lastSample` ≤ ping start). A pong cannot enter a WebSocket message already started, and the stream calls `Observe` before reading the next message, so a frame the pong waited behind is always observed first. Conservative: a message that finished during the ping marks it dirty even if the pong was not behind it; no upper bound at the pong, since `lastSample` keeps only the latest message.
- `latency_ms` = half the minimum RTT of the clean pings of the last 60 s; without any, of the latest clean ping (kept past the window); with no clean ping ever, of all pings (as before).
- Shortcut: holds for unfragmented messages (the Python client); a client that fragments could let a pong through between fragments.
- Docs: RECORDING.md (Network, Latency), README (`Ping (ms)`).

## Verification
- `go vet ./...`, `gofmt`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; new table test `TestEstimatorLatencyFromCleanPings` (7 cases).
- `client/scripts/bench_network.py`, no limit then 5 Mbit/s (warmup 15 s, measure 90 s), heartbeat `latency_ms` over time:

| | before saturation | after ~60 s at 5 Mbit/s |
|---|---|---|
| main (c49dbf0) | 0.10–0.17 ms | 1967.9 ms |
| this branch | 0.11–0.15 ms | 0.11–0.15 ms |

The script's summary table (median over the measure window) shows 0.15 / 0.17 for both: the jump on main comes halfway through the window.

Not yet checked on the Raspberry Pis (bottleneck in the proxy on the Mac here): the phase 4.4 slow-network runs (R6, `tc` on the Pi) follow this PR.

author: snowingfox
body:
The objective names `npx` explicitly, and **nothing tested it**. Both existing checks run a command that is already installed — globally, and in a project `node_modules` — so neither exercises npx's own path: resolve the package from the registry, install into a cache, and run the bin, with no `node_modules` anywhere in the caller's directory.

## Verified by hand first

From a clean directory against a throwaway registry, on the current packages:

```
$ npx @example/rsnode@0.1.0 -e "console.log('npx works', process.version)"
npx works v28.0.0-nightly20261111e8c1160d20
```

## What the check does

It shells out to `npx --yes <name>@<version> -e ...` with:

- `HOME` set to a fresh directory, and
- `npm_config_cache` set to a fresh directory,

because a warm cache would let a previous run satisfy the invocation and the check would prove nothing. It then asserts the exit code is 0 **and** that the script actually ran, since `npx` returning 0 without running the command is exactly the silent-success shape this repository has been bitten by before.

## It can fail

Inverting the expectation makes it report:

```
FAIL: npx ran the command ('npx-ran v28.0.0-nightly20261111e8c1160d20')
```

so the assertion is load-bearing rather than an always-true print.

## Full suite still passes

`tools/npm-package-test.py` on the current packages: all checks pass, including the new one.

## Not covered here

Still linux-x64 glibc only. macOS and ARM need a CI matrix; this VM cannot cross-build them (no rustup targets, no aarch64 linker, no zig).

author: xuepoo
body:
## What

Fix-forward for the two residuals #3226 recorded on the plugin-store change (`%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` adoption). Tasks: **CTX-1878** and **CTX-1876**.

Related #3226 (not closed: it is merged; these are the follow-ups its review named).

### CTX-1876 — an upgraded Windows install keeps its plugins

Population, stated once in `legacy_store_root_with_platform_env` and nowhere else: **Windows + `$HOME` set + a non-empty `$HOME/.local/share/bitty/plugins`**, i.e. no `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (it always outranked `$HOME`, so an XDG install never wrote the legacy root), a `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (it is what now shadows `$HOME`, the only way the legacy root can be stranded), and a `$HOME`. That is an environment shape, not a build target, so there is no `cfg(windows)` gate: the migration is live on any host and the acceptance test runs in the normal Linux leg.

`bitty_runtime::plugin_runtime::legacy_store::adopt_legacy_store` moves that tree into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bitty\plugins` once, at root resolution:

| state | outcome | store root afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new root exists | `NewRootPresent` — **never merged** | new root |
| legacy root absent/empty | `NoLegacyRoot` — nothing written | new root |
| rename succeeds | `Moved` (whole tree, package bytes included) | new root |
| rename refused (cross-volume: `C:` vs a share) | `Copied` — bounded copy staged in a sibling `.adopting-<pid>` dir, renamed into place; legacy tree left in place | new root |
| both fail | `Failed` | legacy root (plugins stay visible; next start retries) |

No dual-root read: exactly one root is ever authoritative, so discovery still reads one `current.json` and there is no second alias authority. Records hold relative roots and every manifest/digest is re-verified at load, so a moved store resolves exactly as before. `Failed`/`Copied` emit one warn line (redacted, paths only).

Every production consumer now resolves through `effective_store_root_with_platform_env`, so reads and installs agree: startup discovery (`store_root()`), `bitty list plugins` / `list services`, `bitty init`, `bitty plugin install|remove|doctor`, `bitty extension`. `store_root_with_platform_env` stays the pure resolver and its doc says which one production uses.

### CTX-1878 — component state root gets the `%LOCALAPPDATA%` fallback

`state_home_for` / `component_state_root_for` take the Windows root and rank it exactly like the data resolver: `$XDG_STATE_HOME` > `%LOCALAPPDATA%` > `$HOME/.local/state`. Ranking it below `$HOME` would make it unreachable on the one host that needs it. No record migration is needed or done: activation records are a last-recorded *diagnostic projection*, rewritten on the next transition, not a trust boundary, and a legacy record beside `current` remains a read fallback. Call sites updated: `bitty extension` (`component.rs`), `state_root_from_env`, `runtime_inspect` (and `main.rs` already passes `%LOCALAPPDATA%` in the same context).

### Resolver doc note (the second ask in the review)

`data_home_with_platform_env` now explains *why* the order is what it is — `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is the native non-roaming per-user root, `$HOME` on Windows is a shell-exported compatibility variable, `%APPDATA%` is roaming (right for configuration, wrong for a store) — and that the state root follows the same list. Named the failure mode: reordering strands an installed store or component tier.

## Tests (non-vacuous; each was proven to bite)

- `plugin_runtime::tests::upgraded_windows_install_still_discovers_its_legacy_store_packages` — plants a real installed package (manifest + `lua/init.lua`, index with the **real** `manifest_hash` and `content_digest`) in the legacy root, asserts the post-#3226 root is an empty store *first* (the symptom), then asserts the package is discovered at the new root through `store_discovery_rows_at` (the index-plus-manifest read `bitty list plugins` uses, so package bytes must have moved, not just the index), the legacy tree is gone, and a second resolution is a no-op.
- `plugin_runtime::tests::legacy_store_adoption_covers_only_the_windows_home_population` — XDG set, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` unset, empty legacy root, and an existing new root each leave the resolved root untouched (and the existing new root is not merged with the legacy one).
- `legacy_store::tests` — move, no-merge, absent/empty, cross-volume copy fallback (injected refused rename, so no second filesystem needed), failed copy (writes nothing, reports `Failed`, leaves no staging dir).
- `component::activation::tests::windows_local_app_data_outranks_home_for_the_state_root` — `%LOCALAPPDATA%` beats `$HOME`, XDG still beats both, override and trimming still apply.

Discrimination proved on a scratch copy of this commit (never the worktree), with its own target dir:

- delete the `%LOCALAPPDATA%` arm in `state_home_for` → `windows_local_app_data_outranks_home_for_the_state_root` FAILS (`left: Some("/home/u/.local/state")`, `right: Some("C:/Local")`).
- delete the adoption step in `effective_store_root_with_platform_env` → `upgraded_windows_install_still_discovers_its_legacy_store_packages` FAILS (`rows.len()` 0 vs 1).

## Gates (local, this commit)

| gate | rc |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --check` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy -p bitty-runtime --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy -p bitty-terminal --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings` | 0 |
| `cargo test -p bitty-runtime --offline` | 0 |
| `cargo test -p bitty-terminal --offline` | 0 (1655 bin tests; two `profile`/`init` backup tests flaked once under parallel load and pass individually and on the rerun — untouched by this diff) |
| `cargo +1.85 check -p bitty-runtime --tests --offline` | 0 |
| `cargo +1.85 check -p bitty-terminal --tests --offline` | 0 |
| `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo check -p bitty-runtime --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --offline` | 0 |
| `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo check -p bitty-terminal --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --offline` | 0 |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p bitty-runtime --no-deps --offline` | 0 |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p bitty-terminal --no-deps --offline` | 0 |

No dependency edge changed; `Cargo.lock` untouched.

## Deliberately out of scope

- `bitty_plugin_host::grant::grants_path_for` (persisted grants) still resolves `$XDG_STATE_HOME` > `$HOME/.local/state` with no `%LOCALAPPDATA%` arm. That is a security-relevant store, so moving it strands existing grants and needs its own migration; it is not a diagnostics projection like the activation record.
- `stall_watchdog::state_file_path` keeps its own `XDG_STATE_HOME` > `HOME` > `LOCALAPPDATA` order (its `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is a last resort for a host with no `HOME` at all). Unifying the two state resolvers is a separate change; this PR only adds the missing arm to the component state root, which CTX-1878 names.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` entry: the file is written at release time (its newest entry is far behind `Cargo.toml`), and this is a migration, not a feature note.

body:
## Why
A bounded production Food Lion test returned a DataDome HTTP 403 iframe with no body text. GroktoCrawl lost the provider and reported working fallbacks as unavailable. This builds on #732's source HTTP-status handling rather than treating a challenge page as content.

## What
- Recognize real DataDome challenge iframes before short-content gates, without matching prose or lookalike domains.
- Preserve source HTTP status and sanitized provider metadata through API/recovery envelopes.
- Distinguish unavailable transport from service/protocol/extraction/no-content outcomes.
- Report DataDome as unsupported and skip unrelated fallback attempts. This does **not** claim to solve DataDome or grant access to Food Lion.

author: dexhunter
body:
## TL;DR

- Speed up `sguid()` during firmware parsing, including scans with many candidate volume headers.
- Use native hex conversion for the GUID tail and fixed unpack formats for each byte order.
- Median 16 MiB scan time drops from 364.43 ms to 193.12 ms: 47.0% faster, saving 171.32 ms per pass.
- The required four test files pass all 90 tests; full unittest discovery passes 159 tests.

## What & Why

Previously, `sguid()` formatted each tail byte in Python and joined the results. It also built the unpack format on each call.

Now, `bytes.hex("-", 6)` builds the tail with its separator, and the function selects a fixed unpack format. The same fields retain their byte order, lowercase digits, and zero padding.

## Validation

Measured with Python 3.12.13. The flash-scan row measures the repository regression workload, including GUID behavior checks. Other rows show median pytest test durations from five runs, including input construction, rounded to milliseconds.

| Situation | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 MiB flash scan, 65,536 candidate headers | 364.43 ms | 193.12 ms | 47.0% faster |
| 32,768 firmware files, 1,000-byte bodies | 359 ms | 283 ms | 21.2% faster |
| 16,384 sections in one file | 138 ms | 120 ms | 13.0% faster |
| 16 MiB volume with 8,184 block-map entries | 23 ms | 23 ms | No measured change |

The scan timing statistics are:

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| Median new/old time ratio | 0.530 (47.0% faster) |
| 95% CI of the median (bootstrap, 10,000 resamples) | 0.526–0.533 (46.7–47.4% faster) |
| Mean ± SD of the ratio | 0.530 ± 0.005 |
| P95 ratio (slowest 5% of pairs) | 0.539 |
| Number of old/new pairs (n) | 27 (3 runs) |

The block-map case does not benefit because it makes few GUID conversions. Its unchanged median shows no slowdown at the recorded precision.

Run the focused tests with:

```sh
python -m pytest tests/test_termination.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_malformed.py tests/test_me.py
```

Reproduce the scan comparisons with:

```sh
python -m pytest tests/test_termination.py::ScanTimeTest --durations=10
```

From `tests/`, full discovery used `PYTHONPATH=.. python -bb -m unittest discover`.

## Why this is safe and easy to maintain

The change replaces three lines with two and adds no branches or dependencies. Input checks and unpacking errors stay unchanged. Semantic checks cover both byte orders, malformed inputs, bytearrays, and contiguous and noncontiguous memoryviews. Native tests cover firmware scans, rebuilding, malformed data, and ME parsing.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from Aiden. Candidates were tracked with Weco Observe.

author: deryferd
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

The phase-one contract document disagreed with the shipped registry in three places that matter when someone retests the package, and each disagreement made a false statement look authoritative because it sat next to the real tool list.

- The build and compatibility section called `shared/mcp-profiles.json` the single public list of 14 registered names. The same document announces 16 names two sections earlier, `shared/phase1-tools.ts` exposes 16, and `shared/mcp-profiles.json` contains 16 entries including the `openmotion_assets` compatibility alias.
- The public-name table announced 16 rows but carried 17. `openmotion_media_use` appeared twice, and the second row put fixture and test filenames (`tests/byok.test.ts`, `tests/provider-settings.test.ts`) in the "implemented boundary" column, which reads as a contract guarantee rather than as verification evidence.
- The retest commands pointed at `dist/openmotion-0.6.3-phase1.zip`. The packager cannot produce that file: `scripts/package.ts` derives the artifact name from `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, whose version is 0.0.1, and appends `-dev` for the DEV template environment. The 0.6.3 label also clashes with the reserved historical namespace.

The table now has exactly one row per registered name, and the count matches `shared/mcp-profiles.json`, `shared/phase1-tools.ts` and the other documents that cite it. The verification content that the duplicate row carried moved into the existing public-tool verification table, where the other test references live, so nothing is lost and the contract table stops making claims about tests. The artifact name is described through its source of truth (`.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, with the `-dev` suffix) instead of a literal version that will drift again, and the introduction no longer claims a package version that the packager never produced.

## Validation

- `node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/mcp-onboarding.test.ts` passes, 8 of 8, after the rewrite. That suite asserts parity between the handbook, the capability cards and the registry, so it would fail if the document and the registry drifted apart again.
- Table row count is 16 and matches the `phase1.tools` array in `shared/mcp-profiles.json` entry for entry.
- `npm run check` passes on the rebased tree.

## Boundaries

Documentation only. No tool name, schema, transport, registry entry or runtime behavior changed, and the historical verification sections that predate the current registry are left as they were. The document still describes the phase-one package honestly: it does not claim a publication or a host acceptance that did not happen.

author: gitchrisqueen
body:
Compact v2 of the org profile, after Christopher read v1 on the live page: too much text. He chose "Hero + 2nd drawing" on 2026-11-17.

## What changes

- **Visible on load:** the hero, a two-line lead, one call to action drawn as a button (`profile/assets/cta-{light,dark}.svg`: navy `#0F1B2D` fill in light, lifted gold `#C8B53A` in dark; alt text "Book a free 30-minute call"), and a second drawn sheet that wires three failures to the check that catches each. Visible prose drops from 835 words to 34 (method below).
- **Folded into four `<details>`:** the audit, the 30-day build, the three checks with their limits, and code with live CI and upstream fixes. The text keeps its full wording. It stays in the page HTML, so search engines and AI crawlers still read it; only the reader's first view gets shorter.
- **New assets:** `profile/assets/sheet2-{light,dark}.svg` (1280×470) and `sheet2-phone-{light,dark}.svg` (720×990). These are static line drawings in the brand pack's tokens (ivory `#F6F6F2`, navy `#0F1B2D`, deep gold `#7C6D0F`; dark ground `#12161D`, gold `#C8B53A`), with the same embedded Figtree (OFL-1.1). The sheet links to the project write-ups. It has full alt text, and the "three checks" fold-out carries the same facts as real text.
- **`assets.json`** gains entries for sheet 2 and the button. In the hero SVGs, `.val` and `.acc` (the captions and prices) go from 20 to 22 px and `.lab` (the stage labels) from 22 to 24 px. At the 848 px README width the captions then render at about 14.6 px. The hero files also carry the sheet-2 style classes (`.h2`, `.fail`, `.chk`, `.src`), because one generator writes every drawing's stylesheet. They are unused in the hero.
- **No new claims:** every number and statement comes from the merged v1, #3, which passed the claims review. Three fold-out lead sentences were shortened to match the sheet ("nothing checks it", "A release waits", "A job runs green"). The CI table refreshes itself, so its run ids change.

## Size

"Visible prose" is the text a reader sees before opening any fold-out. It is measured by the script below, run as `git show <ref>:profile/README.md | python3 measure_visible.py`. The script strips `<details>` blocks, the CI-status block, `<picture>` blocks, other HTML tags, Markdown link targets and the characters `* [ ] # | -`, then collapses whitespace. A different stripping method gives different counts; this one is stated so the figures reproduce.

| Ref | Words | Characters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1, `8e8c276` (live today) | 835 | 5,042 |
| v2 first push, `001272b` | 39 | 287 |
| v2 head, `f335aac` | 34 | 261 |

For comparison, the whole README of the best peer org profiles we read is 0.6 to 4.3 KB: dottxt-ai 605 bytes, trailofbits 1,123, parlance-labs 2,162, evilmartians 3,204, promptfoo 4,293, e2b-dev 4,325. Command: `gh api repos/<org>/.github/contents/profile/README.md`, field `size`.

<details><summary>measure_visible.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Count the prose a reader sees on load in an org-profile README.

Strips: <details> blocks, the CI-status block, <picture> blocks, every other HTML
tag, Markdown link targets "(...)" after "]", and the characters * [ ] # | -.
Then collapses whitespace. Prints words (split on spaces) and characters.
Usage: git show <ref>:profile/README.md | python3 measure_visible.py
"""
import re
import sys

s = sys.stdin.read()
s = re.sub(r"(?s)<details>.*?</details>", "", s)
s = re.sub(r"(?s)<!-- CI-STATUS:START -->.*?<!-- CI-STATUS:END -->", "", s)
s = re.sub(r"(?s)<picture>.*?</picture>", "", s)
s = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s)
s = re.sub(r"\]\([^)]*\)", "]", s)
s = re.sub(r"[*\[\]#|-]", "", s)
t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
print(f"words {len(t.split())} chars {len(t)}")
```

</details>

author: caraioniurie47
body:
On Unix, a `Socket` operation racing `Socket.Dispose` can throw `ObjectDisposedException` from poll-thread registration instead of failing with a `SocketException`. `UnixHandleAsyncContext` registers its handle with the poll thread when the first operation is queued, registration calls `SafeHandle.DangerousAddRef`, which throws once the handle is closed, and `Socket.Dispose` closes the `SafeHandle` before it aborts the async context. This was reproduced for `Socket.ReceiveAsync`, for a blocking `Socket.Receive` on a handle an earlier asynchronous call made non-blocking, and for `Socket.SendAsync`, `Socket.AcceptAsync` and `Socket.ConnectAsync`; the other socket operations reach the same registration call.

`UnixHandleAsyncContext.Register` now catches the `ObjectDisposedException` and returns `Aborted`, which `StartOperation` returns to the caller, as it already does once the instance is disposed. System.Net.Sockets already maps `Aborted` to `SocketError.OperationAborted`. The Wasi `Register` returns `AsyncResult.Pending` instead of `true`.

Options not taken:

- Catching the exception at each System.Net.Sockets call site. That is ten places (the nine `StartAsyncRead`/`StartAsyncWrite` calls and `PerformSyncOperation`), and `UnixHandleAsyncContext` would still throw for any other caller.
- On a closed handle, queueing the operation without registering and leaving it to `AbortAndDispose` to abort it: without registration the operation gets no poll events, so it completes only once the context is aborted, the operation is canceled or, for a synchronous one, its timeout expires, while returning `Aborted` from `Register` depends on neither.

No test is added. The handle has to be closed after the operation's first non-blocking attempt and before registration, and no public `Socket` API runs code in between.

Checked with the repro from the issue and, on Ubuntu 22.04, with a probe adding a similar sleep to `SystemNative_Send`, `SystemNative_Accept` and `SystemNative_Connect`: before the change, most iterations threw `ObjectDisposedException`; after it, every iteration failed with a `SocketException`.

Resolves dotnet/runtime#137760

> [!NOTE]
> AI-generated, written at my direction and reviewed by me before posting. Verified with CoreCLR on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 x64. With and without the change, no System.Net.Sockets functional test failed on 22.04; on 24.04, the same tests failed. System.Private.CoreLib also compiles for wasi.

author: penelopeduncan
body:
One file: `.github/workflows/generate-builds.yml`. No code and no test changes. Refs #1692.

## Why

On 2026-11-17 the Windows leg of pull-request CI took 1 h 50 min to 3 h, against under an hour the day before. Measured over that day's runs, the time went to compiling: the CMake build step was 55% of the Windows leg (median 61 minutes), the rando test tier 30% (median 40), queueing 8%.

The build step follows the sccache miss count almost exactly: about 10 minutes plus 2.2 seconds per miss. It took 7 to 12 minutes with a warm cache, about 61 at a 56% hit rate, and 126 to 128 with no cache at all.

Two pull requests (#1686, #1694) found no cache to restore. Main's Windows sccache entry was 4.9 GiB, half of the repository's 10 GiB Actions-cache quota. Every main save is a new timestamped entry and nothing deletes the old ones, so the cache always sits at the quota and GitHub evicts whichever entry was read longest ago. No Windows job read main's entry for ninety minutes, and it was the one evicted.

## What changes

- **Windows sccache `max-size` from `5G` to `1536M`.** A cold build of all 3,333 translation units fills 393 MiB, so this still holds almost four builds, and hits only come from recent main commits anyway. A smaller entry is far less likely to be the least recently read one. The value is an integer on purpose: sccache's size parser takes whole numbers with K, M, G or T, so `1.5G` does not parse and sccache would silently use its 10 GiB default (checked in sccache v0.10.0, `src/config.rs` `parse_size`, the version the cache action installs).
- **`timeout-minutes`** on `build-linux` (180), `netplay-relay` (120) and `build-windows` (300, the same as macOS). The longest green jobs in the last 100 runs were 98, 53 and 181 minutes. A hung job no longer holds a runner for GitHub's six-hour default.
- **Comments.** The header no longer says `build-macos` is a required check (the ruleset requires `build-linux`, `build-windows` and `clang-format`). The sccache comment's stale statements are replaced with the measurements above.

## What this does not do

- It does not remove the cause of the eviction. Superseded timestamped entries still pile up; only deleting them would stop that, and that needs a token with `actions: write`. This makes the bad case rarer.
- It does not touch the rando tier's 40 minutes (#1692).
- `netplay-relay`'s ccache stays at 1.5G: its working set is 1.0 to 1.2 GB and it already prunes at that cap, so a smaller one would make it evict its own objects.

## How it was checked

- The YAML parses, and the three timeouts sit at job level.
- `tools/tests/test_required_checks.py`, `test_repo_invariants.py` and `test_retry_unacquired_macos.py`: 185 passed, 48 skipped (the skipped ones need a bash the local run did not have).
- Two read-only reviews. One found the `1.5G` parse problem and the other found that an earlier draft's smaller netplay cap was below that job's working set; both are fixed here.
- No local gate applies: nothing the game builds from changed. This pull request's own CI is the test. **To confirm on the Windows job:** the "sccache stats (Windows)" step should print `Max cache size` as 1536 MiB, and the restored 4.9 GiB entry should be trimmed during the build.
