author: oscar-dom
body:
Dos commits sobre `develop`.

## 1. Skill en ingles, regla anti-IA opcional y auditoria que verifica GitHub

- Todo en ingles: `SKILL.md`, referencias y scripts, con nombres nuevos (`configure-github.sh`, `merge-pr.sh`, `audit-setup.sh`, `rename-main-branch.sh`). Claude sigue hablando al usuario en su idioma.
- Regla anti-IA opcional: las plantillas marcan sus bloques y `ai-attribution.sh keep|remove` los conserva o los quita enteros (paso del CI, seccion de `CONTRIBUTING`, instruccion del agente). `.claude/settings.json` solo se copia con un si. La pregunta solo se hace si el repo lo gestiona una IA.
- `audit-setup.sh` lee de vuelta lo aplicado en GitHub: ajustes de fusion, los tres rulesets activos, la regla de PR y el check `Commit messages` de Actions en `main` y `develop`, secret scanning y el token de workflows (aviso). Comprueba tambien que el CI llego a `develop`, que no quedan marcadores y, con `--no-ai-attribution`, que ningun commit lleva la marca. Sin acceso a GitHub ya no da el montaje por cerrado.

## 2. El agente gestiona el git diario con una sola confirmacion

- `ship.sh`: rama, commit, push, PR, espera al CI, squash y limpieza en una llamada (`--commit-only`, `--pr-only`). Valida el titulo antes de subir, rebasa si `develop` avanzo y aborta sin subir nada si hay conflictos o no hay cambios.
- `release.sh`: `--suggest` (solo lectura) propone la version segun los commits; con la version abre el PR `develop -> main`, espera al CI, merge commit, etiqueta y release.
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` con recetas en vez de leer la chuleta: el agente inspecciona, propone un plan en lenguaje sencillo, pregunta una vez y lo ejecuta todo.

## Como se ha probado

- `ship.sh` y `release.sh` contra un remoto local con un `gh` simulado que hace las fusiones de verdad: subida desde `develop`, titulo invalido, `--commit-only`, CI en rojo y reintento, sin cambios, desde `main`, rebase cuando `develop` avanzo, conflicto (aborta limpio), primera release, sugerencia de parche y etiqueta repetida.
- `ai-attribution.sh` en los dos modos; con `remove` el CI sigue siendo YAML valido y sin el paso.
- `audit-setup.sh` en un repo local (marcadores olvidados, commit con marca, sin GitHub) y sus lecturas de la API contra este repo.
- Pendiente: un montaje real de principio a fin contra GitHub; la ruta de permisos de Actions la bloquea el proxy del entorno de pruebas.

body:
- fix: use executed trade values in post-trade previews cp-8.21.0 (#39942)

## **Description**

The composer's in-flight card (the "post this trade" preview) was built
from the typed amount and the market price, not from what the trade
executed. The feed builds the same card from backend data once the trade
is indexed, so the two disagreed. TSA-1790 is the case: the card showed
$11 while the bottom sheet showed $11.07.

This PR makes the in-flight previews use the executed values:

- **Perps, long and short:** Cost is the filled size times the average
fill price. Entry is the average fill price. The share card stays
pending on the typed amount until the order completes, then completion
patches Cost and Entry from the order result. It falls back to the typed
amount only when the result has no fill size.
- **QuickBuy buy:** Cost is the trade's USD value. Entry is that USD
value divided by the tokens received in the quote being submitted. It
used to be the token's market price.
- **QuickBuy sell:** Cost is the trade's USD value. Entry is that USD
value divided by the tokens sold in the quote. It used to be the swap
rate string (for example `1 ETH = 2,000 USDC`), which is not a price per
token.
- QuickBuy Cost is now shown in USD, matching the feed's `boughtUsd`,
instead of the user's display currency.

On each card, Cost and Entry now come from the same numbers, so Entry
times size equals Cost.

## Test layer placement

- Unit: `app/components/UI/Perps/utils/perpsPostTradeShare.test.ts`
covers the perps Cost and Entry from the fill, the short direction, the
typed-amount fallback, and the completion patch.
- Hook / integration:
`app/components/UI/QuickBuy/hooks/runQuickBuyControllerCases.ts`, run
through `useQuickBuyController.test.tsx`, covers the quoted buy and sell
Entry, the currency conversion, and the missing-quote case.
- No component-view test was added. The card renders the values it is
given, and the existing card view tests are unchanged.

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: null

## **Related issues**

Refs: TSA-1790 (https://consensyssoftware.atlassian.net/browse/TSA-1790)

## **Manual testing steps**

```gherkin
Feature: Composer card shows the executed trade values

  Background:
    Given a wallet with a funded Hyperliquid perps balance
    And a funded token balance for QuickBuy on Base
    And trade posting to the feed is enabled for the account

  Scenario: Perps long card matches the order sheet
    When the user opens ETH perps, sets a $11 long at 1x, and submits the market order
    And the user chooses to post the trade from the share sheet
    Then the card's Cost is the filled size times the fill price, about $11.07
    And the card's Entry is the average fill price

  Scenario: Perps short card uses the same fill cost
    When the user submits a $11 ETH short at 1x and posts it from the share sheet
    Then the card's Cost is the filled size times the fill price
    And the card's Entry is the average fill price

  Scenario: QuickBuy buy card uses the quoted entry, not the market price
    When the user buys $20 of a token from QuickBuy and chooses to post it
    Then the card's Cost is $20.00
    And the card's Entry is $20 divided by the tokens received in the quote
    And the card's Entry is not the token's market price

  Scenario: QuickBuy sell card shows a USD price per token
    When the user sells $20 of a token from QuickBuy and chooses to post it
    Then the card's Cost is $20.00
    And the card's Entry is a USD price per token sold
    And the card's Entry is not a token-to-token swap rate
```

body:
Follow-up to #48, from a second comment on the same prototype panel ("this looks like a list of items; could it be shown in a way that is easier to understand?", said of a note like "1 assessment template · 7 assessments · 6 ratings").

## What

- **Unambiguous States, rule 9**:
  - A quantity the person compares or looks for is a number set apart with its unit beside it, one per element. It never goes inside a sentence or gets strung with others between separators.

author: matto00
body:
Linear: [HEL-1733](https://linear.app/helioapp/issue/HEL-1733/live-draft-preview-h-create-edit-and-delete-outputs-inside-a-draft)

## Summary

While a pipeline draft is open, these actions are now draft entries instead of being blocked with "Save or discard your draft first":
- Output create (on a saved step, on a step new in the draft, or on the pipeline source)
- Output edit and delete
- "Add Outputs from a shape"
- "Add as tail with aggregate"

They are applied in one atomic `draft/save` on Save & run and dropped on Discard. With no draft open, every action keeps its immediate behavior. Only add/remove source stays blocked; roots are HEL-1734.

- **Draft model:** overlay v3. Output create/delete join the ordered op log, replayed together with the step ops, so a step delete cascades its Outputs in order. Output edits go in a map holding the whole merged config (the same result as the server's shallow PATCH merge).
- **Kept drafts:** v3 adds an `outputsBase` signature; v2/v1 drafts still restore and are not stale. Restore still fires once steps are ready. The Output part waits for this page's own Outputs fetch, and the Output-base stale check runs before any dropped op is counted.
- **Output editor in a draft:** column types and binding eligibility come from the server's projection of the unsaved draft, via the existing read-only `POST /api/pipelines/analyze-proposal`. A client port of `buildNodeCapabilities` turns that projection into binding options. A shared Scala/jest parity fixture keeps the port in step with the server. If the projection is unavailable (for example an editor grantee who does not own the source, which gets a 404), kinds with numeric or time-ordered slots cannot be saved from the editor. The preview uses draft rows.
- **Output delete** (owner ruling Q1): the sheet keeps its exact two-click "Confirm delete (removes from N dashboards)", which records the delete. Save & run then shows the existing "This save removes other things" dialog listing the Output, its bound panels and its alert rules. The effect at Save is identical to today's delete: both call `deleteOutputsCoreAction`.
- **Spine and Live Output column** show draft Outputs. Card meta reads "New · not saved" or "Edited".
- **Backend:** `DraftDiff.planOutputs` now validates a draft Output edit against the stored config, like `PATCH /api/outputs/:id` (the tolerance rule). Before, an Output carrying a stored legacy key returned 400 on any draft edit. Undo uses the restore policy and writes back the journaled config verbatim. `buildNodeCapabilities` moved unchanged to the `PipelineNodeReads` companion.
- **Shapes:** on this backend `/expand` returns no Outputs for any shape, so a real shape adds steps only. The draft path also handles an Output-bearing expansion; this is unit-tested and covered by one e2e that stubs `/expand`.

One PR covers Outputs and shapes together (owner ruling Q2, one-pr). No Flyway migration.

## Test plan

- **Red first:**
  - `e2e/hel1733-draft-outputs-shapes.spec.ts` against main: all 19 tests fail on the disabled "Save or discard your draft first" control. This covers the 8 actions on desktop-light and phone-dark, both smokes, and Discard.
  - The type-seam e2e has its own red run.
  - Backend `DraftDiffSpec`/`DraftSaveApiSpec`: 3 failures on main, green after the fix.
- **Green:**
  - jest: 9638 frontend and 579 root tests.
  - `sbt testFull`: 9588 succeeded, 0 failed.
  - The new e2e: 32 passed, including the 4 sheet-hint placement tests.
  - The new spec together with hel1631, hel1632, hel1684, hel1685, hel1704 and hel1705: 89 passed (Playwright workers 2).
- **Visual:** checked in the running app in light and dark, on desktop and at 375px, by the evaluator and the final skeptic. Screenshots are in the archived change's `evidence/`.
- **Gates:** design gate CONFIRM at round 6 (one extra round granted by the owner); evaluator PASS at cycle 2; final skeptic CONFIRM at round 2.

## Behavior notes and risks

- A kept draft that changes only steps now restores as stale when a saved Output was changed concurrently. This matches the spec ("steps or Outputs") and costs one "Reload the saved pipeline" click.
- Undo of a save that removed a bound panel or alert rule is refused with the existing 409. This is unchanged server behavior.
- Self-approved decisions:
  - actions draft only while a draft exists;
  - the editor's fallback when the projection is unavailable;
  - the draft hint placed under the header fields;
  - the card meta copy;
  - post-save resolution of a picked created Output;
  - the restore validation policy;
  - a shape recorded as a single overlay update.
- Not part of this change, worth a follow-up: at 375px the existing "Confirm delete (removes from 1 dashboard)" label overflows its button, and it is now reachable inside a draft too.
- Branch history held a 15 MB raw sbt log before the squash; the squash commit carries only the summary excerpt.

Replay checks whether a coding agent can redo a change that really shipped: rewind the repository, give the agent the commit message, let the real change's tests decide. | Setup | Passed | Rate (95% interval) |

| Sonnet, working method and review | 28 of 30 | 93% (79% to 98%) |
| Opus, working method and review | 26 of 30 | 87% (70% to 95%) |

The new setup (`--harness protocol-review`: a written working method, then a second agent call that reviews the diff against the task and repairs gaps) made no measurable difference: same rate as plain Sonnet here, and 90% with or without it for Opus on 42 earlier cases. author: ethanblackburn
body:
## The problem

A reviewer holds a conversation with tools (`model.chat`). On chat completions, OpenAI refuses tools to a model that thinks:

```
Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-6.1-terra in /v1/chat/completions.
To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.
```

So an OpenAI model could review only with its thinking off. With `reasoning_effort: none`, `gpt-6.1-terra` ran as the judge pack's reviewer and settled nothing.

## The change

`backend` names the protocol a node speaks, and this adds a fourth: `backend: responses`, OpenAI's Responses API, through rig's own model for it.

```yaml
inference:
  reviewer:
    backend: responses
    api_key: "${OPENAI_API_KEY}"
    model: gpt-6.1-terra
    extra: { reasoning: { effort: low } }
```

- It needs `api_key`, as `anthropic` does, and says so when the pipeline is built.
- `url` is read only to reach the API at another address; unset, it is OpenAI's.
- `extra` goes in the body as on every backend.
- `backend: openai` is unchanged: chat completions, for OpenAI and every compatible server.

**For you to decide: the name.** I took `responses` because the other three name a protocol (`openai` is "the protocol, not the vendor"). `openai_responses` would say whose it is.

## Tested

- `the_responses_backend_asks_the_responses_api`: against a stand-in server, the request is `POST /responses` with the bearer key, `max_output_tokens`, `extra` in the body, the prompt and the record, and the verdict schema as the text's format; the reply is read as any other backend's.
- `a_backend_that_needs_a_key_says_so`: `anthropic` and `responses` both refuse a missing or empty key.
- Live, on the 11 Okta and Workspace fixture records with the reviewer wired in: `gpt-6-luna` as judge and `gpt-6.1-terra` as reviewer, both on `responses` with low reasoning. 11 judged, 7 alerts, 7 reviewed, each review after a query of the lake, no errors.

Terra called all 7 "unresolved", where Claude Sonnet 5.5 and DeepSeek V4 Flash called most of the same alerts malicious. That is the model's judgment on thin fixtures, not the backend; a run on the eval corpus is next.

author: goranai
body:
Fixes #1873

`utils.params()` split the Content-Type header at every `;` and kept each raw value. For `Content-Type: text/html; charset="UTF-8"` this made `res.charset` equal to `"UTF-8"` with the quote characters. A `;` inside quotes, as in `boundary="a;b"`, also split the value.

Change in `src/utils.js`:

- split at `;` only when it is outside a quoted string (backslash escapes are honored)
- when a value is a quoted string, take the text between the quotes and turn `\x` into `x`
- the text inside the quotes is taken as sent, so `boundary="a = b"` stays `a = b`

Behavior changes:

- quoted values lose their quotes and escapes: `charset="UTF-8"` gives `UTF-8`
- a `;` inside quotes no longer splits the value
- an empty quoted value (`charset=""`) is now skipped, like an empty unquoted value. Before it gave `""`
- a malformed header with a stray or unterminated quote is no longer split at the `;` after that quote. Example: `a=x"y; b=c` gave `{ a: 'x"y', b: 'c' }` and now gives `{ a: 'x"y; b=c' }`
- headers without a `"` give the same result as before

The fix is longer than the line it replaces because a regex split cannot skip a `;` inside quotes. Tabs around `;` and `=` are still not trimmed, as before.

How I checked it:

- compared against the `content-type` package (1.0.5, installed here as a dependency of express) on 100000 random valid headers with quoted values, escapes and latin-1 characters: the new code matched every time, the old code differed on 56495
- 200000 random strings without `"` (spaces, `=`, `;`, backslash, tab, CR, LF, unicode): old and new results identical
- new test in `test/node/utils.js`. It fails on master and passes with the change

Tests on Node 24, Windows: `mocha --exit --require should --timeout 5000 test/*.js test/node/*.js` gives 428 passing, 9 pending, 1 failing. The failure is `req.attach ignores null file` (timeout), and it fails the same way on master here. `eslint -c .eslintrc` on the changed files passes, and `prettier --check src/utils.js` passes. I did not run the HTTP2 variant or `make test`. dist and the version are not changed.

Validated with Claude Opus 5.5.

author: abbosc
body:
## Plan

Bug on production (owner, 17 November 2026; deploy is the owner's, by hand). Step 2 "Oʻquv yuklamasi" of a draft's readiness refuses every class whose sport is taught in boys' and girls' mixed halves ("Darslari dars slotlaridan koʻp sinflar"), although the load fits the week; this blocks generation and publish.

**Cause.** `classWeekLessons` (`packages/timetable-rules/src/totals.ts`) adds, per class, the class rows plus, for each subject, the largest group row of that subject. One-sex mixed halves pair *across subjects* (edge/timetable, Structure: "A mixed block is allowed: boys have physical education while girls have technology, and the reverse in another slot. Its two lessons are parts of two subjects drawn from the same class, or from the same pair of classes … and together they hold every student of those classes exactly once"; `06`, Rules: "a mixed block pairs parts of two subjects instead"). A subject taken by one sex only (boys' taekwondo 2, girls' gymnastics 2) is counted in full although each of its lessons shares its slot with a lesson of the other sex. Labzak, quarter 2: boys PE 2 + Swimming 1 + Taekwondo 2 = 5, girls PE 2 + Swimming 1 + Gymnastics 2 = 5, sport needs 5 slots; today it counts 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 7, so grade 1 to 4 classes show 42 for 40 slots.

**When done.** The weekly total of a class counts the one-sex mixed halves of each split it belongs to (its own class, or its pair of classes) by the slots they really need: the larger of the boys' total and the girls' total. Every other row counts as today. The load page's totals, step 2 of the readiness and the publish check read the same function and agree.

### Database
None. No migration, no row changes (stop-list item 3 does not apply).

### Rule engine (`packages/timetable-rules`)
- `totals.ts`: `TotalsRow` gains `mixedBlock: boolean`; the second argument of `classWeekLessons` becomes a map of the group's classes and sex (`Pick<BlockGroup, 'classIds' | 'sex'>`) in place of the classes alone.
- New rule in `classWeekLessons`, per split (`isSplit`, `splitKeyOf` of `blocks.ts`: one class or a pair of classes):
  - the split's rows marked mixed whose groups are all for one sex form two sides, boys and girls; a side's total is the sum over subjects of the most lessons of that side's rows of the subject (each boy is in exactly one group of a subject, `05`, Group, so two boys' groups of one subject in one split need the larger of their lessons, not the sum);
  - the split counts `max(boys, girls)` for each of its classes (a pair's split counts for both classes, as a group of two classes does today);
  - every other row counts as today: whole-class rows summed; group rows (not mixed, mixed halves that are not one-sex, groups across more than two classes, and every mixed row of a split that has any mixed half for everyone, its one-sex mixed rows included) per subject, the most lessons of the subject's group rows drawing from the class.
  - Rows of the same subject and class outside the split (a taekwondo group across three classes that includes one of them) stay in today's per-subject count beside the split's sides.
- The existing test of `classWeekLessons` and every builder of `TotalsRow` are updated for the new field and argument and keep their expected values (its `pe` group of `oxford` + `edinburgh` is a pair split not marked mixed, so `oxford` stays 5 + 3 + 2).
- `index.ts`: nothing new exported unless needed by the caller.
- No change to the check (`check.ts`), the blocks, `partnersIn`, the pattern model or the solver input: they place and check lessons, they never use the weekly total. The teacher totals (`teacherWeekLessons`) are a sum of rows and stay right (a teacher of two halves teaches both, in different slots, decision 12 of 3.4b).

### API
- `timetable.service.ts` `totalsOf`: pass `mixedBlock: row.mixed_block` in each totals row and the whole `BlockGroup` map from `readBlockGroups` (it already reads `sex`). This one function feeds the totals route (load page), `readinessOf` (builder step 2) and the publish check (`publish.service.ts` reads `readiness.load.classesOver` from `readinessOf`), so the three agree. No route, schema or permission changes; no `pnpm api:client` change expected.

### Web
None: the load page and the builder show the totals the API answers.

### Tests (failing first, in `packages/timetable-rules/src/totals.test.ts`)
1. The Labzak shape with invented names: a pair of classes (7 Sydney, 8 Columbia invented) each with 35 whole-class lessons and a pair split of one-sex mixed rows (boys PE 2, Swimming 1, Taekwondo 2; girls PE 2, Swimming 1, Gymnastics 2) counts 35 + 5 = 40 for each class. Also the one-class version (a class's own split). Rule: edge/timetable, Structure (mixed block); `06`, Building a timetable, step 2.
2. An unpaired extra half still counts: boys get one more Taekwondo lesson (3), girls stay at 5 → 35 + 6 = 41.
3. Halves not for one sex marked mixed (a split of group 1 and group 2) count as today, per subject.
4. One-sex groups not marked mixed (a load problem of their own, `load_one_sex_not_mixed`) count as today.
5. A group across three classes, and a group of two grades not of a split, count as today; the existing test stays.
6. A class with its own split and a pair split: each split counted once for it.
7. A split with one-sex mixed halves and a mixed half for everyone together: all of its mixed rows count per subject, as today.
8. Rows outside the split: boys' taekwondo in the pair's split and a taekwondo group across three classes that includes one of them: the outside group counts per subject beside the sides.
9. Two boys' groups of one subject in one split (boys PE-a 2, PE-b 2, girls PE 2) count 2, not 4.
- API (`apps/api/src/modules/timetable/readiness.test.ts`): a draft whose class has whole-class rows and one-sex mixed halves that fit the week by pairing but not by today's count: `load.classesOver` is empty and `load.ready` true; the totals route answers the same lessons; publish is not refused for step `load` on that count. author: amckinley
body:
## What

On SIGTERM or Ctrl-C, `marco serve`, `seek serve` and `seek builder` now stop in four steps instead of dropping their listeners at once:

1. **Lame duck.** `/readyz` answers 503 `shutting down` at once, and every listener keeps serving for `--shutdown-drain-secs` (default 10 s): reads, writes and new connections. Each HTTP/1 answer carries `Connection: close`, so a keep-alive client dials again. A second signal ends the drain early (handy with Ctrl-C).
2. **Stop accepting.** The listeners close (a new connection is refused), each HTTP/2 connection gets a GOAWAY, an idle HTTP/1 connection closes. This is axum's `with_graceful_shutdown`, which drives hyper's `graceful_shutdown` per connection.
3. **Finish what's in flight**, up to `--shutdown-grace-secs` (default 10 s).
4. **marco only:** then, as before, ingest gets up to 10 s to hand over, and the last change segment is written, so every write marco acknowledged, including during the drain, is in the snapshot.

| Flag | Env | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--shutdown-drain-secs` | `MARCO_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECS` / `SEEK_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECS` | 10 (0: stop at once) |
| `--shutdown-grace-secs` | `MARCO_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS` / `SEEK_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS` | 10 |

The pieces:

- `marco-ops::drain::Drain`, shared by both binaries: `lame_duck()`, `stop(grace)`, `run(drain, grace)`, `spawn(server)` to register an axum server, `stopped()` for its `with_graceful_shutdown`, the `close_http1` middleware, and `signal()` (SIGTERM or Ctrl-C).
- marco: `App::drain`; every listener (API, `--listen-extra`, admin, `--ops-listen`) is registered with it; `/readyz` checks it first.
- `PeerListener`'s accept loop now ends when the listener is dropped. Before, the socket stayed open after the server stopped, so a connection after the stop was accepted and then closed instead of being refused.
- seek: `Pod::drain` (`readiness()` says `shutting down`), the builder's router takes the drain, the ops listeners are registered too. `seek serve` used to handle only Ctrl-C, so SIGTERM killed it outright; it now drains. The builder's cycle loop runs as its own task so a build blocking its thread can't delay the signal, and the process exits without waiting for a build or state save in progress (`shutdown_timeout`). Both write their files by rename, so that's safe.
- Docs: operations.md has a new Stopping section and the flags; seek.md has the flags and a Stopping section; durability.md links them.

## Why it's generally useful

Anyone running marco or seek behind a load balancer or a Kubernetes Service sees failed requests on every restart today. The listeners vanish with the process: in-flight requests fail, and clients that hold connections (gRPC and other HTTP/2 clients, or keep-alive pools through a Service, which pins each connection to one pod) get connection errors instead of being told to move. `/readyz` also stays 200 until the process is gone, so a load balancer can keep sending new connections in the window before it notices. With this change a restart is invisible to a client that follows GOAWAY and `Connection: close`, as long as what's in flight finishes within the grace.

Recommended `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`: drain + grace + 10 s (ingest handover) + the longest checkpoint (`marco_checkpoint_seconds`; the last segment waits for a running checkpoint). That's about 90 s for marco with the defaults on the whole network. Kubernetes' default of 30 s is too short for marco and enough for seek. No `preStop` sleep is needed.

## How it was tested

- `crates/marco-server/tests/shutdown.rs`:
  - `drain_serves_then_stops`, in process. A 3 s CPU profile is in flight over HTTP/2. In lame duck, `/readyz` is 503 on the API and admin listeners, `/healthz` and an HTTP/2 connection from before the drain still answer, and HTTP/1 answers say `Connection: close` and close. `stop()` waits for the profile, which completes with 200. API, admin and ops then refuse new connections, and the old HTTP/2 client's next call fails, since nothing is listening.
  - `grace_bounds_the_wait`: `stop(500 ms)` returns false within 2 s while a 5 s request is still running. The listeners are already refusing, and the request itself still completes.
  - `sigterm_drains_then_exits` runs the real `marco serve` binary and sends it SIGTERM with a profile in flight. `/readyz` turns 503 within a second. During the drain, a write on a new connection to the admin listener is acknowledged and a read on the old HTTP/2 connection sees it. New connections are refused only after the 2.5 s drain. The profile completes and the process exits 0. A server reopened on the snapshot has the drain's write.
  - The PeerListener fix was checked by reverting it: all three tests fail with "still accepts".
- `crates/seek-server/tests/pod.rs`: `drain_answers_then_refuses` covers a pod in lame duck. `/readyz` is 503 `shutting down` while a logged-in gRPC query is still answered (blocks filtered through marco), then the stop refuses new connections. The pod harness now registers its server with the drain, the way `main` does.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --locked --bins`, `cargo test --locked --workspace` (rust 1.100.0, Linux), and `npm run check-docs`.

body:
Moves to amplifier-agent v0.30.0, lowers the default reasoning effort, and updates locked dependencies within the 7 day cooldown. No dependency minimums are raised, so projects that use Digital Twin Universe as a library keep their current ranges.

Defaults
- The default reasoning effort is `medium` instead of `high`, matching the other smart tools.
- Default models are unchanged: `gpt-6.1-sol` (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol` on `amplifier-agent`), `claude-opus-5-5` on `claude`.

Agent SDKs
- amplifier-agent v0.25.0 to v0.30.0. Smart tools, on by default since v0.28.0, are turned off so agents get only the tools named for each run.
- openai-codex is capped at `<1.0.0` instead of `<0.160.0`. Each openai-codex version pins the Codex CLI release of the same number, so a new minor is a routine CLI release.
- Locked: github-copilot-sdk 1.0.31, openai-codex 0.167.0, claude-agent-sdk 0.2.180.

Dependencies and security
- Caps raised for fastapi (`<0.163.0`), uvicorn (`<0.55.0`), and typer (`<0.29.0`). typer 0.29 changes `TyperOption.__init__` in a way the custom help options do not support, so it stays excluded.

- `dashboard/`: dependency updates within the cooldown, including @types/node 26 and @rolldown/plugin-babel 0.3. @babel/core stays on 7, since babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0 is built against it, and TypeScript stays below 6.1 for typescript-eslint. A pnpm override moves minimatch to 11.x. The compiled dashboard is rebuilt.

Docs

- Model examples use `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.

author: tycorc
body:
## What

`wledlab.py install --cfg` wrote a config overlay with one `/json/cfg` body. WLED 16.0.1 hears the four OTA switches (`ota.lock`, `lock-wifi`, `aota`, `same-subnet`) in such a body only with the OTA lock off (`cfg.cpp`, `pwdCorrect`); with the lock on they are taken from the security form with the OTA password (`set.cpp`). On a locked controller the install therefore wrote everything else and ended with `cfg: MISMATCH | ota.same-subnet: wanted false, lamp has true`.

Now the install reads the config back after the body and, for an OTA switch that did not land, sends the security form with the controller's credentials (the existing `write_security`, which verifies the four switches), then reads back again. Without credentials the mismatch stays an error.

## Checked

- `make test`: 149 tests OK. Two new tests on the lamp fake, which now models both firmware paths: the switch lands through the form and the locks stay on; without credentials the install fails as before.
- Revert check: with the form call disabled the first new test fails.

## Not checked

- On a controller: the next install run of the infrastructure repository is the first.

author: danie1le
body:
## Why

Spec #21 stories 36, 39, 51 and 88-89: back the alert claims with numbers.

## What changed

- `bench alert-latency`: one process publishes breach Readings and listens on SignalR as a new Operator; p95 of receive minus publish (bar 500 ms), split at the Alert's `CreatedAt` into server and push time (clock offset corrected).
- `bench offline`: Scenario of long and short Power offs and Coverage gaps against an Offline rule. Detected = Alert `CreatedAt` within last Received + rule seconds + 2 s; an Alert with no matching long dropout is a false alarm.
- `bench hysteresis`: Threshold rules with Hysteresis 0 and the real one on every Asset, evaluating the same noisy Readings in one run; false Alert = raised outside every Fault window of the Manifest; counts and % reduction.
- Results are JSON with environment like the telemetry bench (`BenchTarget.WriteResultAsync`); `BenchRun.RunAsync` takes an optional `Scenario`.
- Pure scoring in `AlertScoring.cs` (unit tests), committed fleet `fleets/alerts.json` and two Scenarios.

## How to review

`AlertScoring.cs` and its tests first (the definitions), then `OfflineBench.cs` (last-Received query in `AlertBenchSupport.cs`), `AlertLatencyBench.cs`, `HysteresisBench.cs`, then CLI glue (`AlertBenches.cs`, `BenchCli.cs`, help text). Look hardest at the offline scoring rules.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Hysteresis runs both arms in one run on identical Readings instead of two runs; same input by construction. The noise is seeded (`--seed`, default 1) and the result records the seed and each Device's Boot, so a run can be repeated.
- The Offline +2 s bar is tight on a loaded machine (see below). Curated clean re-runs belong to #50.
- Adds the .NET SignalR client to the Simulator (version already pinned centrally). Each latency run leaves a bench Operator and rules behind; use a fresh stack.

## How verified

- `dotnet build`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Unit tests 377 passed. `AlertBenchTests` (3 integration tests, in-process ingest and hub) pass.
- Real run against a local compose stack (project ft45, shared 8-core machine):
  - alert-latency, 200 Alerts over 10 Devices: total p50 77 ms, p95 355 ms, p99 1,296 ms (server p95 222, push p95 215), 0 missed, PASS.
  - offline, 20 s rule, 10 long + 10 short dropouts: 0 missed, 0 false alarms, 9 detected, 1 late (22.6 s after last Received vs the 22 s bar, a ~2 s sweep hiccup under load): FAIL as scored.
  - hysteresis (before the seed option, so not reproducible; not re-run since), threshold 90, noise sigma 2.5, Hysteresis 8: 54 false Alerts without vs 44 with (18.5% fewer), PASS.

Closes #45

author: sargunv
body:
On macOS, `mln-desktop --benchmark --backend webgpu` kept a CPU core busy while its window was hidden. wgpu returns `Occluded` for a hidden window, every frame finishes as `TargetNotReady`, and benchmark mode asked for the next frame at once. Now, after a `TargetNotReady`, benchmark mode waits for the frame pacing's refresh interval, and goes back to running unpaced once a frame renders.

Fixes #590.

Measured with `/usr/bin/time` on the release build, with the window hidden by AppleScript from 2 s until `--quit-after 8`, two runs each:

| | user + sys CPU |
| --- | --- |
| before | 8.0 s, 7.1 s |
| after | 0.8 s, 1.0 s |

After rebasing onto the new benchmark mode (#592), `--benchmark --laps=0 --quit-after 8`, hidden from 3 s on, used 2.0 s and 0.2 s. I also checked by hand that drawing resumes at 120 fps once the window is shown again.

Stays draft: 0.3.0 lane, CI only

`dutchman contents FILE [--json]` and the MCP `contents` tool list a file's bodies, feature
timeline and parameters, and give each feature the mapper's verdict for SolidCraft, without
converting, writing anything or running SolidCraft.

## What users get

- Bodies: kind (`solid`, `sheet`, `wire`, `general`), name, hidden.
- Features in timeline order: kind, name, suppressed, and a verdict: `mapped`,
  `needs_solidcraft_check` (fillet/chamfer input edges found on SolidCraft's replay, inferred
  profile regions, whole multi-profile sketches, unchecked profile regions), `not_needed`,
  `left_out`, `not_supported_yet` with the reason, or `after_blocker`.
- Parameters: name, value, unit (`mm`, `deg`), expression as written, owning feature.
- A new `dutchman.contents/1` schema; existing reports are unchanged.

## How it works

- `dutchman-core::contents` lists bodies, parameters and suppressed ordinals from CADIR.
- `SolidCraftWriter::verdicts` runs the same history mapping `inspect` and `convert` use, with the
  profile-inference check accepted and blend proofs not run; the steps that would need
  SolidCraft are named from the mapping's own records (pending blends, unconfirmed whole
  sketches, inferred candidates, `profile_unverified`). Assemblies list each distinct part once.
- The report is built in one place (`json::contents`) for the CLI and MCP.

## Measurements

`nice -n 10`, `/usr/bin/time`, two runs each; contents vs today's `inspect --json` on the same
file. No SolidCraft runs in either. Decoding dominates both, so `contents` costs what `inspect`
costs; the listing adds nothing measurable.

author: zanattamichael
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ZanattaMichael"} -->
_Requested by **McLovin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016ncusmiifUgXbeeEb6CR9E?thread=cmsg_016ncusmiifUgXbeeEb6CR9E4VwcMKuQzeorCvjRXMMmZX)_

## What this changes

Phase 7 (first part) of [the language expansion plan](docs/plans/language-expansion.md#18-delivery-in-phases): a secret in a resource's `params` now reaches the tool, by a private channel, for a target that declares it takes one.

- **Protocol and SDK.** `Capabilities.secrets`; the graph names each secret its params refer to (`ResourceGraph.secrets`, `Resource.secret_params`, with the mask left in `params_json`); the run context carries the values for `Plan` and `Apply` only, over the plugin's private socket, taken straight into protected memory on the plugin's side. All additive, so the protocol version does not change. New SDK helpers: `ResourceGraph::secrets_written_as`, `Secrets` (`get`, `of`, `json_file`), `Tool::stdin_secret`, `Part::JsonString`.
- **Orchestrator.** For a capable target a secret in a param stays a secret through compile, plan and apply; the artifact holds a reference, never a value. For any other target the stage stops as before, now naming the targets that take one. A rollback fetches a document's secrets again at its turn; the run keeps none once a stage ends.
- **Targets.** `ansible`: `{{ meridian_secret_<name> }}`, the task marked `no_log: true`, an extra-vars file passed as `--extra-vars @<path>`. `terraform` and `opentofu`: `${var.meridian_secret_<name>}` with the variable declared `sensitive`, `-var-file` on `plan`, and the saved plan overwritten and removed after use because it holds every variable. The test target records what it was handed (names and channel, never a value) and copies the private file to a sink a test names.
- **Docs.** [Handing a secret to a tool](docs/reference/dsl/secrets.md#handing-a-secret-to-a-tool), the [concept page](docs/concepts/secrets-in-memory.md#across-the-plugin-boundary), the [plugin guide](docs/contributing/writing-a-plugin.md#secrets), the three target pages, the capability matrix (new `secrets` column) and the plan's 11.6 and 11.8 "as built" notes. New example `examples/language/secret-to-a-tool.yaml`.

Design choices to review: a value made from a secret and text is one secret, handed over as `derived_<n>` (the whole text is protected, so no name of the document's is its own); the values ride in the run context message rather than on a stream of their own (one message, one copy, dropped once sent, which the plan's 11.8 note explains); `compile` writes the reference for a capable target, so the compiled files are what the tool is run with.

Still to come in phase 7: credential types in documents, delivery on the other targets, the recording tool as one suite.

## How it was tested

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `python3 tools/check_links.py` (95 files, 0 broken links).
- New tests: SDK wire round trips (a secret crosses as a place and a slot, a misplaced one is refused, a context carries values into protected memory and `outputs` carries none); `Secrets` and the JSON file (escaping, a non-text secret refused); `Tool::stdin_secret` against `cat`; the real fake plugin process handed a secret by name and by value; stand-ins for `ansible-playbook`, `terraform` and `tofu` that keep a copy of the file they were pointed at, their arguments and their environment (value in the file, mode `0600`, file gone after the run, nothing on the command line or in the environment, Terraform's saved plan scrubbed); the CLI end to end against the fake target (compile writes the reference; plan and apply hand the value over in a private file the test reads back, and it is in nothing else printed, applied or kept; a target that takes none stops the stage).
- Real tools: the new `ansible`, `terraform` and `tofu` real tests (check mode with diff prints nothing of the value; `(sensitive value)` in what Terraform prints; the plan file gone; the value reaches the file on disk or the tool's own state; nothing in the work directory the plugin wrote holds it) all pass locally against ansible-core, Terraform 1.9.8 and OpenTofu 1.8.8, and run again in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked`
- [x] `python3 tools/check_links.py`
- [x] A test covers the change; a bug fix has a test that fails without it
- [x] Golden files were recorded on purpose and their diff was read (`docs/reference/capability-matrix.md`: the new column)
- [x] The documentation is updated in this pull request

## For a new or changed plugin

- [x] Everything the tool cannot express is refused with a reason, and each refusal has a test (a target without the capability refuses a secret in a param)
- [x] The declared capabilities, category and resource types claim only what a test proves
- [x] `docs/targets/<name>.md` says how each of the three targets hands a secret over
- [x] The capability matrix lists the new column for every target

## Needs a second reviewer

- [ ] Builds or escapes a shell command string
- [x] Handles a secret or a sensitive output
- [ ] Changes what is written to the run-state
- [x] Changes the plugin protocol

author: wrkode
body:
Supersedes #117, which bumped Hadron alone to v0.6.5 and left
`KAIROS_INIT_IMAGE` on kairos-init v0.14.6. Pinning the two images
independently turned out to be wrong in both directions.

## kairos-init v0.14.6 is on a dead version line

`kairos-io/kairos-init` is **archived** (last push 2026-08-19; final release
v0.17.3). kairos-init now ships from the **kairos monorepo** and shares the
Kairos release version, so the live line is **v4.x** (module path
`github.com/kairos-io/kairos/v4/kairos-init/...`). Renovate had both
`renovate/kairos-init-image` (-> v0.17.3) and
`renovate/major-kairos-init-image` (-> v4) queued; the v0.17.3 one is the end
of a dead line, and the "major" one is the real upstream.

## Hadron v0.6.5 is not the base Kairos builds on

Kairos resolves its base from the published composite tags
`quay.io/kairos/hadron:<hadron>-core-amd64-generic-<kairos-tag>`, per
`.github/public-cloud/resolve-hadron-container-image.sh` in kairos-io/kairos.
Querying those tags:

| Kairos release | Hadron base |
|---|---|
| v4.5.2 (latest) | **v0.6.3** |
| v4.5.0 | v0.6.3 |
| v4.4.0 | v0.6.3 |

**No Kairos release has ever been built on Hadron v0.6.4 or v0.6.5** (zero
composite tags for either). Hadron now auto-releases twice a week
(kairos-io/hadron#832), so its newest tag runs chronically ahead of the
version Kairos validates. "Newest Hadron" is therefore the wrong target for
this pin, and Renovate will keep proposing it.

## This PR

Takes the pair upstream actually ships and tests:

```
KAIROS_BASE_IMAGE  ghcr.io/kairos-io/hadron:v0.6.3@sha256:a5a47225...
KAIROS_INIT_IMAGE  quay.io/kairos/kairos-init:v4.5.2@sha256:7de7999e...
```

Both Dockerfile ARGs and both Makefile mirrors, digest-pinned to the
multi-arch index (kairos#4203). `make verify-pins` passes.

The `KAIROS_INIT_IMAGE` comment is rewritten because it had become
misleading: it warned about "older pins (e.g. v0.6.0)" in kairos-init's old
0.x numbering, which now reads as a Hadron v0.6.x version.

## Verification

Container e2e cannot boot the result, so the compatibility risk was checked
directly rather than assumed.

**CLI compatibility** of kairos-init v4.5.2 with the final stage's
invocation, read from the v4.5.2 source: entrypoint is still
`/kairos-init`, and `--level/-l`, `--stage/-s` (`init|install|all`),
`--model/-m` (`generic` is in `SupportedModels`), `--trusted/-t` (still
defined, in `addSharedFlags`) and `--version` all still exist. Note
`--version` is now a required flag; we already pass it.

**The initramfs regenerates**, which is the failure this pin exists to
guard against. Running the final stage's exact two-phase invocation
(`-s install` then `-s init`, `-m generic -t false`) on hadron v0.6.3 with
kairos-init v4.5.2 completes with **no error or warning** and rewrites
`/boot/initrd` (57 MB, build timestamp) via `dracut -f`. The result reports:

```
KAIROS_INIT_VERSION="v4.5.2"
KAIROS_FLAVOR_RELEASE="v0.6.3"
KAIROS_VERSION="v0.0.0-dev+pairtest"   # from --version
```

The same test against the pins currently on main (hadron v0.4.0 +
kairos-init v0.14.6) behaves identically, so this is a like-for-like
comparison rather than a one-sided check.

**Not verified: an actual boot.** A VM boot test remains the open gap for
any base-OS change, and CI's container-based e2e does not close it.

author: deviantintegral
body:
A Proxmox VM is a full clone of the base template, and a clone inherits the template's cores and memory. The template is sized once, by whichever create first built the base, so every later create or reset got that first VM's size regardless of what it asked for, with no error.

The clone's post-clone config write now carries cores and memory as well, on both the create and reset paths. An unset or unparseable size is left out so the template's value stands rather than sending PVE a zero.

## Summary

**The cap bug.** Settings > Advanced had one field, "Model route daily cap", hard-wired to the OpenRouter route's setting (`model:spend_cap_usd:openrouter`). The gateway reads `model:spend_cap_usd:<route>` per route, and the Anthropic API-key route (`anthropic`, the route of an agent bound to a key account) fell back to the $100 default. Raising the field to $500 left agents on a key account stopped at "402 ... $100.00". There is now one cap field per gateway route, OpenRouter and the Anthropic API key route, each with its own label, description and search entry (`model:spend_cap_usd:anthropic` is a search keyword too).

**The Saved note.** A row that names its setting (`SettingRow` `settingKey`) shows "Saved" on its label line once the write has succeeded, which fades over the app's confirmation linger (`--duration-linger`, the same timing as the "copied" note) and, under reduced motion, holds and then goes. A failed write shows "Not saved: the setting could not be written" under the control (the `Field` error slot, which also marks the control invalid) until the next write.

- `set` (settings-controls.tsx) reports each write's result to `settings-saved.ts`.
- A number field commits after its own debounce, so the flag shows once after the write, not per keystroke. A burst of writes to one setting keeps the flag up and fades it once after the last.
- `Field` gains an `adornment` slot, shown on the label's line outside the `<label>`, so the control's accessible name stays its label. The flag's live region (`role="status"`, polite) is present and empty at rest and speaks when "Saved" appears.
- The row does not change height while the note shows (see the macOS check below): the note's wrapper takes the flag's font size and one em of line height.
- Every Advanced row names its setting. The other sections take one `settingKey` prop per row; they are not in this PR (about 90 rows over 17 files).

## Tests

- `settings-saved-flag.test.tsx`: nothing at rest; "Saved" only after the write resolves; gone after the linger; a burst fades once after the last; a failure shows and stays (it does not fade) until the next write clears it; a throw before the request is treated the same; a row naming no setting has no flag; the label stays the control's name.
- `settings-saved-row.layout.test.ts` (real browser): the label row is the same height at rest and while the note shows. It failed on the first version of the fix (15 px against 14 px) and passes now.
- The Advanced section's pinned snapshots are regenerated (the two cap rows, the label row and the empty status region on each keyed row), and the writes snapshot now records `set model:spend_cap_usd:anthropic 500`.

Her first pass on 3ecc273190 found the row growing 2.5 px while the note showed; fixed in c07e2db378 and re-checked: the row height is the same in every frame, at 1161 px and 500 px, dark and Latte, for the cap field and the toggle.
- **Linux** (Maricon): all items pass on c07e2db378, including row height at rest equal to row height while "Saved" shows, the narrow 500 px layout, reduced motion, and the same contrast figures.

body:
## Objective
Add wet races: less grip, longer braking, wheelspin under power, visible rain, and a 1.5× prize. Second PR of the stack.

## Why
Every race played the same. Rain adds variety and a risk–reward choice without new tracks, and it reuses the drivetrain from the previous PR (spinning wheels hold the RPM up).

## How
- `src/domain/weather.ts` and `WEATHER_PROFILES`: the weather scales each car's `DriveSpec` (grip ×0.82, brakes ×0.7, slide recovery ×0.7, traction limit at 36 % of grip). The AI plans corners and braking from the same spec, so it adapts with no special case, and it feathers the throttle at the traction limit.
- Past the traction limit the wheels spin: less push, less lateral grip, a small deterministic fishtail.
- Forecast rolled from the race seed (30 % rain). Coached races stay dry. Shown on the pre-race and boss screens.
- Wet races pay 1.5×, for events and bosses; the result screen shows the rain bonus.
- Visuals: rain, puddles, wet road, spray, wheelspin smoke, a "PLUIE" HUD tag.
- Dry races stay bit-identical to `main` (balance output identical).

author: heeyuncho
body:
Fixes #215

## Summary

**Which stream fails first:** stdout, the MCP channel. I traced every `error` event that `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` emitted, without adding listeners, using a scratch `--import` preload in a server whose client closed its pipes before the server started. That is the case of the short-lived servers in #212, which fail about 0.3 s after `role`. The sequence was:

1. The startup `console.error` ("bridge listening …") fails on stderr. The global console's own `once('error', noop)` swallows that failure.
2. The `initialize` answer fails on stdout with `EPIPE`. stdout has no listener, so this is the **first `uncaught-exception`**.
3. The handler's `console.error` fails on stderr again, this time with no listener. Each failure is a new uncaught exception: `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` can't be destroyed (Node "undestroys" them), so every write emits a fresh `error`.

The loop kept the event loop busy enough that the peer's normal close never finished, so `drain-timeout` ended the process, as seen in the field.

```diff
 process.on("uncaughtException")
-  console.error(...)              # throws EPIPE again → loop
+  toStderr(...)                   # skipped once stderr failed; never throws
   diagnostics.crash(...)          # EPIPE logged once per process
+process.stderr.on("error")  → stderrOpen = false
+process.stdout.on("error")
+  EPIPE | ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED → endSession("stdout-closed")
+  other                        → crash line, as before
-process.stdin.on("close", async () => { exitReason = "stdin-closed"; … })
+process.stdin.on("close") → endSession("stdin-closed")
+endSession(reason)               # the old stdin-closed body, run once, whichever comes first
```

Docs: the README's server.log events list `stdout-closed` and `drain-timeout` as `exit` reasons and say that EPIPE is logged once. `docs/testing.md` describes the new tests.

## Evidence

New system test, `test/system/serverLog.test.ts` "#215: a client that closed stdout and stderr …":

```text
spawn dist/index.js (temporary TEAMS_MCP_HOME, port 0), destroy our ends of stdout/stderr, send initialize
wait for an exit or uncaught-exception line, then end stdin
expect ≤ 1 EPIPE line, a last line "exit … role=hub reason=stdout-closed code=0", and exit − start < 5 s (the drain bound)
```

- **Before** (origin/main, built): `AssertionError: expected 3065 to be less than or equal to 1` (Node 24), and `expected 4698 …` (Node 20.20.2).
  **After:** passes on both.
- Unit test, `test/unit/serverLog.test.ts` "#215: logs a broken pipe (EPIPE) once per process …": 51 EPIPE crashes and 2 TypeErrors give 1 EPIPE line and 2 TypeError lines. Before the fix it gave 51 EPIPE lines.
- Field-like scratch probe: a **peer** whose client closed its pipes before the server started. Before: 1,789 EPIPE lines, then `exit reason=drain-timeout` after about 7 s. After: 0 EPIPE lines, then `exit role=peer reason=stdout-closed code=0` 73 ms after `role`.

Local runs (load average 275–925, with another agent's tests running):

- Type-checks `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit`: both exit 0.
- `npm test` (Node 24.14.0): 964 passed, 8 skipped, **1 failed**: `test/unit/byteCache.test.ts` "3.4: after 100 large transcripts …" hit the 5 s test timeout. Run alone it passes, 4/4.
- Node 20.20.2, `vitest run --fileParallelism=false test/unit test/system/serverLog.test.ts`: 336 passed, 3 skipped, **1 failed**: the same byteCache test hit its timeout. Run alone at load ~900 it timed out twice at the default 5 s. With `--testTimeout=60000` it passes 4/4, so its assertions hold. The test is CPU-bound and doesn't touch this PR's code. It is one of the timing tests the handoff notes say fail under load. I couldn't confirm it at the default timeout on Node 20 locally, so CI's run is the check for it.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A plain revert undoes it. No data or config changes.

**Blast Radius:** shutdown

Every `serve` process now ends its session when stdout fails with EPIPE or ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED, even if stdin is still open. Before, it stayed up, unable to answer. A hub that ends this way still drains other sessions' calls first, as on `stdin-closed`. Other stdout errors are logged as before and don't end the session. `setup`, `reload-extension` and `token` are unchanged.

Out of scope, as the issue says: which client starts these short-lived servers, and the hand-over resets in #212.

body:
# Motivation

An empty `Move <symbol> to` step should explain what the list shows and how to return to the receive choices. When a populated list becomes empty, the message should also identify the change the user just saw.

# Changes

- Reuse OISY’s shared EmptyState in the Move step for Swap and Get Token.
- Show “The network list changed” after the current Move step has shown destinations for the same pay token and group. The description says the swap no longer shows other networks for that ticker and points back to receive choices.
- Show “No other networks listed for USDC” for an initially empty Move list when USDC is the group ticker. Use “No networks listed” when the ticker is unavailable.
- Keep one Back button and an always-mounted live status region. Focus moves to Back when the focused network row disappears.

Stacked on #14676.

# Tests

- Changed-file Prettier and ESLint with zero warnings, plus `npm run check` and `npm run check:tests` on Node 24.15.0.
- 60 tests across the two affected component specs, one file per invocation with `--maxWorkers=2`. Covers the initial and live-empty messages, ckUSDC → USDC in both modal flows, reset on reentry or pay token/group change, and focus recovery.
- In the loopback mock with bundled headless Chromium, emptied a populated list while a row had focus and pressed Enter on Back to return to receive choices. Checked wrapping and Back at 320 × 568 in both themes.

body: A Fusion Base Feature whose body a later feature changes (an offset face, a fillet, a deleted face) is no longer refused when cadmpeg keeps the base feature's own body as a history body. author: thedotmack
body:
Rehost of #6254 by @Afloat16, whose commit is cherry-picked unchanged (`git cherry-pick -x`), so they stay its author on main. #6254's branch doesn't allow maintainer edits, and main needed a one-line follow-up before this could land.

What it does (from #6254): the hook spool drain reads, removes, claims, expires and quarantines files with `fs/promises`, so draining a metadata backlog no longer holds the worker's event loop. Hooks, the viewer and `/health` keep answering. `HookSpool.entries()` becomes async; it has no production callers.

What we added: main gained a test in `tests/worker/remote-hook-spool.test.ts` (summary dedupe across a database reopen) that reads `spool.entries()` without `await`. That one line now awaits it.

Verified: typecheck, and the 23 changed or related spool test files (178 pass, 0 fail), on current main.

Fixes #6247.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the worker’s durable metadata drain path and async `entries()` API, but behavior is intended to be equivalent and is heavily covered by spool tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors **hook spool** metadata draining so listing, reading, unlinking, renaming, expiring, and quarantining entries use **`fs/promises`** instead of blocking synchronous `fs`, so large backlog drains no longer freeze the worker’s event loop (hooks, viewer, **`/health`** stay responsive).

> **`HookSpool.entries()`** is now **`async`**; tests and helpers (`spooledEntries`) were updated to **`await`** it. A new **`hook-spool-responsiveness`** test asserts a health check is served while draining a 1024-entry backlog and that the loop yields during accepted removals.
> 
> Durable hand-off semantics (dedupe, consumed markers, expiry, quarantine) are unchanged; enqueue/hot paths still use sync checks where appropriate.

author: laugustyniak
body:
Fixes #886

Root cause: `get_extracted_facet_counts_by_jurisdiction` unnested text[] fields and counted elements, so a document repeating a value in one array was counted several times while the share denominator (`covered`) counts documents, giving shares above 100%.

Fix: new migration `20261117000001_facet_counts_distinct_documents.sql` counts `COUNT(DISTINCT id)` per (jurisdiction, value). Signature, return type, security and grants unchanged. Backend (`share = count / covered`) and the schema-tally path (already dedupes tokens per document) need no change.

**The migration must be applied to prod after merge.**

Verification: new DB-contract test `test_array_field_counts_documents_not_elements` fails without the migration (4 vs 2) and passes with it; all 7 tests in test_compare_rpcs_contract.py pass on pgvector/pg17.

body:
## Issue

Closes #115

## Rule IDs and covering cases

| Rule ID | Conformance cases |
|---|---|
| CS-2.7 | Runner tests (the issue puts the case files that use load options out of scope): `case_file::tests::cs_2_7_reads_a_case_without_load_options`, `cs_2_7_reads_the_load_options_of_a_case`, `cs_2_7_reads_every_load_option`, `cs_2_7_rejects_an_unknown_load_option`, `cs_2_7_rejects_an_unknown_ossie_format`; `load_options::tests::cs_2_7_an_omitted_load_options_member_gives_every_default`, `cs_2_7_an_omitted_option_takes_its_default`, `cs_2_7_every_option_the_case_sets_is_kept`; `runner::tests::cs_2_7_the_load_options_of_a_case_reach_the_load_call` (acceptance criterion: `load_options: {ossie_format: development}`), `cs_2_7_a_case_without_load_options_is_loaded_with_the_defaults` |

## What changed

- `case.rs`: new optional `Case::load_options` member of type `CaseLoadOptions`, with the four members of CS-2.7 (`ossie_format`, `model_name`, `namespace`, `grant_authenticated_to_all`), each optional. `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` makes an unknown member a case-format error (`RunnerErrorKind::Malformed`, CS-1), like every other unknown case field. `ossie_format` reuses the public contract enum `OssieFormat`, so a value other than `release` or `development` is also a case-format error.
- `load_options.rs` (new): `resolve_load_options` turns the case's options into the public contract type `LoadOptions`, giving each omitted option the default of architecture section 3.5 (`release`, `false`, `semantic_compiler`, no model name).
- `runner.rs`: `prepare_case` now returns the resolved `LoadOptions` of the case. `load` (#45) does not exist yet, so the case stays pending; when #45 lands, these options are what the runner passes to it.
- Separate refactor commit: `ossie/prepare.rs` uses the shared `DEFAULT_NAMESPACE` constant instead of its own copy, so the default lives in one place. No behavior change.

### Internal choices

- The parsed case keeps the options as written (`Option` per member) and resolution to defaults happens in a separate function, so data types stay apart from logic and a later reader can still tell an explicit default from an omitted one.
- `data_source` (a load option of section 3.5 not listed in CS-2.7) is rejected as an unknown member, as the issue requires.
- The acceptance test of the runner prepares a case against the existing `conformance/models/sample` fixture rather than adding a new fixture.

## Out of scope, confirmed untouched

- No conformance case file uses `load_options` (left to #30 and #31, as the issue says).
- No call to `load`: it belongs to #45.
- No change to the specification, the core or any compiler stage.

## Checklist

- [x] Only files in the issue's scope are changed
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo deny check`, `just conformance`, `python3 scripts/build_index.py --check`, `python3 scripts/check_examples.py` pass
- [x] No behavior beyond the specification; deviations raised as issues
- [x] No check weakened
- [x] Everything in English

author: joshgreenlion07
body:
From the owner's screen recording (Chrome on Mac): 37 one-frame black flashes, textures arriving 2–26 s late, 14–22 fps, freezes up to 0.65 s. Three branches merged (no-flicker, gpu-budget, fast-load) on top of main with the soil fills.

**Motion (GPU)** — adaptive render scale while moving (canvas never resized; eases back to full when still), depth of field off while moving, water mirror only when water is in view and cropped, earlier plant LODs and lighter far copies, wind skipped where sub-pixel, turf tiles culled, night lights free in daylight, NaN guard. Paired GPU timing vs main on a big yard: moving 0.44–0.45x, still 0.66–0.78x.

**Loading** — yard built in ~8 ms slices (main thread blocked 15 ms instead of 2.4 s; rebuild 10 ms instead of 4.3 s), construction built lazily, textures applied as soon as ready with newest-first queue, 512 px quick copies, stale previews dropped, sliced uploads; a new color shows in under 1 s instead of ~18 s; quality change no longer blocks.

**Flicker** — opaque WebGL context, one stable label layer (no per-label compositing layers toggling over the canvas), stepped near plane (≈5x fewer depth-range changes), labels kept off the toolbar and screen edges, Diagnostics lines for frames not drawn while moving and GPU frames over 33 ms (one shared GPU timer).

Not verifiable here: the black frames on the owner's Mac (never reproduced locally) and a real `vite build` (checked by Vercel).

body:
M9's exit (#207) met every task but M9-03, and left M10 undrafted. This drafts M10, *Usability and warm-up*, in M8's and M9's format: six tasks, each with where it comes from (PR numbers), a precise **Done when**, and the milestone's **Exit** line. Docs only; nothing ticked.

## The tasks

- **M10-01 · The native launcher as GraalVM's standalones ship it** *(early)*: GraalVM's thin C++ launcher (`launcher.cc`) in front of the image built as a shared library with `-H:-ParseRuntimeOptions`, the maintainer's choice among #206's alternatives. Marked in progress on branch `M10-01-thin-launcher` (another agent; no PR yet).
- **M10-02 · Interpreter warm-up and host compilation**: carried from M9-03. Directions: an AOT cache trained on the interpreter (JEP 515's method profiles; `bazel-bin/scheme` already has a cache trained on a small program, the benchmarks' runtime none), a smaller `continueAt` (`@InliningCutoff`, fewer quickened variants), `boolean` boxing elimination, `storeBytecodeIndexInFrame`'s cost, and tail call handlers natively (#205's follow-ups). Done when the interpreter's geomean improves by 10% over M9's report (42.89 → 38.6, without the native column) or each direction is measured and recorded.
- **M10-03 · `apply`'s cost after #195**: #207's A/B (`scheme` later iterations 1.03-1.09×).
- **M10-04 · Options the launcher drops** *(early)*: #205's `TraceTransferToInterpreter` and `InstrumentBoundaries` findings; every option class through both launchers.
- **M10-05 · I/O follow-ups** *(early)*: bulk read in `SPort` and input file ports closed at context close (#200), G1's GC lines in `bench-report` (#197). #208 (merged, `SPort`'s virtual calls) covers none of them; the bulk read follows its shape.
- **M10-06 · Recompilation after splitting**: #205's split deopts in `scheme`, and `deriv-interpreter`'s unexplained 0.81× from #184 (#207).

## Checks

- `bazel test --test_tag_filters=lint //...`: 32 pass. `//tests:conformance_status`: passes (the status block is unchanged).
- docs/usage.md unchanged. No conformance section changed state.

## Follow-ups

None.

## Surprises

The M9 exit note's `--vm.` follow-up from #197 ("the JVM launcher could warn about, or apply, `--vm.` options") was already done by #203, so it isn't carried.

author: dannybud19
body:
## What this adds
A neural season encoder (masked-feature pretraining, then contrastive training on same-player season pairs) behind the Phase 2 interface, a fixed 54-run search, the Phase 3 report, the sanity marks for its comps, and a read-only walkthrough notebook. `score_sanity.py` now takes `--report PATH`.

## Gate (validation; chosen setting: embedding size 32, temperature 0.05, pretraining; mean over 3 seeds)
- PASS: beats B2 on non-adjacent hit@10 (0.746 vs 0.668)
- FAIL: beats B2 on next-season RMSE (0.620 vs 0.608)
- FAIL: beats persistence on next-season RMSE (0.620 vs 0.610)
- PASS: stability check (consecutive-to-random distance 0.165 vs B2 0.243)
- PASS: position probe well above chance (0.656)
- REPORTED: sanity comps, encoder 8 pass / 6 partial / 1 fail, mean 1.80 vs B2 6 / 8 / 1, mean 1.70

## Findings
- The encoder wins on identity retrieval (36 of 54 runs beat B2) and loses on next-season forecasting (no run below 0.617). Both are recorded; the metric is unchanged.
- Era is now readable from the embedding (0.323 vs 0.190 for B2, chance 0.20), which is the problem Phase 4 targets.
- Sanity comps are slightly better (mean 1.80 vs 1.70). Known pairs are unchanged: Nash and Paul still fail.
- Validation also chose the setting, so encoder numbers are optimistic. The 27 encoder-only comp names were marked by Claude from researched consensus at Danny's request, so the sanity comparison is less independent than Phase 2's.

author: marknolan
body:
DEV-1496. Shimmer3 and Shimmer3R fit the same CAT24C16 EEPROM, but each firmware carried its own copy of the chip driver in `Shimmer_Driver/CAT24C16/`. The copies had drifted:
- Shimmer3 waited out the 5 ms write cycle before each page; Shimmer3R waited after each page.
- Only Shimmer3 filled a failed read with `0xFF`, which `ShimBrd_resetDaughterCardId()` already assumes.

The DEV-1494/DEV-1495 self-test restore had to be written, tested and reviewed twice: ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#330 and ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#144. This PR puts one driver here, and both firmwares switch to it:
- ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#145
- ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#331

## The driver: `EEPROM/cat24c16.{h,c}`
It reaches the bus only through the callbacks in `cat24c16dev_ctx_t`: `write`, `read`, `mdelay` and a `handle`. This is Shimmer3R's interface. Each firmware fills the callbacks in from its own I2C HAL in `hal_CAT24C16.c`, which also keeps power and bus bring-up. Shimmer3R keeps its second context, for the factory rig on I2C4.

What changes against either old copy:
- **Write cycle.** A write waits 5 ms (tWR max, CAT24C16 datasheet, A.C. Characteristics) after every page, a failed page included. So `CAT24C16_write()` returns with the part idle, and a read, another write or a power-off can follow at once. The part acknowledges nothing during a cycle (Acknowledge Polling). The extra waits ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#330 and ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#144 each added to their restore are therefore no longer needed. The number of waits per write is unchanged.
- **Failed reads.** A failed read fills the buffer with `0xFF` on both platforms. That is new on Shimmer3R.
- **Bounds check.** It no longer computes `address + length`. That sum wraps in the MSP430's 16-bit `unsigned int` for an address near 65535, and such an address then passed the check.
- **Bus callbacks.** Both now take the 7-bit device address. The driver works out the block bits and the word address, so the two platforms' callbacks are the same shape. Before, Shimmer3R's write took a shifted address and its read took a memory address.
- **Test pattern.** The self-test writes Shimmer3's incrementing pattern on both, offset by the pass number so every byte differs from the previous pass's. On Shimmer3R this replaces ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#330's `rand()` and the `sys_tick` callback that seeded it.
- **Restore.** As in ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#330 and ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#144, every exit after the first write puts the region back, with up to 3 tries, and ORs in `EEPROM_TEST_FAIL_NOT_RESTORED` when it can't.
- **Report text.** `CAT24C16_testFailReason()` and `CAT24C16_testLeftTestData()` give both factory reports the same reason text. The strings are `SELF_TEST_STR_EEPROM_*` in `Test/shimmer_test.h`. Each firmware keeps its own line format.

Includes of `CAT24C16/CAT24C16.h` in `Boards/`, `EEPROM/` and `Comms/` now name `EEPROM/cat24c16.h`.

## Tests
`Test/host/test_cat24c16.c`, a new standalone suite, runs the driver against a fake part:
- 16-byte pages that wrap rather than cross, block bits in the I2C address, and an address counter that runs on across blocks;
- a 5 ms write cycle that starts at the STOP and NACKs every transfer until it ends;
- time that moves only through `mdelay()`, so a missing wait shows up as a NACK, never as a flaky test.

It covers:
- page and block splitting;
- that every write returns with the part idle, a failed page's included;
- the bounds, including the 16-bit wrap case;
- a failed read reading as `0xFF`;
- DEV-1494/DEV-1495's 11 self-test fault cases, plus a second context;
- the report text for every result code.

The suite fails when the driver is broken on purpose (copies built only to check the test, not committed):

| Broken copy | Failed checks |
|---|---|
| No wait after pages | 47 |
| No wait after a failed page | 5 |
| No restore | 14 |
| No `0xFF` fill | 1 |
| The same pattern every pass | 2 |
| Block bits dropped from the address | 5 |

`make -C Test/host` passes: 37 suites, the Python checks, and `platform-check` with `EEPROM/cat24c16.c` added for both MCUs. Run on Windows, three cross-check scripts couldn't start the test binaries from the Makefile's `out/` paths. They pass when given `out\…` paths, and on Linux CI the Makefile's paths work. The old `stubs/Shimmer_Driver/CAT24C16/CAT24C16.h` is gone, since the real header is now here.

The firmware builds are on the firmware PRs:
- Shimmer3: CCS 12.8.1, Release and Debug.
- Shimmer3R: STM32CubeIDE 1.15.1, Release.

**Not benched.**

## Docs
- `SHIMMER3_EEPROM_MEMORY_MAP.md`:
  - new §1.1 on the driver: the callbacks, the waits, the `0xFF` fill and the bounds check, and how the two old copies differed;
  - the source table and §2.1 name the new location.
- `SHIMMER3R_FACTORY_TEST_REPORT.md` §5.7: the incrementing pattern, and that Shimmer3 runs the same code.
- `SHIMMER3_TEST_PROCEDURE.md`: `test_cat24c16` in §2.2, and DEV-1494/DEV-1495 in the §7 regression cases.
- The protocol doc, the architecture overview and the stubs README name `EEPROM/cat24c16.h`.

## Merge order
This PR is stacked on #242 (the DEV-1494/DEV-1495 docs), whose text it updates. Both firmware PRs point their submodules at this branch's commit.
1. ShimmerResearch/shimmer3r-firmware#330, ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#144 and #242.
2. This PR.
3. Re-point each firmware PR's submodule at the merge commit on `main`.
4. Merge the firmware PRs.

A firmware that moves its submodule past this PR without its own PR won't build. Its own `CAT24C16.h` would meet this one: the enum and the functions would be declared twice, with different signatures. So the firmware PRs should follow promptly.

Host APIs: nothing owed. The wire format and the EEPROM map are unchanged.

## Review fixes

- Make OEM reads and propagation honor each segment's usable time interval, including boundaries between samples, gaps, and shared endpoints. Reject overlapping usable intervals and changes of reference frame or central body that would give an ambiguous state.
- Write reverse-propagated samples in chronological order. When a mission traverses the same times twice, keep the first pass under the requested filename and write the return pass to a numbered sibling such as `orbit.arc-2.oem`. GMAT reports the new filename and skips existing siblings.
- Use precise sample times and velocities for sparse Cartesian interpolation when the available samples support it. The two-sample linear fallback is preserved.
- Protect folder-run comparison baselines when a report points to the same file, including redirects during a mission. Clear stale satellite import settings when a different file is selected.
- Add regression coverage for the review findings and update the folder-run fixture to exercise a real initialization failure and recovery.

author: roodboi
body:
HACK-2324, gap G2 (the interim the lead approved). On native, a Compose service that declares `restart: unless-stopped` (or `always` or `on-failure`) and receives private values refused startup with `graph_restart_policy`: "Services with managed environment delivery cannot yet use an automatic restart policy". Private values are managed env and privately resolved interpolation (shell values).

Global managed values reach every service, so real projects hit this on most app services.

## Why it refused

Private delivery is staged once per container through a lease that cannot be renewed (`packages/runtime-core/src/provider/graph/environment.rs`), and values are never kept at rest in the container. An engine-driven restart would bring the container back without them.

## Change

- **Runtime** (`provider/graph/restart_policy.rs`, `admit`): for a service with managed delivery, return no engine policy instead of refusing. The container runs with `RestartPolicy: no`, and the receipt records no restart authority.
  - Still refused: host dependencies, unrouted native HTTP probes and dependency-cache initializers.
  - When a service has both managed delivery and host dependencies, the host-dependency refusal still applies.
- **`up`:** names each active, privately delivered service with an automatic policy, and what is lost:

  > Service web: restart: unless-stopped is not applied, because the service receives private values that native delivers once per container start. If it crashes it stays stopped until you run hack restart, which restarts the whole project with a fresh delivery.

  The set mirrors the runtime's managed set: services with non-empty managed values or privately resolved shell values. Native `hack restart` does not take service names, so the advice names the whole-project restart.
- **File-only recipients keep their policy.** A service that receives only a private file (such as the gcloud ADC snapshot from #896) keeps its entrypoint and its staged read-only file for the container's lifetime, so an engine restart still works. The runtime keeps its policy and the notice does not name it.
- **Preflight:** the same line, as the warning `restart_policy_not_applied` per service.
- **Docs:** `docs/guides/native-candidate.md`, restart policies.
- **Not done here (follow-up):** Hack's graph owner restarting such a service with a fresh delivery. Values stay single-use and never at rest.

**Reviewer:** the persistent Codex reviewer, two rounds (file-only parity, empty maps), ended **VERDICT CLEAN at `24370163ee`**.

## Validation (Linux)

- **Rust:**
  - `restart_policy.rs` unit tests: managed delivery gives no policy; host dependencies still refuse, including with managed delivery.
  - graph tests: `prepare_delivery` gives `RestartPolicy {"Name":"no"}` and no `restart_policy` on the resource; the start review's `start_refusals` are empty.
  - `installed_candidate_contract`: the managed-service context round-trip now produces no refusal.
  - The restart tests (37 + 3) and the installed-candidate test pass. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass (Rust 1.97.1).
- **TypeScript:**
  - notice unit tests: only active services with managed or shell values and an automatic policy are named; a `no` policy, inactive services, empty maps, file-only recipients and bad names are not.
  - start: web (managed value, `unless-stopped`) is named once, worker (no private values, `always`) is not, and no value is printed.
  - The restart notice, start, preflight CLI and start-refusal test files: 207 pass.
- **Other checks:** `tsc` and `docs:check` pass. Biome has no new warnings; the three remaining warnings are unchanged from `next`.

**Not verified:** a crash of such a service on the Mac VM (it should stay stopped, and `hack restart` should bring it back with a fresh delivery), and that a file-only recipient's staged file survives an engine restart (static trace only).

mrueg
body:
## Summary

`template/resources/kubeconform.sh` skipped `Gateway`, `HTTPRoute` and `DNSEndpoint`. These resources contain `${SECRET_DOMAIN}`, which Flux only substitutes at apply time. Without substitution they fail the schemas' hostname patterns, so they were never validated at all. A broken listener, hostname or protocol passed `mise run configure` and CI unnoticed.

The rendered output is now piped through `flux envsubst --strict` with `SECRET_DOMAIN=example.com` before it reaches kubeconform, and only `Secret` is still skipped.

- `flux envsubst` also handles the `${SECRET_DOMAIN/./-}` replacement form used in the templates.
- `--strict` fails on any other unset variable, which catches typos in variable names.
- `flux` is already a mise-managed tool (`flux2` in `.mise/config.toml`).

## Testing

- **Valid fixtures:** rendered all 8 `valid/` fixtures and ran the script. All pass, and between 3 and 5 Gateway, HTTPRoute and DNSEndpoint resources per fixture are now reported as valid instead of skipped.
- **Negative test:** set the `flux-webhook` HTTPRoute hostname to `Bad_Host!.${SECRET_DOMAIN}`. kubeconform now reports `HTTPRoute flux-webhook is invalid` and exits 1.
- **Lint:** `shellcheck` is clean.
