author: pabloprx
body:
## Problema

La app usa ~30-40 % de CPU de forma continua, incluso con la ventana oculta.

`RootView` guarda `MeterModel` y `NowPlaying` con `@StateObject`. `@StateObject` se suscribe a `objectWillChange`. `MeterModel` publica ~16 propiedades 30 veces por segundo. Resultado: SwiftUI recalcula la ventana completa (faceplate, los 16 faders) en cada tick.

En un `sample` del proceso aparecían `RootView.faceplate`, `RootView.faderWell` y `Fader.body` en cada tick.

## Cambio

`RootView` no lee ningún valor de esos modelos: sólo los pasa a las vistas hijas (`VUMeterView`, `DisplayPanel`, `BandLEDs`, `PlayerBar`), que ya los observan con `@ObservedObject`. Ahora `RootView` los guarda en un contenedor `ObservableObject` que nunca publica. Las vistas hijas se siguen actualizando igual.

## Medición

macOS 27, M4 Max. `top` de la app, 5 lecturas tras 10 s de arranque, mismo estado:

| | CPU |
|---|---|
| `main` (6c1f869) | 28,5 % |
| este PR | 16,5 % |

Tras el cambio, `RootView`/`faceplate`/`faderWell` desaparecen del `sample` y el trabajo de AttributeGraph baja a la mitad.

No medido: con audio pasando por el tap (el build local sin firmar no tenía permiso de captura, `callbacks=0`).

## Siguiente candidato (no incluido)

Lo que queda es sobre todo `NowPlaying` en el hilo principal: `audioProcesses()` (dos consultas a coreaudiod por proceso) corre en cada línea del puente (1/s) y en el timer de 2 s cuando el audio sale de una app que no es reproductor (p. ej. un navegador). `pollScripts()` lanza AppleScript a Spotify cada 2 s.

body:
## O que muda

O **Corporativo** passa a ser a soma da DRE de todos os negócios (pedido do cliente: "traga os dados de todos os negócios e consolide o resultado no Corporativo").

- **Projeção:** nova primeira opção do seletor, *Corporativo — todos os negócios* (só para quem enxerga todos, `Auth::veTudo`). É **só leitura** e diz quantos negócios já lançaram proposta.
- **Painel:** a linha do Corporativo, que era "—", mostra a mesma soma (ROL e resultado líquido, projeção e proposta). Ela **sai das somas do cartão**, que já é a soma dos negócios, para não dobrar.
- **Dossiê:** o contexto Corporativo imprime a Projeção consolidada como página, em vez de se declarar ausente.
- É **conta derivada, não carga**: soma o `montar()` de cada negócio, então nunca discorda das telas dos negócios e não cria uma segunda cópia do número.

## Testes

- Bateria completa: 1320 provas, nenhuma vermelha.
- `provasProjecaoCorporativo` refaz a soma conta a conta a partir de cada negócio e ancora a ROL realizada jan–out (R$ 2.885.752.746) num valor somado mês a mês no Qlik.
- Duas provas antigas do Painel afirmavam o contrário do pedido e foram reescritas.
- Contra versões quebradas (omite um negócio; conta o Corporativo no cartão): 8 falhas, como deviam.
- Não coberto: perfil que não enxerga todos os negócios (a bateria não tem usuário restrito).

author: charliermarsh
body:
## Summary

Compiling a bytearray as executable Python source can fail before execution reaches the `compile()` call intended to catch its `MemoryError`. Link bounded checked `exec` and `eval` bodies ahead of time while preserving decoding, mode checks, and source complexity limits. Unlinked runtime `eval` remains unsupported.

For an explicitly interposed scoped-call ABI, preserve the positional entry route only for a currently linked source function called from a module frame or an exact native string method. Evaluate and root the callable and arguments once, then consult the live function body after argument effects so rebinding, `__code__` replacement, bound methods, and descriptors retain Python behavior.

Stop fallback checking after a uniquely selected source call proven not to return: `take(indirect(), True)` cannot reach its second argument when `indirect()` only calls a function that raises, while `take(True, indirect())` still rejects its first argument. Preserve the selected entry filename in fallback diagnostics and grow the checker stack before recursive expression lowering. Keep a suspended disabled loop's checked else body in its original frame, derive its normal edge from physical control flow, and stop emitting later source statements once that edge closes.

Keep tracked Python tests and fixtures at their canonical LF bytes on Windows. Git autocrlf otherwise moves an unchanged fixture's raw `def probe` offset from 507 to 524 while the Python parser correctly normalizes it back to 507. The general checkout policy covers top-level and nested `tests/**/*.py`; a scratch autocrlf checkout preserved the untouched LF fixture and the separately marked CRLF decimal corpus byte for byte. Apply pinned formatting to the two newly merged hash-worker source arms.

The complete tests and benchmarks trees, original allocation injector, fixtures, SDK sources, and original inline test modules match current main. Full pinned formatting, the original compiler and Windows-failure controls on Linux, six Thread wait/hash/slot originals, and developer workspace Clippy passed locally; the developer Ohm run allowed its newer-toolchain deprecation warning while hosted CI uses pinned Rust. The exact published head passed hosted pinned workspace checks (1,024 compiler tests and 538 runtime tests) and the pristine unchanged 24-control allocation proof. Hosted Windows, ASan, ThinLTO, and remaining artifact checks are still in progress; keep this PR in draft.

author: andreas-lepak
body:
MOOSE differentiates the mortar dual basis with automatic differentiation, so it needs the coefficients of `FEGenericBase<Real>::compute_dual_shape_coeffs()` with a dual number type. It currently duplicates that code, including the transformed quadratic basis on `QUAD8`, `TRI6` and `TRI7` (idaholab/moose#34178). This moves the computation into the public template `compute_dual_shape_coefficients<T>()`, and the element-dependent part into `dual_shape_transformed_vertices()`. `compute_dual_shape_coeffs()` calls both with `Real`, so libMesh results are unchanged. The existing dual basis test now also checks that the free function reproduces the coefficients computed in `reinit()`.

author: rileybleeker
body:
Built headlessly by an OpenRouter builder (claude-haiku-5-5) in the Onyx SDLC (Riley approved 2026-11-17). Pre-merge checks: type check / py_compile passed in the builder pipeline. Codex reviews after merge; findings come back as backlog items.

## Builder summary
Committed `2d19c974` on `claude/or-plan-perf-hrv-pollen-read`. This helps repeat visits only. A first visit still makes the full server read, so the 1127 ms cold-path call may not be fixed.

**Where the time goes**
- **Supabase query:** already minimal. `POLLEN_COLUMNS` are all seven columns that `shapePollenRows` reads, `count_date` is the primary key so the date-range read is indexed, and the 1000-row limit is only a cap (at most ~730 rows). Option (a) has nothing to trim.
- **Server shaping:** trivial for ~730 rows.
- **Client:** the panel called `cachedJson` without `freshMs`, so every `/analytics/hrv` visit made a new GET `/api/pollen`. That is what the timing harness counted.

**Change**
- `frontend/src/components/PollenPanel.tsx`: `cachedJson(POLLEN_URL, { check, freshMs: 5 * 60_000 })`, the same opt-in pattern `/log` uses (commit `f5e9cfbd`). A copy fetched in the last 5 minutes is reused with no GET.
- `frontend/tests/pollen-a11y.test.cjs`: one source-level test for the constant and the call.
- Response shape, 730-day window, `no-store` header, and owner-only access are unchanged. No SQL, no budget or perf-report changes.

**Checks**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `frontend/`: passed, no output.
- Tests: not run. The task says not to run automated tests and AGENTS.md forbids it before merge, so `pollen.test.cjs` and `pollen-a11y.test.cjs` are unrun.
- Commit was made but not pushed; no PR opened.

**PR body (for when you open it)**

> Reuses a copy of GET /api/pollen fetched in the last 5 minutes on /analytics/hrv (`freshMs`), so a repeat visit makes no second request. The server query already reads only the seven shaped columns on the primary key, so no query change was made. Response shape, window, no-store and owner-only access are unchanged.
>
> Live timing has not been measured for this change. It must be confirmed by the next scheduled Production Performance Timing run on one serving revision. Cold (first) views still pay the server read; if that stays over 1000 ms, the next lever is server-side (Vercel region or a longer-cached response).

## Summary

The billing findings from the review (#783), one commit each:

- **77** The hourly subscription review leaves out a tenant whose other subscription on the same plan still keeps it there (by `SubscriptionPlan`'s rules: active, past due or on hold within the grace, cancelled but paid for, not refunded). A tenant that re-subscribed was read from Dodo every hour for its old, ended subscription.
- **78** A Dodo failure now means what it is, decided in one place (`ProviderFailure`):
  - A timeout is an `HttpRequestException` like any other failure to reach Dodo. `ProviderTimeoutHandler` replaces `HttpClient.Timeout`, whose `TaskCanceledException` nobody caught, so it was a 500. The handler also times the body read.
  - A refusal (4xx other than 401, 403, 408 and 429) is a 409 `BILLING_PROVIDER_REFUSED`, which a retry would not change. Everything else stays a 503.
  - A failed upgrade puts back the downgrade it dropped after a refusal. After a timeout or server error it reads the subscription first, and puts the downgrade back only if the subscription is still on its old product, so an upgrade that did go through is not undone.
- **79** A credit pack payment that did not succeed is done, not set aside, so a declined card no longer fires `BillingWebhooksSetAside` ("may have reached no tenant").
- **80** Putting an operator's plan on a tenant whose subscription is still billing is refused with 409 `PLAN_SUBSCRIPTION_BILLING`, which names the subscription. The request can set `keepSubscription` for a plan given on top on purpose. A change to an operator plan the tenant is already on is not asked about again. Billing.md's Business paragraph now says to cancel the subscription first.
- **81** `TenantPlanChangedEvent` carries `PreviousLimitOverrides`, so the downgrade email states the limits the tenant actually had (a 5,000-client contract, not the catalogue's 2,000).

## Follow-ups outside this repo

- **wbskt/Wbskt.Admin:** `AdminSetTenantPlanRequest` gains an optional `keepSubscription`. Until the admin page offers it, a staff plan over a billing subscription is refused and audited as `Refused` with the subscription named, which is the intended default.

## Deploy notes

- No schema change beyond the review procedure's query. The event field is optional, so an event written before reads the catalogue as before.

## Testing

- `dotnet build Wbskt.slnx`, `dotnet test Tests/Wbskt.Host.Tests` (3149 passed), and the auth dacpac build.
- New unit tests:
  - A refusal versus a 503, by status.
  - A timed-out upgrade puts the downgrade back only when the subscription did not move.
  - The timeout handler gives up on a hanging response and on a hanging body, and lets the caller's own cancellation through.
  - A declined pack is not set aside.
  - An operator plan over a billing subscription is refused unless `keepSubscription` is set, and only when the operator plan is first put on.
  - The downgrade email uses the old overrides.
- New SQL integration test `Review_leaves_out_an_ended_subscription_while_another_keeps_the_plan`. It needs SQL, so CI runs it; I didn't run it here.

Refs #783

Post-open review: I read the full diff again as a reviewer. Before opening I had found that the timeout handler did not cover the response body, which `HttpClient` reads after the handlers return; it now buffers the body inside its timer, with a test. On the open diff I checked: every `HttpRequestException` catch in billing (checkout, plan change, read-back, portal, duplicate refund, the reconcile workers), which now also sees timeouts, with the refund path keeping a timed-out refund unconfirmed as before; the review query's `NOT EXISTS` against `SubscriptionPlan.Decide` case by case; and that the operator-plan check never runs for billing's own plan writes or for staff limit and end-date changes. Nothing else found.

author: glyzer
body:
Closes #222
Package: review-followup-fixes
Risk: high — it changes merge, accept, gated-path and retry logic across the engine (the issue is rated high)
Tier: feature

Decisions made:
- Each item was checked on main first; the ones already fixed there are ticked below with the reason, and nothing was changed for them.
- `reviews.log` gets an 11th field, `<kept>` (the pre-existing items the brake kept), so `--kpi-review` stops counting them as demoted. This is an additive change to contracts §8: lines written before read as `0`, and the older readers ignore the extra field.
- The brake's release writes `brake-released` (the newest merged PR at the release); `brake_tick` engages again only once the window has moved past it.
- Holds: a low disk and `PACE=pause` now hold new work only. Resumes of started work go on, as `draining` does (#216 part 6.3).
- `PING_KINDS` accepts commas as well as spaces, as `config set` already did.
- `ready_unpark` lifts a needs-you with `ny_stage=ci` once CI is green. A red CI keeps the needs-you.
- `canccu-status` lists a unit in check whose PR conflicts with main while auto-merge is off. The line says who acts next: the worker, the merge by script, or a new head.
- `REVIEW.md`: fenced blocks, CRLF and `<!-- … -->` lines are handled in `review_md`. A git error other than "does not exist" is logged and the file is read as none.
- Checkpoints are read as open (`-L 500`) and closed (`-L 200`) lists, merged, so an old open checkpoint is never taken for gone (#226). The harness's default route now matches `-s *`.
- `tests/review-set/run`: without `--model`, it uses the project's review model (`review_model`). An engine that exits non-zero is `error`, and the run exits 2 with no log line, no baseline and no brake (#235).
- The release gate prints `missing: lib/<file> <name>` for a listed name the file lacks, and `release check --body` fails on it, so a rename cannot turn the gate off silently (#235). CI's tag fetch gets `|| true` for a repo with no tag yet.
- `canccu-up` with `LEADER=on` and no kit starts no leader: the pane stays `lead`, with a plain `claude` and a warning.
- `lib/canccu-merge.sh` went past 400 lines. Its merge-queue functions moved to `lib/canccu-mqueue.sh`; no exemption was added.
- New tests go in `tests/canccu-followups*.sh` and in each area's existing test file.

Checklist (#222):
- [x] postpass rename: already fixed on main: `--no-renames` is on both the `--name-only` and the `--numstat` diff.
- [x] C-quoted paths: `git -c core.quotePath=off` in `postpass_full`, `change_stats` and `changed_lines`.
- [x] stage after a fix-check pass: any pass clears it.
- [x] `passed_before`: already fixed on main: the newest `reviews.log` line for the PR and sha decides.
- [x] `merge_unpark`: keeps the accept's owner and writes no new ask line.
- [x] old `accept_sha`: cleared in `requeue`.
- [x] `accepted` removed before `merge_auto`: it is now removed after `merge_auto` returns 0.
- [x] a stray `accepted`: each holder is tried.
- [x] `ping_states`: no accept ping when any member has the label.
- [x] `ACCEPT_CHANNELS` without `label`: requests and pings offer only the channels that count.
- [x] 124/137: treated as transient (`MUT_RC`, `mut_transient`).
- [x] `merge_tries`: cleared on a requeue and on a new head.
- [x] "already enabled": an armed PR is read as merging.
- [x] transient `main_merge` error: retried up to `MERGE_TRIES`.
- [x] `ci_failed`: `REVIEW_CHECKS` are dropped.
- [x] `ci_rerun`: waits until the run's jobs have completed; confirmed for the leader's PR #207 case.
- [x] a named close refused for good: needs-you at once; only transient errors wait.
- [x] `needs_work_from_pr`: returns when `lead_of` is empty.
- [x] `canccu-stop`: removes the marker only after the label edit succeeds.
- [x] holds on resumes: see Decisions.
- [x] `nudge_reset`: cleared by `canccu-resume --usage`.
- [x] `- none` / `(none)` items: skipped. The retry reason names a missing block or count line.
- [x] a settled security finding: still blocks.
- [x] open items under a `full review` ask: kept `open`.
- [x] `findings_count`: case-insensitive.
- [x] `FIX_ATTEMPTS=0`: no extra round.
- [x] reviewer prompt: any wrong behaviour is `correctness`.
- [x] `leader_ack`: capped at the last id, and reset when the ids restart.
- [x] `idle` items: handed over.
- [x] `PING_KINDS`: commas.
- [x] same-second reload: the stamp includes sub-second time and the inode.
- [x] a broken layer: `config show` names the file.
- [x] `USAGE_MAX_AGE_MIN`: takes 0.
- [x] `running_areas`: live carried packages are included.
- [x] root areas: an empty area overlaps everything.
- [x] a rejected next-wave plan: the running wave's packages still start.
- [x] `wave_rolls`: no roll when there is nothing to plan.
- [x] `merged_left`: already handled on main: a named member still open is confirmed and closed by script after `MERGE_CLOSE_MIN`.
- [x] a fresh follow-up's test rule: a one-line rule is added, aligned with #209.
- [x] a health unit's follow-up: names the health pass and its limits.
- [x] worker trap: kills first; the EXIT trap removes the tree.
- [x] polish issue with no URL: looked up by its title, else logged.
- [x] test environment: the harness clears `WORKER_*`; `CANCCU_ACTOR` and the locale were already cleared.
- [x] leak-check: `tests/leak-check.sh` is clean on this branch.
- [x] `docs/upgrading.md` "Going back": format 3 → 2 is safe by hand; releases before 0.1.3 have no format check.
- [x] CHANGELOG 0.2.0: the upgrade and feature lists are split, and `STEP_TAG` says the title's leading number.
- [x] after #201: `canccu-ship` refuses the leader with `LEADER=off`; an unknown `--project` refusal reaches the actions log.
- [x] after #205: the body send-backs wait out the back-off and the pause, use `is_plan_body` as the review does, and come after the "pushed no fix" needs-you.
- [x] after #210: the kit's wait loop starts from the stored ack; `canccu-up` starts no leader without its kit.
- [x] after #212: fences, CRLF and comment lines in `review_md`; git errors are logged.
- [ ] after #207 (ask markers, ping PATCH): left unticked, because PR #207 is still open.

Leader's items:
- [x] `ci_rerun`: see above.
- [ ] post-pass merge of main: left unticked. A clean merge of main already counts only the lines that are not on main (`count_from`). body:
## Summary

**Draft. Documentation only: one file, no code, no canon or `CLAUDE.md` change. No merge, no deploy.**

On 2026-11-17 the founder answered a list of open decisions with "make best choices for all". This file records the defaults chosen under that delegation so later sessions neither re-ask the questions nor mistake a default for a ruling. **They are defaults chosen by Claude, reversible by the founder on one line. They are not founder rulings and not ratified canon, and must not be cited as either.** Each is labelled `DESIGNED`, `DECIDED-DEFAULT` or `NOT DELEGATED`, never `LIVE`.

## Changes

`docs/programme/DELEGATED_DEFAULTS_2026-11-17.md` (349 lines):

- **D1** Practitioner session ownership for the 22 handlers #2325 leaves open: **fail closed, recoverable** (owner-only with no existence oracle; no unowned rows created; legacy unowned rows unreachable, recovery by a founder-run audited backfill that is *not* built, plus a read-only counts-only census; delete owner-only; lists own rows only). Being built as a separate draft PR stacked on #2325.
- **D2** Host facts the repo cannot know (`ACCESS_CONTROL_MODE`, `portal_inquiries` count): founder-run, read-only, counts only. Exact commands given; the SQL was run on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 built from the baseline DDL with fictional rows.

- **D4** What was **not** delegated: merging, deploying, marking ready, auto-merge, lifting the R105 worker-deployment hold, opening the held PR-C, any production access, canon or `CLAUDE.md` changes, ratifying a default as a ruling.
- **D5.1 to D5.24** Every decision the three study reports raise, each with the question, default, why, what would change it, what it does **not** authorize, status and the owed acceptance test. Each default keeps authority with the member and the writer (no guru stance, no manufactured meaning, no ranking, no authorship by MAIA). A traceability map ties each study decision to its section.
- A list of where the studies are stale at the tip (9-versus-8 lens count absent; Sanctuary enforced in source in the Work and Develop lanes by #2194; `/writers-studio/plans` exists).

## What this does not do

- It decides nothing that was not delegated and builds nothing. Three defaults are judgement calls the founder could reasonably reverse: **D5.5** departs from the studies' detector-driven crisis card and chooses a member-initiated control that infers nothing from a person's text (no copy is written; human review comes first); **D5.13** adopts the Circles no-counts/no-ranks rule as a design constraint for new practitioner work without amending it; **D5.18** answers **no** to opening WS2-08C and stays design-only, because earlier founder acts hold 08B to 08E.

- The records it cites for D1 and D3 include commits on unmerged branches. They resolve while those branches exist on origin; `check:record-shas` follows the documented rule for such citations.
- **Basis is canonical `ddf584b28`.** #2326 (closed doors, account copy) was merged by the founder after that basis; the record treats it as open "awareness only". Nothing in it depends on #2326's state.
- The host commands in D2 were **not run against production** and must not be by an agent. The two values stay UNKNOWN until the founder runs them.

## Order and deploy

Merging this to `clean-main-no-secrets` is a founder act (D4 says so) and changes no behaviour.

author: anthonykrupko
body: ## What Fixes the three Windows problems the FFI lane found (`FFI.md` findings 1–3; roadmap FFI-14, FFI-15, FFI-16). 1. **Replacing a package that is open now works on any Windows file system.** On NTFS and ReFS the plain rename already replaces a package another Wayfarer process has mapped (see the Windows results below). Where Windows can't rename with POSIX semantics (FAT32, exFAT, some network shares), a rename over a memory-mapped file fails with `Access is denied (os error 5)`. `PackageFile::move_into_place` now renames the open package aside to `.replaced-` (allowed, because Rust's `File::open` shares delete access), moves the new one in, and deletes the old file once nothing maps it: at once if it can, otherwise on the next replacement of the same path. Both package writers use it (the compiler's `write_file` and `PackageFile::write_encoded`). Linux and macOS keep the plain rename. If the second rename fails, the old package is put back. 2. **Non-ASCII paths from C on Windows.** New Windows-only `wayfarer_open_w` and `wayfarer_verify_w` take a `wchar_t` path. This is additive, so `WAYFARER_ABI_VERSION` stays 1. The header and the FFI README now say that paths are UTF-8 on Windows too. `route.c` and `cancel.c` take their arguments from `wmain` and convert them with `WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, ...)`, so `...\Łódź ścieżka\pakiet.mrt` opens. 3. **Static linking needs `/MD`.** The FFI README and the example headers now give the MSVC commands for the DLL and for static linking, the system libraries, why to use `/MD` (one C runtime; `/MT` fails with `__imp_clock`, `__imp__wassert`, `__imp_qsort_s` once zstd's C code is linked in), and the `+crt-static` build for `/MT` hosts. ## Tests - `wayfarer-package`: `replace_tests` (3 tests). They replace a mapped file and check that the old mapping keeps its bytes, run the Windows fallback directly, and check that cleanup deletes only its own names. - `wayfarer-ffi --test compile`: `a_compile_replaces_a_package_that_is_open`. It compiles Monaco, opens it, compiles again onto the same path, routes on the old handle, opens the new package, then checks that a third compile leaves only `monaco.mrt`. - `wayfarer-ffi --test abi`: `packages_open_from_non_ascii_paths`. It runs over UTF-8 on every platform, and over `wayfarer_open_w`/`wayfarer_verify_w` on Windows. Checked in the cloud (Linux): `cargo fmt --check`; workspace clippy `-D warnings` (with and without `compiler`); tests for `wayfarer-package`, `wayfarer-ffi` (with `compiler`) and `wayfarer-compiler`. The Windows code was cross-checked with clippy for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. `replace_tests` passes under Wine, and with the fallback turned off the first test fails there with access denied, as it does on Windows. ## Checked on Windows (tony-pc) Windows 11 (10.0.26300), MSVC (VS 18 Build Tools), Rust 1.99.1, worktree on a ReFS Dev Drive. - `cargo test -p wayfarer-package --lib replace_tests`: 3/3 pass. - `cargo test -p wayfarer-ffi --features compiler --test compile --test abi`: 16/16 pass, including `a_compile_replaces_a_package_that_is_open` and `packages_open_from_non_ascii_paths` (which runs over `wayfarer_open_w`/`wayfarer_verify_w` here). - `cargo clippy -p wayfarer-ffi -p wayfarer-package --features wayfarer-ffi/compiler --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo build --release -p wayfarer-cli -p wayfarer-ffi`, then compiled Monaco to `...\Łódź ścieżka\pakiet.mrt`: OK. - `route.c` and `cancel.c` built with `cl` both ways (against `wayfarer_ffi.dll.lib`, and static with `/MD` plus `ws2_32 userenv ntdll bcrypt advapi32`): all four route (or cancel) on the non-ASCII path. - Replace-while-open by hand: a C host held the package open through `wayfarer_open_w` while `wayfarer.exe compile` wrote onto the same path. The compile succeeded, the held handle kept routing, a fresh open got the new package, and a third compile after the host exited left only `pakiet.mrt`. **No `.replaced-*` file appeared**, because on NTFS and ReFS `std::fs::rename` uses POSIX semantics and Wayfarer opens packages with delete sharing, so the plain rename succeeds (a small Rust probe confirmed this on C: NTFS, D: NTFS and E: ReFS). The 0.1.3 CLI also succeeds against a Wayfarer holder. The `Access is denied` in the FFI lane came from a Python mmap holder, which opens without delete sharing. That still blocks both 0.1.3 (os error 5) and this branch (os error 32, from the rename aside), and the old package is left intact. The rename-aside fallback was not exercised on real Windows; it covers file systems without POSIX rename semantics. - `+crt-static`: `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+crt-static"` builds a `wayfarer_ffi.lib` that links with `cl /MT` and routes. The default static library also links with `/MT` (it has no C code; zstd only comes in through `wayfarer-road-graph`'s `snapshot` feature). Fixes from the Windows check (docs only, no code changes): - `Docs: on NTFS and ReFS a rename already replaces an open package`: the changelog, root and compiler READMEs, FFI README, `wayfarer.h` and the `move_into_place` docs now say the rename aside is for file systems without POSIX rename semantics. - `FFI README: say why /MD, without claiming every /MT link fails`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

body:
Flags the operator's own aito.ai visits and leaves them out of the web numbers. This is the "tagged, not dropped" decision of 17.11.2026, ticket td-20261117233642591246. aito-website #410 tags those browsers with the event property `internal: true`; it has been live since 18.11.

## What changes
- `web_sessions.likely_internal` is a new nullable Boolean. It is true when any event of the session carries `internal: true`. Any value other than true, false, "true" or "false" raises with the event (rule 3).
- Every read that left out `likely_bot` now also leaves out internal sessions. That covers web_traffic, web_view, web_kpis, web_paths, predict_next_path, onward_drivers, journeys, web_visitors, web_steps, post linking, the web funnel and the weekly engagement KPIs. The field is never a driver.
- The pull summary, web_traffic and the Web view totals count `internal` sessions separately. The Web view now reads "N likely bot and M internal sessions left out".
- docs/35 describes the field. docs/44 lists 18.11 as a data break, because visits from before that date are untagged.

## What the book found
Rows stored before the column have no value. In Aito, both `{"likely_internal": {"$not": true}}` and `{"$not": {"likely_internal": true}}` also drop those rows, which would have removed every older visit from the KPIs. Reads therefore match `false` or `null`. The new book uploads a row without the field and checks that it still counts in web_traffic, web_view, web_kpis and web_paths.

## Review
- The new book is `test_antti_s_own_visits_are_flagged_internal_and_left_out`. The other snapshot changes add the field, an `internal: 0` count or the new filter. No existing number changed.

The shared test Aito moved to engine 2.12.2, which changes the build line in test_mcp and test_modify_visibility. test_remote_mcp's disabled `/mcp` now returns 404 instead of 405, which main showed before this branch. test_roles and test_search_vector failed once and passed on a rerun.

## To ship (operator)
1. Merge.
2. `./do migrate aito` adds the column. Until the next pull re-writes a day, existing rows stay null and still count.
3. Deploy.

The web numbers change, so this needs the operator's yes; it is not an obvious fix.

body:
Lets native MCP clients connect to the hosted connector (https://mcp.facturxapi.com/mcp). Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http …`) and Codex (`codex mcp login`) log in through a loopback redirect, which the worker refused until now (400 « redirect_uri is not a Claude or ChatGPT callback »).

Stacked on #8 (the worker): base branch `grok/mcp-worker-20261115`.

What changes (workers/mcp):
- `redirects.ts`: new `isLoopbackRedirect`. It accepts plain http on `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or `localhost`, on any port (RFC 8252 §7.3: the client picks a free port per login), with no userinfo, query or fragment. `redirectAllowed` and dynamic registration accept it; lookalike hosts (`localhost.evil.example`, `127.0.0.1.evil.example`), other private addresses and `https://localhost` stay refused.
- `consent.ts`: a loopback client cannot keep a secret. A loopback request without a PKCE `S256` code challenge gets no consent page (400), and an approval without it never completes the authorization. This holds even for a client registered with a secret.
- Already true in `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` and unchanged: only `S256` is accepted, PKCE is required for public clients, and a loopback redirect matches the registered one whatever its port.
- The consent page already warns when the access goes to an application on this computer (`redirectIsLoopback`).

Tests (`npm test`, node:test):
- 19/19 pass, including 4 new tests:
  - loopback hosts accepted on any port, lookalikes refused;
  - dynamic registration of a loopback client accepted;
  - no consent page without PKCE S256 (none, `plain`, or a challenge without a method);
  - a loopback approval without S256 never completes.
- Mutant (the S256 check turned off): the 2 PKCE tests fail.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

Deployment of the hosted worker is a separate step, after review.

author: pjdotson
body:
## Linear issue [SY-6249](https://linear.app/synnax/issue/SY-6249) ## Description The relay skipped every `@sedosaur` reply on a finding's thread from a member whose org membership is private. The `dismiss` job gated on `author_association`. Of all relay runs for review comments, only replies from the one public member ever passed it, while `issue_comment` events from a private member pass the same check. So a review comment event does not report `MEMBER` for a private member. Run 44193383489 on #6359 is one such skip. The job now starts for any reply from a person or an agent on a same-repo pull request. The step reads the thread root and stops unless Sedosaur wrote it, then reads the permission of a person and stops unless it is `admin` or `write`. A mention is no longer needed. The `issue_comment` `@sedosaur dismiss` path does not change, and reviews still read only the code. The answer job posts the usage once per thread for a reply with no dismiss command, such as "Fixed in abc123". Without that limit, an agent reply would get a usage answer that makes the thread need action again. The sweep also skips the bot's own replies: the usage text holds `@sedosaur dismiss`, so a later run answered it with a refusal. ## Review tier `review/human`: it changes who can start Sedosaur's answer job. https://claude.ai/code/session_01SMnqxJYrXgumiprUb32dy3

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge: I traced the new relay gate and the usage sweep and found no defect.

Summary

- The relay now sends every reply on a same-repo pull request to the dismiss job when a person or one of the two agent apps posts it. A mention is no longer needed, and the job no longer checks `author_association`. - The relay step stops when Sedosaur did not write the root comment of the thread. It also stops when the person's permission from the collaborators API is not `admin` or `write`. Agent replies skip the permission check, and `authority` still refuses them later. - The dismiss sweep posts the usage once to each open thread whose replies hold no dismiss command. It also skips the bot's own replies, so the `@sedosaur dismiss` text inside the usage no longer gets a refusal. - The docs (CONTRIBUTING, shepherd.md, workflow headers, docstrings) now say that any reply gets the usage once. Tests cover a reply with no mention, the once-per-thread limit, a missed earlier run, and a resolved thread. Reviews (3) · Last reviewed commit: [SY-6249: Answer the usage in the thread sweep](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/commit/5263c6ae0e38e60b1964e820431ccbb13115c1b9) · [Run](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/actions/runs/44201521081)

The Foundation now puts students first. The two programmes that bring real value lead the site: the event "Vivere più a lungo: sport e intelligenza artificiale" and the Agentic AI High School Innovation Program. The main goal is to get as many people as possible to register for the event.

## What changes
**Homepage (`app/page.tsx`, `app/home.module.css`, `lib/home/*`, `components/home/*`)**
- Hero with the event image, the new message ("We train students to build digital scientists"), an Italian event card with "Iscriviti gratis" and a live countdown.
- The event in numbers and "What is a digital scientist".
- Italian event block: both days, seats left per day from `event_seats_remaining()`, speakers wall and registration.
- The programmes: school, Agentic AI course, university track, talks with the next talk.
- **Live numbers** (`lib/home/numeri.ts`):
  - aggregate counts only, read with the service role, refreshed hourly via ISR;
  - each count has a 5 s timeout and is hidden when missing or tiny;
  - the section disappears without a database.
- **Our vision** (non-profit, students come first) and **Our story**: a real photo of the Taranto Biotech Days 2024 and a timeline from 2024 to 2026, every fact sourced (`lib/home/copia.ts`).
- News, get involved, partners, FAQ (rewritten) and a closing call to register.
- `ARCHIVE_MODE` switches the calls to register to the recap after the event.
- Scroll reveal and count-up render real content on the server and respect reduced motion.

**Site-wide**
- **Menu:** The Event, Schools, AI Course, Talks, About Us, Articles, "Log in" and "Join the event". The full menu shows from 1024px.
- **Footer:** the old startup and research pages are out of the menu but online, under "More", with /taranto added.
- **Metadata:** new title, description, Organization JSON-LD and share images (`og-home.jpg` on the homepage, undated `og-brand.jpg` as the site default).

**Other pages**
- **About:** opening, "How We Work", partners and calls aligned with the non-profit positioning. Team, values and publications are unchanged.
- **Articles:** "ecosystem" wording replaced, the founding newsletter listed, the launch card in date order.
- **Other fixes:** the people pages' research link and the Contact description.

**Judges' guide** (`licei/commissione/guida/contenuto.ts`): "Le date e cosa fare" and "Come si entra in Commissione".

No file under `app/eventi` changes apart from the guide content. The event pages, the areas, tickets and printed QR targets are untouched.

## Checks
- Two independent multi-agent reviews, every finding adversarially verified. All 37 confirmed findings are fixed.
- `tsc`, `eslint` and `next build` pass. The homepage stays static with 1-hour ISR.
- Leak check on `.next/static` and the homepage HTML: no Meet link, no service key.
- All key routes return 200.
- Desktop, tablet and phone screenshots of every section, including a local run with sample numbers that was not committed.

author: jzhu13
body:
## Problem

- A Prometheus rule with `for: 1h` or longer cannot become a metrics alert that fires at the same time.
- Prometheus fires a full `for:` after the first breach, so `for: 1h` needs 61 one-minute checks. Metrics alerts stop at 60.

## Changes

- A metrics alert can look back over 1441 checks, enough for `for: 24h`.
- A check fails once its Snuffle response passes 8 MB, read as a stream and before decoding. An hour of checks over 1000 series is about 3 MB.
- No cap on the window's time span: an expression can already ask for `[60d]`.
- Regenerated API and MCP types are mechanical.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the new size budget test fails without the streamed cap. The cap and form tests move to 1441.

Not run: a 1441-step query against real Snuffle.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

**Skills:** `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** the cap stays a count of checks, as `SourceConfigSpec.max_evaluation_periods` already is, rather than an interval-aware span.
- **Decisions:** the response is capped while streaming, not counted after decoding, so memory stays bounded. Other `snuffle_payload` callers read unbounded as before.
- **Read closely:** `_read_body` in `products/metrics/backend/promql.py`.

</details>

author: jbookout
body:
Closes #624.

Stores all six documented suggestion kinds and lets a partner accept or dismiss them once. Next-step edits land with acceptance. Filing records the chosen open deal and correction reason without creating a deal. Phase moves are derived from the quote and checked again at acceptance. Includes the job-only router queue with paging, resolved senders, open deals, recent filing history and suppressed deal IDs from recorded removals.

Queue limitations while #619 is unmerged: intake sender display names, ordered recipients, conversation IDs and mailbox membership are unavailable. Those fields are omitted, including from thread entries. The queue currently scopes by the email's original changed_for_user_id stamp, so second-mailbox visibility and same-conversation history beyond 30 days still wait for #619. Keep the router switch off until those facts are wired in. Known senders use the matched party's name. The schema has no property city column, so city is null. It also has no separate lead-to-client relationship for client_party_ids; current contact-company client links are returned.

The document gives no request shape for the separate propose-email-lead candidate door. That call remains on the old system. The documented new_lead suggestion for an existing party is implemented.

Schema adds the two filing kinds, permits no target only for possible_new_deal, and stores the filing decision's deal and reason in typed columns. Database rules require an open deal and correction reason, and keep decisions final.

Verified npm ci and npm run check on disposable postgres:18 at 127.0.0.1:56724 with trust auth and max_locks_per_transaction=256. All 1,318 tests passed, along with lint, types and Worker build. Removing the database filing-reason rule made the filing test fail; restoring it passed. Container removed. No production access or screen verification. No dependency, script or lasting design decision added.

Size is 681 added and 9 removed lines across eight files, above the approximate target. Includes the coupled schema, routes, queue and 279 lines of request tests. Independent review and real-screen verification remain with the coordinator.

## What changed
- Range already came from the last 10 km driven, but it jumped straight from the 180 Wh/km guess to the raw figure after just 1 km, and demo mode forgot everything on reload.
- Now: every 0.25 km we note distance and energy out of the pack (volts x amps). Newest driving counts most (half weight every 5 km back, 20 km kept). The figure is pulled gently toward the lifetime average (worth 1.5 km), so one steep climb can't swing the range much.
- Kept across restarts on the Pi (trips.json, as before) and in the browser for `?demo=drive`.
- Trips screen says how much driving the figure is learnt from ("Still learning: 2.3 km so far" / "Learnt from your last 20 km").

- `dash` pytest: 49 passed, including new tests for settling on new driving, a short climb not swinging it, carrying on after restart, and a fresh pack.

author: carbon14-48
body:
closes #2766 

`ELIST` is an imaginary token, so it took the position of its first child `EXPR`, which is the position of the expression's root operator. For a wrapped argument such as `foo("a"\n + "b")`, `ELIST` was reported on the line of the `+` instead of right after `(`.

### Change

`JavaAstVisitor#visitExpressionList` now sets the `ELIST` line and column from the first token of the expression list. Empty `ELIST` nodes are not created there, so their positions are unchanged.

Example from the issue, before and after:

    |--LPAREN -> ( [3:40]
    |--ELIST -> ELIST [4:27]   -> now [3:41]

### Impact on checks

- **Indentation**: no behavior change. 
- **BooleanExpressionComplexity**: the check logs on the parent of the `EXPR`, which is `ELIST` for method arguments. A violation in a wrapped method argument is now reported at the start of the argument instead of on the wrapped operator line. `InputBooleanExpressionComplexity` and its test were updated (3 violations).
- 
- **XPath**: `ELIST` no longer matches violations reported at the lambda arrow or the assignment operator, so `XpathRegressionExpressionOverBlockLambdaTest` and `XpathRegressionInnerAssignmentTest` no longer expect the `.../METHOD_CALL/ELIST` query.
- **FOR_ITERATOR**: it takes its position from its `ELIST` child, so it also moves to the first token, e.g. from `++` to `i` in `i++`.

author: therealbillyb
body:
## Summary

A follow-up to #558's spy test, `test_both_opens_ask_for_binary_mode`. #558 merged before this change.

The test pretended `O_BINARY` was 0x8000. On Linux aarch64, 0x8000 is `O_NOFOLLOW`, which the helpers already pass. So on that platform the test would pass without the fix.

The test now uses `FAKE = 1 << 30`, for:
- the patched `os.O_BINARY` and `tool_directory._BINARY`;
- the spy's mask;
- the assertion.

On macOS, `1 << 30` is `O_EXEC`. The helpers never pass that, but a bit that seems unused can still collide somewhere, so the test checks itself on whatever system runs it:

1. **Flag off.** It runs `held_write_bytes` and `held_read_bytes` with `os.O_BINARY` and `tool_directory._BINARY` set to 0. It asserts there are two opens of the data file, and that neither carries the bit.
2. **Flag on.** It runs them again with both set to `FAKE`, and asserts that both opens carry the bit.

Pass 2 alone could be fooled by a colliding flag; pass 1 rules that out. If some platform's own flags include the bit, the test fails at pass 1 instead of passing silently.

## Checked

- Against `tool_directory.py` from main before #558 (85a13010), it fails at pass 2's assertion.
- Against main with the fix, it passes, along with the rest of the file.
- Only `tests/test_held_files_are_binary.py` changes.

Add a fixed-union learner and passive proof family that use the Trainer's frozen-reference policy KL. Contracts, checkpoints and continuation bind the bootstrap checkpoint, architecture, step and coefficient. A zero coefficient loads no reference and performs no reference forward; a positive coefficient uses frozen reference weights in evaluation mode outside optimizer ownership.

The saved-state certificate records actual student/reference forward counts and reference immutability alongside model, optimizer, dose, journal and RNG evidence. Sampling remains globally uniform, and the real partial-tail factor applies to the whole objective. Existing optimizer and loss implementations are reused. Independent review accepted the final source and its composition with the bounded replay integration with no findings.

All five jobs passed in CI run 44206973659 on merge b3d4dce4c5948faefb3f482709652dba67b45135, tree fb3a18eb629e3b34e8e8716fa4a8b47fcfcecef9. All ten new Tiny cases passed, covering the zero path, positive KL through actual optimization, frozen reference identity, continuation/RNG equivalence and tampering. CI caught test comparisons between JSON lists and in-memory architecture tuples; both whole-identity assertions now use the existing canonical representation. Production code was unchanged by that correction.

Validation: capped regression 24 passed; ordinary parallel suite 11,561 passed; serial suite 5,240 passed. The runner deliberately deselected 135 unaffected script-only test modules against current Main, explaining the lower aggregate counts than the earlier stacked run. This selects no coefficient, experiment, deployment or playing-strength claim. The active saved-model evaluation remains on its qualified runtime.

## Summary

```diff
 e2e/mapping-composition.spec.ts
   nearFixtures reset test
+  await waitForSceneReady(page);   // after openMapping, before the first read
   Isolate hover test
+  await waitForSceneReady(page);   // after Isolate is pressed
```

The #136 hunt's diagnostics (now in main) showed every name-placement failure had `text measured -> measured` — text measurement was not the cause — but a **different map scale**:

body:
Do not merge until hyssostech/stp feature/STP-942 merges into main.

## What was added

This raises the OpenRPC contract (`json-api/sketch-thru-plan-api.json`) to **0.9.12** for STP-1706 P2. It adds the WebSocketsBridge naming surface of hyssostech/stp PR #967 (head `64e56d4e`):

- **`GetNaming`** (`read`, no params): returns the session's effective naming convention as a `NamingNotice`.
- **`PublishNaming`** (`destructive`): takes `target` (global / plan / both), `baseStamp`, `checkOnly` and `layer`. `layer` is a `NamingCustomization` object, its JSON as a string, or null. It returns a `NamingPublishResult` with a status of `applied`, `check_only`, `stale_base` or `refused`. `success` is false for `stale_base` and `refused`. `x-stpEmits`: `NamingChanged` (to the session) when an applied publish changes the effective convention, and `StpMessage` when the call fails.
- **`NamingChanged`** event: its params are the `NamingNotice` properties.
- New schemas for these payloads, in the engine's snake_case JSON: `NamingNotice`, `NamingLayerStamp`, `WordListDelta`, `NamingRowDelta`, `NamingRegistration`, `NamingIssue`, `NamingCustomization`, `WordListChange`, `NamingRowChange`, `NamingPublishResult` and `NamingLayerEffect`.
- `json-api/sketch-thru-plan-validations.json`: version 1.0.12, now checked against contract 0.9.12. It adds a `PublishNaming` rule (no preconditions, no expected events, a confirm text). The repo's own validations test requires this rule and lists `PublishNaming` as exempt from `activeScenario`.
- **No-scenario refusal (operator ruling 283(a), stp #967 head `a5dc938c3`):** a `plan` or `both` publish in a session with no active scenario is refused (status `refused`, nothing stored, `checkOnly` included), as is a plan publish from a connection with no session. A `global` publish needs no scenario. Both refusals are listed in `PublishNaming`'s edge cases, and a refusal example is included.
- A CHANGELOG entry.

`PublishNaming` is classed as `destructive` because it replaces the target layer whole, and a global publish does so for every session. If you want it classed as `write` instead, remove its `confirm` rule as well.

The examples and edge cases come from reading the engine source, not from a live capture. They are marked as illustrative.

## Checks

- `tools/check-openrpc-surface.sh` from the PR #967 worktree with `OPENRPC_CONTRACT` set to this file: PASS (engine 78 methods / 37 events; contract 79 methods / 37 events; C2SIM option keys pass)
- `node json-api/check-openrpc.js`: Validation OK

author: jasonbahl
body:
The Secure Custom Fields + Content Blocks integration cell looks up the latest WPGraphQL Content Blocks release with an unauthenticated `curl` to the GitHub API. Since 2026-11-16 that lookup has come back empty on nine runs, including a push to `main`, the release PR and a Dependabot PR, each failing with "Failed to resolve WPGraphQL Content Blocks latest release tag". Because the cell feeds the required Integration Tests check, each one blocks a merge until the job is re-run.

Content Blocks hasn't released since `v4.8.9` on 2026-10-23, and the endpoint answers normally, so the failure is on our side. Unauthenticated API requests are limited to 60 an hour per IP, which shared runners can exhaust. The old step couldn't tell us for sure: `curl -s` hid the HTTP status and an error body turned into an empty version string.

This switches the lookup to `gh api` with the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (read-only, and also available to fork PRs), which raises the limit to 1,000 requests an hour, and on failure `gh` prints the API error, so the log says why. The version check and error message are unchanged otherwise.

This was the only unauthenticated `api.github.com` call in our workflows and scripts.

author: omarjatoi
body:
M10-03: the trampoline's inline caches run value-returning primitives in place, as call sites already do (design.md "Primitives run in place"). This wins back #195's cost to `apply`-heavy code without bringing back a performance warning.

## Cause

#195 stopped marking primitive roots trivial (`RootNode.isTrivial`). Truffle's Javadoc defines a trivial root as one that *"never contains loops"*, so the flag was wrong for `+`, `vector` and `string<?`. But Graal's `DefaultInliningPolicy` expands and inlines a trivial callee outside both of its budgets, and tier 1 inlines nothing else. Without the flag, the trampoline's `DirectCallNode`s to primitive roots competed for the inlining budget.

Evidence comes from `--compiler.TraceInlining` on ecraven's `scheme` (10 iterations, the report's count), tallying tier-2 call trees, one traced run each. `string<?` reaches the trampoline from the interpreter's `((oper rte) a b)` (`gen-combination-2`), whose tail site is past `MakeTailCall`'s in-place cache.

| | `string<?` inlined | cut off | tier-2 compilations | tier-2 code |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| main | 65 | 232 | 129 | 3.4 MB |
| main + `isTrivial` (before #195) | 214 | 0 | 124 | 2.8 MB |
| this PR | no call node | | 101 | 1.7 MB |

So the cost was the call boundary: compiled code called `string<?`'s root wherever the budget ran out. It was not a frame cost, and not tier-1 inlining alone (first iterations hardly moved).

## Change

- `Trampoline.TailCalls.doDirect`: each cache entry now holds either a `DirectCallNode` or, for a primitive that only returns values (`PrimitiveRootNode.inPlace`), a `PrimitiveNode` of its own, which it runs in place after checking the arity. Each entry's node is a constant, so partial evaluation keeps one branch. Primitives share the cache's limit with closures, as they did before, so a tail call of a closure checks no more entries than before. Errors leave the trampoline for the call site, as they did from the root. A trampoline past its cache still calls indirectly.
- Variant measured and not kept: a separate `doPrimitive` specialization before `doDirect`, the way `Call` does it. Same `scheme` gain (fix vs fix2 below), but its checks sit in front of every closure's entry.
- Not chosen:
  - `isTrivial` for loop-free primitives only: `string<?` loops, so `scheme` gains nothing.
  - `forceInlining()`: #195 tried it, and it didn't restore the time.
- Docs: design.md ("Primitives run in place", with a *Why in the trampoline* note); PrimitiveRootNode's and Trampoline's Javadoc; performance-research.md item 8. M10-03 is ticked.

## Tests

- `PrimitivesInPlaceTest.primitivesThatTrampolinesCallRunInPlace` checks:
  - `apply` of `%raise-uncaught`, in non-tail and tail position, leaves no frame of the primitive in the guest stack trace;
  - a tail site past `MakeTailCall`'s cache, called with nine primitives and closures;
  - errors (`car: not a pair`, an arity error, a handler that escapes through `k`) are raised as before.
  
  It failed before the change.
- `PrimitivesInPlaceTest.primitivesThatApplyCallsAreNotCalledInCompiledCode` traces inlining while a compiled `step` applies `+`, `string<?` and `vector`. It asserts that `apply` is in the call tree and none of the three is. Before the change, each was `Inlined` twice and `Cutoff` twice.
- `primitivesCalledThroughTheirRootsCompileWithoutPerformanceWarnings` (#195's test) still passes. None of the A/B runs printed a `perf warn`, against 1137 over 5 runs of `e70adbb`'s `scheme`.
- `NumbersTest.fixnumArithmeticKeepsItsFastPathAfterAnOverflow` reached the primitive's root node through `apply`. That path now runs in place, so the test reaches the root through `via-root` instead: an `apply` whose trampoline has already cached four other primitives, so the fifth goes to the root. The assertions are unchanged, and they still fail if the root's node isn't reached.

## Performance

Interleaved A/B: `e70adbb` (before #195), main, and this PR. 5 rounds, fresh JVMs, 10 iterations at the report's counts (`--scale 0.1`), medians. The load was 5-8 (another agent's native-image builds). Times are in ms.

| Program | Iteration | before #195 | main | this PR | PR/main | PR/before |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `scheme` | first | 1119 | 1121 | 1096 | 0.94 | 0.98 |
| `scheme` | 2-3 | 545 | 571 | 488 | 0.87 | 0.90 |
| `scheme` | 6-10 | 391 | 414 | 368 | **0.89** | **0.94** |
| `compiler` | first | 1447 | 1498 | 1448 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| `compiler` | 6-10 | 294 | 286 | 286 | 1.00 | 0.97 |
| `peval` | first | 1036 | 1059 | 1046 | 0.99 | 1.01 |
| `peval` | 6-10 | 298 | 296 | 298 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| `conform` | first | 742 | 726 | 748 | 1.02 | 1.01 |
| `conform` | 6-10 | 265 | 264 | 264 | 0.99 | 1.00 |
| `(apply + args)` and `(apply vector args)` loop | 6-10 | 260 | 265 | 265 | 1.01 | 1.02 |

- **`scheme`**: PR/main per round, iterations 6-10: 0.91, 0.89, 0.92, 0.87, 0.89. PR/before: 0.89, 0.94, 0.97, 0.93, 0.96. It is back past `e70adbb`, not just within noise of it.
- **Other runs agree:**
  - 6 rounds at load 3-8, main against both variants: `scheme` 6-10 at 0.91 and 0.90; `compiler`, `conform` 0.99-1.02.
  - 6 rounds at load 5-11 with `before`: `scheme` 6-10 0.93 of `e70adbb`, main 1.03.
- **Apply micro-benchmark:** iterations 2-3 are 1.06 times main's (5/5 rounds). That is `e70adbb`'s 0.99. Once compiled it is the same.
- **`bench-check`:** all 25 within their thresholds, machine factor 1.00 (`peval` 1.00, `cpstak` 0.83, `tak-interpreter` 1.05). Thresholds unchanged.

## Checks

- `bazel test //...`: 638/638 after rebasing on main (634/634 before).
- `bazel run //:r7rs -- test --compile`: chibi 1225/1225, Larceny 2160/2166 (the listed exceptions). No conformance section changed state.

## Follow-ups

- `Call`'s `doPrimitive` is a specialization of its own in front of `doDirect` (limit 4 each). The one-entry shape used here may suit it too. Measure it before changing.
- A trampoline past its cache calls primitive roots through `IndirectCallNode`, which is never inlined. So does `scheme`'s megamorphic `first` cache, for any primitive past the first four targets.

## Surprises

- `scheme`'s tier-2 code halved: 3.4 → 1.7 MB, and 129 → 101 compilations, fewer splits. Each primitive root call node had counted toward the call trees that Truffle explored and split for.
- `tools_terminal` timed out once (121 s) under load during a `bazel test //...`. It passed in 9.7 s when rerun, and in every other run.

  - **Contexts:** both still exist, the expansion board's on I2C1 and the factory rig's on I2C4 (`S3R_TEST_0024`), filled in by one helper.
  - **Removed:** `get_sys_tick()` and the `sys_tick` field, since the self-test no longer seeds `rand()`.
- **`hal_FactoryTest.c`:** the `S3R_TEST_0023` line takes its reason from `CAT24C16_testFailReason()` and its `- bytes 16-143 not restored` suffix from `CAT24C16_testLeftTestData()`. The printed lines are unchanged.
- **Submodule** moves from `dd5ba17` to log-and-stream-common `e703cff` (ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#243's branch). That is 10 commits of `main` as well as this change and ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#242's docs. The build below includes them.

## What changes on the device
- **Write timing.** A write now waits 5 ms after a page that failed too. It already waited after each page that succeeded, so it always returns with the part idle, and #330's extra wait at the start of each restore try is gone.
- **Failed reads** now fill the buffer with `0xFF`, as Shimmer3's always have: what an erased part holds. A failed read of the expansion-board ID page therefore reads as unprogrammed (DEV-1019). Before, the buffer kept whatever the HAL had left in it.
- **Test pattern.** The self-test writes an incrementing pattern, offset by the pass number, instead of #330's `rand()` one. Every byte still differs from the previous pass's.
- **Bounds.** No change here; the new check differs only on 16-bit targets.

## Testing
- **STM32CubeIDE 1.15.1 headless, clean Release build:** 0 errors, 0 warnings. `text` 345,100 bytes, 360 fewer than #330's build, which also lacked the 10 log-and-stream-common commits.
- **log-and-stream-common host suite:** `test_cat24c16` runs the shared driver against a fake part with fault injection, including a second context. See that PR.
- **Not benched.** Owed on a unit:
  - `S3R_TEST_0023`, and `0024` with the rig if one is to hand;
  - a daughter-card memory read and write over Bluetooth;
  - the expansion-board ID read at boot;
  - the BT MAC backup record (§7 of the EEPROM map).

## Merge order
1. #330 and ShimmerResearch/shimmer3-firmware#144.
2. ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#242, then ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#243.
3. Re-point this PR's submodule at ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#243's merge commit on log-and-stream-common `main`, then merge.

Merging this PR before ShimmerResearch/log-and-stream-common#243 would leave the submodule on a branch commit that a squash merge makes unreachable.

body:
## What

The button label looked blurry. It was shaded inside the 3D scene pass, so three things softened it: the mip-biased mask, FXAA, and the adaptive resolution drop (down to 0.6× on slower GPUs).

## How

- The shading pass no longer draws the label. Through a second render target it records only where the label is visible (not under goo or the hand) and the local shadow and AO.
- The final pass now runs at full device resolution, always. It does FXAA (upscaling the scene targets when adaptive quality lowered them) and then draws the label from its 4× mask with the same polished-metal shading.
- The canvas keeps its full size. Only the scene targets shrink under adaptive quality, so text stays sharp on slow devices too.
- Still 3 draw calls per frame.

author: drzee99
body:
What

Drop -target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu from the two amdclang command lines in cuda_lt.sh (PIC and non-PIC objects), so clang uses its default (host) target. The device targets still come from --offload-arch.

Why ?

Bug fix: on a non-x86 host such as aarch64, the host-side part of the HIP compile looks for the x86_64 C++ headers and the ROCm EC kernels fail to build:

```
  cuda_wrappers/cmath:30:22: error: "Could not find standard C++ header 'cmath'"
  fatal error: 'cstdlib' file not found
```

The triple has been there since the amdclang build was added (#899), and that PR doesn't say it's needed. On x86_64 hosts the default target is x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, so x86_64 builds are unchanged.

How ?

Two-line change in cuda_lt.sh. Tested with a native aarch64 build of UCC 1.9.0 with ROCm 10.1 (Arch Linux ARM): all amdclang HIP compiles run without -target and the build succeeds. cuda_lt.sh is identical in v1.9.0 and master.

author: mgoldsborough
body:
Closes #2028.

## What

- **`release.yml` gets a fifth job, `publish-cli`,** that publishes `packages/cli` to npm as `nimblebrain` at the tag's version.
  - It runs after `release`, so the images the CLI installs are on GHCR first.
  - A GA tag publishes to `latest` and a pre-release to `next`, so `npx nimblebrain` never resolves to a pre-release. A hotfix tag (`-hotfix.N`) is for one deployment and publishes nothing.
  - The version is set from the tag inside the job, then built in and checked (`--version` must match). `package.json` stays `0.0.0-dev`, per RELEASING.md.
  - It authenticates by **npm trusted publishing** (GitHub OIDC), so there is no npm token. A version already on npm is skipped, so re-running the workflow is safe.
- **`doctor` accepts arm64.** v0.73.0 published `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images.
- **`cli-e2e` runs on both platforms**, `ubuntu-latest` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, each against the newest release.
- **Docs:**
  - a new page, *npx nimblebrain* (`cli/nimblebrain`), covering the commands, flags, the JSON and error codes, connecting an agent, and what it writes
  - the quickstart opens with a tip pointing to it
  - the CLI overview links to it
  - the README, quickstart and installation pages no longer say the images are amd64-only; they now say both platforms. Both GHCR names the docs pull, `nimblebrain` and `nimblebrain-runtime`, hold both platforms.
- **RELEASING.md:** job 5 is described in §7, and a new §4e says how to verify the CLI on npm.

## Needs doing once, outside this PR (owner)

1. **On npmjs.com,** open the `nimblebrain` package's settings and add a trusted publisher: GitHub Actions, repository `NimbleBrainInc/nimblebrain`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `npm`. Until this exists, `publish-cli` fails with an authentication error. The image release and prod promotion are unaffected, since they don't depend on this job.
2. **In this repo's settings,** have the `npm` environment (GitHub creates it on first use) admit only `v*` tags as deployment refs, the same way the `pypi` environment admits only `server-sdk-py/v*`.

## Timing

The docs deploy when this merges, but the CLI reaches npm only at the next release. Until then, `npx nimblebrain` resolves to the old `0.0.1` placeholder. Cutting a release right after merging closes that gap.

## Verified

- **The whole lifecycle ran natively on an Apple Silicon Mac** with `NIMBLEBRAIN_TAG=v0.73.0`: `packages/cli/test/e2e.sh` passed every step, including MCP `tools/list` returning 200, the port bound to 127.0.0.1 only, and a clean `uninstall`.
- `bun run test:cli`: 48 pass, including the new aarch64 and arm64 `doctor` case.
- `bun run check:cli`, `format:check` and `lint` pass.
- The workflow-shell-input, release-ci-gate and image-merge tests pass (18).
- actionlint is clean on `release.yml` and `cli-e2e.yml`.
- The docs build passes with all internal links valid.
- `publish-cli` itself can only run at a release, so the first proof is the next tag (RELEASING.md §4e).

author: jvallery
body:
A grow light switched by hand is held by the controller for 15 minutes, and two paths left that hold in place when the light should have gone back to automatic.

**Root cause** (live run 2026-11-17 21:47Z, recorded on #1671):
1. `scripts/dashboard-smoke.sh --role operator --lights` returned to automatic with its own reason. The operator API releases the controller's hold only for a write of the automatic switch to 1 with the reason "Back to automatic", so no release was queued. While the hold stands, the controller's intent follows it (`manual_hold_off`), so the leg read intent == state, found nothing to restore, and the main light stayed off for the full 15 min.
2. API-20 timed every switch (15 min by default), and a confirmed timed switch queues a controller hold. The Equipment page's own Back to automatic resync sends API-20 with the reason "Back to automatic", so that restore switch queued a fresh 15 min hold at the intent, and the light stopped following the controller. The server's own resync was already untimed.

(The explicit Back to automatic write at 21:49:38Z was not a repeat-value defect: its readback at 21:50:11Z would have confirmed it, but the waiting in-process resync was dropped when the operator API was paused for a migration qualification at 21:49:49Z.)

**Change**
- `api/operator_routes/writes.py`: a switch with the reason "Back to automatic" is untimed and queues no controller hold, like the server's resync.
- `scripts/dashboard-smoke.sh --lights`: writes the switch as the page does (1, not manual, "Back to automatic"), waits up to 2 min for API-13's `auto_reason` to leave `manual_hold_*`, restores with an untimed "Back to automatic" switch, and its final check requires the light off its hold. Runbook line updated.
- Tests: `tests/test_operator_lights.py` (an untimed Back to automatic switch queues no hold; the smoke leg uses the releasing reason) and `tests/test_k3s_smoke_g10.py` (the fake models the hold; the lights leg ends off it). Locally: both files 216 passed.

Delivery: rides host release 8b, which promotes api from the build after this and #1789 merge.

Restart: verdify-api, verdify-operator-api via the 8b promotion.

author: maffooch
body:
**Description**

`bulk_add_tag_mapping` (`dojo/tags/utils.py`) found the existing tags it adds with

```python
tag_model.objects.annotate(name_lower=Lower("name")).filter(name_lower__in=[...])
```

which is `LOWER(name) IN (...)`. No index serves `LOWER(name)`: not the unique index on `name`, and not the `UPPER(name)` index `dojo.0308` added (#16801). So every call read the whole tag table. Its callers are `bulk_apply_parser_tags` (an import whose parser sets tags, once per batch) and tag inheritance (`dojo/tags/inheritance.py`).

The lookup now joins the requested names to the tag table on the expression tagulous's own `get_or_create(name__iexact=...)` uses:

```sql
SELECT t.*, requested.name AS requested_name
FROM unnest(%s::text[]) AS requested(name)
JOIN "dojo_tagulous_finding_tags" t ON UPPER(t."name"::text) = UPPER(requested.name)
ORDER BY t.id
```

Each tag is keyed by the name as requested, so no Python-side case folding is involved. PostgreSQL upper-cases both sides, which matters: measured against PostgreSQL's `upper()` in an `en_US.utf8` database over every code point, Python's `str.upper()` differs for 129 of them (the 102 letters it expands, like `ß` -> `SS`, and 27 letters newer than glibc's Unicode tables, like U+019B). A Python-side `name.upper()` key would match a different row than tagulous does for those. `LOWER` and `UPPER` also disagree on letters like the dotless i: before this change, `ID-TAG` against an existing `ıd-tag` missed the bulk lookup and needed a per-name `get_or_create` to find the tag. The case-sensitive branch (`name__in`) is unchanged.

**Test results**

Measured on a finding tag table of 3,000,001 rows (`generate_series` names, `ANALYZE`d, rolled back), with `dojo.0308` applied:

- `bulk_apply_parser_tags` for 5 findings x 3 tags (1 existing, 2 new), 7 runs after a warm-up: **369.5 ms -> 7.8 ms** median wall time per call; 18 statements per call before and after.
- The lookup itself, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`:
  ```
  old: Parallel Seq Scan on dojo_tagulous_finding_tags  Filter: (lower((name)::text) = ANY (...))  Rows Removed by Filter: 1000004 (x3)  Buffers: shared hit=25116  Execution Time: 356.916 ms
  new: Nested Loop -> Function Scan on unnest requested -> Index Scan using idx_tagulous_finding_tags_upper_name  Index Cond: (upper((name)::text) = upper(requested.name))  Buffers: shared hit=12  Execution Time: 0.052 ms
  ```
- By batch size (half the names existing), old -> new execution time: 10 names 345 ms -> 0.11 ms; 100 names 1,283 ms -> 0.61 ms; 1,000 names 1,210 ms -> 4.5 ms; 5,000 names 1,230 ms -> 20.6 ms. The new plan stays on the `UPPER(name)` index at every size.

New `BulkTagMappingNameLookupTest` in `unittests/test_tag_utils_bulk.py`, 6 tests:
- The lookup an import issues plans an index scan on `idx_tagulous_finding_tags_upper_name` and no sequential scan, on a 5,000-row tag table with fresh statistics (like `test_tag_name_upper_index.py`).
- A requested name resolves to the same row `name__iexact` resolves it to, for the dotless i, `ß`, an ASCII case variant, and a letter newer than the database's Unicode tables. Where tagulous finds a tag, the bulk lookup finds it without a per-name fallback query.
- Two case variants in one batch share the existing tag, with one lookup.

Before the change, `test_the_tag_lookup_uses_the_upper_name_index` and the dotless-i case fail (`Seq Scan ... Filter: (lower((name)::text) = ANY (...))`, and 2 name lookups instead of 1). After it, all 38 tests in `test_tag_utils_bulk.py` pass. `test_tag_inheritance.py` passes with and without the change. I ran `test_tag_inheritance_perf.py` and `test_tags.py` in a container where some of their tests fail for reasons unrelated to tags (the classic UI is disabled there, and its statement baselines differ); the same tests fail with and without the change, and the statement counts differ by at most the run-to-run variation (3 statements out of about 5,400). `ruff check` (0.16.10, `ruff.toml`): clean.

**Documentation**

No user-visible change: the same tags are applied.

author: tygedavis
body:
Implements #9 (the layer barrier part).

## What it does
- A thin wall (12 px, `barrier_thickness` is tunable) sits on every layer boundary, centred on the line. It has high HP (`barrier_hp_multiplier` x the tile HP of the layer above) and breaks once per run.
- The drill and shots are blocked by it and damage it; enemies are blocked but never damage it.
- Breaking it pays `barrier_payout_base * layer` into the run's gem value immediately.
- Enemies never spawn below an unbroken barrier; spawn points that would land there are mirrored upward so they stay off screen.
- Break juice lives in `BarrierEffects`: flash and sparks while damaged, shake that grows as it weakens, then hit-stop, particle burst, coin shower, bigger shake and a "+money" popup.

## Testing
Headless scripts in `tests/` (run each with `godot --headless --path . --script tests/<name>.gd`): model, collision (including a step larger than the wall), effects, and a smoke test on the real run scene. All pass, and the project loads cleanly.

author: thanosa75
body:
Adds a CLI command for every Martech API operation except the Developer keys endpoints, and bumps the version to 0.1.3.

## Commands

| Command | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `score` | `POST /v1/score` (job, waited for by default, `--async`) |
| `optimize` | `POST /v1/optimize` (job) |
| `job JOB_ID` | `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` (waits, `--no-wait`) |
| `performance` | `POST /v1/performance` |
| `uplift` | `POST /v1/uplift` |
| `catalogue` | `GET /v1/catalogue` |
| `server-version` | `GET /version` |
| `asset create FILE...` (alias `upload`), `asset list`, `asset get`, `asset download` | `/v1/asset/*` |

Each command that takes input builds its request from flags, from `--file` (JSON), or both. It validates the request locally before sending anything. With `-e/--edit` it opens a built-in Bubble Tea v2 editor on a commented JSON template; the editor shows its keys on screen and does not start an external program. `-o json` prints the server's JSON unchanged.

## Packages

- `src/pkg/api`: the client. It retries `429 rate_limited` and `503` up to 3 times, honouring `Retry-After`. It also holds the models and spec-based validation.
- `src/pkg/editor`: the `--edit` editor.
- `src/pkg/cli`: one file per command, each with its `_test.go`.

## Verification

- `make ci` passes: fmt, vet, golangci-lint, govulncheck, race tests and build. Total coverage is 96.7 %: `api` 98.1 %, `cli` 96.5 %, `editor` 96.8 %.
- Every command was run against staging (`stg-api.persado.com`).
- Four review agents checked the code against the spec, the user experience, error handling and code quality. Their findings are fixed, and the lessons are in AGENTS.md Rules 11 to 16.

Open items are listed in `REMAINING_WORK_2026-11-18.md`.

  - #41 **Beef Tips & Noodles** → optional **Crockpot Beef Tips & Noodles** (contains **cream of mushroom soup and mushrooms**; existing household shopping template is mushroom-free).

Reverting to the original restores existing household planning ingredients where mapped.

body:
2026-10-19 公開の **GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf**(high)で、TypeScript SDK の CI の `npm audit --workspaces --audit-level=high` が落ちるようになった(#1066 で検出。main でも次の実行から落ちる)。

- `picomatch` の ReDoS。対象は `<= 4.0.7` 全部で、修正版はない(npm 上の最新が 4.0.7)
- 経路は dev 依存だけ(`tsup` → tinyglobby / fdir、`vitest` → vite)。`npm audit --workspaces --omit=dev` は 0 件で、公開パッケージには入らない
- `npm audit fix --force` の提案は vitest 3.1.4 への downgrade で使えない

`deny.toml`(#1063)と同じ扱いにする。

## 変更

- `sdk/npm-audit-allowlist.txt`(新規): 許容する GHSA と、その理由・外す条件(#1067)
- `.github/workflows/sdk.yml` の typescript ジョブの audit:
  - 問題なし → これまでどおり通過。許可リストに項目が残っていれば「外せる」と warning
  - レジストリ障害 → これまでどおり最大 5 回まで再試行
  - 指摘あり → `npm audit --json` から high/critical の勧告(GHSA)を取り出し、すべて許可リストにあれば warning を出して通過。1 件でも許可リストになければ、その GHSA を名指しして失敗

追跡: #1067

## 検証

audit ステップの `run` をワークフローから取り出し、`sdk` の package.json / lockfile を複製した作業場所で実行(本物の許可リストには触れない):

| 許可リスト | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 現在の内容 | exit 0、`::warning::accepted allowlisted advisories …: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf` |
| 空 | exit 1、`::error::advisories not on sdk/npm-audit-allowlist.txt: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf` |
| 別の GHSA だけ | exit 1、同上 |

この PR 自身の typescript ジョブでも確認する。

author: albanandrieu
body:
## Objectif
Fermer par défaut le mode de compatibilité `HOMELAB_PUBLIC_DIAGNOSTICS_READONLY` : en l'absence de variable, l'accès aux routes diagnostiques OWNER échoue en mode fail-closed. Valeur `true` explicite encore disponible pour une migration contrôlée.

## Vérification du consommateur
Le site `nabla-site-alban` n'utilise plus `/api/homelab-topology`. Les routes serveur Next.js lisent `/api/site/catalog/v2` et `/api/site/health/v2` à l'aide d'une variable sensible Vercel `DIAGNOSTICS_ACCESS_KEY` passée en `X-Diagnostics-Key`. Le middleware FastAPI classe ces routes `SERVICE` ; elles ne dépendent pas du mode public.

## Modifications
- Default `HOMELAB_PUBLIC_DIAGNOSTICS_READONLY`: `true` → `false`.
- Tests du mode explicite et du fail-closed par défaut.
- Nouveau contrat : SERVICE v2 autorisé avec clé alors que la topologie OWNER demeure interdite hors CIDR.
- Runbook de validation et effets attendus.

## Avant bascule en production
- [ ] Prouver HTTP 200 depuis Vercel Production sur **les deux** endpoints v2 avec la clé masquée (ne pas révéler les secrets).
- [ ] Tester `/fr/truenas`, `/en/truenas` et Architecture depuis la source propriétaire.
- [ ] Résoudre UX de `/api/topology` : `/api/public-topology` est encore classé OWNER, donc la topologie anonyme peut devenir inaccessible.
- [ ] Poser explicitement `HOMELAB_PUBLIC_DIAGNOSTICS_READONLY=false` sur les runtimes Cloud et TrueNAS, vérifier HTTP 401/403 non authentifié et conserver `/api/ui/services` public.
- [ ] Exécuter les contrôles CI sans bypass.

**Limitation :** la clé Vercel existe en Production et Preview, mais sa validité face au FastAPI déployé n'a pas été attestée. Un changement du défaut dans Git ne modifie pas les variables déjà définies sur FastAPI Cloud. Draft pour éviter de prétendre à un cutover confirmé.

## Distinct site-public fallback
`nabla-site-alban` has a separate `HOMELAB_PUBLIC_READONLY_ENABLED` switch: its current code defaults to `true` if missing and only allows the sanitized SERVICE v2 projections anonymously. Vercel's environment-variable inventory does not show that switch set explicitly. **Disabling FastAPI's broader public diagnostic switch does not close the site-specific sanitized public projection**; change this independent setting only if the desired product policy is owner-only even for sanitized site cards.
